ITQAN:v2p305#2/r23.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p305#2/r23.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p305#2/r23.claim: العفو means what remains in your wealth beyond what is needed.
ITQAN:v2p305#2/r23.anchor:
﴿ فمن فرض ﴾ أحرم
1529 ﴿ قل العفو ﴾ ما لا يتبين في أموالكم

DAMGHANI:v1p325/r18.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p325/r18.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p325/r18.claim: ʿAfw means surplus wealth, what remains beyond one’s needs.

SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r1.claim: Khamr properly denotes grape juice after fermentation and frothing; by metaphor it also covers any other liquid that ferments and froths.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r1.anchor: الخمر: المعتصر من العنب إذا غلى وقذف بالزبد

SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r2.claim: The famous derivation connects khamr with covering: it veils the mind like a woman's veil. خامري حضاجر is an admonition to a fool to hide; the segment also cites the hadith about covering vessels and poetry using خمر الطريق for concealing vegetation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r2.anchor: أنها سميت بذلك لأنها تخمر العقل أي تستره

SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r3.claim: A second derivation says wine is covered until it ferments and strengthens, illustrated by the hadith about covering vessels.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r3.anchor: والثاني: لأنها تغطى حتى تدرك وتشتد، ومنه

SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī derives khamr from its mingling with the mind, as in the phrase the disease mixed with him.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r4.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري - لأنها تخامر العقل أي: تخالطه

SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r5.claim: A fourth derivation connects khamr with leaving something until it matures, as dough is left to rise or an opinion until its sound course becomes clear. On all four accounts it is originally a verbal noun used for an active or passive participle.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r5.anchor: والرابع: لأنها تترك حتى تدرك، ومنه: " اختمر العجين "

SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r6.claim: Maysir means gambling and is formed on mifʿal from yusr/yasara-yaysiru. Alqama's line uses ييسرون and another poet's uses ييسرونني as usage evidence.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r6.anchor: والميسر: القمار، مفعل من اليسر، يقال: يسر ييسر.

SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r7.claim: The participant in drawing lots is called yusr and pluralized as أيسار; another account treats يسر as a plural of ياسر, like حرس from حارس.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r7.anchor: واليسر: الذي يدخل في الضرب بالقداح، ويجمع على أيسار

SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r8.claim: One derivation takes maysir from ease, because winnings are easy to obtain; another derives it from wealth, since gambling strips a person of wealth.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r8.anchor: أحدها: من اليسر وهو السهولة، لأن أخذه سهل. الثاني: من اليسار وهو الغنى

SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r9.speaker: مجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī attributes to Mujāhid a derivation from يسر لي كذا, meaning something became due to me; Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r9.anchor: حكاه الطبري عن مجاهد. ورد ابن عطية عليه

SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r10.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r10.claim: Another derivation links maysir to yasar, slaughtering or cutting: a yāsir is the butcher who divides a camel. Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the camel staked for lots was called maysir as the source of gain, then the arrows took that name by proximity.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219/r10.anchor: قال ابن عطية: " وسميت الجزور التي يستهم عليها ميسرا لأنها موضع اليسر

SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r1.claim: The draw used ten lots, or eleven in one account: seven bore one through seven marked shares (الفذ، التوءم، الرقيب، الحلس، النافس، المسبل، المعلى); three blanks were المنيح، السفيح، الوغد, with an optional fourth blank called المضعف.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r1.anchor: فالكيفية أن لهم عشرة أقداح وقيل أحد عشر، لسبعة منها حظوظ

SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r2.claim: They added blank lots to prevent the impartial dealer (الحرضة) from favoring anyone; he knelt, wrapped himself in a cloth, exposed his head, shook the lots in a bag, and drew one for each named person.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r2.anchor: وإنما كثروا بهذه الأغفال ليختلط على الحرضة وهو الضارب، فلا يميل مع أحد

SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r3.claim: A marked lot won its assigned share; a blank meant the person paid toward the camel. This was done in winter scarcity, with the meat given to the poor, not eaten by participants; they took pride in it and called nonparticipants البرم.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r3.anchor: فإن كان من ذوات السهام فاز بذلك النصيب وأخذه، وإن كان من الأغفال غرم

SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r4.claim: Most divided the camel into ten portions, one per lot.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r4.anchor: والجزور تقسم عند الجمهور على عدد القداح فتقسم عشرة أجزاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r5.speaker: الأصمعي
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r5.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says the camel was divided by the count of marked lines, producing twenty-eight portions.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r5.anchor: وعند الأصمعي على عدد خطوط القداح، فتقسم على ثمانية وعشرين جزءا

SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls al-Aṣmaʿī's division mistaken.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r6.anchor: وخطأ ابن عطية الأصمعي في ذلك

SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r7.claim: The author calls that correction surprising: Arabs may have divided the camel by ten lots on one occasion and by twenty-eight marked shares on another.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#2/r7.anchor: وهذا عجيب منه، لأنه يحتمل أن العرب كانت تقسمها مرة على عشرة ومرة على ثمانية وعشرين

SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r1.claim: A noun is omitted after عن: the question concerns the ruling on wine and gambling, including permissibility or prohibition, not the substances themselves; the answer matches that understood question.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r1.anchor: وقوله { عن الخمر } لا بد من حذف مضاف، إذ السؤال عن ذاتي الخمر

SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r2.claim: فيهما is the fronted predicate and إثم the delayed subject. Fronting is optional because indefiniteness is also licensed by description or coordination; a noun meaning their use is omitted because sin is not inherent in the substances.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r2.anchor: الجار خبر مقدم، و " إثم " مبتدأ مؤخر، وتقديم الخبر هنا ليس بواجب

SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r3.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read كثير; the others read كبير. The majority form suits sin described as grave, drinking and gambling as major sins, and the seven readers' ب in وإثمهما أكبر.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة الكسائي: " كثير " بالثاء المثلثة، والباقون بالباء ثانية الحروف

SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r4.claim: The much-sin reading may describe the many individual sins of drinkers and gamblers, or the repeated and multiplied punishment resulting from their acts.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r4.anchor: وأما وجه قراءة الأخوين: فإما باعتبار الآثمين من الشاربين والمقامرين فلكل واحد إثم

SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r5.claim: It can also encompass the bad words and deeds produced by drinking, and all involved with wine from grape to consumption; the Prophet cursed wine and ten parties connected with it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r5.anchor: وإما باعتبار ما يترتب على شربها مما يصدر من شاربها من الأقوال السيئة والأفعال القبيحة

SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r6.claim: The plural benefits contrasts with singular sin, so describing the sin as many matches the collective sense. The author says each reading should be supported without weakening the other, as in the earlier ملك and مالك discussion.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r6.anchor: مقابل ل " منافع " و " منافع " جمع، فناسب أن توصف مقابلة

SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r7.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ calls the ب reading better: grave sins are called كبائر and lesser ones صغائر. He still regards the ث reading as sound, since abundance is a kind of greatness just as smallness can mean lowliness or scarcity.
SAMIN-DURR:2:219#3/r7.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء: " الأحسن القراءة بالباء لأنه يقال: إثم كبير وصغير

ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r1.claim: Wine is the agreed case; by analogy, anything that acts like it is also called khamr and has the same prohibition.
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r1.anchor: (الخمر) المجمع عليه، وقياس كل ما عمل عملها أن يقال له خمر

ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r2.claim: Khamr is named from covering: it applies to what veils a person, a woman’s veil, a prayer mat covering the face, and dough covered by fermentation.
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r2.anchor: وتأويل الخمر في اللغة أنه كل ما ستر العقل، يقال لكل ما ستر الإنسان مق شجر وغيره خمر

ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r3.claim: All intoxicants are khamr because they mix with and cover the intellect, whatever name they are given; drinkers are described as intoxicated or suffering a hangover.
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r3.anchor: فهذا كله يدل على أن كل مسكر خمر وكل مسكر مخالط العقل ومغط عليه، وليس يقول أحد للشارب

ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r4.speaker: أبو الأسود الدؤلي
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r4.claim: After someone claimed a differently named intoxicant was lawful, Abū al-Aswad recognized it as wine’s kin; his poem says the two are siblings nurtured by the same mother.
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r4.anchor: وقد لبس على ابي الأسود الدؤلي فقيل له: إن هذا المسكر الذي سموه بغير الخمر حلال

ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r5.speaker: قراء
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r5.claim: A variant reading has kathīr (‘much’) in place of kabīr (‘great’) in the phrase about sin.
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r5.anchor: وقال أهل التفسير في قوله عز وجل: (قل فيهما إثم كبير) وقرئت " كثير "

ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r6.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r6.claim: Some say this verse only discouraged wine and gambling, with their prohibition made explicit later in al-Māʾida.
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r6.anchor: قال قوم زهد فيها في هذا الموضع

ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r7.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r7.claim: Others say the prohibition is already conveyed here and is clarified by the Book elsewhere.
ZAJJAJ:v1p291/r7.anchor: وقال قوم: لا بل تحرم بما بين ههنا مما دل عليه الكتاب في موضع آخر.

ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r1.claim: Wine is prohibited by the Qur’anic text because it is called a great sin, and God explicitly forbids sin; Zajjāj cites 7:33 despite consensus.
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r1.anchor: لأنه قال: (إثم كبير) وقد حرم الله الإثم نصا فقال: (قل إنما حرم ربي الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن والإثم والبغي بغير الحق).

ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r2.claim: Wine causes enmity and hatred and obstructs reason, by which one distinguishes things and recognizes duties toward the Creator.
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r2.anchor: فأما الإثم الكبير الذي في الخمر فبين، لأنها توقع العداوة والبغضاء وتحول بين المرء وعقله الذي يميز به ويعرف ما يجب لخالقه.

ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r3.claim: Gambling breeds enmity and hatred, and transfers a person's property to another without compensation.
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r3.anchor: والقمار يورث العداوة والبغضاء وإن مال الإنسان يصير إلى غيره بغير جزاء يؤخذ عليه

ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r4.claim: Wine's benefits include pleasure and profit from trading in it.
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r4.anchor: وأما المنافع للناس فيه فاللذة في الخمر والربح في المتجر فيها

ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r5.claim: Gambling can bring a person property without toil or effort.
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r5.anchor: وكذلك المنفعة في القمار، يصير الشيء إلى الإنسان بغير كد ولا تعب

ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r6.claim: The sin in wine and gambling outweighs their benefits.
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r6.anchor: فأعلم الله أن الإثم فيهما (إثم) أكبر من نفعهما.

ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r7.claim: Both accusative and nominative are possible for al-ʿafw when mā-dhā is treated as one noun and al-ʿafw is referred back to it.
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r7.anchor: النصنب والرفع في (العفو) جميعا، من " جعل (ماذا) اسما واحدا رد العفو عليه

ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r8.claim: If mā is a noun and dhā a predicate meaning alladhī, al-ʿafw is nominative as the answer to what they spend.
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r8.anchor: من جعل " ما " اسما و " إذا " خبرها وهي في معنى الذي رد العفو عليه فرفع، كأنه قال: ما الذي ينفقون؟ فقال: العفو

ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r9.claim: Al-ʿafw may be accusative as the object of yunfiqun: spend the surplus, even when mā is a noun by itself.
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r9.anchor: ويجوز أن ينصب العفو وإن كان ما وحدها اسما فتحمل العفو علي ينفقون، كأنه قيل أنفقوا العفو.

ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r10.claim: Al-ʿafw may also be nominative with compound mā-dhā, understood as the predicate in, Say: it is the surplus.
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r10.anchor: ويجوز أيضا أن ترفع - وإن جعلت (ماذا) بمنزلة شيء واحد على "قل هو العفو".

ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r11.claim: Al-ʿafw means surplus or abundance; ʿafā al-qawm describes a people who became numerous.
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r11.anchor: والعفو في اللغة الفضل والكثرة، يقال عفا القوم إذا كثروا.

ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r12.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r12.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r12.claim: People were commanded to give away surplus until alms tax was prescribed; consensus holds zakat rules specify dues on the kinds of property.
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r12.anchor: فأمروا أن ينفقوا الفضل إلى أن فرضت الزكاة، فكان أهل المكاسب يأخذ أحدهم من كسبه ما يكفيه ويتصدق بباقيه

ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r13.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r13.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r13.claim: Exegetical reports describe earners keeping enough income and owners of gold and silver keeping a year's provision, then donating the remainder.
ZAJJAJ:v1p292/r13.anchor: ويأخذ أهل الذهب والفضة ما يكفيهم في عامهم وينفقون باقيه هذا قد روي في التفسير

ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r1.claim: The clarification about wine and gambling exemplifies how God makes His signs clear.
ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r1.anchor: أي مثل هذا البيان في الخمر والميسر (يبين الله لكم الآيات)

ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r2.claim: The Prophet's address also addresses his community; singular address followed by a plural is common in Arabic and frequent in the Qur’an.
ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r2.anchor: لأن خطاب النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - مشتمل على خطاب أمته كما قال عز وجل: (يا أيها النبي إذا طلقتم النساء)

ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r3.claim: A plural group can be treated as a collective tribe and referred to with singular dhālika; the Qur’an likewise uses dhālika after addressing the Prophet's wives with minkunna.
ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r3.anchor: قال الله تعالى: (يا نساء النبي من يأت منكن بفاحشة مبينة يضاعف لها العذاب ضعفين وكان ذلك على الله يسيرا (30) - والأصل ذلكن، إلا أن الجماعة في معنى القبيل.

ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r4.claim: In this world and the next may attach to you reflect, meaning reflect on the affairs of both worlds.
ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r4.anchor: يجوز أن يكون (تتفكرون في الدنيا والآخرة) من صلة تتفكرون المعنى لعلكم تتفكرون في أمر الدنيا وأمر الآخرة

ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r5.claim: Alternatively, in this world and the next may attach to God clarifies the signs, meaning signs concerning both worlds are clarified so people reflect.
ZAJJAJ:v1p293/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في الدنيا والآخرة من صلة كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات). أي يبين لكم الآيات في أمر الدنيا وأمر الآخرة لعلكم تتفكرون.

ASAD-NOTES:2:219#n204/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:219#n204/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:219#n204/r1.claim: Ithm literally means sin or anything conducive to sinning; because it is contrasted with benefits, Asad considers “evil” a suitable rendering.
ASAD-NOTES:2:219#n204/r1.anchor: Lit., "sin", or anything that is conducive to sinning.

ASAD-NOTES:2:219#n204/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:219#n204/r2.speaker: Razi
ASAD-NOTES:2:219#n204/r2.claim: Razi and other classical commentators point out that ithm is used as the antithesis of manafiʿ, “benefits.”
ASAD-NOTES:2:219#n204/r2.anchor: As some of the classical commentators (e.g., Razi) point out, the term ithm is used in this verse as the antithesis of manafi' ("benefits")

ASAD-NOTES:2:219#n205/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:219#n205/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:219#n205/r1.claim: Although this verse says their evil outweighs their benefit, Asad points to the clear prohibition of intoxicants and games of chance in 5:90–91.
ASAD-NOTES:2:219#n205/r1.anchor: For a clear-cut prohibition of intoxicants and games of chance, see 5:90-91 and the corresponding notes.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r1.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read kathīr with thāʾ; the rest read kabīr with bāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r1.anchor: فقرأ الكسائي وحمزة: إثم كثير بالثاء. وقرأ الباقون: كبير بالباء

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r2.speaker: سعيد عن قتادة
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r2.claim: Qatāda says the verse condemned wine without prohibiting it while it was lawful; the prayer and later al-Māʾida verses then prohibited every amount.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r2.anchor: سعيد عن قتادة: قل فيهما إثم كبير ذمها ولم يحرمها، وهي يومئذ حلال

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r3.speaker: أهل النظر
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r3.claim: Some scholars infer prohibition because God forbids sin in 7:33 and this verse calls wine and gambling a great sin.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r3.anchor: ومن أهل النظر من يذهب إلى أن قوله جل وعز : قل فيهما إثم كبير

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r4.claim: Al-Fārisī also reads the sin as arising in deeming wine and gambling lawful; only some qualities of otherwise ordinary things are forbidden.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r4.anchor: وقال: قل فيهما إثم كبير، والمعنى: في استحلالهما.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r5.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa says looking at wine for sensual enjoyment is itself forbidden.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r5.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة فيما أخبرنا أبو الحسن: أنه إذا نظر إليها على وجه التلذذ بها

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r6.claim: The sin refers to sinful acts committed through wine and gambling and the causes leading to them.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r6.anchor: وكذلك قوله تعالى : وإثمهما أكبر من نفعهما إنما هو إثم معاص تفعل فيها

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r7.speaker: بعض نقلة الآثار
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r7.claim: Transmitters report that this verse descended without prohibiting wine; reports differ on whether prohibition came here or in al-Māʾida.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p307/r7.anchor: وقال بعض نقلة الآثار: تواتر الخبر أن الآية التي في البقرة نزلت، ولم يحرم بها

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p309/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p309/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p309/r1.claim: Al-Fārisī says ithm can denote appropriated property; ‘sin or offense’ distinguishes a wrong against God from a wrong against people, and the verse arose over theft.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p309/r1.anchor: ولكن الإثم قد وقع في التنزيل على ما يقتطعه الإنسان من مال من لا يجوز له أن يقتطع من ماله

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p310/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p310/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p310/r6.claim: Taʾaththama and taḥawwaba mean avoiding sin although their forms might suggest committing it, like tafawwaqa and tajarraʿa.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p310/r6.anchor: وقالوا: تأثم الرجل: إذا ترك الإثم واجتنبه، وتحوب: إذا ترك الحوب

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p312/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p312/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p312/r1.claim: Labīd’s h-j-d forms contrast sleeping with staying awake; the Qurʾān uses tahajjud for night prayer, illustrating the specialized sense.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p312/r1.anchor: قال هجدنا فقد طال السرى أي: نومنا. وقالوا تهجد إذا سهر

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p312/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p312/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p312/r2.claim: Al-Fārisī favors kabīr: great sin contrasts with small sin, matching kabāʾir and akbar; great sin is also ʿaẓīm, while kathīr would contrast with qalīl.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p312/r2.anchor: حجة من قرأ بالباء: إثم كبير أن يقول: الباء أولى، لأن الكبر مثل العظم

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p312/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p312/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p312/r3.claim: The thāʾ reading is supported by the warning that wine and gambling produce enmity and obstruct remembrance and prayer.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r1.claim: The Prophetic report about ten persons involved with wine being cursed supports the kathīr reading.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك عن النبي
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r2.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet cursed ten people involved in wine, including buyers, sellers, producers, carriers, servers, and those who consume its price.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r2.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: «لعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r3.claim: Even if harms arise from effects of wine and gambling, revelation assigns blame to them; gambling includes wrongful taking of wealth.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r3.anchor: فقد وقع الذم في التنزيل عليها

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r4.claim: Since sin is balanced against benefits, kathīr naturally means many harms, like the Qurʾānic description of numerous livestock benefits.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r4.anchor: ومما يقوي قراءة من قرأ كثير

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p314/r5.claim: Wine is not linguistically identical to nabīdh; primary names are not assigned by analogy, as Abū al-Aswad’s poem calls wine its sister.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr alone reads al-ʿafw nominative; others read it accusative, also reported from Ibn ʿĀmir. A Meccan transmission from Ibn Kathīr has nominative, though Meccans now read accusative.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r1.anchor: فقرأ أبو عمرو وحده: قل العفو رفعا. وقرأ الباقون: العفو نصبا.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās defines al-ʿafw as what remains beyond the family’s needs.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: العفو: ما فضل عن أهلك.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r3.speaker: عطاء وقتادة والسدي
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ, Qatāda, and al-Suddī define al-ʿafw as surplus.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r4.speaker: الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says it is the non-straining good surplus of one’s wealth, excluding the principal.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r4.anchor: قال الحسن: قل العفو: ما لا يجهدكم صفوه من أموالكم، ليس بالأصول.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda defines it as affordable capacity or moderation and connects it to what is clear or available.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r5.anchor: أبو عبيدة: العفو: الطاقة التي تطيقها، والقصد، يقال: ما عفا لك

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r6.speaker: غيره
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r6.claim: Another authority glosses al-ʿafw as wealth beyond one’s exertion.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r7.claim: Mādhā can be one compound interrogative noun; retaining the alif in ʿammā dhā tasʾalu shows mā is not word-final, unlike ʿamma and fīma.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r7.anchor: أحدهما: أن يكون ما مع ذا اسما واحدا

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r8.claim: Alternatively, dhā can mean ‘that which’; a cited poem uses mādhā in that sense.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r8.anchor: والآخر: أن يكون ذا بمنزلة الذي

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r9.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r9.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r9.claim: In the poet’s question about the women, mādhā functions like mā alone; parsing dhā as a relative pronoun is unnatural.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p315/r9.anchor: يا خزر تغلب ماذا بال نسوتكم ... لا يستفقن إلى الديرين تحنانا

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r1.claim: The reading with bāʾ, kabīr, is supported by the next phrase's akbar rather than akthar.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن قرأبالياء قوله بعد ذلك ﴿ وإثمهما أكبر من نفعهما ﴾ ولم يقل أكثر

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r2.claim: The reading with thāʾ, kathīr, suits the counted items of consumed wine and gambling; a verse elsewhere uses akthar for degree or amount.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن قرأبالثاء أنه لما وقع اللفظ على أعداد وهي الخمرة المشروبة والميسر وهو القمار كانت الثاء في ذلك أولى

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r3.claim: With rafʿ, mā and dhā are separate: dhā is relative, and al-ʿafw is the predicate answering what they should spend.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r3.anchor: فمن رفع جعل ذا منفصلة من ما فيكون بمعنى الذي فكأنه قال ما الذي ينفقون فقال الذي ينفقون العفو فترفعه بخبر الابتداء

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r4.claim: With naṣb, mādhā is one interrogative word and al-ʿafw is the object of yanfiqūn.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r4.anchor: والحجة لمن نصب أنه جعل ماذا كلمة واحدة ونصب العفو بقوله ينفقون كأنه قال قال ينفقون العفو

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r5.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r5.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r5.claim: Mā and dhā combine because both are general and ambiguous, covering rational and non-rational things; man is restricted to rational beings, so man and dhā do not combine.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p96/r5.anchor: لما كانت ما عامة لمن يعقل ولما لا يعقل وذا مثلها في الابهام والعموم بنوهما للمشاركة ولما اختصت من بمن يعقل لم يبنوها مع ذا

NASHR:v2p226/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p226/r6.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
NASHR:v2p226/r6.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read إثم كثير with thāʾ; the other readers read إثم كبير with bāʾ.
NASHR:v2p226/r6.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي بالثاء المثلثة، وقرأ الباقون بالباء الموحدة.

NASHR:v2p226/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p226/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p226/r7.claim: Abu Amr reads العفو with nominative; the other readers use accusative.

NASHR:v2p159/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p159/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p159/r6.claim: The joined form ماذا has six possible analyses: interrogative plus demonstrative, interrogative plus relative, compound interrogative, a single noun meaning thing, extra ما plus demonstrative, or interrogative ما plus extra ذا.
NASHR:v2p159/r6.anchor: ويختلف فيه أهل العربية نحو (ماذا) يأتي في العربية على ستة، أوجه.

NASHR:v2p159/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p159/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p159/r7.claim: Abu Amr's nominative العفو favors two words, interrogative ما and relative ذا, allowing a pause after either; other readers' accusative favors one compound word and a pause only after ذا.
NASHR:v2p159/r7.anchor: فمن قرأ العفو بالرفع، وهو أبو عمرو يترجح أن يكون ماذا كلمتين. ما استفهامية وذا بمعنى الذي

QIRAAT-ER:2:219:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:219:7#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:219:7#1/r1.claim: The canonical vowel variant changes the hāʾ of fīhimā from kasra to ḍamma, with both dual pronoun forms grammatically valid.
QIRAAT-ER:2:219:7#1/r1.anchor: Vowel shift: kasra to ḍamma on hā — fīhimā (standard) vs fīhumā

QIRAAT-ER:2:219:9#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:219:9#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:219:9#1/r1.claim: A dot variant changes bāʾ to thāʾ, changing k-b-r greatness to k-th-r abundance: the sin is abundant rather than great.
QIRAAT-ER:2:219:9#1/r1.anchor: Dot-variant: bā' → thā' shifts k-b-r (greatness) to k-th-r (abundance)

QIRAAT-ER:2:219:24#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:219:24#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:219:24#1/r1.claim: The nominative al-ʿafwu reading treats it as subject or predicate, while accusative al-ʿafwa is an object reading, restructuring the syntax.
QIRAAT-ER:2:219:24#1/r1.anchor: Nominative variant: al-ʿafwu (ḍamma) = subject/predicate reading vs al-ʿafwa (fatḥa)

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r1.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r1.claim: Mujahid and Qatada report that when this verse came, some people continued drinking and others abstained, until wine was prohibited in al-Maʾida.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r1.anchor: عن قتادة عن رجل عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر ﴾ قالا لما نزلت هذه الآية شربها بعض الناس

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r2.anchor: حتى نزل تحريمها في سورة المائدة قال قتادة والميسر القمار

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r3.speaker: مجاهد وسعيد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r3.claim: Mujahid and Saʿid define all gambling as maysir, including children’s game of walnuts.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r3.anchor: عن ليث عن مجاهد وسعيد قالا الميسر القمار كله حتى الجوز الذي يلعب به الصبيان

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud warns against playing with dice or knucklebones, calling them a form of gambling.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r4.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص قال سمعت ابن مسعود يقول إياكم وزجرا بالكعبين أو قال بالكعبتين فإنهما من الميسر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r5.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r5.claim: Qatada glosses al-ʿafw as surplus wealth.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ قل العفو ﴾ قال هو الفضل

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r6.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r6.claim: Qatada says reflection on this world and the next lets people recognize the superiority of the afterlife over worldly life.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p88/r6.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ لعلكم تتفكرون في الدنيا والآخرة ﴾ قال يقول لعلكم تتفكرون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r1.claim: Khamr is grape juice that has boiled, strengthened, and thrown up foam; it is named from covering because it veils the intellect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r1.anchor: هي المعتصر من العنب إذا غلى واشتد وقذف بالزبد، سمي بذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r2.claim: Another derivation says wine is so called because it is covered and left until it ripens and strengthens.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r2.anchor: لأنها تخمر: أي تغطي حتى تدرك وتشتد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbari derives the name from wine mixing with the intellect; related verbs mean that illness mixes with something.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r3.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: سميت بذلك لأنها تخامر العقل أي: تخالطه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r4.claim: Other derivations invoke leaving dough or an opinion until it matures or becomes clear; on these derivations خمر began as a verbal noun used as an active or passive participle.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r4.anchor: تترك حين تدرك، يقال: اختمر العجين بلغ إدراكه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r5.claim: Maysir means gambling and follows the pattern maf'il from yasara, as maw'id derives from wa'ada; yasartu al-maysir means I gambled.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p398/r5.anchor: القمار، وهو مفعل من: يسر، كالموعد من وعد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r1.claim: The name maysir is variously derived from ease, affluence because gambling strips it away, something becoming due, or slaughtering and cutting up a camel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r1.anchor: اشتقاقه من اليسر وهو السهولة، أو من اليسار لأنه يسلب يساره،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r2.claim: The poem's use of تيسرون and يسرت supports connecting maysir with gambling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r2.anchor: تيسرون بخيل قد يسرت بها ... وكل ما يسر الأقوام مغروم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r3.claim: The camel used for drawing lots was called maysir as the site of a windfall; by proximity the arrows were also called maysir.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r3.anchor: وسميت الجزور التي يسهم عليها ميسرا لأنها موضع اليسر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r4.claim: Yusr, the participant in drawing lots, has plural aysār; another analysis makes yusr a plural of yāsir, like ḥāris and ḥaras.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r4.anchor: واليسر، الذي يدخل في الضرب بالقداح وجمعه، أيسار، وقيل: يسر جمع ياسر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r5.claim: The game used ten arrows, or eleven; seven carried shares from one to seven, assigned to named arrows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r5.anchor: وصفة الميسر أنه عشرة أقداح، وقيل: أحد عشر على ما ذكر فيه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r6.claim: The three blank arrows were al-maniḥ, al-safīḥ, and al-waghd; another count has four, adding al-masdar and al-muḍaʿʿaf.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r6.anchor: وثلاثة أغفال لا حظوظ لها، وهي: المنيح، والسفيح، والوغد، وقيل: أربعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r7.claim: Blank arrows increased and mixed the lots to prevent the dealer from favoring anyone; the dealer was also called the roller, drawer, or striker and was regarded as just.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r7.anchor: لتكثر السهام وتختلط على الحرضة وهو الضارب بالقداح، فلا يجد إلى الميل مع أحد سبيلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r8.claim: The dealer knelt, covered himself with a cloth, placed the arrows in a quiver, mixed them, and drew one for each named man.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r8.anchor: ثم يجثو الضارب على ركبتيه، ويلتحف بثوب، ويخرج رأسه يجعل تلك القداح في الربابة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r9.claim: A winning arrow awarded its marked share; a blank won nothing and its holder had to cover the full cost of the camel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r9.anchor: فمن خرج له قدح من ذوات الأنصباء أخذ النصيب الموسوم به ذلك القدح، ومن خرج له قدح من تلك الثلاثة لم يأخذ شيئا، وغرم الجزور كله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r10.claim: Arabs played in winter hardship to provide for the poor: the players bought and slaughtered a camel, dividing it into ten shares according to Abu Amr or twenty-eight according to al-Asma'i.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p399/r10.anchor: وكانت عادة العرب أن تضرب بهذه القداح في الشتوة وضيق العيش وكلب البرد على الفقراء، فيشترون الجزور وتضمن الأيسار ثمنها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya says al-Asma'i was mistaken to divide the camel into twenty-eight portions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وأخطأ الأصمعي في قسمة الجزور على ثمانية وعشرين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r2.claim: A winner shared his portion with the poor, ate none of it, and took pride in generosity; those who abstained were called baram and disparaged, though gamblers sometimes ate for themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r2.anchor: وأيهم خرج له نصيب واسى به الفقراء، ولا يأكل منه شيئا، ويفتخرون بذلك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r3.speaker: الأعشى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r3.claim: Al-A'sha's verse praises feeding a winter guest and providing food for the gambler, evidence of the game's association with generosity.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r4.speaker: زهير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r4.claim: Zuhayr's verse uses baram for a man who is neither shamelessly greedy nor miserly when his companions win.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r4.anchor: وقال زهير في البرم: حتى تآوى إلى لا فاحش برم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r5.claim: The gamblers sometimes took a portion of the meat for themselves.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r6.claim: Tafakkur is turning thought over a matter; fikr is the mind.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p400/r6.anchor: التفكر: في الشيء إجالة الفكر فيه وتردده، والفكر: هو الذهن.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r8.speaker: عمر ومعاذ
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r8.claim: The occasion reported is that ʿUmar and Muʿādh asked the Prophet for a ruling on wine and gambling, saying they destroy reason and strip away wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r8.anchor: سبب نزولها سؤال عمر ومعاذ، قالا:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r9.claim: The question follows discussion of charitable spending and fighting because wine and gambling consume wealth that might otherwise go to charity or jihad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r9.anchor: إذ هما أيضا من مصارف المال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r10.speaker: بعض من ألف في الناسخ والمنسوخ
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r10.claim: Some works on abrogation say most scholars regard this verse as abrogating the prior permissibility of wine, setting aside the Meccan Anʿām passage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r10.anchor: وقال بعض من ألف في الناسخ والمنسوخ:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r11.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r11.claim: Ibn Jubayr describes a staged prohibition: some abstained after this verse, while others drank for its benefits until prayer-time restriction and then the final command to avoid it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r11.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: لما نزل قل فيهما إثم كبير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r12.speaker: مكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r12.claim: Makkī takes the sequence reported by Ibn Jubayr to show that this verse was abrogated by the later prohibition in al-Māʾida.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r12.anchor: قال مكي: فهذا يدل على أن هذه منسوخة بآية المائدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r13.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r13.claim: Qatāda says this verse disparaged wine without yet prohibiting it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r13.anchor: وقال قتادة: ذم الله الخمر بهذه الآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r14.speaker: بعض الناس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r14.claim: Some reject calling this abrogation of an earlier permission: wine had simply been left unaddressed, and people continued their customary practice until prohibition came.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p402/r14.anchor: وقال بعض الناس: لا يقال إن هذه الآية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r1.claim: The plural verb is used although the reported questioners were two, since Arabic can attribute one person’s act to a group.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r1.anchor: وجاء: ويسئلونك بواو الجمع وإن كان من سأل اثنين: وهما عمرو ومعاذ،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r2.claim: They ask about the legal status, permissibility, and use of wine and gambling, not about what substances they are; the answer therefore addresses their ruling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r2.anchor: والسؤال هنا ليس عن الذات، وإنما هو عن حكم هذين من حل وحرمة وانتفاع،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r3.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r3.claim: The majority define wine in law as anything drunk that overcomes and corrupts the intellect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r3.anchor: وأما في الشريعة، فقال الجمهور: كل ما خامر العقل وأفسده مما يشرب يسمى خمرا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r4.speaker: الرازي عن أبي حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī reports Abū Ḥanīfa’s definition of khamr as specifically what is made from grapes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r4.anchor: وقال الرازي، عن أبي حنيفة: الخمر اسم ما يتخذ من العنب خاصة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r5.speaker: السمرقندي عن أبي حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r5.claim: Al-Samarqandī reports Abū Ḥanīfa including grape, raisin, and date drinks, while treating corn and wheat drinks as mind-confusing foods rather than beverages.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r5.anchor: ونقل عنه السمرقندي: أن الخمر عنده هو اسم ما اتخذ من العنب والزبيب والتمر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls the sound report from Abū Ḥanīfa that even a drop of these drinks is khamr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r6.anchor: وقيل: الصحيح، عن أبي حنيفة، أن القطرة من هذه الأشربة من الخمر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r7.claim: Maysir first named pre-Islamic Arab gambling; in law it covers every form of gambling, whose prohibition is agreed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r7.anchor: وأما في الشريعة فاسم الميسر يطلق على سائر ضروب القمار، والإجماع منعقد على تحريمه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r8.speaker: علي، وابن عباس، وعطاء، وابن سيرين، والحسن، وابن المسيب، وقتادة، وطاووس، ومجاهد، ومعاوية بن صالح
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r8.claim: These authorities classify every gambling game, including dice, chess, and children’s knucklebones or nuts, as maysir, except permitted horse wagers and lots for allocating rights.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r9.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r9.claim: Mālik distinguishes amusement maysir, such as dice and chess, from gambling maysir, in which people wager against one another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r9.anchor: وقال مالك: الميسر ميسران: ميسر اللهو فمنه: النرد والشطرنج والملاهي كلها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r10.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r10.claim: ʿAlī calls chess “the maysir of the non-Arabs.”

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r11.speaker: القاسم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r11.claim: Al-Qāsim says anything that distracts from remembering God and prayer counts as maysir.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r11.anchor: وقال القاسم، كل شيء ألهى عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة فهو ميسر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r12.speaker: القفال
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r12.claim: Al-Qaffāl gives a four-stage sequence for wine: the palm-and-grape verse, this verse, the prayer restriction, then final prohibition; gradualism eased a people accustomed to drinking.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p403/r12.anchor: قال القفال: ووقع التحريم على هذا الترتيب، لأنه تعالى علم أن القوم كانوا ألفوا شربها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r1.speaker: الربيع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r1.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says this verse was revealed after wine had already been prohibited.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r1.anchor: وقال الربيع: نزلت هذه الآية بعد تحريم الخمر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān’s apparent reading is prohibitive: consuming either entails grave sin, and anything sinful or containing sin is forbidden; sin outweighs benefit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r2.anchor: والظاهر أنها تدل على ذلك، والمعنى: قل في تعاطيهما إثم كبير، أي: حصول إثم كبير،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan states the general rule that whatever contains sin is forbidden.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: ما فيه الإثم محرم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r4.claim: A cited poet calls wine “sin,” because drinking it makes the drinker lose reason; the usage reflects the sin associated with it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r4.anchor: ولما كان في شربها الإثم سميت إثما في قول الشاعر:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r5.speaker: مخالفو التحريم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r5.claim: Those denying that the verse prohibits argue that a forbidden thing cannot have benefits and that the Companions waited for the prayer and al-Māʾida verses before abstaining.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r5.anchor: ومن قال: لا تدل على التحريم، استدل بقوله: ومنافع للناس، والمحرم لا يكون فيه منفعة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān answers that prohibited things may have immediate worldly benefits, and some Companions sought an unmistakable explicit command to make the prohibition unequivocal.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r6.anchor: وأجيب بأن المحرم قد يكون فيه منفعة عاجلة في الدنيا، وبأن بعض الصحابة سأل أن ينزل التحريم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والربيع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Rabīʿ assign the sin to the period after prohibition and the benefits to the earlier period.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، والربيع: الإثم فيهما بعد التحريم، والمنفعة فيهما قبل التحريم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers the apparent sense: sin and benefit are both being reported as present, and the sin is wrongdoing that brings punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r8.anchor: والظاهر أنه إخبار عن الحال، والإثم الذي فيهما هو الذنب الذي يترتب عليه العقاب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r9.speaker: طائفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r9.claim: One group identifies wine’s sins as loss of reason, verbal abuse, slander, and aggression produced by the drinker.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r9.anchor: وقالت طائفة: الإثم الذي في الخمر: ذهاب العقل، والسباب، والافتراء، والتعدي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r10.speaker: الأكثرون ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r10.claim: Most commentators, including Mujāhid’s reported explanation, take wine’s benefit to mean profit and earnings from its trade.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r10.anchor: والمنفعة التي في الخمر، قال الأكثرون: ما يحصل منها من الأرباح والأكساب، وهو معنى قول مجاهد:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r11.speaker: الأطباء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r11.claim: Medical writers cited worldly benefits such as relief from sorrow, cheerfulness, digestion, strength, sexual vigor, generosity, complexion, and courage; they also catalogued many harms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p404/r11.anchor: وقيل ما ذكر الأطباء في منافعها من ذهاب الهم، وحصول الفرح، وهضم الطعام، وتقوية الضعيف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r1.claim: One stated benefit of gambling is that a winner becomes wealthy without work or exertion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r1.anchor: والمنفعة التي في الميسر إيسار القامر بغير كد ولا تعب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r2.claim: Another claimed benefit is aid to the needy: winners of the camel-meat game distributed their share to the poor.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r2.anchor: وقيل: التوسعة على المحاويج، فإن من قمر منهم كان لا يأكل من الجزور،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r3.claim: This verse does not address jurisprudential details such as other intoxicants, the drinker’s prescribed penalty, how flogging is done, or places to avoid striking; those belong to fiqh.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r3.anchor: ولم تتعرض الآية لشيء من ذلك، وهو مذكور في علم الفقه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r4.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r4.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read إثم كثير (“many sins”); the majority read كبير (“great sin”). كثرة can refer to many offenders, cumulative punishment, many sinful acts, or the many parties involved in wine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r4.anchor: وقرأ حمزة، والكسائي: إثم كثير، بالثاء، ووصف الإثم بالكثرة إما باعتبار الآثمين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r5.claim: A Prophetic report curses wine and the many people connected with producing, selling, transporting, serving, drinking, and profiting from it, illustrating the multiplicity of its sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r5.anchor: فقد لعن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الخمر، ولعن معها عشرة: بائعها، ومبتاعها، والمشتراة له،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r6.speaker: الباقون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r6.claim: The remaining canonical readers read كبير; Abū Ḥayyān says this is apt because drinking wine and gambling are major sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r6.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: كبير، بالباء، وذلك ظاهر، لأن شرب الخمر والقمار ذنبهما من الكبائر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects attempts to rank one of the two canonical readings above the other, since both are God’s speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r7.anchor: وهذا خطأ، لأن كلا من القراءتين كلام الله تعالى، فلا يجوز تفضيل شيء منه على شيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r8.claim: In ʿAbd Allāh’s codex and reading, “أكثر” and “كثير” appear with thāʾ in the comparative and the earlier phrase.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r8.anchor: وإثمهما أكبر من نفعهما في مصحف عبد الله وقراءته: أكثر، بالثاء كما في مصحفه:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the comparison as the punishment of sin exceeding the pleasures, social advantages, and winnings associated with drinking and gambling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r9.anchor: قال الزمخشري: وعقاب الإثم في تعاطيهما أكبر من نفعهما، وهو الالتذاذ بشرب الخمر، والقمار،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r10.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r10.claim: A reading attributed to Ubayy has أقرب (“nearer”) in place of أكبر.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p405/r10.anchor: وفي قراءة أبي: وإثمهما أقرب، ومعنى الكثرة أن: أصحاب الشرب والقمار يقترفون فيهما الآثام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Muqātil say sin after prohibition exceeds benefit before it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، وسعيد بن جبير، والضحاك، ومقاتل: إثمهما بعد التحريم أكبر من نفعهما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r2.claim: Another explanation is that sin is greater because its punishment endures while worldly benefits disappear; what lasts is greater than what passes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r2.anchor: وقيل: أكبر، لأن عقابه باق مستمر والمنافع زائلة، والباقي أكبر من الفاني.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r3.claim: The spending question had already been asked; this answer now clarifies the quantity or amount to spend.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r3.anchor: ويسئلونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو تقدم هذا السؤال وأجيبوا هنا بذكر الكمية والمقدار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r4.claim: The questioner is identified either as ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ or, more apparently, the believers collectively, as the plural verb suggests.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r4.anchor: والسائل في هذه الآية، قيل: هو عمرو بن الجموح،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r5.claim: The spending may be for jihad or charity; most who say charity understand voluntary almsgiving.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r5.anchor: والنفقة هنا قيل: في الجهاد، وقيل: في الصدقات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r6.claim: Some say the question concerns obligatory giving, specifically zakāt, whose details were later set out by the Sunna.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r6.anchor: وقيل: في الواجب، والقائلون في الواجب، قيل: هي الزكاة المفروضة، وجاء ذكرها هنا مجملا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r7.claim: Another view says people were required before zakāt to give earnings beyond their annual needs, and that duty was superseded by the zakāt verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r7.anchor: وقيل كان واجبا عليهم قبل فرض الزكاة أن ينفقوا ما فضل من مكاسبهم عن ما يكفيهم في عامهم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses al-ʿafw as what remains beyond the needs of one’s family and property.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r8.anchor: والعفو: ما فضل عن الأهل والمال، قاله ابن عباس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r9.speaker: طاووس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r9.claim: Ṭāwūs understands al-ʿafw as an easy, modest amount that does not damage one’s wealth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r9.anchor: أو اليسير السهل الذي لا يجحف بالمال قاله طاووس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r10.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan defines al-ʿafw as the moderate amount between extravagance and falling short.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r10.anchor: أو الوسط الذي لا سرف فيه ولا تقصير، قاله الحسن،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r11.speaker: الربيع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r11.claim: Al-Rabīʿ glosses al-ʿafw as the good, choice, or best portion.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r12.claim: Al-ʿafw is also explained as abundance, from the sense “they became numerous”; an anonymous poetic line is cited for this usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r12.anchor: حتى عفوا أي: كثروا، قال الشاعر:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r13.claim: Another lexical sense is purity or clarity: the idiom أتاك عفوا means something came to you pure and unclouded, supported by a poetic line.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r13.anchor: أو: الصفو، يقال أتاك عفوا، أي: صفوا بلا كدر، قال الشاعر:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r14.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r14.claim: Qatāda says the required pre-zakāt surplus was what remained above one thousand dirhams, or its equivalent in gold.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r14.anchor: أو: ما فضل عن ألف درهم، أو: قيمة ذلك من الذهب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r15.claim: Other thresholds proposed are the surplus beyond a third, or beyond a year’s agricultural subsistence, a month’s for desert folk, or a day’s for laborers; hardship led to zakāt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r15.anchor: أو: ما فضل عن الثلث، أو: عن ما يقوتهم حولا لذوي الزراعة، وشهرا لذوي الفلات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r16.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r16.claim: Mujāhid identifies al-ʿafw with obligatory charity.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r17.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r17.claim: Al-Ḥasan also defines the amount as one that does not exhaust the giver’s resources and leave him begging others.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p406/r17.anchor: و: ما لا يستنفد المال ويبقي صاحبه يسأل الناس، قاله الحسن أيضا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r1.claim: A report about someone offering a gold egg is followed by the warning that giving away all one’s wealth can leave one dependent; charity should come from sufficiency.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r1.anchor: وقوله: «يجيء أحدكم بماله كله يتصدق به ويقعد يتكفف الناس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r2.speaker: سعد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r2.claim: Saʿd’s hadith says it is better to leave heirs wealthy than to leave them dependent on others.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r2.anchor: وفي حديث سعد: «لأن تذر ورثتك أغنياء خير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī defines al-ʿafw as the opposite of exertion: spend what does not require exhausting effort or capacity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: العفو نقيض الجهد، وهو أن ينفق ما لا يبلغ إنفاقه منه الجهد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says to spend what exceeds one’s needs without depriving oneself and becoming dependent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: المعنى: أنفقوا ما فضل عن حوائجكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r5.speaker: الراغب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r5.claim: Al-Rāghib says al-ʿafw covers both obligatory and voluntary giving and means surplus beyond comfortable means.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r5.anchor: وقال الراغب: العفو متناول لما هو واجب ولما هو تبرع،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r6.speaker: الماتريدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r6.claim: Al-Māturīdī defines al-ʿafw as the amount left over from subsistence.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r7.claim: Most readers vocalize العفو in the accusative as the object of an omitted ينفقون; this matches ماذا as an interrogative object asking what they spend.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r7.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: العفو، بالنصب وهو منصوب بفعل مضمر تقديره: قل ينفقون العفو،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r8.claim: Alternatively, ما is a nominative interrogative subject and ذا a relative pronoun meaning “that which”; its resumptive pronoun is omitted, so the reply matches in meaning, not wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ما استفهامية في موضع رفع بالابتداء، وذا موصولة بمعنى الذي، وهي خبره،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r9.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads العفو in the nominative; the preferred parsing makes it the predicate of an omitted subject and treats ما as subject with ذا relative.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو: قل العفو، بالرفع،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r10.speaker: ابن كثير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r10.claim: Ibn Kathīr is reported with both the accusative reading of the majority and the nominative reading of Abū ʿAmr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r10.anchor: واختلف عن ابن كثير في العفو،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r11.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects to Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s paraphrase “al-ʿafw is your spending,” since the question asks what is spent, not the act of spending; the mixed case combinations are permissible, not weak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p407/r11.anchor: وتقديره: العفو إنفاقكم، ليس بجيد، لأنه أتى بالمصدر، وليس السؤال عن المصدر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r1.claim: The kāf in كذلك either qualifies an omitted verbal noun or, on Sībawayh’s account, functions circumstantially: God explains in a manner like that explanation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r1.anchor: الكاف للتشبيه وهي في موضع نعت لمصدر محذوف، أو في موضع الحال على مذهب سيبويه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says the demonstrative most immediately refers to the clarification of the proper amount and condition for spending.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r2.anchor: واسم الإشارة الأقرب أن يعود إلى الأقرب من تبينه حال المنفق، قاله ابن الأنباري،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the reference to be the conclusion that giving the surplus is better than exhausting oneself in expenditure.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ما يؤول إليه وهو تبيين أن العفو أصلح من الجهد في النفقة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r4.claim: Other possible referents include the rulings on wine and gambling, spending, fighting and the sacred month, the destination and reward of spending, or the amount to spend.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يشار به إلى بيان ما سألوا عنه، فبين لهم كتبيين مصرف ما ينفقون،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r5.claim: It is too restrictive to make the demonstrative refer only to wine and gambling; even farther-fetched is taking it to cover every ruling mentioned earlier in the sūra.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r5.anchor: وأبعد من خص اسم الإشارة ببيان حكم الخمر والميسر فقط، وأبعد من ذلك من جعله إشارة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r6.claim: The singular address in the demonstrative may address the Prophet, a listener, or a group; singular address to a group is Arabic usage, and لكم confirms collective address.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r6.anchor: وكاف الخطاب إما أن تكون للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، أو للسامع أو للقبيل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r7.claim: لكم is governed by يبين; its lām conveys information to someone as in “I said to you,” while a causal reading is unlikely.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r7.anchor: لكم متعلق: بيبين، واللام فيها للتبليغ، كقولك: قلت لك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r8.claim: Here āyāt means signs and evidences; clear explanation is intended to lead people to reflect on worldly and afterlife concerns.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r8.anchor: والآيات: العلامات، والدلائل لعلكم تتفكرون، ترجئة للتفكر تحصل عند تبيين الآيات.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers attaching “in this world and the next” to reflection generally, rather than limiting reflection to one particular matter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p408/r9.anchor: وفي الدنيا والآخرة الأحسن أن يكون ظرفا للتفكر ومتعلقا به،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says people should consider what concerns both abodes and choose what is best for themselves.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r1.anchor: تتفكرون فيما يتعلق بالدارين، فتأخذون بما هو أصلح لكم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r2.claim: Another explanation is that reflection concerns God’s commands and prohibitions, leading to obedience in this life and reward in the next.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r2.anchor: وقيل: تتفكرون في أوامر الله ونواهيه، وتستدركون طاعته في الدنيا، وثوابه في الآخرة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r3.speaker: المفضل بن سلمة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r3.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Salama applies reflection to spending: retain enough for worldly livelihood and give the rest for the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r3.anchor: وقال المفضل بن سلمة: تتفكرون في أمر النفقة في الدنيا والآخرة، فتمسكون من أموالكم ما يصلحكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Zamakhsharī explain that people should reflect on the world’s passing and the afterlife’s permanence, then work for what endures.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r4.anchor: وقيل: تتفكرون في زوال الدنيا وبقاء الآخرة، فتعملون للباقي منهما. قال معناه ابن عباس والزمخشري،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also links reflection to wine’s worldly benefits and afterlife harms, and to holding back worldly means while giving for the hereafter.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r5.anchor: وقيل: تتفكرون في منافع الخمر في الدنيا، ومضارها في الآخرة، فلا تختاروا النفع العاجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r6.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan attaches “in this world and the next” to God’s explaining the signs rather than to people’s reflection.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r6.anchor: وجوزوا أن يكون، في الدنيا، متعلقا بقوله: يبين لكم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r7.claim: If explanation occurs only in this life, the phrase must mean signs concerning both abodes; if signs appear in both, no reinterpretation is needed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r7.anchor: ولا بد من تأويل على هذا إن كان التبيين للآيات يقع في الدنيا، فيكون التقدير في أمر الدنيا والآخرة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r8.claim: The proposed fronting-and-delaying analysis is unnecessary: لعل functions causally, so it and the locative phrase are both complements of يبين; an intervening parenthesis is another possible parsing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p409/r8.anchor: وليس هذا من باب التقديم والتأخير، لأن: لعل، هنا جارية مجرى التعليل، فهي كالمتعلقة: بيبين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p410/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p410/r1.speaker: ابن عطية ومكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p410/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya and Makkī explain that God shows believers signs in this world and the next, indicating both abodes and their standing so people will reflect.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p410/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطية، وقال مكي: معنى الآية أنه يبين للمؤمنين آيات في الدنيا والآخرة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p410/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p410/r2.speaker: مكي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p410/r2.claim: Makkī treats الآيات as indefinite, making the two prepositional phrases descriptions of signs existing in both abodes; Abū Ḥayyān calls this a semantic paraphrase.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p410/r2.anchor: وشرح مكي الآية بأن جعل الآيات منكرة، حتى يجعل الظرفين صفة للآيات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p410/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p410/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p410/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects saying the phrase syntactically attaches to الآيات: a noun cannot govern the prepositional phrase; it must modify the noun through an implicit participle or state.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p410/r3.anchor: وما ذكره ابن عطية من أنه متعلق على هذا التأويل بالآيات إن عنى ظاهر ما يريده النحاة بالتعلق فهو فاسد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p415/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p415/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p415/r3.claim: As wine among drinks and gambling’s food are prohibited, polytheist spouses are prohibited among those one may marry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p415/r3.anchor: ومناسبة أخرى: أنه لما تقدم حكم الشرب في الخمر، والأكل في الميسر، وذكر حكم المنكح، فكما حرم الخمر من المشروبات، وما يجر إليه الميسر من المأكولات، حرم المشركات من المنكوحات.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p417/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p417/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p417/r11.claim: As with wine and gambling, some benefit from a forbidden thing does not establish permissibility.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p417/r11.anchor: كما أن الخمر والميسر فيهما منافع، ولا يقتضي ذلك الإباحة، وما من شيء محرم إلا يكاد يكون فيه نفع ما.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p431/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p431/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p431/r11.claim: The believers asked the Messenger about wine and gambling as God had foretold; the answer that both involve grave sin was meant to lead them to abstain and indicates their prohibition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p431/r11.anchor: إخبار الله تعالى عن المؤمنين أنهم يسألون رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الخمر والميسر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p431/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p431/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p431/r12.claim: The sin is described as great in one reading and numerous in another; Abū Ḥayyān relates the wording to the Qurʾānic category of major sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p431/r12.anchor: وما اكتفى بمطلق الإثم حتى وصفه بالكبر في قراءة، وبالكثرة في قراءة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p431/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p431/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p431/r13.claim: Benefits include money from trading in wine, gambling, and other gains; even prohibited things have some benefit, especially when people naturally desire them or grow accustomed to them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p431/r13.anchor: من: أخذ الأموال بالتجارة في الخمر، وبالقمر في الميسر، وغير ذلك، لأنه ما من شيء حرم إلا فيه منفعة بوجه ما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p431/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p431/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p431/r14.claim: The sin's harm, which leads to Hell, outweighs the benefit that ends with its occasion; a rational person should avoid lasting punishment for temporary gain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p431/r14.anchor: ضرر الإثم الذي هو جالب إلى النار، أعظم من النفع المنقضي بانقضاء وقته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p432/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p432/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p432/r1.claim: Asked what to spend, believers are told to give whatever is easy for them to part with; this reflects that religion imposes no undue hardship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p432/r1.anchor: فأجيبوا بأن ينفقوا ما سهل عليهم إنفاقه، ويشير ما جعل عليكم في الدين من حرج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p432/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p432/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p432/r2.claim: God explains the signs as He has clarified wine, gambling, and spending, so that reflection on this world and the next may lead people to prefer the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p432/r2.anchor: يحصل الرجاء في تفكر حال الدنيا والآخرة، فإذا فكر فيهما يرجح بالفكر إيثار الآخرة على الدنيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p434/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p434/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p434/r10.claim: Abū Ḥayyān praises the passage's eloquence, its joined clauses and elegant structure, and its movement from warning about disobedience at the opening to glad tidings for believers at the end.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p434/r10.anchor: فكان ابتداء هذه الآيات بالتحذير عن معاطاة العصيان، واختتامها بالتبشير لأهل الإيمان

ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r1.speaker: الواحدى
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says ʿUmar, Muʿādh ibn Jabal, and a group of Anṣār asked the Prophet for a ruling because wine and gambling destroy reason and consume wealth; this verse was revealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r1.anchor: نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب . ومعاذ بن جبل . ونفر من الإنصار

ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r2.speaker: بعض الروايات
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r2.claim: Another account says the verse first came after the Prophet arrived in Medina; people continued drinking until ʿAbd al-Raḥmān’s feast, where intoxicated ʿAlī omitted “no” while leading prayer, prompting 4:43.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r2.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم قدم المدينة وهم يشربون الخمر ويأكلون الميسر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r3.speaker: بعض الروايات
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r3.claim: At a later feast hosted by ʿUtban, Saʿd’s boasting poem insulted the Anṣār; a man struck and wounded him, after which Saʿd appealed to the Prophet and the final prohibition was revealed days after al-Aḥzāb; ʿUmar declared they had stopped.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r3.anchor: ثم اتخذ عتبان بن مالك صنيعا ودعا رجالا من المسلمين فيهم سعد بن أبي وقاص

ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r4.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r4.claim: ʿAlī says he would not pray from a minaret built over a well into which wine had fallen, nor let his animal graze where wine had fallen into the sea.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r4.anchor: وعن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه لو وقعت قطرة منها في بئر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r5.speaker: إبن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says that if he dipped his finger into wine, it would not follow him, an image of complete avoidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r5.anchor: وعن إبن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما لو أدخلت أصبعي فيها لم تتبعني

ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r6.speaker: الإمام أبي حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r6.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa defines wine narrowly as grape juice that boils, ferments, and casts up foam; the term is explained as covering the mind, like a woman’s veil covers her face.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r6.anchor: التي من ماء العنب إذا غلى وأشتد وقذف بالزبد

ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r7.claim: Other proposed etymologies connect wine with covering, mixing with the mind, or being left until it matures; these accounts are close in sense, and the noun may be an agent, patient, or intensive verbal noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r7.anchor: لأنها تخالط العقل وخامره داء خالطه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r8.speaker: الإمامان
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r8.claim: Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad do not require foam to appear; fermentation alone suffices because the intoxicating cause is then present.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r8.anchor: وذهب الإمامان إلى عدم اشتراط القذف ويكفي الإشتداد لأن المعنى المحرم يحصل به

ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r9.speaker: الإمام أبي حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r9.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa regards boiling as the beginning of fermentation and foam rising and settling as its completion; legal consequences attach to completion, as with the fixed penalty and sale prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r9.anchor: وللإمام أن الغليان بداية الشدة وكمالها بقذف الزبد وسكونه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r10.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r10.claim: Some jurists adopt Abū Yūsuf and Muḥammad’s threshold for the drinking ban as a precaution.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r10.anchor: وأخذ بعضهم بقولهما في حرمة الشرب إحتياطا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r11.claim: In the Hanafi position and common Arabic usage, calling a drink from other substances “wine” is figurative; some people argue that the word is literal for every intoxicant.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p111#2/r11.anchor: مجاز عندنا وهو المعروف عند أهل اللغة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r1.speaker: الشيخان وأبو داؤد والترمذي والنسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r1.claim: Reports in the two Ṣaḥīḥs and Sunan collections state that every intoxicant is wine.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r2.speaker: أبو داؤد
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r2.claim: Abū Dāwūd reports that the prohibition was revealed for wine made from five sources—grapes, dates, wheat, barley, and corn—and that wine is what clouds the mind.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r2.anchor: من العنب والتمر والحنطة والشعير والذرة
