ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r3.claim: Muslim reports from Abū Hurayra that wine comes from these two trees, with the Prophet pointing to the vine and date-palm.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r3.anchor: عن أبي هريرة ( الخمر ) من هاتين الشجرتين وأشار إلى الكرم والنخلة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r4.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r4.claim: Anas reports that grape wine was scarce when wine was prohibited and most of their wine came from unripe dates and dates.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r4.anchor: حرمت الخمر حين حرمت وما يتخذ من خمر الأعناب إلا قليل

ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r5.claim: Al-Alusi reads these reports as teaching the legal rule that all intoxicants are forbidden, not defining Arabic vocabulary; the Prophet’s mission was guidance, while his audience already knew Arabic.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r5.anchor: ويمكن أن يجاب أن المقصود من ذلك كله بيان الحكم وتعليم أن ما أسكر حرام كالخمر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r6.claim: Deriving “wine” from its covering the mind does not prove that the word covers every intoxicant; “star” likewise derives from appearing but names a particular star.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r6.anchor: فإن النجم مشتق من الظهور ثم هو أسم خاص للنجم المعروف لا لكل ما ظهر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r7.claim: A middle position says Arabic uses “wine” literally for intoxicating grape juice and figuratively for other sources, while Islamic law made it a technical term for every intoxicant, like prayer, fasting, and alms.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r7.anchor: إن ( الخمر ) حقيقة في لغة العرب في التي من ماء العنب

ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r8.claim: The disagreement is substantial: permitting grape wine is disbelief by consensus, while permitting other intoxicants is not, since their designation as wine is disputed and their prohibition is inferential.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r8.anchor: ولقوته ووقوع الإجماع على تسمية المتخذ من العنب خمرا دون المسكر من غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r9.claim: Grape wine itself is forbidden independently of intoxication, so all amounts, even a drop, are forbidden and its drinker is liable to the fixed penalty.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r9.anchor: عين الأول حرام غير معلول بالسكر ولا موقوف عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r10.claim: One who denies wine’s intrinsic prohibition and says only its intoxicating effect is forbidden is an unbeliever for rejecting scripture, which calls it impurity; the cited verse is 5:90.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r10.anchor: لجحوده الكتاب إذ سماه رجسا فيه والرجس محرم العين

ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r11.claim: A report says wine is forbidden in itself, with a version adding that its small and large amounts are alike; intoxication rules govern other drinks.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r11.anchor: وفي الخبر حرمت الخمر لعينها وفي رواية بعينها قليلها وكثيرها سواء

ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r12.claim: Cooking cannot erase an already established prohibition; however, a cooked drink is not subject to the fixed penalty until it intoxicates, since that penalty for a small amount applies specifically to raw wine.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r12.anchor: إن الطبخ لا يؤثر لأنه للمنع من ثبوت الحرمة لا لرفعها

ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r13.claim: Bādhq and munṣaf, grape must cooked until less than two-thirds evaporates, are forbidden if fermented and foaming; al-Alusi says their thinness, intoxication, and pleasure attract sinners, so they are banned to prevent corruption.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r13.anchor: يسمى الباذق والمنصف وهو ما ذهب نصفه بالطبخ فحرام عندنا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r14.speaker: الأوزاعي وأكثر المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r14.claim: Al-Awzāʿī and most Muʿtazilites permit this drink because it is pleasant and not wine; the author responds that it is intoxicating and attracts sinners, so it should be prohibited to prevent corruption.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r14.anchor: أكثر المعتزلة : إنه مباح لأنه مشروب طيب

ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r15.claim: Raw date infusion, called sakar, is forbidden; the author invokes the Companions’ consensus and the verse’s initial, pre-prohibition setting.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r16.speaker: شريك
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r16.claim: Sharik argues date infusion must be permitted because the verse mentions it as a favor, which could not be forbidden; the author rejects this using consensus and the verse’s earlier setting.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p112/r16.anchor: إنه مباح للإمتنان ولا يكون بالمحرم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r1.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r1.claim: One reading takes the verse about date produce as a rebuke: people make intoxicating drink from it and leave wholesome provision.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r1.anchor: أتتخذون منه سكرا وتدعون رزقا حسنا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r2.speaker: الأوزاعي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r2.claim: Raw raisin infusion is forbidden once it ferments and boils, though al-Awzāʿī disputes the ruling.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r2.anchor: حرام إذا أشتد وغلى وفيه خلاف الأوزاعي

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r3.speaker: أبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r3.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and Abū Yūsuf permit lightly cooked date or raisin nabīdh, even when fermented, if the amount is thought not to intoxicate and is drunk without revelry.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r3.anchor: عند أبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف وعند محمد والشافعي حرام

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r4.speaker: محمد والشافعي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r4.claim: Muḥammad and al-Shāfiʿī forbid lightly cooked date or raisin nabīdh even in the restricted quantity described by Abū Ḥanīfa and Abū Yūsuf.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r5.speaker: الإمام الأول والثاني
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r5.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and Abū Yūsuf permit drinks made from honey, figs, grains, or grape juice cooked down by two-thirds; Muḥammad and al-Shāfiʿī forbid them.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r5.anchor: حلال عند الإمام الأول والثاني وعند محمد والشافعي حرام أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r6.speaker: المتأخرون
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r6.claim: Later Hanafi jurists issued fatwas following Muḥammad’s prohibition for the other beverages; Ibn Wahbān says this ruling is also transmitted from all the imams.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r6.anchor: وأفتى المتأخرون بقول محمد في سائر الأشربة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r7.claim: Al-Alusi’s preferred rule is that any non-grape drink is forbidden if it can intoxicate an unaccustomed drinker; a small amount is like a large one, and drinking incurs the penalty, divorce effect, and severe impurity.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r7.anchor: وعندي أن الحق الذي لا ينبغي العدول عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r8.claim: In the Ṣaḥīḥayn the Prophet answers a question about honey nabīdh that every intoxicating drink is forbidden; Abū Dāwūd reports his prohibition of every intoxicant and stupefier.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r9.claim: Prophetic reports say that whatever intoxicates in a large quantity is forbidden in a small quantity, and that even a palmful is forbidden if a full measure intoxicates; the author calls the reports mutually reinforcing.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r9.anchor: ما أسكر كثيره فقليله حرام وفي حديث آخر ما أسكر الفرق منه فملء الكف منه حرام

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r10.claim: Al-Alusi laments that contemporary drinkers favor intoxicants other than grape wine, inventing names such as amberiyya and iksīr to imagine the new names make them lawful.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r10.anchor: وقد وضعوا لها أسماء كالعنبرية والإكسير

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r11.claim: These other drinks carry a lesser prohibition than grape wine, so permitting them is not disbelief because the ruling is ijtihād-based; declaring all permitters unbelievers would leave almost nobody.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r11.anchor: نعم حرمة هذه الأشربة دون حرمة الخمر حتى لا يكفر مستحلها كما قدمنا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113/r12.claim: Maysir is a verbal noun on the pattern of mawʿid or marjiʿ, used for gambling; its derivation may refer to taking wealth easily, losing wealth, dividing shares, or a stake becoming due.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r1.claim: Maysir derives from taking money easily, losing wealth, dividing shares, or a stake becoming due; the gambler was called yasir because he won a share of the slaughtered camel.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r1.anchor: يسرته إذا قمرته واشتقاقه إما مناليسر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r2.speaker: الواحدي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r2.claim: Al-Wāḥidī derives maysir from something becoming due, calling the gambler the one who owes the stake.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r2.anchor: من يسر الشيء إذا وجب والياسر الواجب بسبب القدح

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r3.claim: The traditional game used ten arrows, three blank; the other seven awarded one through seven shares of a camel divided into twenty-eight parts, while a blank-draw loser paid the entire cost.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r3.anchor: لهم عشرة أقداح هي الأزلام الفذ والتوأم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r4.speaker: الأزهري
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r4.claim: Al-Azharī gives another description of the arrow names and omits al-waghd; al-Alusi relies on the account preferred by al-Zamakhsharī and many others.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r4.anchor: ونقل الأزهري كيفية أخرى لذلك ولم يذكر الوغدفي الأسماء

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r5.claim: An unnamed poet composed a mnemonic listing the ten gambling arrows and their shares, including the three blank arrows.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r5.anchor: كل سهام الياسرين عشره فأودعوها صحفا منشره

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r6.claim: Maysir includes all gambling and wagering: backgammon, chess, children’s nuts and dice, risky lots outside division, and every kind of stake; Ibn Sīrīn says anything involving risk is maysir.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r6.anchor: كل شيء فيه خطر فهو من الميسر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r7.claim: The question concerns engaging in wine and gambling, as the answer’s “in them” makes clear; their sin comes from leading to neglected duties and committed prohibitions.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r8.claim: Their benefits include pleasure, joy, digestion, improved complexion, sexual vigor, courage, generosity, and helping the weak; these benefits exist before and after prohibition, and no proof says prohibition removes them.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r8.anchor: من اللذة والفرح وهضم الطعام وتصفية اللون وتقوية الباه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r9.speaker: إبن أبي الدنيا
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abī al-Dunyā recounts a drunk man urinating into his hand and washing his face with it as if performing ablution.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p113#2/r9.anchor: ذكر إبن أبي الدنيا أنه أمر بسكران وهو يبول بيده ويغسل به وجهه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r1.speaker: العباس بن مرداس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r1.claim: Al-ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās says in the pre-Islamic period that he would not put his ignorance into his belly by drinking, nor be a leader in the morning and a fool by evening.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r1.anchor: أنه قيل له في الجاهلية : ألا تشرب الخمر فإنها تزيد في حرارتك

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r2.claim: Wine distracts from remembrance and prayer, commonly produces hostility and fights, deepens into addiction, and can cause illnesses and death; loss of reason and uprightness alone suffices to make it the source of vices.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r2.anchor: ومنها صدها عن ذكر الله تعالى وعن الصلاة وإيقاعها العداوة والبغضاء غالبا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r3.claim: The Prophet said to avoid wine because it is the mother of all evils; al-Alusi adds that no prophets are reliably reported to have drunk it at any time.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r4.claim: Gambling takes wealth wrongfully and leads many gamblers to theft, loss of life, neglect of dependents, shameful conduct, and hidden or open enmity.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r4.anchor: أن فيه أكل الأموال بالباطل وأنه يدعو كثيرا من المقامرين إلى السرقة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r5.speaker: بعض العلماء
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r5.claim: Some scholars infer that the verse itself prohibits wine because the greater harm outweighs its benefit; others add that “great sin” means punishment or its cause, which applies only to the forbidden.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r5.anchor: ذهب بعض العلماء إلى أنها هي المحرمة للخمر فإن المفسدة إذا ترجحت على المصلحة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r6.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r6.claim: Qatāda says the verse is not explicit proof of prohibition: “sin” can mean harm, and a preponderance of harm alone establishes preference, not a ban; Companions drank until the al-Māʾida prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r6.anchor: والحق أن الآية ليست نصا في التحريم كما قال قتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r7.claim: One reading has “much sin” with thāʾ, and Ubayy reads “their sin is nearer than their benefit.”

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r8.claim: Placing sin first, describing it as great or numerous, and delaying benefits while limiting them to people signals the dominance of the harm.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r8.anchor: وفي تقديم الإثم ووصفه بالكبر أو الكثرة وتأخير ذكر المنافع مع تخصيصها بالناس

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r9.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r9.claim: Ibn Isḥāq reports from Ibn ʿAbbās that companions ordered to spend in God’s path asked how much to give; before the verse, some spent everything and then lacked food or charity.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r9.anchor: أخرج إبن إسحاق عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنه أن نفرا من الصحابة أمروا بالنفقة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r10.speaker: معاذ بن جبل وثعلبة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r10.claim: A report through Abān from Yaḥyā says Muʿādh and Thaʿlaba, with households and dependents, asked the Prophet how much of their wealth to spend.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r10.anchor: أنه بلغه أن معاذ بن جبل وثعلبة أتيا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r11.claim: This question coordinates with the earlier one as a new topic; another report links it to ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ, who first asked about recipients and then about the amount to give.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r11.anchor: عطف القصة على القصة وقيل : نزلت في عمرو بن الجموح

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r12.claim: The answer shows that the question asks the quality or amount of what to spend: “what” functions as a question about a description, as in asking what someone is and answering “generous.”
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r12.anchor: فالمعنى يسئلونك عن صفة ما ينفقونه قل العفو

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r13.claim: ʿAfw is the opposite of exertion: what remains beyond need or does not burden the giver; smooth, easy-to-tread ground is also called ʿafw.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r14.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains ʿafw as the surplus remaining after providing for dependents.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r14.anchor: وفي رواية عن إبن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما الفضل من العيال

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r15.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r15.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains ʿafw as an amount that does not strain the giver.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r16.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r16.claim: The Prophet says the best charity is given from sufficiency and that one should begin with those one supports; this is reported by al-Bukhārī, Muslim, Abū Dāwūd, and al-Nasāʾī.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r16.anchor: خير الصدقة ما كان عن ظهر غنى وأبدأ بمن تعول

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r17.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r17.claim: Ibn Khuzayma’s version says the best charity leaves sufficiency, the upper hand is better, and one should begin with dependents; wife, slave, and child each plead for support.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r17.anchor: خير الصدقة ما أبقت غنى واليد العليا خير من اليد السفلى

ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r18.speaker: جابر
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r18.claim: Jābir reports that Abū Ḥuṣayn al-Sulamī offered his only egg-sized piece of mined gold as charity; after repeatedly turning him away, the Prophet took and threw it, warning against giving everything and then begging.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p114/r18.anchor: قدم أبو حصين السلمي بمثل بيضة الحمامة من ذهب فقال

ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads “mādhā yunfiqūn” with nominative inflection, parsing the question as subject and predicate; the others read the accusative, supplying a verb with “what” as its object to match the answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r1.anchor: بالرفع بتقدير المبتدأ على ( أن ماذا ينفقون ) مبتدأ وخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r2.claim: “Thus” may point to the explanation that surplus charity is better than exhausting one’s means because it preserves resources and benefits the afterlife; it may also encompass the whole preceding discussion.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r2.anchor: المشار إليه ما يفهم من قوله سبحانه : ( قل العفو ) وإيراد صيغة البعيد

ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r3.claim: Taking “thus” to refer only to “their sin is greater than their benefit” is remote.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r3.anchor: على ما فيه لا يخفى بعده

ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r4.claim: The kāf is accusative as an adjective of an omitted noun, while the definite article in “the signs” is generic: God clarifies rulings by clear revelation, another verse, or the Prophet’s explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r4.anchor: والكاف في موضع النصب صفة لمحذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r5.claim: Although a plural form might be expected to match “for you,” the demonstrative stays singular by construing it as a collective noun with singular form, for lighter expression.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r5.anchor: لكنه وحد بتأويل نحو القبيلة أو الجمع مما هو مفرد اللفظ جمع المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r6.claim: Another explanation says the singular signals every recipient of the address, as in “We pardoned you after that” (2:52); al-Alusi objects that this would create multiple addressees within one uncoordinated sentence.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r6.anchor: الإفراد للأيذان بأن المراد به كل من يتلقى الكلام

ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r7.claim: Contemplating the signs means deriving rulings and understanding the interests and benefits attached to them; this makes reflection a fitting aim of their clarification.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p115/r7.anchor: في الآيات فتسنتنبطوا الأحكام منها وتفهموا المصالح والمنافع المنوطة بها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r1.claim: The verse was revealed after ʿUmar, Muʿādh ibn Jabal, and a group of Anṣār asked about wine and gambling because they impair reason and consume wealth.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r1.anchor: نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب ومعاذ بن جبل رضي الله عنهما ونفر من الأنصار أتوا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r2.claim: The staged prohibition began with a Meccan verse describing drink from dates and grapes alongside good provision; wine was then lawful and Muslims drank it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r2.anchor: في الخمر أربع آيات نزلت بمكة وهي: "ومن ثمرات النخيل والأعناب تتخذون منه سكرا ورزقا حسنا"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r3.claim: After this verse descended, the Prophet said that God had begun to address wine’s prohibition; some gave it up over its sin, while others continued because of its benefits.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن الله قد تقدم في تحريم الخمر" فتركها قوم لقوله {إثم كبير}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r4.claim: At ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf’s meal, guests drank and became intoxicated; the person leading Maghrib omitted لا from the recitation of al-Kāfirūn, after which 4:43 forbade approaching prayer while drunk.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r4.anchor: فقرأ "قل يا أيها الكافرون أعبد ما تعبدون" هكذا إلى آخر السورة بحذف "لا"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r5.claim: Some quit wine altogether after the next restriction; others only stopped at prayer times, drinking after ʿIshāʾ so they were sober by morning or after Fajr so they were sober by Ẓuhr.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r5.anchor: فلما نزلت هذه الآية تركها قوم، وقالوا لا خير في شيء يحول بيننا وبين الصلاة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r6.claim: At ʿItbān ibn Mālik’s feast, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ and others drank after eating camel’s head; Saʿd boasted and recited poetry insulting the Anṣār, and a man struck and split his head with a camel jawbone.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r6.anchor: واتخذ عتبان بن مالك صنيعا ودعا رجالا من المسلمين فيهم سعد بن أبي وقاص وكان قد شوى لهم رأس بعير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r7.speaker: عمر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r7.claim: After Saʿd complained to the Prophet about the injury, ʿUmar prayed for a clear ruling on wine; this segment ends before the prayer’s sequel.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p249/r7.anchor: فانطلق سعد إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وشكا إليه الأنصاري فقال عمر: اللهم بين لنا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r1.claim: Wine is not restricted to what is made from grapes or dates; the passage also names intoxicants from honey, wheat, and barley.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r1.anchor: فثبت أن الخمر لا يختص بما يتخذ من العنب أو الرطب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r2.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r2.claim: ʿUmar smelled a drink on a man who claimed he drank ṭilāʾ; he said he would investigate and apply the full ḥadd if it intoxicated, and then did so.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r2.anchor: عن السائب بن يزيد أنه أخبره أن عمر بن الخطاب خرج عليهم فقال إني وجدت من فلان ريح شراب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r3.claim: Reports about ʿUmar, Abū ʿUbayda, and Muʿādh concerning ṭilāʾ refer to the drink after it was boiled until it ceased to intoxicate.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r3.anchor: وما روي عن عمر وأبي عبيدة ومعاذ في الطلاء فهو فيما طبخ حتى خرج عن أن يكون مسكرا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r4.claim: When asked about bādhīq, Ibn ʿAbbās says Muhammad had already ruled on it: anything intoxicating is forbidden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r4.anchor: وسئل ابن عباس عن الباذق (3) فقال سبق محمد الباذق فما أسكر فهو حرام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r5.claim: Al-Maysir means gambling; it derives from yassara li, something becoming due, and the gambler is called yāsir or yasir.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r5.anchor: {والميسر} يعني القمار، قال ابن عباس: كان الرجل في الجاهلية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes pre-Islamic gambling in which a man wagered his family and property against another, and the winner took the loser’s family and property.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان الرجل في الجاهلية يخاطر الرجل على أهله وماله فأيهما قمر صاحبه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r7.claim: The original Arab form of maysir involved wealthy men buying and slaughtering a camel and dividing its meat by lots drawn for ten shares: seven marked lots awarded one through seven portions and three blank lots.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r7.anchor: وكان أصل الميسر في الجزور وذلك أن أهل الثروة من العرب كانوا يشترون جزورا فينحرونها ويجزؤونها عشرة أجزاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r8.claim: The lots were drawn from a bag by a trusted selector; under one account a blank drew no share but made its holder pay for the whole camel, while another account says a blank was simply void.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r8.anchor: ثم يجعلون القداح في خريطة تسمى الربابة ويضعونها على يدي رجل عدل عندهم يسمى المجيل والمفيض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r9.claim: On the alternative account, the meat went to the poor and participants did not eat it; they boasted of the practice and derided one who abstained as al-barim.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p252/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم كان لا يأخذ شيئا ولا يغرم ويكون ذلك القدح لغوا ثم يدفعون ذلك الجزور إلى الفقراء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r1.claim: The verse covers all forms of gambling, down to children’s games with nuts and dice; Baghawī reports that Ṭāwūs, ʿAṭāʾ, and Mujāhid included them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r1.anchor: قمار فهو من الميسر حتى لعب الصبيان بالجوز والكعاب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r2.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r2.claim: A report from ʿAlī classifies backgammon and chess as maysir.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r2.anchor: وروي عن علي رضي الله عنه في النرد والشطرنج أنهما من الميسر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r3.claim: The grave sin in wine and gambling includes quarrelling, mutual abuse, and obscene speech.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r3.anchor: وزر عظيم من المخاصمة والمشاتمة وقول الفحش

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r4.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r4.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read ithm kathīr, many sins; the other readers read the standard ithm kabīr, a great sin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r4.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي إثم كثير بالثاء المثلثة وقرأ الباقون بالباء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r5.claim: Baghawī connects the sin in wine and gambling to the enmity, hatred, and diversion from prayer described in 5:91.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r5.anchor: ما ذكره الله في سورة المائدة. "إنما يريد الشيطان أن يوقع بينكم العداوة والبغضاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r6.claim: Wine’s benefits include pleasure, cheer, making food agreeable, and trade profits; gambling can bring unearned money and support the poor, but losses without compensation provoke resentment and hostility.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253/r6.anchor: فمنفعة الخمر اللذة عند شربها والفرح واستمراء الطعام وما يصيبون من الربح بالتجارة فيها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r1.speaker: الضحاك وغيره
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r1.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and others say their sin after prohibition outweighs their benefit before prohibition.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r1.anchor: قال الضحاك وغيره: إثمهما بعد التحريم أكبر من نفعهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r2.claim: Another explanation says the sin exceeded the benefit even before prohibition because of the enmity and hatred they caused.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r2.anchor: وقيل: إثمهما أكبر من نفعهما قبل التحريم وهو ما يحصل من العداوة والبغضاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r3.claim: When the Prophet urged them to give charity, people asked what they should spend, and the answer was al-ʿafw.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r3.anchor: وذلك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حثهم على الصدقة فقالوا ماذا ننفق؟ فقال {قل العفو}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads al-ʿafw in the nominative, meaning what they spend is the surplus; the other readers use the accusative, meaning spend the surplus.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r4.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو العفو بالرفع، معناه: الذي ينفقون هو العفو

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r5.speaker: قتادة وعطاء والسدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r5.claim: Qatāda, ʿAṭāʾ, and al-Suddī define al-ʿafw as what exceeds one’s needs; the Companions kept necessary expenses and donated the surplus under this rule, later abrogated by the zakat verse.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid says charity should be given from one’s means without leaving oneself dependent on other people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: معناه: التصدق عن ظهر غنى حتى لا يبقى كلا على الناس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r7.claim: Abū Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that the best charity is given from abundance, the upper hand is better than the lower, and one should begin with dependants.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "خير الصدقة ما كان عن ظهر غنى واليد العليا خير

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r8.speaker: عمرو بن دينار
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r8.claim: ʿAmr ibn Dīnār interprets al-ʿafw as a moderate amount, without extravagance or stinginess, linking it to 25:67.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r8.anchor: وقال عمرو بن دينار: الوسط من غير إسراف ولا إقتار قال الله تعالى "والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r9.speaker: طاووس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r9.claim: Ṭāwūs says al-ʿafw is what is easy; the same word can mean what is easy or readily available in a person’s character, as in 7:199.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r9.anchor: وقال طاووس: ما يسر، والعفو: اليسر من كل شيء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r10.claim: Abū Hurayra reports a man with four dinars was told to spend them in order on himself, his child, his family, and his servant; with anything left, he could decide for himself.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p253#2/r10.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال يا رسول الله عندي دينار

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p254/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p254/r1.speaker: الزجاج
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p254/r1.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the singular كذلك addresses a plural because the group is treated as one collective, as if addressed as a single tribe.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p254/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: إنما قال كذلك على الواحد وهو يخاطب جماعة، لأن الجماعة معناها القبيل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p254/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p254/r2.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p254/r2.claim: Another explanation takes the address as directed to the Prophet, whose address includes the community, as in 65:1.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p254/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأن خطابه يشتمل على خطاب الأمة كقوله تعالى:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p254/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p254/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p254/r3.claim: One view says the signs about spending prompt people to reserve what sustains worldly life and give the remainder for the afterlife.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p254/r3.anchor: قيل: معناه يبين الله لكم الآيات في أمر النفقة لعلكم تتفكرون في الدنيا والآخرة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p254/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p254/r4.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p254/r4.claim: Most commentators say reflection on the world's passing and the afterlife's permanence should lessen attachment to the former and increase desire for the latter.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p254/r4.anchor: وقال أكثر المفسرين: معناها هكذا: يبين الله لكم الآيات في أمر الدنيا والآخرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r1.claim: A chronology says the earlier verse about date and grape products led Muslims to drink; Umar, Muadh, and other Companions asked about wine, and this verse followed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r1.anchor: روي أنه نزل بمكة قوله تعالى:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r2.claim: At a later banquet hosted by Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, a drunken prayer prompted the prohibition on approaching prayer intoxicated.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r2.anchor: ثم دعا عبد الرحمن بن عوف ناسا منهم فشربوا وسكروا،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r3.claim: The account next describes Utban inviting Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas and others; drunken boasting led Saʿd to insult the Anṣār, and an Anṣārī wounded him with a camel jaw.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r3.anchor: ثم دعا عتبان بن مالك سعد بن أبي وقاص في نفر

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r4.speaker: عمر
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r4.claim: After the injury and complaint, Umar prayed for a clear ruling; the final prohibition descended and he declared that they had stopped.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r4.anchor: فقال عمر رضي الله عنه: اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا فنزلت

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r5.claim: Khamr comes from covering; the name applies to fermented grape or date juice because it covers the mind, as sukr names what blocks it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r5.anchor: والخمر في الأصل مصدر خمره إذا ستره،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r6.claim: Wine is categorically forbidden, as are all intoxicants according to most scholars.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r6.anchor: وهي حرام مطلقا وكذا كل ما أسكر عند أكثر العلماء.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r7.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa permits drinking fermented raisin or date infusion if boiled until two-thirds evaporates, provided the drinker does not become intoxicated.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r7.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى: نقيع الزبيب والتمر

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r8.claim: Maysir is a verbal noun like mawʿid; gambling is so called because it takes another’s wealth easily or strips away prosperity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r8.anchor: سمي به القمار لأنه أخذ مال الغير بيسر

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r9.claim: The question is about engaging in wine and gambling, as shown by the answer’s reference to what is in both.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r9.anchor: والمعنى يسألونك عن تعاطيهما لقوله تعالى:

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r10.claim: Their sin consists in leading people to neglect what is commanded and commit what is forbidden.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r10.anchor: من حيث إنه يؤدي إلى الانتكاب عن المأمور، وارتكاب المحظور.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r11.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r11.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read kathīr, “much,” with thāʾ instead of kabīr, “great.”

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r12.claim: Benefits include earning money, excitement, pleasure, and companionship; wine may embolden the coward, enhance manliness, and strengthen the constitution.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r12.anchor: من كسب المال والطرب والالتذاذ ومصادقة الفتيان،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r13.claim: The harms arising from wine and gambling outweigh their expected benefits.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r13.anchor: أي المفاسد التي تنشأ منهما أعظم من المنافع المتوقعة منهما.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r14.claim: Some say the excess of harm over benefit is what prohibits wine, since predominant harm entails prohibition; al-Bayḍāwī rejects this as reviving the Muʿtazilite doctrine previously invalidated.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r14.anchor: ولهذا قيل إنها المحرمة للخمر لأن المفسدة إذا ترجحت على المصلحة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r15.claim: The reported argument says a preponderance of harm over benefit entails that the act is prohibited.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r15.anchor: لأن المفسدة إذا ترجحت على المصلحة اقتضت تحريم الفعل،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r16.speaker: عمرو بن الجموح
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r16.claim: Amr ibn al-Jamuh is said to have asked first about what to spend and whom to give it to, then about how to spend.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r16.anchor: قيل سائله أيضا عمرو بن الجموح سأل أولا عن المنفق والمصرف،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r17.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r17.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r17.claim: Al-ʿafw is the opposite of exertion: spend what is readily available without exhausting yourself.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219/r17.anchor: العفو نقيض الجهد ومنه يقال للأرض السهلة،

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219#2/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219#2/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219#2/r1.claim: A cited poem uses al-ʿafw in the sense of an easy or generous amount offered to preserve affection.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219#2/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219#2/r2.claim: The Prophet turned away from a man offering a gold egg from spoils, then tossed it and said giving all one’s wealth leaves one begging; charity is from sufficiency.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219#2/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219#2/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219#2/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads al-ʿafw in the nominative.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219#2/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219#2/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219#2/r4.claim: “Thus” refers either to showing that surplus is better than exhausting effort or to the rulings just stated; kāf is an accusative adjective for an omitted verbal noun, and the singular is collective in sense.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219#2/r4.anchor: مثل ما بين أن العفو أصلح من الجهد

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219#2/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219#2/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:219#2/r5.claim: The signs are explained so people may reflect on the proofs and legal rulings.

BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r1.claim: The cited Mathnawī couplet urges disciplining the soul away from Satan, keeping angelic company, and feeding it lawful sustenance that brings light and perfection.
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r1.anchor: طفل جان ازشير شيطان بازكن بعد ازانش باملك انباز كن

BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Companions were exceptionally good: they asked the Messenger only thirteen questions, all answered in the Qurʾan, and asked only about matters beneficial to them and Muslims.
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ما رأيت قوما كانوا خيرا من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما سألوه إلا عن ثلاث عشرة مسألة

BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r3.claim: The question is about the ruling on consuming wine, since permissibility, prohibition, sin, and obedience attach to accountable acts, not to objects in themselves; the ruling also covers sale and purchase.
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r3.anchor: عن حكم تعاطيها بقرينة الجواب لأن الحل والحرمة والإثم والطاعة إنما هي من عوارض أفعال المكلفين

BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r4.claim: Khamr is named from the root for covering: grape juice that boils, thickens, and foams covers the intellect and discernment, as though it were itself a veil.
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r4.anchor: والخمر مصدر خمره أي : ستره سمي به

BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r5.claim: Maisir is a verbal noun from yasara; it may be named for taking wealth easily without labor or for impoverishing the loser.
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r5.anchor: مصدر ميمي من يسر كالموعد والمرجع

BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r6.claim: Maisir includes every kind of gambling, chess, and even children's games with walnuts and dice.
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r6.anchor: ويدخل فيه جميع أنواع القمار والشطرنج وغيرهما حتى لعب الصبيان

BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r7.claim: The phrase refers to engaging in and using wine and gambling.

BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r8.claim: Their grave sin is that wine destroys reason, the pivot of religion and worldly life, and both wine and gambling ruin wealth.
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r8.anchor: مسلبة للعقول التي هي قطب الدين والدنيا مع كون كل منهما

BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r9.claim: Wine had perceived benefits including exhilaration, resale profit, strengthening the weak, aiding digestion and sex, easing grief, emboldening the fearful, loosening the miser's hand, improving complexion, and stirring speech and resolve.
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r9.anchor: من كسب الطرب والمغالاة بثمن الخمر إذا جلبوها من الأطراف وفيها تقوية الضعيف

BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r10.claim: Gambling could bring unearned money and meat for the poor, since winners distributed the camel's meat to people in need.
BURSEVI:v1p277#2/r10.anchor: ومنافع الميسر إصابة المال من غير كد ولا تعب

BURSEVI:v1p278/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p278/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p278/r1.claim: Wine incites enmity and hatred and diverts from remembrance of God and prayer; it makes the sensible foolish, as illustrated by an obscene drunkard's behavior.
BURSEVI:v1p278/r1.anchor: وفي الخمر إيقاع العداوة والبغضاء والصد عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة

BURSEVI:v1p278/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p278/r2.speaker: ابن أبي الدنيا
BURSEVI:v1p278/r2.claim: Ibn Abī al-Dunyā recounts seeing a drunkard urinate into his hand, wipe his face as if performing ablution, and praise Islam and water; no grading is given.
BURSEVI:v1p278/r2.anchor: كما ذكر ابن أبي الدنيا أنه مر على سكران وهو يبول في يده

BURSEVI:v1p278/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p278/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p278/r3.claim: When a gambler loses his money without compensation, he resents the winner, becomes his enemy, and seeks to harm him.
BURSEVI:v1p278/r3.anchor: وفي الميسر أنه إذا ذهب ماله من غير عوض ساءه ذلك فعادى صاحبه

BURSEVI:v1p278/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p278/r4.speaker: المفسرون
BURSEVI:v1p278/r4.claim: Commentators describe a four-stage prohibition: the first, Meccan verse mentioned wine made from dates and grapes alongside good provision, and Muslims initially drank it as lawful.
BURSEVI:v1p278/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون تواردت في الخمر أربع آيات نزلت

BURSEVI:v1p278/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p278/r5.speaker: المفسرون
BURSEVI:v1p278/r5.claim: After ʿUmar, Muʿādh, and other Companions asked about wine because it removes reason, the verse on wine and gambling was revealed; some tried to take its benefits while avoiding its sin, while others abstained.
BURSEVI:v1p278/r5.anchor: افتنا يا رسول الله في الخمر فإنها مذهبة للعقل فنزلت

BURSEVI:v1p278/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p278/r6.speaker: المفسرون
BURSEVI:v1p278/r6.claim: At a gathering hosted by ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, a drunken reciter omitted the negation in Sūrat al-Kāfirūn; the prayer-time prohibition followed.
BURSEVI:v1p278/r6.anchor: قام أحدهم فقرأ قل يا أيها الكافرون أعبد ما تعبدون

BURSEVI:v1p278/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p278/r7.speaker: المفسرون
BURSEVI:v1p278/r7.claim: After the prayer-time restriction, some still drank outside prayer hours, expecting to sober up between the evening or dawn prayer and the next prayer.
BURSEVI:v1p278/r7.anchor: وشربها قوم في غير حين الصلاة حتى كان الرجل يشربها بعد صلاة العشاء

BURSEVI:v1p278/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p278/r8.speaker: المفسرون
BURSEVI:v1p278/r8.claim: At ʿItbān ibn Mālik's feast, Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ recited a poem insulting the Anṣār and praising his clan; a guest struck and wounded Saʿd with a camel's jawbone, after which Saʿd complained to the Messenger.
BURSEVI:v1p278/r8.anchor: ثم اتخذ عتبان بن مالك ضيافة ودعا رجالا من المسلمين فيهم سعد بن أبي وقاص

BURSEVI:v1p278/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p278/r9.speaker: عمر
BURSEVI:v1p278/r9.claim: After Saʿd's injury, ʿUmar prayed for a decisive clarification; the final prohibition verses were then revealed and he answered that they had desisted.
BURSEVI:v1p278/r9.anchor: فقال عمر : اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا

BURSEVI:v1p278/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p278/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p278/r10.claim: Wine was prohibited in the third year after the Hijra, a few days after the Battle of the Trench.
BURSEVI:v1p278/r10.anchor: وحرمت الخمر في السنة الثالثة من الهجرة بعد غزوة الأحزاب بأيام

BURSEVI:v1p278/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p278/r11.speaker: القفال
BURSEVI:v1p278/r11.claim: Al-Qaffāl explains the staged ban as gentle instruction: people were accustomed to wine and benefited from it, so an immediate prohibition would have burdened them; after the final ruling, it was poured out.
BURSEVI:v1p278/r11.anchor: قال القفال والحكمة في وقوع التحريم على هذا الترتيب

BURSEVI:v1p278/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p278/r12.speaker: ابن عمر
BURSEVI:v1p278/r12.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says that when the final ban came, some Companions broke their wine jars and others washed them with water and clay; rain later revealed wine's color and smell in Medina's streets for a time.
BURSEVI:v1p278/r12.anchor: قال ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما : خرجنا بالحباب إلى الطريق

BURSEVI:v1p278/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p278/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p278/r13.claim: Wine had been exceptionally beloved to the Arabs, and God prohibited nothing more forcefully than it.
BURSEVI:v1p278/r13.anchor: ولم يكن يومئذ للعرب عيش أعجب منها وما حرم الله عليهم شيئا أشد من الخمر

BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r1.claim: As outward wine comes from grapes, dates, raisins, and grains, inward wine comes from heedlessness, desire, caprice, and love of the world; these intoxicate the human soul and intellect and are sinful.
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r1.anchor: والإشارة في الآية أن خمر الظاهر كما يتخذ من أجناس مختلفة من العنب والتمر والزبيب

BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r2.claim: Since intoxicants are sinful, every intoxicant is forbidden, and anything whose large amount intoxicates is forbidden even in a small amount.
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r2.anchor: ولهذا كل مسكر حرام وما يسكر كثيره فقليله حرام

BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r3.claim: A different spiritual wine intoxicates hearts, spirits, and secrets: it is the drink of spiritual arrivals in cups of witnessing, poured by the cupbearer of divine attributes' self-disclosure.
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r3.anchor: ومنها ما يسكر القلوب والأرواح والأسرار فهو شراب الواردات في أقداح المشاهدات

BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r4.claim: That spiritual drink quiets appetites; hearts are absorbed in ecstasies, spirits in witnessing, and secrets in the glimpse of beauty, so it is beneficial and lawful.
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r4.anchor: فإذا دارت على النفوس وانخمدت شهواتها وسكرت القلوب بالمواجيد عن المواحيد

BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r5.claim: Some are intoxicated by the drink's existence, others by witnessing its cupbearer; a couplet contrasts their states.
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r5.anchor: فالعجب كل العجب أن قوما أسكرهم وجود الشراب وقوما أسكرهم شهود الساقي

BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r6.claim: In the spiritual journey, turning away from the cups of union at the end is a greater loss than a thousand years of seeking at the beginning is a gain.
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r6.anchor: وأتم الإعراض عن كؤوس الوصال في النهاية أكبر من نفع الطلب ألف سنة في البداية

BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r7.claim: Just as a wine-drunk person is barred from prayer, one drunk with heedlessness and caprice is veiled from communion.
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r7.anchor: سكران الغفلة والهوى محجوب عن المواصلات

BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r8.claim: The inward sin of gambling is the prevalence of trickery, deception, lying, and foul speech in the way people pursue the spiritual path; it is grave to the elect and alien to the righteous.
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r8.anchor: وأما إثم الميسر فهو أن آثار القمار هي شعار أكثر الديار في سلوك طريق الحيل

BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r9.claim: The inward benefit of gambling is disregard for both worlds and effacement of worldly forms in the singularity of the Kaaba's imprint.
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r9.anchor: وأما نفعه فعدم الالتفات إلى الكونين وبزل نقوش العالمين في فردانية نقش الكعبتين

BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r10.claim: The al-Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya reading says sins outweigh benefits because the sins affect the many while benefits belong to the elect, and the many outnumber the elect.
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r10.anchor: لأن إثمهما للعوام ونفعهما للخواص والعوام أكثر من الخواص

BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r11.claim: The charity question continues the topic of what to spend raised by the earlier verse; when 2:215 was revealed, ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ asked what he should spend, prompting the instruction al-ʿafw.
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r11.anchor: قال عمر بن الجموح ما أنفق فنزل قوله

BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r12.claim: Al-ʿafw is the opposite of effort and hardship: spend what is easy, available, and surplus to one's own needs and the needs of dependents.
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r12.anchor: أنفقوا العفو وهو نقيض الجهد وهو المشقة ونقيضه اليسر والسهولة

BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r13.claim: The kāf is accusative as an adjective for an omitted absolute object, meaning clarification like this; singular address can target a plural audience conceived as a group.
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r13.anchor: والكاف في محل النصب صفة لمصدر محذوف

BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r14.claim: God makes the signs concerning legal rulings clear in their import and indication, not after they were obscure or confused.
BURSEVI:v1p279#2/r14.anchor: الدالة على الأحكام الشرعية لا بيانا أدنى منه

BURSEVI:v1p280/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p280/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p280/r1.claim: Thinking about both abodes means choosing what is better and easier in this life, what benefits in the next, and avoiding what harms one there.
BURSEVI:v1p280/r1.anchor: لكي تتفكروا في أمور الدارين فتأخذوا بما هو أصلح لكم

BURSEVI:v1p280/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p280/r2.speaker: البغوي
BURSEVI:v1p280/r2.claim: Al-Baghawī says to reflect on the world's passing nature and renounce it, and on the Hereafter's permanence and turn toward it.
BURSEVI:v1p280/r2.anchor: قال البغوي : يبين الله لكم الآيات في أمر الدنيا والآخرة

BURSEVI:v1p280/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p280/r3.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v1p280/r3.claim: A man offered the Prophet his only possession, a gold egg from a campaign, as charity. The Prophet first turned away, then angrily took and threw it, rebuking him for giving away all his wealth and leaving himself dependent; charity should come from surplus. No grading is given.
BURSEVI:v1p280/r3.anchor: وعن النبي عليه السلام أن رجلا أتاه ببيضة من ذهب

BURSEVI:v1p280/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p280/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p280/r4.claim: Al-ʿafw also hints that a donor's gift should leave no trace in the heart, meaning it should be given freely and cheerfully; the root sense is erasure.
BURSEVI:v1p280/r4.anchor: وفي لفظ العفو إشارة إلى أن ما يعطيه المرء ينبغي أن يعفو أثره عن قلبه

BURSEVI:v1p280/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p280/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p280/r5.claim: The elect give from wealth beyond sufficiency, while the elite of the elite practice selfless preference and give what they need, even to a wealthy recipient.
BURSEVI:v1p280/r5.anchor: ثم الإخراج عن فاضل الأموال على قدر الكفاية طريقة الخواص

BURSEVI:v1p280/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p280/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p280/r6.claim: The highest form of self-preference is supported by the verse describing believers who give others priority even while themselves in need.
BURSEVI:v1p280/r6.anchor: ويؤثرون على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم خصاصة

BURSEVI:v1p280/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p280/r7.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BURSEVI:v1p280/r7.claim: ʿUmar donated half his wealth to outdo Abū Bakr, but when asked what remained for his family he said half; Abū Bakr gave everything, saying Allah and His Messenger remained for them, and ʿUmar conceded he would not compete again.
BURSEVI:v1p280/r7.anchor: وعن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه قال : أمرنا رسول الله

BURSEVI:v1p280/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p280/r8.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v1p280/r8.claim: A report says the Prophet described the distance between ʿUmar and Abū Bakr as like the difference between their two answers about what they left for their families; no grading is given.
BURSEVI:v1p280/r8.anchor: روي أن النبي عليه السلام قال عند ذلك

BURSEVI:v1p280/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p280/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p280/r9.claim: The account shows Abū Bakr's superiority over ʿUmar in this respect, but excellence in one matter does not establish inferiority in every other matter; ranking depends on knowledge of God.
BURSEVI:v1p280/r9.anchor: ومنه يعرف فضل أبي بكر على عمر لكن الفاضلة من وجه لا تنافي المفضولية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r2.claim: Wine was then allowed during the night of fasting; people commonly drank date and raisin nabīdh, which could ferment in the hot climate.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r2.anchor: كان الشراب مما أذن فيه في ليل الصيام وكان غالب شرابهم النبيذ من التمر والزبيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r3.claim: Intoxication obstructs worship, especially military striving, because a drunk person cannot contribute judgment or physical force.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r3.anchor: فكان عائقا عن العبادة لا سيما الجهاد لأن السكران لا ينتفع به في رأي ولا بطش

BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r4.claim: Unlike food, wine was not necessary to sustain the body, so explaining its status could be deferred until more urgent matters were addressed.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r4.anchor: ولم يكن ضروريا في إقامة البدن كالطعام آخر بيانه إلى أن فرغ مما هو أولى منه بالإعلام

BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r5.claim: The author says the intervening verses were concluded by returning to the theme of striving with which they began, before later verses on permissions.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r5.anchor: وختم الآيات المتخللة بينه وبين آيات الإذن بما بدأها به من الجهاد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r6.claim: After discussing striving as a ground for hoping in mercy, the passage fittingly turns to what the author calls the greatest folly and sources of evils: wine and gambling.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r6.anchor: الجهاد وما ذكر معه في محل الرجاء للرحمة فاقتضى الحال السؤال : هل سالوا عن أهزل الهزل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r7.claim: The author says wine was among the spoils taken by Abdullah ibn Jahsh's expedition, which occasioned the preceding verses.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r7.anchor: أحد ما غنمه عبد الله بن جحش رضي الله تعالى عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r8.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r8.claim: Harali relates khamr to covering: vegetation hides what is visible, while wine conceals the intellect and obscures the boundary between clear reason and brute animality.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r8.anchor: قال الحرالي : وهو مما منه الخمر - بفتح الميم - وهو ما وارى

BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r9.claim: Harali defines wine as anything intoxicating, whatever the drink and whether its amount is small or large.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r9.anchor: وهي ما أسكر من اي شراب كان سواء فيه القليل والكثير

BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r10.claim: Harali calls maysir a pre-Islamic gambling institution intended to benefit the weak and to gain the spoils of victory.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r10.anchor: قال الحرالي : اسم مقامرة كانت الجاهلية تعمل بها لقصد انتفاع الضعفاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r11.claim: Wine and gambling are paired because both undermine striving and other goods by transferring wealth without the owner's willing consent.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r11.anchor: لتآخيهما في الضرر بالجهاد وغيره بإذهاب المال مجانا عن غير طيب نفس

BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r12.claim: The author says wine and gambling are paired here as they are in the Maidah passage.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r12.anchor: ما بين سبحانه وتعالى من المؤاخاة بينهما هنا وفي المائدة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r13.claim: The pronoun refers to using or consuming both wine and gambling.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r13.anchor: { قل فيهما } أي في استعمالهما { إثم كبير }

BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r14.claim: The sin includes lying, abuse, loss of reason, and taking another's property; declaring the acts sinful establishes their prohibition and identifies them as major sins.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r14.anchor: لما فيهما من المساوي المنابذة لمحاسن الشرع من الكذب والشتم وزوال العقل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r15.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r15.claim: Harali notes readings with bāʾ and thāʾ, كبير and كثير, which indicate both great magnitude and large quantity of sin; either should deter a sound person.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r15.anchor: قال الحرالي : في قراءتي الباء الموحدة والمثلثة إنباء عن مجموع الأمرين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r16.claim: The author frames the question and gradual explanation as an expression of divine forbearance, leaving matters beyond the subject at pure permissibility.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p408/r16.anchor: مبينا لما اقتضاه الحال من حلمه فيبقى ما عداه على الإباحة المحضة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r1.claim: The benefits people seek include trading in wine, enjoying its taste, winning money through gambling, aiding the poor, boasting over nonparticipants, and gaining companions and their food, drink, and gifts.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r1.anchor: يرتكبونهما لأجلها من التجارة في الخمر واللذة بشربها , ومن أخذ المال الكثير في الميسر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r2.claim: Because the sin outweighs the benefits, the harms take precedence; the author invokes the principle that preventing harms comes first.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r2.anchor: ودرء المفاسد مقدم فكيف { وإثمهما أكبر من نفعهما }

BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r3.speaker: أهل المعرفة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r3.claim: Some people of insight said the benefit of gambling was that, during winter and famine, Arabs wagered camels and gave the meat to the poor, improving their circumstances.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r3.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعرفة : والنفع الذي ذكر الله في الميسر أن العرب في الشتاء والجدب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r4.speaker: الأعشى
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r4.claim: The author cites al-Aʿsha's line praising people who feed guests in winter and distribute provisions through the gambling shares as evidence for the reported benefit.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r4.anchor: قال الأعشى في ذلك : المطعمو الضيف إذا ما شتوا والجاعلو القوت على الياسر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r5.speaker: غيره
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r5.claim: Another account says gamblers gave the meat to the poor without eating it themselves, boasted of the generosity, and called a person who abstained al-barm.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r5.anchor: وقال غيره : وكانوا يدفعونها للفقراء ولا يأكلون منها ويفتخرون بذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r6.speaker: المجد الفيروزآبادي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r6.claim: Al-Fayruzabadi's dictionary defines maysir as playing with arrows, the camel staked in the game, backgammon, or gambling in general.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r6.anchor: قال المجد الفيروز آبادي في قاموسه : والميسر اللعب بالقداح

BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r7.speaker: صاحب كتاب الزينة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r7.claim: The lexicon gives yusr as the plural of yāsir and aysār as the plural of yusr, illustrating a plural formed from another plural.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r7.anchor: وقال صاحب كتاب الزينة : وجمع الياسر يسر وجمع اليسر أيسار فهو جمع الجمع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r8.claim: Qimār is any wager based purely on uncertain risk; the author derives its name from the moon because a gambler's wealth waxes and wanes like the moon.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r8.anchor: والقمار كل مراهنة على غرر محض وكأنه مأخوذ من القمر آية الليل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r9.speaker: مجاهد
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r9.claim: Mujahid is quoted as defining maysir broadly as anything involving gambling, even children playing with walnuts.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r9.anchor: قال مجاهد : كل شيء فيه قمار فهو الميسر حتى لعب الصبيان بالجوز

BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r10.speaker: الشافعي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r10.claim: Al-Shafiʿi is quoted as defining maysir as any game requiring a person to pay or receive money; chess without a wager, abusive speech, or missed prayer is not maysir.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r10.anchor: وفي تفسير الأصبهاني عن الشافعي : إن الميسر ما يوجب دفع مال أو أخذ مال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r11.speaker: الأزهري
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r11.claim: Al-Azhari derives maysir from dividing the staked camel into shares; yāsir first meant the butcher who apportioned its meat, then the gamblers who caused the slaughter.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p409/r11.anchor: وقال الأزهري : الميسر الجزور الذي كانوا يتقامرون عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r1.claim: Continuing al-Azhari's lexical entry, the text records yasar al-qawm for gambling and yāsir or yusr for a gambler, with aysār as the plural.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r2.speaker: القزاز
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r2.claim: Al-Qazzaz gives forms for the person who gambles and the camel staked in the game, and records aysāʾ as a plural of yusr.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r2.anchor: القزاز : فأنت ياسر وهو ميسور برجع والمفعول ميسور - يعني الجزور

BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r3.speaker: القزاز
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r3.claim: Al-Qazzaz calls the gamblers collectively yusr, with an individual yāsir; he also uses yusr for an arrow thrower and maysir for dice, but not chess because its meaning differs.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r3.anchor: وقال القزاز : واليسر القوم الذين يتقامرون على الجزور

BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r4.speaker: عبد الحق
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r4.claim: Abd al-Haqq defines maysir as the place where portions are divided.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r4.anchor: وقال عبد الحق في الواعي : والميسر موضع التجزئة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r5.claim: Abu Abd Allah describes buying and slaughtering a camel, then dividing it into portions.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r5.anchor: أبو عبد الله : كان أمر الميسر أنهم كانوا يشترون جزورا فينحرونها ثم يجزئونها أجزاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو والأصمعي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r6.claim: Abu Amr says the camel was divided into ten portions, while al-Asmaʿi says there were twenty-eight.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r6.anchor: قال أبو عمرو : على عشرة أجزاء , وقال الأصمعي : على ثمانية وعشرين جزءا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r7.claim: Ten arrows were drawn: seven carried shares and three were blank; a trusted, impartial man drew an arrow for each participant, and winners received shares according to the arrow.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r7.anchor: ثم يسهمون عليها بعشرة قداح , لسبعة منها أنصباء وهي الفذ

BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r8.speaker: بعضهم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r8.claim: One reported view says a person drawing a blank arrow neither wins nor pays; the drawing is repeated, and that person's turn is treated as void.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r8.anchor: قال بعضهم : من خرجت باسمه لم يأخذ شيئا ولم يغرم ولكن تعاد الثانية

BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r9.speaker: بعضهم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r9.claim: A competing view says the holders of the three blank arrows pay the entire camel's price, while the seven winning holders take their allotted shares.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r9.anchor: وقال بعضهم : بل يصير ثمن الجزور كله على أصحاب هؤلاء الثلاثة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r10.speaker: أبو عبيد
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r10.claim: Abu Ubayd says scholars did not fully explain the game; Abu Ubayda asked Bedouins, who no longer knew its rules because Islam had ended it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r10.anchor: قال أبو عبيد : ولم أجد علماءنا يستقصون علم معرفة هذا ولا يدعونه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r11.claim: Abu Ubayda says the Bedouins he asked did not know the game, which Islam had ended, so they could not explain its rules.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r11.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : وقد سألت عنه الأعراب فقالوا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r12.speaker: أبو عبيد
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r12.claim: Abu Ubayd says the game was practiced among people of high status, wealth, and means.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r12.anchor: قال أبو عبيد : وإنما كان هذا منهم في أهل الشرف والثروة والجدة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r13.speaker: صاحب الزينة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r13.claim: The Zina account calls arrows that carry a share marked because their shares are assigned; seven people each held one arrow, though a player might hold two and be praised for it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r13.anchor: وقال صاحب الزينة : فالتي لها الغنم وعليها الغرم أي من السهام

BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r14.speaker: النابغة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r14.claim: Al-Nabigha's verse praises giving people two shares each and clothing a group, cited in connection with a player taking two arrows.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p410/r14.anchor: قال النابغة : إني أتمم إيثاري وأمنحهم مثنى الأيادي

BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r1.claim: The ḥarḍa draws the arrows but does not participate or share in winnings or losses, so gamblers choose him; al-barm is the person who declines to participate.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r1.anchor: ويقال للذي يضرب بالقداح : حرضة , وإنما سمي بذلك لأنه رجل يجيل لا يدخل مع الأيسار

BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r2.claim: Al-barm is someone who neither draws arrows nor joins the gamblers in any of their affairs.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r2.anchor: والذي لا يضرب القداح ولا يدخل مع الأيسار في شيء من أمورهم يقال له : البرم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r3.claim: The arrow pouch is called ribāba; it could be leather or cloth, and its ends were gathered and leveled before the draw.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r3.anchor: وتجمع القداح في جلدة , وقال بعضهم : في خرقة , وتسمى تلك الجلدة الربابة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r4.claim: To prevent choosing an arrow by touch, the drawer's hand was covered in leather and his eyes bound; he gathered the arrows and struck their tips so one emerged as the winner.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r4.anchor: وتكسى يده أديما لكي لا يجد مس قدح له فيه رأي وتشد عيناه , فيجمع أصابعه عليها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r5.speaker: غيره
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r5.claim: Another account says the winning arrow was the one that emerged from the pouch without being deflected or obstructed.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r5.anchor: وقال غيره : تكون الربابة فلا يخرج ومنها ما لا يعترض فيطلع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r6.claim: The trusted person beside the ḥarḍa was called raqīb, and the arrow drawer mufīḍ; ifāḍa means pushing the arrows forward together.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r6.anchor: ويقعد رجل أمين على الحرضة يقال له : الرقيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r7.claim: The author connects the arrow drawer's ifāḍa with pilgrimage ifāḍa, the push from Arafat to Jamʿ.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r7.anchor: وكذلك الإفاضة من عرفة هو الدفع منها إلى جمع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r8.speaker: القاموس
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r8.claim: Al-Qamus says gamblers bought a camel on credit, slaughtered it, and divided it into 28 shares or ten portions; the winning arrows took shares while blank arrows incurred the cost.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r8.anchor: وقال في القاموس : كانوا إذا أرادوا أن ييسروا اشتروا جزورا نسيئة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r9.speaker: عبد الغافر الفارسي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r9.claim: Abd al-Ghafir al-Farsi describes maysir as pre-Islamic gambling over a camel or other property divided into shares, but notes that accounts differ and Muslim lexicographers lacked firm knowledge of its procedure.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r9.anchor: وقال عبد الغافر الفارسي في مجمع الغرائب : الياسر هو الضارب في القداح

BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r10.claim: To aid memorization, the author lists seven winning arrows and three blank ones: al-fadh, al-taw'am, al-raqib, al-hils, al-nafis, al-musbil, al-muʿalla, al-maniḥ, al-safih, and al-waghd.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r10.anchor: وقد نظمت أسماء القداح تسهيلا لحفظها في قولي : الفذ والتوأم والرقيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r11.speaker: القاموس
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r11.claim: Al-Qamus defines al-fadh as the first arrow of maysir and begins its definitions of the taw'am and raqib arrows.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p411/r11.anchor: فقال في القاموس : الفذ أي بفتح الفاء وتشديد الذال المعجمة : أول سهام الميسر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r1.speaker: القاموس
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r1.claim: Al-Qamus defines ḍarīb as the person who oversees or draws the arrows, and also as the third arrow.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r1.anchor: وقال في مادة ضرب : والضريب الموكل بالقداح أو الذي يضرب بها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r2.speaker: صاحب الجمع بين العباب والمحكم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r2.claim: The dictionary collection defines raqīb as a keeper or custodian of the arrows, an umpire near the ḥarḍa, or the third arrow, all related uses of the same term.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r2.anchor: وقال في الجمع بين العباب والمحكم : والرقيب الحافظ ورقيب القداح الأمين على الضريب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r3.speaker: صاحب الجمع بين العباب والمحكم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r3.claim: The third raqib arrow carries three shares: its holder wins three shares or owes three if it loses.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r3.anchor: والرقيب الثالث من قداح الميسر , وفيه ثلاثة فروض , وله غنم ثلاثة انصباء إن فاز

BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r4.speaker: سيبويه
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r4.claim: Sibawayh says ḍarīb has the faʿīl form with the active-agent sense; ḍarīb also names the third arrow, called al-raqib.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r5.speaker: القاموس
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r5.claim: Al-Qamus defines ḥarḍa as the game steward, al-ḥils as the fourth arrow, al-nafis as fifth, and al-musbil as sixth or fifth.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r5.anchor: وقال في القاموس : والحرضة أي بضم المهملة وإسكان المهملة ثم معجمة أمين المقامرين

BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r6.speaker: مجمع البحرين
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r6.claim: Majmaʿ al-Baḥrayn gives al-muṣaffah as another name for al-musbil.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r6.anchor: وقال في مجمع البحرين : وهو المصفح أيضا يعني بفتح الفاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r7.speaker: القاموس
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r7.claim: Al-Qamus calls al-muʿalla the seventh arrow and defines al-maniḥ and al-safih as blanks; al-waghd is both a blank arrow and a fool, weakling, or contemptible person.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r7.anchor: والمعلى كمعظم سابع سهام الميسر , والمنيح كأمير أي بنون وآخره مهملة قدح بلا نصيب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r8.speaker: صاحب الزينة
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r8.claim: The Zina account says the camel was divided into ten shares; al-raqib could draw repeatedly, taking three shares each time, and when the camel was exhausted the remaining players paid according to their shares.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r8.anchor: وقال صاحب الزينة : وكانوا يبتاعون الجزور ويتضمنون ثمنه ثم يضربون بالقداح عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r9.speaker: الأصمعي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r9.claim: Al-Asmaʿi instead assigns 28 shares to the arrows, beginning with one for al-fadh and two for al-taw'am; the author reports that most scholars disagreed and considered him mistaken.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p412/r9.anchor: وذكر عن الأصمعي أنه قال : كانوا يقسمون الجزور على ثمانية وعشرين جزءا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r1.speaker: القائلون بهذا القول
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r1.claim: A reported account says that if each arrow received exactly its allotted share, no one would bear a loss or win, so the game would not count as gambling.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r1.anchor: وقالوا : إذا كان ذلك كذلك وأخذ كل قدح نصيبه لم يبق هنالك غرم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r2.claim: The arrows are called aʿshār because the camel was divided into ten portions.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r2.anchor: ومن أجل ذلك قالوا لأجزاء الجزور : أعشار , لأنها عشرة أجزاء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r3.speaker: القزاز
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r3.claim: Al-Qazzāz says al-tawʾam is the second gambling arrow, named for its two stakes and two camel shares; the seven winning arrows carry stakes and shares from one through seven, while three arrows carry no stake.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r3.anchor: وقال القزاز في التاء الفوقانية من ديوانه : والتوأم أحد أقداح الميسر وهو الثاني منها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r4.claim: The three arrows without stakes are called aghfāl, like livestock without a brand.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r4.anchor: ولذلك تدعى أغفالا لأن الغفل من الدواب الذي لا سمة له

BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r5.claim: A camel was slaughtered and apportioned into ten shares: the haunches, rump, withers, chest, back, shoulders, and thighs were divided, with neck and loose skin shared evenly.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r5.anchor: والكتفان وفيهما العضدان جزءان , والفخذان جزءان , وتقسم الرقبة والطفاطف بالسواء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r6.claim: The leftover bone or meat was called al-raym, a surplus beyond the load, and the butcher took it; sellers might also reserve parts, usually the extremities and head.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r6.anchor: وما بقي من عظم أو بضعة فهو الريم وأصله من الزيادة على الحمل وهي التي تسمى علاوة فيأخذ الجازر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r7.claim: A blindfolded handler drew the arrows from a bag while an appointed trustee shook them two or three times; blank arrows were returned to the bag.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r7.anchor: ثم يؤتى بخريطة فيها القداح واسعة الأسفل ضيقة الفم قدر ما يخرج منها سهم أو سهمان

BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r8.speaker: author
