BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r8.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays compares a beloved's eyes to two arrows striking the ten shares of a slain heart: the two winning arrows capture the whole heart.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p413/r8.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس . وما ذرفت عيناك إلا لتضربي بسهميك في أعشار قلب مقتل جعل القلب بدلا لأعشار الجزور

BIQAI-FULL:v1p414/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414/r1.claim: A blank arrow is redrawn; a winner takes the share attached to his arrow and withdraws without loss, and the drawing continues until the shares run out.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414/r1.anchor: فإن كان الذي خرج الفذ أخذ صاحبه جزءا وسلم من الغرم وأعاد الحرضة الإفاضة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p414/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414/r2.claim: If early winners exhaust the camel, the remaining players pay its cost; if a winner's stake exceeds the remaining shares, he takes the remainder and the others compensate the excess proportionally.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414/r2.anchor: فإن زادت سهام من خرج له قدح على ما بقي من الجزور غرم له من بقي ما زاد سهمه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p414/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414/r3.speaker: القائلون بهذا القول
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414/r3.claim: One view divides the camel into twenty-eight portions, matching the total arrow stakes from one through seven.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414/r3.anchor: وقد ذكر أن الجزور تجزأ على عدد ما في القداح من الفروض وهي ثمانية وعشرون جزءا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p414/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414/r4.claim: He rejects the twenty-eight-part view here: if everyone simply took the shares attached to his arrow until all arrows were drawn, there would be no meaningful win, loss, or gambling; he initially judges the other account sounder.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414/r4.anchor: ولا معنى لهذا القول لأنه يلزم أن لا يكون في هذا قمار ولا فوز ولا خيبة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r1.claim: In Imruʾ al-Qays's poem, the beloved strikes the heart with al-muʿallā and al-raqīb and wins the whole heart, as a gambler can win all the camel's shares with two arrows.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r1.anchor: وما ذرفت عيناك إلا لتضربي بسهميك في أعشار قلب مقتل يقول : تضرب بسهميها المعلى والرقيب فتحوز القلب كله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r2.claim: An earlier gloss of Kathīr's verse says travel had emaciated the camel until it had no meat, as if two winning arrows had taken all its shares.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r2.anchor: هذه الناقة هزلها السير حتى لم يبق من لحمها شيء فكأنه ضرب عليها بالقداح

BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r3.claim: He prefers a marginal gloss: the camel's endurance makes it outpace other camels like a gambler whose arrow wins twice; this better fits the line's saying the camel itself won with two arrows.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r3.anchor: ورأيت على حاشية نسخة من كتابه ما لعله أليق

BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r4.speaker: كثير
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r4.claim: Kathīr's verse portrays a camel passing through midday heat and night travel as though it had won with two of the arrow-drawer's arrows.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r4.anchor: ومن هذا قول كثير ووصف ناقة هزلها السير حتى أذهب لحمها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r5.claim: He corrects his earlier dismissal of the twenty-eight-share account: unequal stakes still produce unequal awards, since al-muʿallā yields seven of twenty-eight shares, more than arrows with six or fewer stakes.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r5.anchor: وقوله : لا معنى للتقامر عليها , على تقدير التجزئة بثمانية وعشرين ليس كذلك بل تظهر ثمرته في التفاوت في الأنصباء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r6.speaker: الأصمعي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r6.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī is reported by the author of al-Zīna and others as supporting the twenty-eight-share division of the camel.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r6.anchor: وقد صرح صاحب الزينة وغيره عن الأصمعي كما مضى وهو ممن قال بهذا القول

BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r7.claim: Unequal results can also arise when arrows leave the bag aligned and several fall to one player; if there are fewer players than arrows, one person may win most of the camel.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r7.anchor: وربما خرج له سهمان أو ثلاثة في إفاضة واحدة لاستقامة السهام واعتدالها للخروج ففاز بمعظم الجزور

BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r8.claim: The game remains a gamble even when the number of arrows matches the players: a player may draw none and owe payment, while no one can be sure of winning.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r8.anchor: وبتقدير أن لا يخرج لكل واحد واحد يكون قمارا أيضا , لأن كل واحد منهم غير واثق بالفوز

BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r9.speaker: الكشاف
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r9.claim: Al-Kashshāf says the participants gave their winnings to the poor and kept none for themselves; al-Biqāʿī notes this had also been transmitted from the author of al-Zīna.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r9.anchor: وقال في الكشاف : إنهم كانوا يعطون الأنصباء للفقراء ولا يأخذون منها شيئا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r10.claim: After condemning spending on what dims the spirit and weakens the body, the verse turns to the praiseworthy purposes on which wealth should be spent.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r10.anchor: ولما ذكر ما يذهب ضياء الروح وقوام البدن وذم النفقة فيهما اقتضى الحال السؤال عما يمدح الإنفاق فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r11.claim: The repeated question about what to spend signals repeated prompting and the great importance of spending, which is among the principal supports of jihad.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p414#2/r11.anchor: فأنبأ ذلك بعظم شأنها لأنها أعظم دعائم الجهاد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r1.claim: The conjunction links this spending question to the earlier question and answer about spending in 2:215, which made another spending question expectable; questions about orphans and menstruation lacked that setup.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r2.claim: He rejects revelation together versus separately as a sufficient reason for the conjunction, since it gives no wisdom and many revelation reports show conjunctions; the last revealed verse, 2:281, also begins with wa.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r2.anchor: وادعاء أن سبب العطف النزول جملة وسبب القطع النزول مفرقا مع كونه غير شاف للغلة بعدم بيان الحكمة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r3.speaker: البيهقي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r3.claim: The author cites al-Bayhaqī and al-Wāḥidī for reports that 2:281 was the final revealed verse, noting its opening conjunction; al-Bukhārī also gives it a chapter heading.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r3.anchor: أخرجه البيهقي في الدلائل والواحدي من وجهين في مقدمة أسباب النزول

BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r4.claim: Al-Ḥarālī reads the conjunction as reinforcing the repeated seeking twice, like the Israelites' case; this community may have avoided asking a third time, unlike them.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r4.anchor: وقال الحرالي : في العطف إنباء بتأكد التلدد مرتين كما في قصة بني إسرائيل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r5.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines al-ʿafw as what a person freely gives without strain; the command encourages giving the surplus but does not make that level obligatory, preserving ease for this community.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r5.anchor: وهو ما سمحت به النفس من غير كلفة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r6.claim: Al-Ḥarālī sorts spending into obligatory alms, dispensable surplus that should not be hoarded, and contested property whose donation requires striving and becomes a trade for the afterlife.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r6.anchor: فصار المنفق على ثلاث رتب : رتبة حق مفروض لا بد منه وهي الصدقة المفروضة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r7.claim: When a woman asked what she could give from her husband's wealth, the Prophet answered fresh fruit: it may be eaten or gifted before it spoils.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r7.anchor: قالت امرأة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ما يحل لنا من أموال أزواجنا - تسأل عن الإنفاق منها , قال : الرطب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r8.claim: Here al-rutab is vocalized with ḍamma on rāʾ and sukūn on ṭāʾ; it means produce such as grapes and melons, cooked foods, or other things that spoil if kept overnight.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r8.anchor: لأنه من العفو الذي يضر إمساكه بفساده ؛ لأن الرطب هو ما إذا أبقي ين يوم إلى يوم تغير كالعنب والبطيخ

BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r9.claim: Restricting the recommended gift to freely disposable surplus cautions the drinker before wine was forbidden: intoxicated dealings are generally invalid and regretted on sobering; gambling is worse.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r9.anchor: وفي تخصيص المنفق بالعفو منع لمتعاطي الخمر قبل حرمتها من التصرف

BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r10.claim: The command's late clarification that spending is urged on surplus could inspire self-sacrifice among believers in hardship without imposing a burden; 2:177 had already praised giving wealth despite love of it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r10.anchor: ولعل تأخير بيان أن المحثوث عليه من النفقة إنما هو الفضل إلى هذا المحل ليحمل أهل الدين الرغبة فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r11.speaker: الأصبهاني
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r11.claim: Al-Aṣbahānī reports exegetes' view that people kept a year's household needs from gold, silver, crops, and livestock, or one day's needs if they worked, and donated the rest until the zakat verse abrogated this rule.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r11.anchor: قال الأصبهاني : قال أهل التفسير : كان الرجل بعد نزول هذه الآية إذا كان له ذهب أو فضة أو زرع أو ضرع ينظر ما يكفيه

BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r12.claim: Having detailed the rulings and spending through varied explanations, the verse reassures that God explains the signs likewise; al-Ḥarālī says the plural covers the heart, soul, body, and a person's dealings with others.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r12.anchor: قال الحرالي : فجمعها لأنها آيات من جهات مختلفات لما يرجع لأمر القلب وللنفس وللجسم ولحال المرء مع غيره

BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r13.claim: The initial singular address raises the statement's rank and turns it toward the Prophet, already filled with knowledge; the plural then addresses followers according to their understanding and aspiration. Alternatively, the syntax repeats the act of explaining.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r13.anchor: وأفرد الخطاب أولا وجمع ثانيا إعلاما بعظمة هذا القول للإقبال به على الرأس

BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r14.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r14.claim: Al-Ḥarālī takes the phrase as preparing people for reflection, the soul's hand for grasping knowledge as the body's hand grasps sensible things.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p416/r14.anchor: المعلومات كما تنال بيد الجسم المحسوسات - قاله الحرالي

DURR-FULL:v1p586/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p586/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p586/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Companions asked only thirteen questions before the Prophet's death, all answered in the Quran, including wine and gambling, sacred months, orphans, menstruation, spoils, and spending; they asked about what benefited them.
DURR-FULL:v1p586/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: ما رأيت قوما كانوا خيرا من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما سألوه إلا عن ثلاث عشرة مسألة

DURR-FULL:v1p604/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p604/r9.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p604/r9.claim: Umar repeatedly asks God for a clear ruling on wine because it wastes wealth and reason. The answer comes in stages: 2:219, then 4:43 with a warning not to approach prayer drunk, then 5:91; on hearing its ending Umar says they desist. Al-Tirmidhi and al-Hakim grade the report sound.
DURR-FULL:v1p604/r9.anchor: عن عمر أنه قال: اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا فإنها تذهب المال والعقل فنزلت {يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر}

DURR-FULL:v1p606/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r1.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r1.claim: Anas reports that the Companions drank wine; this verse came down, they said they would drink what benefited them, and after 5:90 prohibited it they declared they had stopped.
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r1.anchor: عن أنس قال: كنا نشرب الخمر فأنزلت {يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر} الآية

DURR-FULL:v1p606/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r2.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r2.claim: Aisha says that when al-Baqara was revealed it contained wine's prohibition, so the Messenger of God forbade it.
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r2.anchor: عن عائشة قال لما نزلت سورة البقرة نزل فيها تحريم الخمر فنهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v1p606/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r3.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r3.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib gives an etymology for khamr, relating it to its clear top and turbid sediment.
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب قال: إنما سميت الخمر لأنها صفاء صفوها وسفل كدرها

DURR-FULL:v1p606/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r4.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r4.claim: Ibn Umar glosses al-maysir as gambling.
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r4.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: الميسر القمار

DURR-FULL:v1p606/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r5.claim: Mujahid says al-maysir means gambling and derives its name from gamblers' phrase aysara jazuran, meaning to stake a camel.
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: الميسر القمار وإنما سمي الميسر لقولهم أيسر جزورا

DURR-FULL:v1p606/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas describes pre-Islamic maysir as wagering one's family and property; whoever defeated his opponent took both.
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر} قال: الميسر القمار كان الرجل في الجاهلية يخاطر عن أهله وماله

DURR-FULL:v1p606/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says wine's great sin is loss to religion, while its benefits are pleasure and joy; the religious loss outweighs that enjoyment.
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر} قال: الميسر القمار

DURR-FULL:v1p606/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r8.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r8.claim: The account describes staged restriction: people avoided wine at prayer, drank after evening prayer, and were sober by noon, before 4:43 restricted prayer while intoxicated.
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r8.anchor: فأنزل الله بعد ذلك (لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى

DURR-FULL:v1p606/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r9.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r9.claim: After some Muslims drank, fought, and spoke offensively, 5:90 prohibited wine.
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r9.anchor: ثم إن ناسا من المسلمين شربوها فقاتل بعضهم بعضا وتكلموا بما لا يرضي الله من القول

DURR-FULL:v1p606/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says this verse was abrogated by the later declaration in 5:90.
DURR-FULL:v1p606/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {يسألونك عن الخمر} الآية

DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r1.claim: Mujahid calls this the first criticism of wine and identifies its benefits as its price and the pleasure it gives.
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {قل فيهما إثم كبير} قال: هذا أول ما عيبت به الخمر {ومنافع للناس}

DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the benefits belonged to the period before prohibition, while the sin describes wine after it became forbidden.
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {قل فيهما إثم كبير ومنافع للناس} قال: منافعهما قبل التحريم وإثمهما بعدما حرما

DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Companions ordered to spend in God's cause asked how much to give, and this verse answered them.
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نفرا من الصحابة حين أمروا بالنفقة في سبيل الله أتوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا

DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r4.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r4.claim: The account adds that before this instruction someone might give away all his property, leaving nothing to donate and needing others to feed him.
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r4.anchor: وكان قبل ذلك ينفق ماله حتى لا يجد ما يتصدق به

DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r5.speaker: يحيى
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r5.claim: Yahya says he had heard that Muadh ibn Jabal and Tha'laba asked what they should spend, since they had dependents and enslaved people.
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r5.anchor: من طريق أبان عن يحيى أنه بلغه أن معاذ بن جبل وثعلبة أتيا رسول الله فقالا: يا رسول الله إن لنا أرقاء وأهلين

DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses al-afw as an amount not conspicuous in one's property and says this preceded obligatory alms.
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ويسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} قال: هو ما لا يتبين في أموالكم

DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas explains al-afw as what remains after providing for one's dependents, also phrased as household surplus.
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ويسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} قال: ما يفضل عن أهلك

DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r8.claim: Ibn Jubayr identifies three uses of al-afw: pardoning sin, moderate spending here, and graciousness between people in 2:237.
DURR-FULL:v1p606#2/r8.anchor: أن عبد الملك بن مروان كتب إلى سعيد بن جبير يسأله عن العفو فقال: العفو على ثلاثة أنحاء

DURR-FULL:v1p607/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r1.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r1.claim: Hasan says giving al-afw means not spending oneself into poverty and then having to ask people for help.
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {قل العفو} قال: ذلك أن لا تجد مالك ثم تقعد تسأل الناس

DURR-FULL:v1p607/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r2.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r2.anchor: عن عطاء في قوله {قل العفو} قال: الفضل

DURR-FULL:v1p607/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r3.speaker: طاوس
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r3.claim: Tawus interprets al-afw as ease or what is readily available in every matter.
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r3.anchor: عن طاوس قال: العفو اليسر من كل شيء

DURR-FULL:v1p607/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r4.claim: Mujahid is reported as taking al-afw here to mean obligatory charity.
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r4.anchor: قال: وكان مجاهد يقول {العفو} الصدقة المفروضة

DURR-FULL:v1p607/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says no fixed amount was prescribed here; 7:199 then commanded taking al-afw, before named dues were revealed.
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {قل العفو} قال: لم تفرض فيه فريضة معلومة ثم قال (خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف)

DURR-FULL:v1p607/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r6.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says the instruction to give al-afw was later abrogated by zakat.
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r6.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {قل العفو} قال: هذا نسخته الزكاة

DURR-FULL:v1p607/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r7.claim: A hadith says the best charity leaves the giver sufficiently provided for, the upper hand is better, and one should begin with dependents, including family, servants, and children.
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أفضل الصدقة ما ترك غنى واليد العليا خير من اليد السفلى وابدأ بمن تعول

DURR-FULL:v1p607/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r8.claim: A second report says the best charity preserves sufficiency, praises the giving hand, and says to start with dependents; examples include one's wife, servant, and child.
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r8.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال خير الصدقة ما أبقت غنى واليد العليا خير من اليد السفلى وابدأ بمن تعول

DURR-FULL:v1p607/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r9.claim: Another wording says charity should come from surplus after need and one should begin with those one supports.
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r9.anchor: عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: خير الصدقة ما كان عن ظهر غنى وابدأ بمن تعول

DURR-FULL:v1p607/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r10.claim: Asked about one dinar, the Prophet directs a man to give first to himself, then his child, wife, and servant, and finally use his judgment; al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r10.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالصدقة فقال رجل: يا رسول الله عندي دينار

DURR-FULL:v1p607/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r11.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r11.claim: Abu Husayn al-Sulami offered egg-sized gold from a mine as his sole wealth; the Prophet took it and tossed it back, and al-Hakim authenticated the report.
DURR-FULL:v1p607/r11.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ جاء رجل وفي لفظ: قدم أبو حصين السلمي بمثل بيضة من الحمامة من ذهب

DURR-FULL:v1p610/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r1.speaker: كدير الضبي
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r1.claim: A Bedouin asks the Prophet for a deed to Paradise and away from Hell: uphold justice and give surplus; when too difficult, feed people and spread peace, or water a needy household from one's camel and waterskin.
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r1.anchor: عن كدير الضبي قال: أتى أعرابي على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: نبئني بعمل يدخلني الجنة

DURR-FULL:v1p610/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r2.speaker: طارق بن عبد الله
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r2.claim: Tariq heard the Prophet urge charity, praise the giving hand, and tell people to begin with parents, then siblings and nearer relatives.
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r2.anchor: عن طارق بن عبد الله قال: أتيت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو يخطب فسمعت من قوله: تصدقوا

DURR-FULL:v1p610/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r3.claim: The Prophet says it is sufficient sin to withhold provision from someone whose needs one controls; Abdullah ibn Amr therefore sends his steward to feed the enslaved people.
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كفى بالمرء إثما أن يحبس عمن يملك قوته

DURR-FULL:v1p610/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the signs invite reflection on this world and the next: the world's disappearance and the afterlife's enduring life.
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات لعلكم تتفكرون} في الدنيا والآخرة

DURR-FULL:v1p610/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r5.claim: Qatada says reflection on both worlds teaches the superiority of the afterlife over this world.
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r5.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {لعلكم تتفكرون} في الدنيا والآخرة قال: لتعلموا فضل الآخرة على الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v1p610/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r6.claim: Hasan says a thoughtful person recognizes this world as trial followed by extinction, and the afterlife as recompense followed by permanence.
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r6.anchor: شهدت الحسن وقرأ هذه الآية من البقرة {لعلكم تتفكرون} في الدنيا والآخرة

DURR-FULL:v1p610/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r7.claim: Qatada says reflection reveals the world's trial and extinction and the afterlife's permanence and recompense, so people should set aside worldly needs for the next life.
DURR-FULL:v1p610/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في الآية قال: من تفكر في الدنيا عرف فضل احداهما على الأخرى عرف أن الدنيا دار بلاء ثم دار فناء

IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r1.speaker: عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r1.claim: Umar repeatedly prayed for clarification about wine; revelation progressed from 2:219 to the prayer restriction in 4:43 and the final prohibition in 5:90-91, after which he declared that they abstained because wine wastes wealth and reason.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r1.anchor: قال : قال عمر : اللهم بين لنا في الخمر . قنزلت فيهما اثم كبير ومنافع للناس

IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the statement about sin and benefits in this verse was abrogated by the final prohibition in 5:90.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r2.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني ، عن ابن غباس في قوله : يسئلونك عن الخمر والميسر قل فيهما اثم كبير ومنافع للناس فنسختها هذه الاية

IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r3.claim: Ibn Umar recounts three stages: this verse, then the ban on approaching prayer intoxicated, then the final prohibition, which the Prophet announced as making wine forbidden.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r3.anchor: عن المصري ، يعني : أبا طعمة قارىء مصر ، قال : سمعت ابن عمر يقول : نزلت في الخمر ثلاث آيات ، فأول شيء : يسئلونك عن الخمر والميسر الاية .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r4.claim: Umar says wine's prohibition concerned products of grapes, honey, dates, wheat, and barley, and defines wine as whatever overwhelms the intellect.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمر بن الخطاب ، قال : قام عمر على . فحمد الله واثنى عليه ، ثم قال : الا وان الخمر نزل تحريمها

IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r5.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r5.claim: Anas reports that people drank wine after the initial verse, then left it when the prohibition in al-Ma'ida was announced; their drink was date nabidh called fadikh.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p388#2/r5.anchor: عن انس بن مالك ، قال : كنا نشرب الخمر فانزلت : يسئلونك عن الخمر والميسر قل فيهما اثم كبير

IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab explains the name wine by saying its clear part rises while its dregs sink.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب ، قال : انما سميت الخمر لانها صفا صفوها وسفل كدرها .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r2.claim: Ibn Umar defines maysir as gambling.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r2.anchor: عن ابن عمر ، قال : الميسر : هو القمار .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r3.claim: Mujahid defines maysir as gambling and connects its name to the expression about staking or dividing a camel.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد 3 قوله : والميسر القمار - قال انما سمي الميسر لقولهم : ايسرو جزورا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود، ابن عباس، عطاء، طاووس، سعيد بن جبير، الحسن، ابن سيرين، قتادة، مقاتل، السدي، عطاء الخراساني
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r4.claim: Abu Muhammad reports these authorities as agreeing with Mujahid that maysir means gambling.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r4.anchor: قال أبو محمد : وروى عن عبد الله بن مسعود وابن عباس وعطاء وطاووس وسعيد بن جبير والحسن وابن سيرين وقتادة ومقاتل والسدي وعطاء الخراساني ، نحو ذلك .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r5.speaker: النبي، أبو موسى الأشعري
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r5.claim: The Prophet says to avoid marked dice used for casting lots, since they are maysir.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r5.anchor: عن أبي امامة ، عن أبي موسى الاشعري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : اجتنبوا هذا الكعاب المرسومة التي يزجر بها زجرا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود، علي، ابن عمر، عائشة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r6.claim: Ibn Masud calls dice non-Arab maysir and warns against them; Ali, Ibn Umar, and Aisha are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r6.anchor: عن أبي الاحوص ، عن عبد الله ، قال : اياكم وهذه الكعاب المومسات ، فانها ميسر العجم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r7.claim: Ali says chess is a form of maysir.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r7.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب ، انه كان يقول : الشطرنج من الميسر .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r8.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r8.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab says a form of pre-Islamic maysir was selling meat for one or two sheep.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r8.anchor: عن داود بن حصين انه سمع سعيد بن المسيب يقول : كان من ميسر اهل الجاهلية بيع اللحم بالشاة والشاتين ،

IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r9.speaker: القاسم بن محمد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r9.claim: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad says backgammon is maysir whenever it distracts from remembrance of God and prayer.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p390/r9.anchor: القاسم بن محمد ، عن النرد : اهي من الميسر ؟ قال : كل مالهى عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة فهو ميسر .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r1.speaker: الأعرج
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r1.claim: Al-Araj defines maysir as casting arrows for stakes of property and fruit.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r1.anchor: عن ابن شهاب ان الاعرج قال : الميسر : الضرب بالقداح على الاموال والثمار .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r2.claim: A report from the Prophet lists betting over pigeons, gambling, and throwing dice as three forms of maysir.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r2.anchor: عن يزيد بن شريح ، ان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، قال : ثلاث من الميسر : الصغير بالحمام ، والقمار ، والضرب بالكعاب .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says their great sin is the religious loss incurred by buying them.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قال قل فيهما اثم كبير يعني : فيما ينقص من الدين عند شريها .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r4.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr explains their sin as neglecting prayer and remembrance of God through wine and gambling.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، قال الله : فيهما اثم كبير لان في شرب الخمر والقمار ، ترك الصلاة ، وترك ذكر الله .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says the benefits of wine are the pleasure and joy people get from drinking it.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومنافع يقول : فيما يصيبون من لذتها وفرحها اذا شربوا .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r6.claim: Mujahid explains the benefits as the price of wine and the camel meat people obtained through gambling.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد 1 قوله : ومنفع للناس المنافع : ثمنها وما يصيبون من الجزور .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r7.speaker: ابن أبي زائدة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r7.claim: A transmission from Mujahid through Ibn Abi Zayda differs, identifying the benefit as wine's price before prohibition.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r7.anchor: قال أبو محمد : خالفه ابن أبي زائدة ، عن ورقاء ، عن ابن أبي نجيح ، عن مجاهد ، فقال : ثمنها قبل ان تحرم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r8.speaker: شبل، ابن جريج
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r8.claim: Shibl and Ibn Jurayj support the report that the benefits included what people obtained from the camel.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r8.anchor: وتابع شبل ، شبابة فقال : من الجزور . وكذلك قاله ابن جريج ، عن مجاهد .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r9.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the verse censured wine and gambling for their greater sin without yet forbidding them; Muslims then drank wine lawfully for its benefits.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p391/r9.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : ومنافع للناس يعني اكبر من نفعهما يعني : قبل التحريم ، فذمها ولم يحرمها

IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas distinguishes the benefits as belonging to the period before prohibition and the sins to the period after prohibition.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : ومنافع للناس ومنافعهما قبل التحريم واثمهما بعد ما حرمت .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says their sin outweighs their benefits because of the loss to religion, despite the pleasure and enjoyment people gain.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : واثمهما اكبر من نفعهما يقول : ما يذهب من الدين ، والاثم فيه ، اكبر مما يصبيون من فرحتها

IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r3.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r3.claim: Muqatil contrasts the greater sin after prohibition with the benefits they had before prohibition.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r3.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان ، قوله : واثمهما اكبر من نفعهما يقول : اثمهما اليوم بعد التحريم اكبر من منفعتهما قبل التحريم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r4.speaker: معاذ بن جبل، ثعلبة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r4.claim: A report says Muadh ibn Jabal and Tha'laba, concerned about their dependents, asked the Prophet what they should spend, occasioning the spending question in this verse.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r4.anchor: انه بلغه ان معاذ بن جبل ، وثعلبة اتيا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالا : يا رسول الله ان لنا ارقاء واهلين

IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r5.speaker: ابن عباس، عبد الله بن عمر، مجاهد، عطاء، الحسن، عكرمة، محمد بن كعب، قتادة، القاسم، سالم، سعيد بن جبير، عطاء الخراساني، الربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas explains al-afw as what remains after providing for one's family; many listed authorities are reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس : ويسئلونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو قال : ما يفضل عن اهلك

IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r6.speaker: طاوس عن مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r6.claim: A report through Mujahid from Tawus defines al-afw as the easy or readily available portion of everything.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r6.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح قوله ويسئلونك ماذا ينفقون قال : اليسر من كل شيء ، عن طاووس .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r7.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r7.claim: Al-Rabi explains al-afw as the good portion of one's wealth, its best and finest part.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p392/r7.anchor: عن الربيع ، قوله : ويسئلونك ماذا ينفقون ، قل العفو : يقول : الطيب منه ، يقول افضل مالك واطيبه .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p393/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p393/r1.speaker: مجاهد عن قيس المكي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p393/r1.claim: A report through Qays al-Makki says Mujahid defined al-afw as the obligatory charity.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p393/r1.anchor: قال : كان مجاهد 1 يقول : العفو الصدقة المفروضة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p393/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p393/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p393/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says al-afw is surplus wealth and that this instruction came before charity was prescribed.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p393/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قوله : ويسئلونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو يقول : مالا يتبين في اموالكم وكان هذا قبل ان تقرض الصدقة .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p393/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p393/r3.speaker: السدي، عطاء الخراساني، أبو محمد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p393/r3.claim: Al-Suddi interprets al-afw as surplus wealth and says the command was abrogated by zakat; Ata al-Khurasani is reported similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p393/r3.anchor: عن السدى ويسئلونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو يقول : الفضل هذا نسخته الزكاة . قال أبو محمد : وروى عن عطاء الخراساني ، نحو ذلك .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r1.claim: Ithm is disobedience through a corrupt act God does not approve; in legal usage it is a blameworthy act opposed to devotional obedience.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r1.anchor: ظاهر اصطلاح الشريعة أن الإثم هو الفعل المذموم في الشرع ، فهو ضد القربة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r2.speaker: الراغب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r2.claim: Al-Raghib suggests the derivation of ithm carries the sense of delay from good.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r2.anchor: وأشار الراغب إلى أن في اشتقاق الإثم معنى الإبطاء عن الخير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r3.claim: Ibn al-Arabi defines sin as blame attached to an act, effectively the opposite of reward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r3.anchor: وقال ابن العربي في تفسير سورة الأعراف : الإثم عبارة عن الذم الوارد في الفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r4.claim: Wine and gambling cause sin through drunken excess and disputes over gambling wins and losses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r4.anchor: فيكون معنى { فيهما إثم كبير } أنهما يتسبب منهما ما هو إثم في حال العربدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r5.claim: Kabir describes an immaterial sin metaphorically: it means exceptionally intense in its kind.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r5.anchor: وإطلاق الكبير على الإثم مجاز ، لأنه ليس من الأجسام ، فالمراد من الكبير : الشديد في نوعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r6.claim: The figurative container preposition fi emphasizes how closely sin and benefit attach to wine and gambling, in their customary use.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r6.anchor: وجيء بفي الدالة على الظرفية لإفادة شدة تعلق الإثم والمنفعة بهما ؛ لأن الظرفية أشد أنواع التعلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r7.claim: Calling the outcome ithm signals that users incur punishment in this world and the next.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r7.anchor: واختير التعبير بالإثم للدلالة على أنه يعود على متعاطي شربها بالعقوبة في الدنيا والآخرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r8.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r8.claim: Most readers have kabir, while Hamza and al-Kisa'i read kathir, using abundance figuratively for intensity of quality.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { إثم كبير } بموحدة بعد الكاف وقرأه حمزة والكسائي ( كثير ) بالثاء المثلثة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r9.claim: Manafiʿ may be a verbal noun whose form intensifies benefit, or a place noun denoting abundant benefit; either way it is stronger than nafʿ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r9.anchor: والمنافع : جمع منفعة ، وهي اسم على وزن مفعلة وأصله يحتمل أن يكون مصدرا ميميا قصد منه قوة النفع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r10.claim: Wine's harms include excess and brawling that breed enmity, divert from God's path and prayer, impair reason, invite ridicule, and waste wealth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r10.anchor: والإثم الذي في الخمر نشأ عما يترتب على شربها تارة من الإفراط فيه والعربدة من تشاجر يجر إلى البغضاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r11.speaker: عمارة بن الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r11.claim: Ibn Ashur introduces Amara ibn al-Walid's poem as evidence of money spent on wine.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p343/r11.anchor: وفي الإنفاق على الندامى حتى كانوا ربما رهنوا ثيابهم عند الخمارين قال عمارة بن الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r1.claim: The spending question accompanied the wine-and-gambling question, so its answer is joined by waw; banning them threatened aid to the poor, making proper spending relevant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r1.anchor: كان سؤالهم عن الخمر والميسر حاصلا مع سؤالهم { ماذا ينفقون } ، فعطفت الآية التي فيها جواب سؤالهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r2.speaker: ابن أبي حاتم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r2.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim reports that Muadh ibn Jabal and Thaʿlaba ibn Ghanima asked what should be spent.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r2.anchor: روى ابن أبي حاتم أن السائل عن هذا معاذ ابن جبل وثعلبة بن غنمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r3.claim: Another view identifies Amr ibn al-Jamuh as questioner, answered in 2:215 and here, with each answer suited to context.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r3.anchor: وقيل هو رجوع إلى الجواب عن سؤال عمرو بن الجموح الذي قيل إنه المجاب عنه بقوله تعالى : { يسألونك ماذا ينفقون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r4.claim: The waw also answers the expectation that banning wine and gambling would remove aid to the poor by directing people to legitimate giving.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r4.anchor: ولإظهار ما يدفع توقعهم تعطيل نفع المحاويج وصلت هذه الآية بالتي قبلها بواو العطف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r5.claim: Al-afw is surplus after usual personal and family expenses; the verse directs people to give from that margin instead of committing sins to support the needy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r5.anchor: والعفو : مصدر عفا يعفو إذا زاد ونمى قال تعالى : { ثم بدلنا مكان السيئة الحسنة حتى عفوا } ( الأعراف : 95 )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r6.claim: Spending surplus supports weak Muslims continuously and evenly without hardship, making this a wise social and economic principle.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r6.anchor: لأن مقصد الشريعة من الإنفاق إقامة مصالح ضعفاء المسلمين ولا يحصل منه مقدار له بال إلا بتعميمه ودوامه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r7.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r7.claim: A prophetic report calls the best charity that given from sufficiency and says to begin with those one supports.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r7.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( خير الصدقة ما كان عن ظهر غنى وابدأ بمن تعول ) فإن البداءة بمن يعول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r8.claim: Supporting dependents prevents them from needing the poor's resources and reduces the number dependent on charity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r8.anchor: لأنه إن تركهم في خصاصة احتاجوا إلى الأخذ من أموال الفقراء ، وفي الحديث :

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r9.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r9.claim: A prophetic report says leaving heirs wealthy is better than leaving them dependent and begging.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r9.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( إنك أن تدع ورثتك أغنياء خير من أن تدعهم عالة يتكففون الناس )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r10.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r10.claim: A prophetic report promises reward for spending to please God, even a bite placed in one's wife's mouth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r10.anchor: ولذلك جاء في الحديث : ( وإنك لا تنفق نفقة تبتغي بها وجه الله إلا أجرت عليها حتى اللقمة تجعلها في في امرأتك )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r11.claim: Giving from surplus does not preclude giving needed or all one's wealth if one can bear it patiently and has no dependent to support.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p351/r11.anchor: فلا تنافي أن ينفق أحد من ماله المحتاج هو إليه أو جميع ماله إذا صبر على ذلك ولم يكن له من تجب عليه هو نفقته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r1.claim: The definite article marks familiar generic surplus, which varies with each person's needs; calling all of it spendable encourages giving.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r1.anchor: وآل في العفو للجنس المعروف للسامعين ، والعفو مقول عليه بالتشكيك ؛ لأنه يتبع تعيين ما يحتاجه المنفق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r2.claim: This supports voluntary spending: consensus and the wider law require obligatory maintenance and zakat, which may be drawn from surplus wealth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r2.anchor: وهذا دليل على أن المراد من الإنفاق هنا الإنفاق المتطوع به ، إذ قد تضافرت أدلة الشريعة وانعقد إجماع العلماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r3.speaker: أبو ذر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r3.claim: Abu Dharr held hoarding wealth forbidden and preached this in Syria; Muawiya complained to Uthman, who recalled him to Medina and settled him at al-Rabadha at his request to avert discord.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r3.anchor: إلا ما شذ به أبو ذر ، إذ كان يرى كنز المال حراما وينادي به في الشام فشكاه معاوية لعثمان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r4.speaker: قيس بن سعد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r4.claim: Qays ibn Saʿd says the verse concerns obligatory zakat; al- then refers to externally defined growth at the zakat threshold.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r4.anchor: وعن قيس بن سعد أن هذه الآية في الزكاة المفروضة ، وعلى قوله يكون ( أل ) في العفو للعهد الخارجي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r5.claim: The majority read al-afw accusative as object of an understood verb, treating dha after interrogative ma as canceled and ma as yunfiqun's fronted object.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور ( قل العفو ) بنصب العفو على تقدير كونه مفعولا لفعل دل عليه { ماذا ينفقون }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r6.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir in one transmission, Abu Amr, and Yaqub read al-afw nominative as predicate of huwa, taking dha as a relative and matching the answer's case to its construction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير في إحدى روايتين عنه وأبو عمرو ويعقوب بالرفع على أنه خبر مبتدأ تقديره هو العفو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r1.claim: Kadhālika means clarification in this manner, with the demonstrative specifying how God clarifies; Ibn Ashur recalls 2:143.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r1.anchor: أي كذلك البيان يبين الله لكم الآيات ، فالكاف للتشبيه واقعة موقع المفعول المطلق المبين لنوع { يبين }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the demonstrative points to the preceding explanation; its distant form magnifies disclosure of rulings, causes, and a spending principle suited to everyone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r2.anchor: أو الإشارة راجعة إلى البيان الواقع في قوله تعالى : { قل فيهما إثم كبير } إلى قوله { العفو }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r3.claim: The demonstrative is not directly addressed to the plural, so it stays kadhālika rather than expected kadhālikum; its distance is abstract and honorific.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r3.anchor: ولكون الكاف لم يقصد بها الخطاب بل مجرد البعد الاعتباري للتعظيم لم يؤت بها على مقتضى الظاهر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r4.claim: The lām expresses favor and distinction: this lucid teaching lets the community receive duties knowingly and its scholars legislate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r4.anchor: واللام في { لكم } للتعليل والأجل وهو امتنان وتشريف بهذه الفضيلة لإشعاره بأن البيان على هذا الأسلوب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r7.claim: Ali answers a man disparaging worldly life by describing it as truthful, saving, enriching for those who use it well, and a place of revelation and worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r7.anchor: ووقع في كلام لعلي بن أبي طالب وقد ذم رجل الدنيا عنده فقال له : ( الدنيا دار صدق لمن صدقها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r8.claim: The matter fit for reflection is the rule on wine and gambling linked to its causes, followed by the related spending instruction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p352#2/r8.anchor: ولا يخفى أن الذي يصلح للتفكر هو الحكم المنوط بالعلة وهو حكم الخمر والميسر ثم ما نشأ عنه قوله : { ويسئلونك ماذا ينفقون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r1.speaker: المؤمنون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r1.claim: The people asking about wine and gambling are believers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى يسئلونك عن الخمر والميسر الآية، السائلون هم المؤمنون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r2.claim: “الخمر” derives from “خمر,” to cover; the Prophet's “خمّروا الإناء” and a woman's “خمار” illustrate the root.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r2.anchor: والخمر مأخوذة من خمر إذا ستر، ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «خمروا الإناء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r3.claim: The word applies to what hides or shades a person, as in a poet's reference to a concealed hollow by the road.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r3.anchor: والخمر ما واراك من شجر وغيره، ومنه قول الشاعر: ألا يا زيد والضحاك سيرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r4.claim: Al-Ajjaj uses “الخمر” for a hidden army; other Arabic usage calls a concealed place “غمار الناس وخمارهم.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r4.anchor: ومنه قول العجاج: في لامع العقبان لا يمشي الخمر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r5.claim: Wine is named for covering and clouding the intellect.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r5.anchor: فلما كانت الخمر تستر العقل وتغطي عليه سميت بذلك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r6.claim: Strictly, wine is fermented grape juice uncooked or insufficiently cooked; other things that cloud reason are treated like it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r6.anchor: والخمر ماء العنب الذي غلي ولم يطبخ أو طبخ طبخا لم يكف غليانه، وما خامر العقل من غير ذلك فهو في حكمه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r7.claim: Abu Hanifa says wine can also be made from grains.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r7.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة: قد تكون الخمر من الحبوب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r8.speaker: ابن سيده
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r8.claim: Ibn Sida suspects the grain definition is a slip, since wine in its proper sense is grape juice alone.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r8.anchor: قال ابن سيده: وأظنه تسفحا منه، لأن حقيقة الخمر إنما هي ماء العنب دون سائر الأشياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r9.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r9.claim: A report from the Prophet says wine comes from grapevine and date palm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r9.anchor: وروي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «الخمر من هاتين الشجرتين: العنب والنخلة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r10.claim: Prohibited wine in Medina was made from honey, raisins, dates, barley, and wheat; there was no grape wine there.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r10.anchor: وحرمت الخمر بالمدينة يوم حرمت وهي من العسل والزبيب والتمر والشعير والقمح، ولم تكن عندهم خمر عنب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r11.claim: The community agrees fermented grape wine that froths is forbidden in all amounts, and the hadd applies to small and large amounts.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r11.anchor: وأجمعت الأمة على خمر العنب إذا غلت ورمت بالزبد أنها حرام قليلها وكثيرها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r12.speaker: جمهور الأمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r12.claim: Most jurists forbid any amount of another drink if a larger amount intoxicates, and require the hadd for it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r12.anchor: وجمهور الأمة على أن ما أسكر كثيره من غير خمر العنب فمحرم قليله وكثيره.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r13.speaker: أبو حنيفة وسفيان الثوري وابن أبي ليلى وابن شبرمة وجماعة من فقهاء الكوفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r13.claim: They allow a non-grape drink in a non-intoxicating amount even if much intoxicates; a person drunk without intending to reach drunkenness incurs no hadd.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r13.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وسفيان الثوري وابن أبي ليلى وابن شبرمة وجماعة من فقهاء الكوفة: ما أسكر كثيره من غير خمر العنب، فما لا يسكر منه حلال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r14.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls the Kufan position weak, saying reason and Abu Bakr, Umar, and the Companions oppose it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r14.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا قول ضعيف يرده النظر، وأبو بكر الصديق وعمر الفاروق والصحابة على خلافه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r15.speaker: النبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r15.claim: A Prophetic report says every intoxicant is wine and forbidden; what intoxicates in a large amount is forbidden in a small amount.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r15.anchor: وروي أن النبي عليه السلام قال: «كل مسكر خمر، وكل خمر حرام، وما أسكر كثيره فقليله حرام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r16.speaker: ابن المنذر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r16.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says the report leaves no argument or defense for a contrary position.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r16.anchor: قال ابن المنذر في الإشراف: «لم يبق هذا الخبر مقالة لقائل ولا حجة لمحتج

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r17.claim: Ibn Atiyya calls this verse the first step toward prohibiting wine, followed by 4:43's ban on approaching prayer while intoxicated.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p292/r17.anchor: وروي أن هذه الآية أول تطرق إلى تحريم الخمر، ثم بعده لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya places the verse in the staged prohibition of wine, citing the later commands to avoid it and the Prophet’s declaration that it was forbidden.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r1.anchor: إنما الخمر والميسر والأنصاب والأزلام رجس من عمل الشيطان فاجتنبوه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r2.claim: The Prophet declared wine forbidden; Ibn ʿAṭiyya gives no grading for this report.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «حرمت الخمر»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r3.claim: The only preserved Prophetic practice on the wine penalty is forty lashes, reported by Muslim and Abū Dāwūd.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r3.anchor: ولم يحفظ عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في حد الخمر إلا أنه جلد أربعين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r4.claim: Another report says the Prophet administered an unspecified general beating; Abū Bakr estimated it at forty, followed by Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r4.anchor: وروي عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه ضرب فيها ضربا مشاعا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r5.claim: As drinking spread, ʿUmar raised the penalty to eighty as the lightest fixed penalty; Mālik agreed, while al-Shāfiʿī held to forty.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r5.anchor: ثم تهافت الناس فيها فشدد عليهم الحد وجعله كأخف الحدود ثمانين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r6.speaker: جماعة من العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r6.claim: A group of scholars required a non-severe beating, such that the striker’s armpit would not show.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r6.anchor: وضرب الخمر غير شديد عند جماعة من العلماء لا يبدو إبط الضارب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r7.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r7.claim: Mālik says every flogging should use the same force, without easing it or striking excessively.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r7.anchor: وقال مالك: «الضرب كله سواء لا يخفف ولا يبرح»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r8.claim: There is consensus to avoid striking the face, genitals, heart, brain, and flanks of the person flogged.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r8.anchor: ويجتنب من المضروب الوجه والفرج والقلب والدماغ والخواصر بإجماع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r9.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r9.claim: Some say the verse’s apparent allowance in mentioning benefits was abrogated by the command to avoid wine and gambling.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r9.anchor: وقالت طائفة: هذه الآية منسوخة بقوله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r10.claim: Maysir derives from y-s-r in the sense of slaughtering; yāsir means the slaughterer, and the camel subject to the draw was called maysir, then the arrows by association.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r10.anchor: والميسر مأخوذ من يسر إذا جزر،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r11.claim: Two cited poetic lines use y-s-r language for the slaughter-and-lottery practice, supporting the derivation from slaughter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r11.anchor: فلم يزل بك واشيهم ومكرهم ... حتى أشاطوا بغيب لحم من يسروا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r12.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r12.claim: Al-Ṭabarī derives maysir from “this became due or available to me” and attributes that etymology to Mujāhid; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says Mujāhid’s quoted words instead mean slaughter.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r12.anchor: وقال الطبري: «الميسر مأخوذ من يسر لي هذا إذا وجب وتسنى»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r13.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r13.claim: Mujāhid’s intended sense was slaughter; a yāsir is someone who participates in drawing lots, plural aysār (also described as yusr).
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r13.anchor: بل أراد مجاهد الجزر، واليسر: الذي يدخل في الضرب بالقداح

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r14.claim: The lottery used seven arrows with assigned shares and three blanks without shares: al-fadhdh, al-tawʾam, al-raqīb, al-ḥils, al-nāfis, al-musbil, al-muʿallā; al-manīḥ, al-safīḥ, and al-waghd were blanks.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r14.anchor: وسهام الميسر سبعة لها حظوظ وفيها فروض على عدة الحظوظ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r15.claim: The three blank arrows were added to multiply and mix the lots so the person drawing them could not favor anyone.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r15.anchor: والثلاثة التي لا حظوظ لها المنيح والسفيح والوغد، تزاد هذه الثلاثة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r16.claim: Arabs used this practice in winter scarcity and severe cold: participants guaranteed the camel’s price, slaughtered it, and divided it into ten portions; al-Aṣmaʿī’s claim of twenty-eight portions is mistaken.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r16.anchor: وكانت عادة العرب أن تضرب بهذه القداح في الشتوة وضيق الوقت وكلب البرد على الفقراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r17.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r17.claim: A winning arrow took its allotted shares for the poor; sometimes participants gambled for themselves, and those who lost paid the price. The practice sustained the neighborhood’s poor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293/r17.anchor: فمن فاز سهمه بأن يخرج من الربابة متقدما أخذ أنصباءه وأعطاها الفقراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r1.speaker: الأعشى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r1.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s verse praises the lottery’s provision of food to guests and the poor in winter, illustrating its social benefit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r1.anchor: المطعمو الضيف إذا ما شتا ... والجاعلو القوت على الياسر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r2.claim: These customs were benefits of maysir, but the practice still consumed wealth unlawfully.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r2.anchor: فهذا كله هو نفع الميسر، إلا أنه أكل المال بالباطل،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن سيرين والحسن وابن عباس وابن المسيب وغيرهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r3.claim: They classify every form of gambling as maysir, including dice, chess, and even children’s nut games.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r3.anchor: وقال محمد بن سيرين والحسن وابن عباس وابن المسيب وغيرهم: كل قمار ميسر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r4.claim: In a cited poem, al-manīḥ is a borrowed, smooth arrow that had won often; this favorable loan-arrow differs from the blank manīḥ, which is praised for its turning back.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r4.anchor: والمنيح في هذا البيت المستمنح، لأنهم كانوا يستعيرون السهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r5.speaker: جرير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r5.claim: Jarīr’s line uses al-manīḥ for the blank arrow, described as one that turns back, rather than the lucky borrowed arrow.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r5.anchor: وإياه أراد جرير بقوله: [الكامل] ولقد عطفن على فزارة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r6.speaker: لبيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r6.claim: Labīd’s line says the lottery need not produce shameful acts, another poetic illustration of the practice’s benefits before the Qurʾānic judgment of its sin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r6.anchor: ومن الميسر قول لبيد: [الطويل] إذا يسروا لم يورث اليسر بينهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والربيع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Rabīʿ say the sin concerns wine and gambling after prohibition, while their benefits belonged to the earlier period.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس والربيع: الإثم فيهما بعد التحريم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r8.speaker: طائفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r8.claim: One group locates wine’s sin in loss of reason, abuse, slander, harm, and transgression by drinkers, and its benefit in pleasure.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r8.anchor: وقالت طائفة: الإثم في الخمر ذهاب العقل والسباب والافتراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r9.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r9.claim: Ḥassān b. Thābit’s poem depicts wine as making drinkers feel like kings and fearless lions, illustrating the pleasure claimed as its benefit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r9.anchor: كما قال حسان بن ثابت: ونشربها فتتركنا ملوكا ... وأسدا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r10.claim: Mujāhid identifies the benefit of wine as the money earned from its sale.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r11.claim: God says the sin outweighs the benefit and brings greater harm in the afterlife; Ibn ʿAṭiyya reads this comparison as a prelude to prohibition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r11.anchor: ثم أعلم الله عز وجل أن الإثم أكبر من النفع وأعود بالضرر في الآخرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r12.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r12.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read kathīr (“many”); the Prophet’s curse on wine and ten connected roles supports many sins, as does pairing plural benefits with plural sins.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r13.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r13.claim: A report says the Prophet cursed wine and ten associated people: its seller, buyer, purchaser for another, pressers, those for whom it is pressed, server, drinker, carrier, recipient, and one who consumes its price; Ibn ʿAṭiyya gives no grading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r13.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعن الخمر ولعن معها عشرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r14.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r14.claim: Most readers use kabīr (“great”), fitting wine and gambling as major sins and the following akbar (“greater”); they reject akthar except in Ibn Masʿūd’s codex, which has kathīr in both places.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r14.anchor: وقرأ باقي القراء وجمهور الناس «كبير» بالباء بواحدة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r15.claim: The codex attributed to Ibn Masʿūd reads kathīr (“many”) at both occurrences, unlike the mainstream agreement on akbar and rejection of akthar.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r15.anchor: إلا ما في مصحف ابن مسعود فإن فيه «قل فيهما إثم كثير وإثمهما أكثر»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r16.claim: “In them is sin” may mean sin in using wine and gambling after the prohibition, or the evil qualities inherent in them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r16.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فيهما إثم يحتمل مقصدين، أحدهما أن يراد في استعمالهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r17.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r17.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr recounts a staged response: after this verse some abstained for sin while others drank for benefit; 4:43 restricted drinking around prayers, then 5:90 commanded avoidance and the Prophet declared wine forbidden.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p293#2/r17.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: لما نزلت قل فيهما إثم كبير ومنافع للناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r1.claim: When 5:91 asked whether they would desist, ʿUmar answered that they had desisted; Ibn ʿAṭiyya uses this as the final step in the prohibition sequence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r1.anchor: ولما سمع عمر بن الخطاب قوله تعالى: فهل أنتم منتهون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r2.speaker: بعض أهل النظر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r2.claim: Some speculative scholars infer that this verse itself prohibited wine: 7:33 forbids sin, and this verse says wine contains sin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r2.anchor: وقال بعض أهل النظر: حرمت الخمر بهذه الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects that inference: the sin found in wine is what is forbidden, not wine itself as that argument requires.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r3.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق رضي الله عنه: ليس هذا النظر بجيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r4.claim: Qatāda says the verse censured wine but did not prohibit it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة: ذم الله الخمر بهذه الآية ولم يحرمها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r5.speaker: قيس بن سعد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r5.claim: Qays b. Saʿd interprets “the surplus” to be the obligatory alms tax.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r5.anchor: قال قيس بن سعد: «هذه الزكاة المفروضة»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r6.speaker: جمهور العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r6.claim: Most scholars interpret the spending requested here as voluntary expenditure.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r6.anchor: وقال جمهور العلماء: بل هي نفقات التطوع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r7.speaker: بعضهم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r7.claim: Some say the command to spend the surplus was abrogated by the later zakat obligation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r8.speaker: آخرون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r8.claim: Others hold the verse remains in force and establishes a claim on wealth beyond zakat.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r8.anchor: وقال آخرون: هي محكمة وفي المال حق سوى الزكاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r9.claim: Al-ʿafw is what one can give without exhausting oneself or one’s assets: spend what remains after needs, without making oneself dependent; the term derives from abundance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r9.anchor: والعفو: هو ما ينفقه المرء دون أن يجهد نفسه وماله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r10.claim: A Prophetic report directs a person with surplus to spend first on self, then dependents, then charity if anything remains; no grading is stated.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r10.anchor: روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: قال: «من كان له فضل فلينفقه على نفسه، ثم على من يعول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r11.claim: Two Prophetic reports commend charity that leaves the giver financially secure, described as giving from sufficiency; Ibn ʿAṭiyya gives no grading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r11.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم: «خير الصدقة ما أبقت غنى» ، وفي حديث آخر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r12.speaker: جمهور الناس وأبو عمرو
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r12.claim: Most readers put al-ʿafw in the accusative; Abū ʿAmr alone raises it, and Ibn Kathīr’s reading is reported as differing.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r12.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «العفو» بالنصب، وقرأ أبو عمرو وحده «العفو» بالرفع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r13.claim: If mā is a subject and dhā its relative predicate, al-ʿafw is nominative; if mādhā is one object of “spend,” al-ʿafw is accusative after an implied verb. The mixed case pairings are possible but weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r13.anchor: فمن جعل «ما» ابتداء و «ذا» خبره بمعنى الذي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r14.claim: “Thus God makes the signs clear” refers to the preceding discussions of wine, gambling, and spending; the signs guide believers to reflect on worldly and afterlife matters as a path to salvation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r14.anchor: الإشارة إلى ما تقدم تبيينه من أمر الخمر والميسر والإنفاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r15.speaker: مكي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r15.claim: Makkī reads “in this world and the next” as modifying “the signs,” while the familiar interpretation associated with Ibn ʿAbbās attaches it to “reflect.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p294/r15.anchor: وقال مكي: «معنى الآية أنه يبين للمؤمنين آيات في الدنيا والآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r1.claim: One occasion report says ʿUmar asked God to give a decisive clarification about wine, after which this verse was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r1.anchor: في سبب نزولها قولان أحدهما أن عمر بن الخطاب قال اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا فنزلت هذه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r2.speaker: الأنصار وعمر ومعاذ
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r2.claim: Another occasion report says a group of Anṣār, including ʿUmar and Muʿādh, asked the Prophet for a ruling because wine removes reason and takes away wealth; this verse was revealed.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r2.anchor: والثاني أن جماعة من الانصار جاؤوا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفيهم عمر ومعاذ فقالوا أفتنا في الخمر فإنها مذهبة للعقل مسلبة للمال فنزلت هذه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن القاسم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r3.claim: Three etymologies are reported: wine is called khamr because it mixes with the intellect, covers it, or veils it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r3.anchor: وفي تسمية الخمر خمرا ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أنها سميت خمرا لأنها تخامر العقل أي تخالطه والثاني لأنها تخمر العقل أي تستره

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says khamr is what covers the intellect; khimār can mean a crowd in which one is hidden, and a woman’s head covering is named for covering.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r4.anchor: وقال الزجاج الخمر في اللغة ما ستر على العقل يقال دخل فلان في خمار الناس أي في الكثير الذي يستتر فيهم وخمار المرأة قناعها سمي خمارا لأنه يغطي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r5.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the named wine is the agreed-upon kind, and by analogy every drink that acts like it shares its prohibition.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r5.anchor: أن يقال له خمر و أن يكون في التحريم بمنزلتها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r6.claim: Scholars agree all gambling is forbidden; the verse names maysir as an example, though strictly maysir applies to gambling over camels.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r6.anchor: لأن العلماء أجمعوا على أن القمار كله حرام وإنما ذكر الميسر من بينه وجعل كله قياسا على الميسر والميسر إنما يكون قمارا في الجزر خاصة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عمر والحسن وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn ʿUmar, al-Hasan, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, Qatāda, and others define maysir as gambling.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r8.claim: Ibn Qutayba derives the word from yāsara, drawing lots with arrows; the person who draws is called yāsir, yāsirūn, yusr, or aysār.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r8.anchor: للضارب بالقداح ياسر و ياسرون ويسر وأيسار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r9.claim: In winter hardship, wealthy men slaughtered a camel and divided it into shares by drawing arrows; winners gave shares to the needy, the benefit named in the verse, and people praised participation and condemned refusal.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p239#2/r9.anchor: وكان أصحاب الثروة والأجواد في الشتاء عند شدة الزمان وكلبه ينحرون جزورا ويجزئونها أجزاء ثم يضربون عليها القداح فاذا قمر القامر جعل ذلك لذوي الحاجة والمسكنة وهو النفع الذي ذكره الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r1.claim: Most reciters read kabīr with bāʾ; Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read kathīr with thāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r1.anchor: قرأ الأكثرون كبير بالباء وقرأ حمزة والكسائي بالثاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r2.claim: One account says wine's sin is that drinking it diminishes one's religion.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r2.anchor: أحدها أن شربها ينقص الدين قاله ابن عباس والثاني

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r3.speaker: السدي عن أشياخه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r3.claim: Another account says drinkers become intoxicated and harm people.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r3.anchor: والثاني أنه إذا شرب سكر وآذى الناس رواه السدي عن أشياخه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r4.claim: Wine's sin includes enmity, hatred, and covering the faculty of reason that enables discrimination.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r4.anchor: و الثالث أنه وقوع العداوة والبغضاء وتغطية العقل الذي يقع به التمييز قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r5.claim: Gambling distracts from remembering God and prayer and causes enmity.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r5.anchor: أحدهما أنه يشغل عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة ويوقع العداوة قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r6.speaker: السدي عن أشياخه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r6.claim: Another view is that gambling invites injustice and withholding what is due.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r6.anchor: والثاني أنه يدعوا إلى الظلم ومنع الحق رواه السدي عن أشياخه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r7.claim: The different harms mentioned for wine and gambling may all be intended together.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r8.claim: Wine benefits people through profit from its sale and bodily enjoyment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r8.anchor: وأما منافع الخمر فمن وجهين أحدهما الربح في بيعها والثاني انتفاع الأبدان مع التذاذ النفوس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r9.claim: Gambling's benefit is that a person can acquire money without effort.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r9.anchor: وأما منافع الميسر فاصابة الرجل المال من غير تعب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير، الضحاك، مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r10.claim: One reading compares post-prohibition sin with pre-prohibition benefit.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r10.anchor: قاله سعيد بن جبير و الضحاك و مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r11.speaker: ابن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r11.claim: Another reading compares sin and benefit before prohibition: the sins arising from their causes already outweighed their benefits.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r11.anchor: والثاني وإثمهما قبل التحريم أكبر من نفعهما قبل التحريم أيضا لأن الإثم الذي يحدث في أسبابها أكبر من نفعهما وهذا منقول عن ابن جبير أيضا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r12.speaker: ابن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r12.claim: Ibn Jubayr says wine had been permitted under the verse about drink made from date palms and grapes.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r12.anchor: النحل 67 قاله ابن جبير والثاني بالشريعة الاولى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r13.claim: Another account says wine was permitted by the earlier divine law and Muslims remained under that rule until prohibition.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r13.anchor: والثاني بالشريعة الأولى وأقر المسلمون على ذلك حتى حرمت

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r14.speaker: السدي عن أشياخه، سعيد بن جبير، مجاهد، قتادة، مقاتل
