IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r14.claim: One position says the verse censures wine without prohibiting it, so this verse was abrogated.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r14.anchor: رواه السدي عن أشياخه وبه قال سعيد بن جبير و مجاهد وقتادة و مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r15.speaker: جماعة من العلماء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r15.claim: Another position finds a prohibition here because sin is forbidden by 7:33; al-Zajjāj transmits this view and Qāḍī Abū Yaʿlā prefers it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r15.anchor: هذا قول جماعة من العلماء وحكاه الزجاج واختاره القاضي أبو يعلى للعلة التي بيناها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r16.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r16.claim: They argue that the first clause balances sin with benefit, but saying sin is greater makes sin dominant and its benefit negligible by comparison, so the prohibitive side prevails.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p240/r16.anchor: واحتج لصحته بعض أهل المعاني فقال لما قال الله تعالى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r1.claim: Gambling follows the same disagreement as wine; if this verse prohibits wine, it prohibits gambling too, while on the disapproval reading al-Māʾida explicitly prohibits gambling.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r1.anchor: فأقوم الاقوال أن نقول إن الآية التي في المائدة نصت على تحريم الميسر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the person who asked what to spend as ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس إن الذي سأله عن ذلك عمرو ابن الجموح

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r3.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r3.claim: Here spending means charitable giving and a donation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r3.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة والمراد بالنفقة هاهنا الصدقة والعطاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads al-ʿafw in the nominative; the other reciters read it in the accusative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r4.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو برفع واو العفو وقرأ الباقون بنصبها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r5.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r5.claim: The accusative treats mādhā as accusative and al-ʿafw as its answer, as in answering “What did you spend?” with “a dirham.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r5.anchor: ماذا في موضع نصب فجوابه العفو بالنصب كما تقول في جواب ماذا أنفقت أي أنفقت درهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r6.claim: The nominative treats dhā as a relative pronoun rather than treating mādhā as one word; the answer then supplies what God sent down.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r6.anchor: ومن رفع جعل ذا بمنزلة الذي ولم يجعل ماذا اسما واحدا فإذا قال قائل ماذا أنزل ربكم فكأنه قال ما الذي أنزل ربكم فجوابه قرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r7.claim: Al-ʿafw can mean abundance or surplus; its root usage includes something that has grown, and it can mean what comes without effort.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج العفو في اللغة الكثرة والفضل يقال قد عفا القم إذا كثروا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r8.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r8.claim: Al-ʿafw means what is readily available, obtained easily without coercion or hardship.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r8.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة العفو الميسور يقال خذ ما عفاك أي ما أتاك سهلا بلا إكراه ولا مشقة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r9.speaker: مقسم عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r9.claim: One interpretation is what remains after a person and their dependents have what they need.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r9.anchor: أحدها أنه ما يفضل عن حاجة المرء وعياله رواه مقسم عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r10.speaker: عطية عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r10.claim: Another interpretation is whatever amount people willingly give, whether little or much.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r10.anchor: والثاني ما تطيب به أنفسهم من قليل وكثير رواه عطية عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r11.speaker: الحسن، عطاء، سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r11.claim: A third interpretation is a moderate amount between extravagance and stinginess.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r11.anchor: والثالث أنه القصد بين الإسراف والإقتار قاله الحسن وعطاء وسعيد بن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r12.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r12.claim: Mujāhid interprets al-ʿafw as the obligatory charity.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r12.anchor: والرابع أنه الصدقة المفروضة قاله مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r13.speaker: طائفة من المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r13.claim: A fifth interpretation is property whose amount is not apparent, drawing on the phrase for a trace that has vanished.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r13.anchor: والخامس أنه مالا يتبين عليهم مقداره من قولهم عفا الأثر إذا خفي ودرس حكاه شيخنا عن طائفة من المفسرين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r14.speaker: السدي عن أشياخه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r14.claim: Al-Suddī's authorities say the spending command was abrogated by the zakat obligation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r14.anchor: فروى السدي عن أشياخه أنها نسخت بالزكاة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r15.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r15.claim: Others deny abrogation; the author distinguishes the rulings by the interpretation: a required surplus or pre-zakat charity was abrogated, while zakat itself or recommended charity remains operative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p242/r15.anchor: فروى السدي عن أشياخه أنها نسخت بالزكاة وأبي نسخها آخرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r1.claim: Although the address is plural, al-Zajjāj says the collective means a group or community, as if addressed as a tribe.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج إنما قال كذلك وهو يخاطب جماعة لأن الجماعة معناها القبيل كأنه قال كذلك يا أيها القبيل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r2.claim: Alternatively, the k-prefix may address the Prophet, whose address includes his community.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r2.anchor: وجائز أن تكون الكفا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كأنه قال كذلك يا أيها النبي لأن الخطاب له مشتمل على خطاب أمته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r3.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r3.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says “thus” points back to the explanation of spending: in the same way, God makes the signs clear.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r3.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري الكاف في كذلك إشارة إلى ما بين من الإنفاق فكأنه قال مثل ذلك الذي بينه لكم في الإنفاق يبين الآيات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r4.claim: Alternatively, “thus” need not point back to the preceding material and simply means “in this way.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون كذلك غير إشارة إلى ما قبله فيكون معناه هكذا قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r5.claim: Reflecting on this world and the next lets people recognize their difference and act for the one that lasts.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p243/r5.anchor: فتعرفون فضل ما بينهما فتعملون للباقي منهما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p578/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p578/r1.speaker: عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p578/r1.claim: In a report from ʿUmar, he repeatedly asks God for a clear ruling on wine: first this verse is revealed, then 4:43 bars approaching prayer while drunk, and finally 5:90–91 commands abstention, to which ʿUmar replies that they desist.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p578/r1.anchor: عن عمر أنه قال: لما نزل تحريم الخمر قال: اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p578/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p578/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p578/r2.claim: The report is transmitted by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and al-Nasa’i through Israel from Abu Ishaq, and by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh through al-Thawri; Abu Zurʿa says Abu Maysara did not hear from ʿUmar, while Ibn al-Madini calls the chain sound and al-Tirmidhi authenticates it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p578/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p578/r3.speaker: ابن أبي حاتم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p578/r3.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim adds ʿUmar’s explanation that wine makes wealth and reason disappear.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p578/r3.anchor: وزاد ابن أبي حاتم -بعد قوله: انتهينا -: إنها تذهب المال وتذهب العقل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p578/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p578/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p578/r4.claim: ʿUmar defines wine as anything that clouds the intellect; Ibn Kathir says the definition will be explained further in the commentary on al-Ma’ida.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r1.claim: Wine’s sins concern religion, while its benefits are worldly: bodily benefit, digestion, elimination, sharpening some minds, and the pleasure of intoxication; gambling winnings could also support a person or family.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r1.anchor: أما إثمهما فهو في الدين، وأما المنافع فدنيوية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r2.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r2.claim: Hassan ibn Thabit’s pre-Islamic verse depicts drinkers as becoming kings and lions undeterred by battle, illustrating wine’s intoxicating pleasure.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r2.anchor: ونشربها فتتركنا ملوكا … وأسدا لا ينهنهها اللقاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r3.claim: Other worldly gains included selling wine and spending its price, or using gambling proceeds for oneself or one’s family.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r3.anchor: وكذا بيعها والانتفاع بثمنها. وما كان يقمشه بعضهم من الميسر فينفقه على نفسه أو عياله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r4.claim: Those benefits do not outweigh the greater harm to intellect and religion; the verse prepares for wine’s categorical prohibition by implication, before 5:90–91 states it explicitly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r4.anchor: ولهذا كانت هذه الآية ممهدة لتحريم الخمر على البتات، ولم تكن مصرحة بل معرضة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r5.speaker: ابن عمر، والشعبي، ومجاهد، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس، وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r5.claim: These authorities say this was the first verse revealed about wine; the verse in al-Nisa’ followed, then the verses in al-Ma’ida, which made wine unlawful.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579/r5.anchor: قال ابن عمر، والشعبي، ومجاهد، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس، وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r1.claim: The word al-afw is read in both the accusative and nominative; Ibn Kathir regards both readings as sound, apt, and close in meaning.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {ويسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} قرئ بالنصب وبالرفع (6) وكلاهما حسن متجه قريب.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r2.speaker: معاذ بن جبل وثعلبة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r2.claim: A report reaching Yahya says Muadh and Thaʿlaba asked how much to spend given their dependents and servants, and this question occasioned the verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r2.anchor: أن معاذ بن جبل وثعلبة أتيا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالا يا رسول الله، إن لنا أرقاء وأهلين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains al-afw as what remains in excess of what one's household needs.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r3.anchor: وقال الحكم، عن مقسم، عن ابن عباس: {ويسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} قال: ما يفضل عن أهلك.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r4.speaker: ابن عمر، ومجاهد، وعطاء، وعكرمة، وسعيد بن جبير، ومحمد بن كعب، والحسن، وقتادة، والقاسم، وسالم، وعطاء الخراساني، والربيع بن أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r4.claim: These early authorities also explain al-afw as the surplus, a sense Ibn Kathir says gathers the reported definitions.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r4.anchor: وكذا روي عن ابن عمر، ومجاهد، وعطاء، وعكرمة، وسعيد بن جبير، ومحمد بن كعب، والحسن، وقتادة، والقاسم، وسالم، وعطاء الخراساني، والربيع بن أنس، وغير واحد:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r5.speaker: طاوس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r5.claim: Tawus defines al-afw as a small amount of everything; Ibn Kathir includes this under the general sense of surplus.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r5.anchor: وعن طاوس: اليسير من كل شيء،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r6.speaker: الربيع
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r6.claim: Al-Rabiʿ also glosses al-afw as one's best and finest property; Ibn Kathir says the definitions return to the idea of surplus.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r6.anchor: وعن الربيع أيضا: أفضل مالك، وأطيبه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says the instruction means not exhausting one's wealth and then having to ask people for help.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r7.anchor: عن الحسن: {ويسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} قال: ذلك ألا تجهد مالك ثم تقعد تسأل الناس.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r8.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r8.claim: In a report in Sahih Muslim, the Prophet tells a man to spend first on himself, then his family and child, and finally to use his judgment about any remainder.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r8.anchor: قال رجل: يا رسول الله، عندي دينار؟ قال: "أنفقه على نفسك". قال: عندي آخر؟ قال: "أنفقه على أهلك".

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r9.speaker: جابر عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r9.claim: Sahih Muslim reports the Prophet's order to begin with oneself, then one's family, then relatives, and then give beyond them as one can.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r9.anchor: ابدأ بنفسك فتصدق عليها، فإن فضل شيء فلأهلك، فإن فضل شيء عن أهلك فلذي قرابتك،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r10.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r10.speaker: أبو هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r10.claim: The Prophet says the best charity is given from a position of means, the upper hand is better than the lower, and one should begin with dependents.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p579#2/r10.anchor: خير الصدقة ما كان عن ظهر غنى، واليد العليا خير من اليد السفلى، وابدأ بمن تعول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r1.claim: A prophetic saying teaches that giving away one's surplus is good, hoarding it is harmful, and a person is not blamed for retaining enough.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r1.anchor: وفي الحديث أيضا: "ابن آدم، إنك إن تبذل الفضل خير لك، وإن تمسكه شر لك، ولا تلام على كفاف"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، عطاء الخراساني، السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, ʿAta al-Khurasani, and al-Suddi report the view that the command to give the surplus was abrogated by the zakat verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r2.anchor: ثم قد قيل: إنها منسوخة بآية الزكاة، كما رواه علي بن أبي طلحة، والعوفي عن ابن عباس،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r3.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r3.claim: Mujahid and others say the command is explained by the zakat verse rather than abrogated; Ibn Kathir prefers this interpretation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r3.anchor: وقيل: مبينة بآية الزكاة، قاله مجاهد وغيره، وهو أوجه.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r4.claim: As God clarified these rulings, He clarifies the rest of His verses concerning rulings, promise, and warning so people will reflect on worldly life and the Hereafter.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r4.anchor: أي: كما فصل لكم هذه الأحكام وبينها وأوضحها، كذلك يبين لكم سائر الآيات في أحكامه ووعده، ووعيده،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r9.claim: Ibn Kathir points back to the many early reports on reflection and taking lessons that he cited under the verse about signs in creation in Al Imran.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p580/r9.anchor: وقد ذكرنا عند قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران: {إن في خلق السماوات والأرض واختلاف الليل والنهار لآيات لأولي الألباب} [آل عمران: 190] آثارا كثيرة

JISHUMI:v1p876/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p876/r8.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v1p876/r8.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read kathir with th; most other readers have kabir with b, which the commentator prefers because of akbar, 4:2, and the majority reading.
JISHUMI:v1p876/r8.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي كثير بالثاء، والباقون بالباء، وهو الاختيار لقوله: أكبر،

JISHUMI:v1p876/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p876/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v1p876/r9.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads al-ʿafw with nominative case, meaning what they spend is the surplus; the others read it accusatively, meaning tell them to spend the surplus.
JISHUMI:v1p876/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو قل العفو بضم الواو، والباقون بالنصب، ووجه الرفع على معنى

JISHUMI:v1p876/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p876/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p876/r10.claim: Khamr derives from covering: one covers a vessel, and a khimar is so named because it covers the head.
JISHUMI:v1p876/r10.anchor: الخمر: أصله الستر، خمرت الإناء: غطيته، ومنه يسمى الخمار؛ لأنه يغطي الرأس.

JISHUMI:v1p876/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p876/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p876/r11.claim: Maysir means gambling; proposed derivations connect it with something won by the arrows, with dividing the camel’s meat into shares, or with ease in arranging the joint purchase, all carried out as a lottery.
JISHUMI:v1p876/r11.anchor: والميسر: القمار، وقيل: أخذ من اليسر، وهو وجوب الشيء لصاحبه، من قولهم: تيسر لي

JISHUMI:v1p876/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p876/r12.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p876/r12.claim: Abu Muslim describes a camel divided by ten arrows: seven marked arrows carried known shares and three carried none; winners got the corresponding meat share and paid its price, while those with blank arrows got no meat and paid nothing. Outsiders were called burma, while the players were called aysar.
JISHUMI:v1p876/r12.anchor: وذكر أبو مسلم أنهم كانوا يبتاعون جزورا ثم يجيلون القداح عشرة، لسبعة منها أنصباء معروفة،

JISHUMI:v1p876/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p876/r13.speaker: أبو عمرو
JISHUMI:v1p876/r13.claim: Abu ʿAmr says they divided the camel into ten portions; another report gives twenty-eight portions. Ten lots were cast and called azlam.
JISHUMI:v1p876/r13.anchor: وقال غيره: كانوا يجزئونها عشرة أجزاء، عن أبي عمرو، وقيل: ثمانية وعشرين جزءا،

JISHUMI:v1p879/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p879/r1.claim: Wine and gambling involve great sin alongside benefits: wine gives pleasure and trading profit, while gambling can yield money without labor.
JISHUMI:v1p879/r1.anchor: أما في الخمر فما يحصل من اللذة بشربها

JISHUMI:v1p879/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p879/r2.claim: Although sin is ascribed to wine and gambling themselves, it means drinking wine and gambling, since sin cannot literally be the substances.

JISHUMI:v1p879/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p879/r3.claim: One explanation places the sin in consequences of drinking, including neglecting prayer, obscenity, enmity, and hatred.
JISHUMI:v1p879/r3.anchor: ترك الصلاة وقول الفحش والعداوة والبغضاء الذي يحدث

JISHUMI:v1p879/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p879/r4.claim: The direct reading is stronger: the sin is attached to wine and gambling, not their consequences, which may not occur even though the sin remains.
JISHUMI:v1p879/r4.anchor: لا بما يحدث عنده، ولأنه قد ينفك من تلك الأمور

JISHUMI:v1p879/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r5.speaker: الربيع والضحاك
JISHUMI:v1p879/r5.claim: Al-Rabiʿ and al-Dahhak say the benefits were present before prohibition and the sin after prohibition.
JISHUMI:v1p879/r5.anchor: المنافع قبل التحريم، والإثم بعد التحريم، عن الربيع والضحاك.

JISHUMI:v1p879/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p879/r6.claim: Another view holds that benefit and sin coexist in one state, while prohibition is a separate matter, as water benefits a fasting person if he drinks it.
JISHUMI:v1p879/r6.anchor: في حالة واحدة، وتحريمه ثانية، وإن كان لو شرب انتفع

JISHUMI:v1p879/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p879/r7.claim: Their sin outweighs their benefit because of the punishment entailed; this is true of every reprehensible thing whose sin exceeds its benefit.
JISHUMI:v1p879/r7.anchor: بما يلزم عليه من العقوبة، وكذلك حال كل قبيح

JISHUMI:v1p879/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وعطاء والسدي
JISHUMI:v1p879/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatada, ʿAtaʾ, and al-Suddi gloss al-ʿafw as surplus beyond one's own and family's needs, given from comfortable means.
JISHUMI:v1p879/r8.anchor: ليكون عن ظهر غنى، عن ابن عباس وقتادة وعطاء والسدي.

JISHUMI:v1p879/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r9.speaker: الحسن وعطاء
JISHUMI:v1p879/r9.claim: Al-Hasan and ʿAtaʾ interpret al-ʿafw as a moderate amount, avoiding both extravagance and stinginess.
JISHUMI:v1p879/r9.anchor: الوسط من غير سرف ولا تقتير، عن الحسن وعطاء.

JISHUMI:v1p879/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r10.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v1p879/r10.claim: Mujahid interprets al-ʿafw as the obligatory alms.

JISHUMI:v1p879/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r11.speaker: الربيع
JISHUMI:v1p879/r11.claim: Al-Rabiʿ interprets al-ʿafw as what is wholesome or good.
JISHUMI:v1p879/r11.anchor: الطيب، عن الربيع كذلك يبين الله لكم

JISHUMI:v1p879/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p879/r12.claim: The phrase may mean that God explains proofs concerning spending, wine, and gambling.
JISHUMI:v1p879/r12.anchor: في أمر النفقة والخمر والميسر، وقيل

JISHUMI:v1p879/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p879/r13.claim: Another view takes the explained signs as all the ordinances of Islam.
JISHUMI:v1p879/r13.anchor: في سائر شرائع الإسلام لعلكم تتفكرون

JISHUMI:v1p879/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p879/r14.claim: One interpretation urges people to consider worldly and afterlife needs, keeping enough for livelihood and spending the rest for the hereafter.
JISHUMI:v1p879/r14.anchor: ما يصلحكم من معاشكم، وتنفقون الباقي لآخرتكم

JISHUMI:v1p879/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p879/r15.claim: Another interpretation contrasts the world's passing nature and mixed troubles with the lasting, unalloyed hereafter, urging obedience and avoidance of sin.
JISHUMI:v1p879/r15.anchor: في الدنيا وزوالها وفنائها، وما يشوبها من الهموم

JISHUMI:v1p879/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r16.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p879/r16.claim: Abu Muslim says the reflection concerns the pleasures of this world and the reward of the hereafter.
JISHUMI:v1p879/r16.anchor: في نعيم الدنيا وثواب الآخرة، عن أبي مسلم.

JISHUMI:v1p879/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p879/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p879/r17.claim: The verse's legal discussion is organized around wine and its analogues, gambling, spending, and the verse's proofs.
JISHUMI:v1p879/r17.anchor: في الآية أحكام وأدلة من وجوه

JISHUMI:v1p881/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p881/r1.claim: Wine is unquestionably forbidden: it was once permitted, prohibition is necessarily known as part of the religion, its denier is an unbeliever, and its drinker a sinner.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r1.anchor: وعلم ذلك من دينه ضرورة حتى يكفر جاحده، ويفسق شاربه.

JISHUMI:v1p881/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r2.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v1p881/r2.claim: Hasan and a group say this verse prohibited wine; al-Qadi chooses this view because calling it a great sin implies prohibition.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r2.anchor: قال الحسن وجماعة: حرمت بهذه الآية، وهو اختيار القاضي

JISHUMI:v1p881/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r3.speaker: قتادة وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p881/r3.claim: Qatada and Abu ʿAli say wine was prohibited by the verse in al-Maʾida.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة وأبو علي: إنما حرمت بآية المائدة

JISHUMI:v1p881/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p881/r4.claim: Reports from some early authorities say intoxicants were prohibited by the command not to approach prayer while intoxicated; a long report also records some Companions withholding judgment.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r4.anchor: وأن السكر حرم بقوله: (لا تقربوا الصلاة وأنتم سكارى)

JISHUMI:v1p881/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p881/r5.claim: Al-Qadi rejects that timing account: a great sin must be forbidden, this verse is more emphatic than a simple prohibition, and any Companion hesitation could await a stronger ruling.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r5.anchor: قال القاضي: وهذا لا يصح؛ لأن ما فيه إثم كبير

JISHUMI:v1p881/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة وجماعة من العلماء
JISHUMI:v1p881/r6.claim: Abu Hanifa and a group define wine as grape juice that ferments, boils, and throws up foam; they agree that this is wine.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r6.anchor: هو عصير العنب إذا اشتد وغلا وقذف بالزبد عن أبي حنيفة وجماعة من العلماء

JISHUMI:v1p881/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r7.speaker: الشافعي
JISHUMI:v1p881/r7.claim: Al-Shafiʿi defines wine as any drink whose large quantity intoxicates, so even a small quantity counts as wine.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r7.anchor: ما أسكر كثيره فقليله خمر، وهو مذهب الشافعي.

JISHUMI:v1p881/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p881/r8.claim: The grape-specific definition is stronger: a Prophetic report distinguishes wine itself from intoxication in other drinks, and the grape definition has consensus while the broader one lacks proof.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r8.anchor: والأول أصح لحديث النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: حرمت الخمر لعينها

JISHUMI:v1p881/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r9.speaker: النبي
JISHUMI:v1p881/r9.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that wine is forbidden for its own essence, while intoxication is forbidden from every drink.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r9.anchor: لحديث النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: حرمت الخمر لعينها، والسكر من كل شراب

JISHUMI:v1p881/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r10.speaker: ابن علية وبشر المريسي
JISHUMI:v1p881/r10.claim: Ibn ʿUlayya and Bishr al-Marisi say cooked grape juice becomes lawful after even minimal cooking.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r10.anchor: إذا طبخ أدنى طبخة حل، عن ابن علية وبشر المريسي

JISHUMI:v1p881/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r11.speaker: جماعة
JISHUMI:v1p881/r11.claim: Another group says cooked grape juice is lawful once half of it has evaporated.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r11.anchor: إذا ذهب نصفه حل، عن جماعة

JISHUMI:v1p881/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r12.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأبو يوسف وسفيان الثوري وجماعة
JISHUMI:v1p881/r12.claim: Abu Hanifa, Abu Yusuf, Sufyan al-Thawri, and others permit it when two-thirds have evaporated and one-third remains; this is also reported from several early authorities.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r12.anchor: ذهب ثلثاه وبقي ثلثه، وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف وسفيان الثوري

JISHUMI:v1p881/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r13.speaker: محمد ومالك والشافعي
JISHUMI:v1p881/r13.claim: Muhammad, Malik, and al-Shafiʿi hold that any drink, raw or cooked, is forbidden in small amounts if large amounts intoxicate.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r13.anchor: ما أسكر كثيره فقليله حرام، ويستوي فيه النيء والمطبوخ، عن محمد ومالك والشافعي

JISHUMI:v1p881/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p881/r14.claim: The author's school classifies drinks as grape-based, date- or raisin-based, and all other drinks.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r14.anchor: الأشربة على ثلاثة أنواع: الأول العنبي

JISHUMI:v1p881/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p881/r15.claim: Grape wine cannot be bought, sold, or drunk; the Prophet is reported to have cursed ten persons connected with wine.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r15.anchor: الخمر، وقد بينا حدها، ولا يجوز بيعها

JISHUMI:v1p881/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r16.speaker: النبي
JISHUMI:v1p881/r16.claim: A report from the Prophet says that ten people connected with wine are cursed.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r16.anchor: المروي عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه لعن في الخمر عشرة

JISHUMI:v1p881/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p881/r17.claim: Among other grape drinks, juice cooked briefly cannot be drunk or sold; the half-cooked type may be sold but not drunk, while reducing it by two-thirds permits sale and drinking subject to the stated exception for amusement and intoxication.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r17.anchor: ما طبخ أدنى طبخة لا يحل شربه ولا بيعه، والمنصف يجوز بيعه

JISHUMI:v1p881/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p881/r18.speaker: الشافعي
JISHUMI:v1p881/r18.claim: Al-Shafiʿi holds that any drink intoxicating in large quantities is forbidden even in a small amount.
JISHUMI:v1p881/r18.anchor: وقال الشافعي: ما أسكر كثيره فقليله خمر حرام.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p287/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p287/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p287/r1.claim: The account begins with the Meccan verse permitting wine made from date palms and grapes; Muslims drank it as lawful.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p287/r1.anchor: نزلت في الخمر أربع آيات نزلت بمكة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p287/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p287/r2.speaker: عمر ومعاذ ونفر من الصحابة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p287/r2.claim: Umar, Muadh, and other Companions asked for a ruling because wine destroys reason and property; the verse about sin and benefit followed, and some drank while others abstained.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p287/r2.anchor: ثم إن عمر ومعاذا ونفرا من الصحابة قالوا يا رسول الله أفتنا في الخمر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p287/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p287/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p287/r3.claim: At Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf's gathering, drunk companions mishandled the recitation of al-Kafirun at prayer; the prohibition on approaching prayer intoxicated followed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p287/r3.anchor: ثم دعا عبد الرحمن بن عوف ناسا منهم فشربوا وسكروا فأم بعضهم فقرأ قل يا أيها الكافرون أعبد ما تعبدون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p287/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p287/r4.speaker: عمر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p287/r4.claim: After Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas was struck with a camel jawbone during a drunken gathering, he complained to the Prophet and Umar prayed for a clear ruling on wine.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p287/r4.anchor: فضربه انصاري بلحى بعير فشجه موضحة فشكا إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال عمر اللهم بين لنا في الخمر بيانا شافيا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r1.speaker: عمر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r1.claim: After the final prohibition was revealed, Umar answered God, “We have stopped.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r1.anchor: فقال عمر رضي الله عنه انتهينا يا رب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r2.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r2.claim: Ali said he would not pray by a structure whose well had received a drop of wine, nor graze land where wine had entered the sea and then dried.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r2.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه لو وقعت قطرة في بئر فبنيت مكانها منارة لم أؤذن عليها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r3.claim: Ibn Umar said that if he put his finger into wine, it would not follow him; al-Zamakhshari calls this true faith and connects it with fearing God fully.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما لو أدخلت أصبعي فيه لم تتبعني وهذا هو الايمان حقا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r4.claim: Wine is fermented grape juice that intensifies and foams; unboiled raisin or date infusion is also forbidden.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r4.anchor: والخمر ما غلا واشتد وقذف بالزبد من عصير العنب وهو حرام وكذلك نقيع الزبيب أو التمر الذي لم يطبخ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r5.claim: Abu Hanifa and some of his followers allow boiled raisin or date drink after two thirds evaporate and it ferments, provided one drinks below intoxication without seeking amusement.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r5.anchor: فإن طبخ حتى ذهب ثلثاه ثم غلا واشتد ذهب خبثه ونصيب الشيطان وحل شربه ما دون السكر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r6.speaker: أكثر الفقهاء
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r6.claim: Most jurists forbid that drink just as they forbid wine, and forbid every drink that intoxicates.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r6.anchor: وعند اكثر الفقهاء هو حرام كالخمر وكذلك كل ما اسكر من كل شراب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r7.claim: Khamr is named for covering the intellect and discernment; sakr likewise names its blocking of them, and khamr may be an intensive verbal noun from covering.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r7.anchor: وسميت خمرا لتغطيتها العقل والتمييز كما سميت سكرا لأنها تسكرهما أي تحجزهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r8.claim: Maysir is a verbal noun for gambling, deriving either from ease because it takes wealth effortlessly or from yasar because it strips away wealth.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r8.anchor: والميسر القمار مصدر من يسر كالموعد والمرجع من فعلهما يقال يسرته اذا قمرته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says that in pre-Islamic times a man would wager his family and wealth; the cited poem's ييسرونني compares what is done to the speaker with what gamblers do to a wagered person.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p288/r9.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما كان الرجل في الجاهلية يخاطر على اهله وماله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r1.claim: The game used ten marked arrows, with seven assigned shares and three blanks; a slaughtered camel was divided into ten portions or, in another account, twenty-eight, then a just person drew arrows to assign shares and losers paid the full cost.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r1.anchor: للفذ سهم وللتوام سهمان وللرقيب ثلاثة وللحلس أربعة وللنافس خمسة وللمسبل ستة وللمعلى سبعة يجعلونها في الربابة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r2.claim: Winners gave their portions to the poor rather than eating them, boasted of generosity, and called anyone who refused to gamble al-baram.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r2.anchor: وكانوا يدفعون تلك الأنصباء إلى الفقراء ولا يأكلون منها ويفتخرون بذلك ويذمون من لم يدخل فيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r3.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r3.claim: A Prophetic report warns against two ill-omened games, described as the non-Arab form of gambling; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r3.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم 118 ( إياكم وهاتين اللعبتين المشؤمتين فإنهما من ميسر العجم )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r4.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r4.claim: Ali classifies backgammon and chess as gambling.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r4.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه ان النرد والشطرنج من الميسر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r5.speaker: ابن سيرين
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r5.claim: Ibn Sirin says that anything involving a stake or risk is gambling.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r5.anchor: وعن ابن سيرين كل شيء فيه خطر فهو من الميسر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r6.claim: The question concerns the consequences of engaging in wine and gambling, as indicated by the following explanation of their sin and benefit.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289/r6.anchor: والمعنى يسألونك عما في تعاطيهما بدليل قوله تعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r1.claim: Their sin is the punishment incurred by consuming wine and gambling; it outweighs benefits such as pleasure, merriment, socializing, gifts, gambling gains, and boasting over abstainers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r1.anchor: وهو الالتذاذ بشرب الخمر والقمار والطرب فيهما والتوصل بهما إلى مصادقات الفتيان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r2.claim: A reading has كثير with thāʾ, and Ubay's reading says وأثمهما أقرب.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r2.anchor: وقرىء ( إثم كثير بالثاء ) وفي قراءة أبي ( واثمهما أقرب )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r3.claim: The reading كثير suits the many kinds of sins committed by people who drink and gamble.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r3.anchor: ومعنى الكثرة أن أصحاب الشرب والقمار يقترفون فيهما الآثام من وجوه كثيرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r4.claim: العفو is the opposite of strenuous effort: spend what does not exhaust one's means; the poem خذي العفو مني uses it for what is easy, and it can also mean soft, level land.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r4.anchor: نقيض الجهد وهو ان ينفق مالا يبلغ انفاقه منه الجهد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r5.claim: The word العفو is read in both the nominative and accusative.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r5.anchor: ويقال للأرض السهلة العفو وقرىء بالرفع والنصب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r6.speaker: النبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r6.claim: The Prophet rejected a man's offer of a golden egg as charity several times, then threw it back and said charity should come from surplus, not leave the donor begging; no grading is stated.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r6.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم 119 أن رجلا أتاه ببيضة من ذهب أصابها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r7.claim: The phrase في الدنيا والآخرة may attach to تتفكرون, so people reflect on matters of both abodes and choose what is more enduring and beneficial.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p289#2/r7.anchor: فى الدنيا والاخرة إما ان يتعلق بتتفكرون فيكون المعنى لعلكم تتفكرون فيما يتعلق بالدارين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p290/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p290/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p290/r1.claim: Another construction connects the reflection to the greater sin: compare the afterlife's punishment with worldly benefit, rather than choosing immediate gain over escape from grave punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p290/r1.anchor: لتتفكروا في عقاب الإثم في الآخرة والنفع في الدنيا حتى لا تختاروا النفع العاجل على النجاة من العقاب العظيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p290/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p290/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p290/r2.claim: A further construction attaches the phrase to يبين: God clarifies signs about both abodes and their concerns so people may reflect.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p290/r2.anchor: على معنى يبين لكم الآيات في أمر الدارين وفيما يتعلق بهما لعلكم تتفكرون

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r1.claim: Māwardī says the Companions asked Muhammad about wine and gambling, and that this was the first verse revealed on the subject.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r1.anchor: يعني يسألك أصحابك يا محمد عن الخمر والميسر وشربها , وهذه أول آية نزلت فيها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r2.claim: Khamr is anything that obscures, veils, and covers the intellect.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r2.anchor: الخمر كل ما خامر العقل فستره وغطى عليه , من قولهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r3.claim: The root idea is covering: khamara is to cover a vessel, and the woman's khimār is named for covering her.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r3.anchor: من قولهم خمرت الإناء إذا غطيته , ويقال هو في خمار الناس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r4.speaker: العجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r4.claim: Al-Ajjaj's line uses al-khamr for a hidden or stealthy approach; the animal in his poem does not approach stealthily but openly with banners and troops.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r4.anchor: قال العجاج : في لامع العقبان لا يأتي الخمر يوجه الأرض

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r5.claim: Maysir means gambling and is connected to the expression yasara lī, meaning that a thing came easily or was attainable.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r5.anchor: فأما الميسر فهو القمار من قول القائل يسر لي هذا الشيء يسرا وميسرا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r6.claim: The player with arrows was called a yāsir; the term was then applied to the gambler.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r6.anchor: فالياسر اللاعب بالقداح ثم قيل للمقامر ياسر ويسر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r7.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r7.claim: An unnamed poet likens himself to a cheated yāsir turning the arrows, illustrating the gambling sense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p275/r7.anchor: كما قال الشاعر : فبت كأنني يسر غبين يقلب بعدما اختلع القداحا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r1.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read kathīr, with thāʾ, instead of kabīr, with bāʾ.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r2.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r2.claim: Al-Suddi says wine's sin is that drunkenness makes the drinker harm people, while gambling's sin is withholding what is due and acting unjustly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r2.anchor: أن شارب الخمر يسكر فيؤذي الناس , وإثم الميسر : أن يقامر الرجل فيمنع الحق ويظلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says wine removes the drinker's reason until awareness of the Creator disappears.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r3.anchor: أن إثم الخمر زوال عقل شاربها إذا سكر حتى يغرب عنه معرفة خالقه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says gambling distracts from remembrance and prayer and produces enmity and hatred, as described at 5:90.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r4.anchor: وإثم الميسر : ما فيه من الشغل عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة , ووقوع العداوة والبغضاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r5.claim: Wine's benefits include its sale price and trading profit, as well as the pleasure of drinking it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r5.anchor: فمنافع الخمر أثمانها وربح تجارتها , وما ينالونه من اللذة بشربها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r6.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r6.claim: Hassan ibn Thabit's verse presents wine as making drinkers feel like kings and lions, illustrating its pleasure or perceived benefit.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r6.anchor: كما قال حسان بن ثابت : ونشربها فتتركنا ملوكا وأسدا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r7.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r7.claim: A second poet contrasts wine's imagined royal grandeur while drinking with humble possessions after sobriety.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r7.anchor: وكما قال آخر : فإذا شربت فإنني … رب الخورنق والسدير

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r8.claim: One account of gambling's benefit is obtaining money without labor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r8.anchor: أحدهما : اكتساب المال من غير كد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r9.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r9.claim: Another account is obtaining a share of the camel gambled over and divided into ten portions among the arrow winners; Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Suddi are cited for this view.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r9.anchor: والثاني : ما يصيبون من أنصباء الجزور , وذلك أنهم كانوا يتياسرون على الجزور

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas reads the comparison as applying after prohibition: the sin and benefit of both practices after prohibition are compared.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r10.anchor: أحدهما : أن إثمهما بعد التحريم أكبر من نفعهما بعد التحريم , وهو قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r11.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reads it as a pre-prohibition comparison: the sins caused by the practices outweighed their benefits.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r11.anchor: والثاني : أن كلاهما قبل التحريم يعني الإثم الذي يحدث من أسبابهما

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r12.claim: One interpretation of al-afw is what remains after providing for one's family.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r12.anchor: أحدها : بما فضل عن الأهل , وهو قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r13.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r13.claim: Hasan takes al-afw as the moderate level of spending, neither extravagance nor parsimony.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r13.anchor: والثاني : أنه الوسط في النفقة ما لم يكن إسرافا أو إقتارا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r14.claim: A further report from Ibn Abbas takes al-afw as whatever people can provide, little or much.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r14.anchor: والرابع : إن العفو أن يؤخذ منهم ما أتوا به من قليل أو كثير

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r15.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r15.claim: One view from Mujahid takes the spending as charity given from a position of sufficiency.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r15.anchor: والخامس : أنه الصدقة عن ظهر غنى , وهو قول مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r16.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r16.claim: A second view from Mujahid takes al-afw as the obligatory charity.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r16.anchor: والسادس : أنه الصدقة المفروضة وهو مروي عن مجاهد أيضا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r17.claim: Ibn Abbas says this spending command was abrogated by the alms tax.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r18.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r18.claim: Mujahid says the command concerning al-afw remains in force.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r19.speaker: قوم من أهل النظر
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r19.claim: Some rationalist interpreters hold that wine was prohibited by this verse.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r19.anchor: فقال قوم من أهل النظر : حرمت الخمر بهذه الآية

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r20.speaker: قتادة وأكثر العلماء
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r20.claim: Qatada and most scholars hold that wine was prohibited by the verse in al-Ma'idah, 5:90.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r20.anchor: وقال قتادة وعليه أكثر العلماء : أنها حرمت بأية المائدة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r21.speaker: أبو القلوص زيد بن علي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r21.claim: Abu al-Qalus's report says the first verse did not end drinking: two Muslims became drunk and entered prayer speaking unintelligibly, after which 4:43 was revealed and they avoided drinking at prayer times.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p276/r21.anchor: روى عبد الوهاب عن عوف عن أبي القلوص زيد بن علي قال : أنزل الله عز وجل في الخمر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r1.claim: Continuing Abu al-Qalus's account, a man drank, lamented those killed at Badr in verse, and the Prophet arrived alarmed; the man sought God's and the Prophet's protection and vowed never to drink again.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r1.anchor: فبلغ ذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فجاء فزعا يجر رداءه من الفزع

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r2.claim: The account concludes that the prohibition in 5:90–91 was revealed, and the people answered that they had stopped.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r2.anchor: فأنزل الله في تحريمها ^ { يا أيها الذين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r3.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r3.claim: Al-Suddi reports that people continued drinking after the first verse; at a meal hosted by Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Ali led a prayer while drunk and failed to recite al-Kafirun correctly, prompting the prayer restriction in 4:43.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r3.anchor: وروى موسى عن عمرو عن أسباط عن السدي قال : نزلت هذه الآية

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r4.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says that before final prohibition they drank after the dawn prayer until midday, then again after the night prayer until midnight, and woke for dawn sober.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r4.anchor: فكانت لهم حلالا يشربونها من صلاة الغداة حتى يرتفع النهار أو ينتصف

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r5.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r5.claim: In al-Suddi's report, a drunken dispute at a meal hosted by Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas led an Anṣari to strike Sa'd's nose with a camel jawbone; the prohibition in 5:90 was then revealed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p279/r5.anchor: حتى صنع سعد بن أبي وقاص طعاما ودعا ناس من أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUJAHID:v1p106/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p106/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p106/r1.claim: Mujahid calls this the first occasion on which wine was censured.
MUJAHID:v1p106/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر قل فيهما إثم كبير ﴾ هذا أول ما عيبت به الخمر

MUJAHID:v1p106/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p106/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p106/r2.claim: The benefits are what people gain from wine and gambling.
MUJAHID:v1p106/r2.anchor: ﴿ ومنافع للناس ﴾ ما يصيبون فيها ومن الميسر

MUJAHID:v1p106/r3.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p106/r3.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p106/r3.claim: Maysir means gambling; its name is linked to the expression aysiru, meaning to slaughter or divide an animal, as in a wager to put up set amounts.
MUJAHID:v1p106/r3.anchor: ومن الميسر والميسر هو القمار وإنما سمي الميسر لقولهم أيسروا أي أجزروا كقوله ضع كذا وكذا

MUJAHID:v1p106/r4.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p106/r4.speaker: طاوس
MUJAHID:v1p106/r4.claim: Tawus interprets al-afw, the amount to spend, as maysir.
MUJAHID:v1p106/r4.anchor: عن طاوس في قوله ﴿ قل العفو ﴾ يعني الميسر

MUJAHID:v1p106/r5.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p106/r5.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p106/r5.claim: Mujahid interprets al-afw as the obligatory alms.
MUJAHID:v1p106/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ العفو ﴾ الصدقة المفروضة

MUQATIL:2:219-220/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r1.claim: The verse was revealed concerning Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Umar ibn al-Khattab, Ali ibn Abi Talib, and several Helpers; maysir means gambling.
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r1.anchor: يعنى القمار، نزلت فى عبدالرحمن بن عوف، وعمر بن الخطاب، وعلى بن أبى طالب، ونفر من الأنصار،

MUQATIL:2:219-220/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r2.claim: In the gambling game, a group bought a camel by shares and drew lots; the person whose lot came out paid the whole price but received no meat, which the others divided.
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r2.anchor: فيقوم نفر، فيشترون الجزور، فيجعلون لكل رجل منهم سهم، ثم يقرعون، فمن خرج سهمه

MUQATIL:2:219-220/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r3.claim: Their sin lies in neglecting prayer and remembrance of God and committing forbidden acts through drinking and gambling.
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r3.anchor: فى ركوبهما؛ لأن فيهما ترك الصلاة، وترك ذكر الله عز وجل، وركوب المحارم،

MUQATIL:2:219-220/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r4.claim: Before prohibition, their benefits were pleasure and trade; gambling could benefit some while causing others, the gamblers, to lose.
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r4.anchor: يعنى بالمنافع اللذة والتجارة فى ركوبهما قبل التحريم، فلما حرمهما الله عز وجل،

MUQATIL:2:219-220/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r5.claim: The sin after prohibition outweighs the benefits before it; their prohibition was revealed a year after this verse.
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r5.anchor: فلما حرمهما الله عز وجل، قال: { وإثمهما } بعد التحريم، { أكبر من نفعهما } ، قبل التحريم، وأنزل الله عز وجل تحريمهما بعد هذه الآية بسنة،

MUQATIL:2:219-220/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r6.claim: Maysir was named from their phrase yassirū lanā thamana al-jazūr, meaning make the camel's price easy for us.
MUQATIL:2:219-220/r6.anchor: وإنما سمي الميسر؛ لأنهم قالوا: يسروا لنا ثمن الجزور، يقول الرجل: افعل كذا وكذا.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r1.claim: The author recounts the stages: the first Meccan verse (16:67) allowed intoxicants; after Umar and others asked about wine’s harm, this verse followed. Some drank and others abstained.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r1.anchor: نزل فى الخمر أربع آيات نزل بمكة ومن ثمرات النخيل والأعناب تتخذون منه سكرا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r2.claim: After this verse, ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf hosted drinkers; an intoxicated imam misrecited the disavowal sūra, prompting 4:43’s ban on approaching prayer while drunk.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r2.anchor: ثم دعا عبد الرحمن ابن عوف جماعة فشربوا وسكروا وأم بعضهم فقرأ قل يا أيها الكافرون

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r3.speaker: عمر
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r3.claim: After ʿUtban ibn Malik’s guests became drunk, argued, and fought, Umar prayed for a clear ruling; 5:90 followed and he said they abstained.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r3.anchor: ثم دعا عتبان بن مالك جماعة فلما سكروا منها تخاصموا وتضاربوا فقال عمر اللهم بين لنا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r4.speaker: علي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r4.claim: Ali said that if wine fell into a well he would not call prayer from a minaret built there, nor graze land exposed by a dried sea where it had fallen.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r4.anchor: وعن على رضى الله عنه لو وقعت قطرة فى بئر فبنيت مكانها منارة لم أؤذن عليها

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r5.claim: Khamr is grape juice that boils, intensifies, and foams; its name means covering because it veils the mind.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r5.anchor: والخمر ما غلى واشتد وقذف بالزبد من عصير العنب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r6.claim: Maysir is gambling, from يسر; it may be named for taking wealth easily without effort or for depriving someone of wealth.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r6.anchor: والميسر القمار مصدر من يسر كالموعد من فعله يقال يسرته إذا قمرته

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r7.claim: The traditional game used ten arrows: al-fadh, taw'am, raqib, hils, nafis, musbil, and muʿalla awarded one to seven shares; manih, safih, and waghd were blanks.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r7.anchor: وصفة الميسر أنه كانت لهم عشرة أقداح سبعة منها عليها خطوط وهو الفذ وله سهم والتوأم وله سهمان

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r8.claim: An impartial arbiter drew arrows from a bag; winners took their marked share, while blank-drawers got nothing and paid the camel’s full cost.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r8.anchor: فيجعلون الأقداح فى خريطة ويضعونها على يد عدل ثم يجلجلها ويدخل يده ويخرج باسم رجل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r9.claim: Winners gave shares to the poor, did not eat them, boasted of generosity, and disparaged those who declined to gamble.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r9.anchor: وكانوا يدفعون تلك الأنصباء إلى الفقراء ولا يأكلون منها ويفتخرون بذلك

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r10.claim: The ruling includes all forms of gambling, such as backgammon and chess.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r10.anchor: وفى حكم الميسر أنواع القمار من النرد والشطرنج وغيرهما

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r11.claim: The question concerns the consequences of participating in drinking and gambling, as shown by the answer about sin and benefits.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r11.anchor: والمعنى يسألونك عما فى تعاطيهما بدليل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r12.claim: Their sin includes quarrels, insults, obscene speech, and falsehood.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r12.anchor: بسبب التخاصم والتشاتم وقول الفحش والزور

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r13.speaker: حمزة وعلي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r13.claim: Hamza and ʿAli read كثير, meaning many, in place of كبير.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r14.claim: Wine benefits include trade and drinking pleasure; gambling may benefit the poor or bring easy money.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r14.anchor: بالتجارة فى الخمر والتلذذ بشربها وفى الميسر بارتفاق الفقراء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r15.claim: Their sin outweighs their benefit because drinkers and gamblers commit sins in many ways.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r15.anchor: لأن أصحاب الشرب والقمار يقترفون فيهما الآثام من وجوه كثيرة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r16.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r16.claim: Al-ʿafw is surplus beyond need; early Muslims had to donate surplus after retaining a year’s provisions as farmers or a day’s as artisans, until the zakat verse abrogated the rule.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r16.anchor: أى الفضل أى أنفقوا ما فضل عن قدر الحاجة وكان التصدق بالفضل فى أول الإسلام فرضا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r17.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r17.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r17.claim: Abu ʿAmr reads العفو in the accusative; then ماذا is one noun as the object and the answer means they spend the surplus.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r17.anchor: أبو عمرو فمن نصبه جعل ماذا اسما واحدا فى موضع النصب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r18.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r18.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r18.claim: If ما is the subject and ذا a relative pronoun with ينفقون as its clause, the answer العفو matches the question’s nominative syntax.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r18.anchor: ومن رفعه جعل ما مبتدأ وخبره ذا مع صلته فذا بمعنى الذى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r19.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r19.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r19.claim: The kāf in كذلك modifies an omitted verbal noun in the accusative: an explanation like this explanation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p104#2/r19.anchor: الكاف فى موضع نصب نعت لمصدر محذوف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r1.claim: The questioners about wine and gambling are believers, as Qurtubi noted earlier.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r2.claim: Khamr is named from khamara, “to cover”: it veils the intellect, just as a woman’s veil covers and anything covering something is said to khammar it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r2.anchor: والخمر مأخوذة من خمر إذا ستر ومنه خمار المرأة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r3.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r3.claim: The unnamed poet’s phrase khamr al-tariq refers to a hollow or depression that conceals a wolf or other creature.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر: ألا يا زيد والضحاك سيرا فقد جاوزتما خمر الطريق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r4.speaker: العجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r4.claim: Al-Ajjaj’s phrase al-khamr describes someone who does not move concealed, illustrating the sense of hiding.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r4.anchor: وقال العجاج يصف جيشا يمشي برايات وجيوش غير مستخف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r5.claim: The expression ghimār or khimār of people can mean a hidden place or a place within the crowd.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r5.anchor: ومنه قولهم: دخل في غمار الناس وخمارهم أي هو في مكان خاف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r6.claim: A second etymology connects khamr with being left to mature, as dough ferments or an opinion is left to become clear.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r6.anchor: وقيل: إنما سميت الخمر خمرا لأنها تركت حتى أدركت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r7.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r7.claim: A third etymology derives the name from mixing with the intellect, from mukhāmarah, “mixing.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r7.anchor: وقيل: إنما سميت الخمر خمرا لأنها تخالط العقل، من المخامرة وهي المخالطة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r8.claim: Qurtubi says the three explanations converge: wine matures, mixes with the intellect, then covers it; concealment is the root sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r8.anchor: فالمعاني الثلاثة متقاربة فالخمر تركت وخمرت حتى أدركت، ثم خالطت العقل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r9.claim: Wine is grape juice that ferments or is cooked; any other substance that intoxicates the intellect has the same legal status.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r9.anchor: والخمر: ماء العنب الذي غلى أو طبخ وما خامر العقل من غيره فهو في حكمه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r10.claim: Qurtubi extends the prohibition to all gambling by consensus, since maysir originally concerned wagering on camels; by the same analogy, other intoxicants take wine’s ruling.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r10.anchor: لأن إجماع العلماء أن القمار كله حرام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r11.speaker: جمهور الأمة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r11.claim: The majority hold that any drink whose large quantity intoxicates is forbidden in both small and large quantities, and that the prescribed penalty applies.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r11.anchor: والجمهور من الأمة على أن ما أسكر كثيره من غير خمر العنب فمحرم قليله وكثيره

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r12.speaker: أبو حنيفة والثوري وابن أبي ليلى وابن شبرمة وفقهاء الكوفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r12.claim: These Kufan jurists allow small amounts of non-grape drinks that intoxicate in large amounts and deny the penalty absent deliberate intoxication; Qurtubi calls this weak and rejects it by reason and transmitted evidence.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r12.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة والثوري وابن أبي ليلى وابن شبرمة وجماعة من فقهاء الكوفة: ما أسكر كثيره

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r13.speaker: بعض المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r13.claim: Some exegetes say God bestowed every honor and good on this community and prescribed laws gradually rather than all at once; wine prohibition likewise came in stages.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r13.anchor: قال بعض المفسرين: إن الله تعالى لم يدع شيئا من الكرامة والبر إلا أعطاه هذه الأمة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r14.claim: Qurtubi says this verse was the first revelation on wine; the later stages are detailed in the following segment.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219/r14.anchor: وهذه الآية أول ما نزل في أمر الخمر، ثم بعده:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r1.claim: Qurtubi places the prohibition on approaching prayer while intoxicated at the next stage of the wine rulings.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r2.claim: He next cites the verse explaining that Satan uses wine and gambling to sow hostility and obstruct remembrance and prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r2.anchor: إنما يريد الشيطان أن يوقع بينكم العداوة والبغضاء في الخمر والميسر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r3.claim: He then cites the command to avoid wine, gambling, idols, and divining arrows as satanic impurity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r3.anchor: إنما الخمر والميسر والأنصاب والأزلام رجس من عمل الشيطان فاجتنبوه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r4.claim: Maysir originally means the Arabs’ gambling with arrows.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r4.anchor: قوله تعالى: { والميسر } الميسر: قمار العرب بالأزلام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says a pre-Islamic man wagered his family and property; the winner took the loser’s wealth and family, and the verse was revealed about this.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان الرجل في الجاهلية يخاطر الرجل على أهله وماله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد ومحمد بن سيرين والحسن وابن المسيب وعطاء وقتادة ومعاوية بن صالح وطاوس وعلي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r6.claim: These authorities define maysir broadly as anything involving gambling, including dice, chess, and children’s games with walnuts or knucklebones, except permitted horse wagers and lotteries for allocating rights.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد ومحمد بن سيرين والحسن وابن المسيب وعطاء وقتادة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r7.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r7.claim: Malik divides maysir into amusement, including dice, chess, and entertainments, and gambling involving wagers.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r7.anchor: وقال مالك: الميسر ميسران: ميسر اللهو

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r8.claim: Ali calls chess “the maysir of the non-Arabs.”
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r8.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب: الشطرنج ميسر العجم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r9.speaker: مالك وجماعة العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r9.claim: Malik and other scholars treat anything wagered upon as maysir.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r9.anchor: وكل ما قومر به فهو ميسر عند مالك وغيره من العلماء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r10.claim: Maysir derives from yusr: it is something that becomes due to its owner; yāsir is the player with the arrows.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r10.anchor: والميسر مأخوذ من اليسر، وهو وجوب الشيء لصاحبه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r11.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r11.claim: The cited line “fa-aʿinhum wa-aysir…” uses a form from y-s-r for playing the arrows or taking part in maysir.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r11.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
فأعنهم وايسر بما يسروا به

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r12.speaker: الأزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r12.claim: Al-Azhari says maysir can name the camel gambled over because it is divided into shares; anything divided is described with the same root.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r12.anchor: وقال الأزهري: الميسر: الجزور الذي كانوا يتقامرون عليه سمي ميسرا لأنه يجزأ أجزاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r13.speaker: الأزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r13.claim: Al-Azhari says yāsir originally means the butcher who portions the camel; by extension it names the arrow players and gamblers who cause the slaughter.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r13.anchor: والياسر: الجازر لأنه يجزىء لحم الجزور

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r14.speaker: الصحاح
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r14.claim: Al-Sihah records that “the people yasara the camel” means they slaughtered it and divided its portions.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#2/r14.anchor: وفي الصحاح: ويسر القوم الجزور أي اجتزروها واقتسموا أعضاءها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r1.claim: The verb yassara means to gamble; yasir and yasir both mean gambler, and their plural is aysār.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r1.anchor: ويقال: يسر القوم إذا قامروا. ورجل يسر وياسر بمعنى. والجمع أيسار قال النابغة:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r2.claim: Al-Nābigha and Ṭarafa use aysār for the people who draw lots for a camel and distribute its meat shares.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r2.anchor: قال النابغة: أني أتمم أيساري وأمنحهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r3.claim: Volunteering to slaughter a camel for the gambling group was praised among the Arabs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r3.anchor: وكان من تطوع بنحرها ممدوحا عندهم قال الشاعر: وناجية نحرت لقوم صدق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r4.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib said pre-Islamic maysir included selling meat for one or two live sheep; Mālik transmitted this in the Muwaṭṭaʾ through Dāwūd ibn Ḥuṣayn.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r4.anchor: روى مالك في الموطأ عن داود بن حصين أنه سمع سعيد بن المسيب يقول: كان من ميسر أهل الجاهلية بيع اللحم بالشاة والشاتين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r5.speaker: مالك وجمهور أصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r5.claim: For animals and meat of the same species, Mālik and most companions classify the exchange as muzābana, uncertainty, and gambling: meat yield is unknown and meat cannot be exchanged unequally.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r5.anchor: وهذا محمول عند مالك وجمهور أصحابه في الجنس الواحد، حيوانه بلحمه وهو عنده من باب المزابنة والغرر والقمار

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r6.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r6.claim: Mālik treats all edible quadrupeds, including camels, cattle, sheep, and game, as one genus, barring exchange of any for meat from that genus.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#3/r6.anchor: والجنس الواحد عنده الإبل والبقر والغنم والظباء والوعول وسائر الوحوش، وذوات الأربع المأكولات كلها عنده جنس واحد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r1.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r1.claim: Mālik treats all birds as one genus and all fish as one; one report from him singles out locusts as their own category.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r1.anchor: والطير عنده كله جنس واحد، وكذلك الحيتان من سمك وغيره. وروي عنه أن الجراد وحده صنف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r2.speaker: الشافعي والليث بن سعد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r2.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī, his companions, and al-Layth ibn Saʿd prohibit exchanging meat for a live animal in all cases, whether species match or differ, relying on the hadith's general wording.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r2.anchor: وقال الشافعي وأصحابه والليث بن سعد: لا يجوز بيع اللحم بالحيوان على حال من الأحوال من جنس واحد كان أم من جنسين مختلفين على عموم الحديث

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r3.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās recounts that Abū Bakr refused a man's request to exchange a share from a ten-part camel for a sheep.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r3.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أن جزورا نحرت على عهد أبي بكر الصديق فقسمت على عشرة أجزاء فقال رجل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r4.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says he knows no Companion who disagreed with Abū Bakr's refusal of the exchange.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r4.anchor: قال أبو بكر: لا يصلح هذا. قال الشافعي: ولست أعلم لأبي بكر في ذلك مخالفا من الصحابة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r5.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r5.claim: Abū ʿUmar notes a report from Ibn ʿAbbās permitting sale of a sheep for meat, but judges it weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r5.anchor: قال أبو عمر: قد روي عن ابن عباس أنه أجاز بيع الشاة باللحم وليس بالقوي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r6.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r6.claim: ʿAbd al-Razzāq transmits through al-Thawrī and Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd that Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib disliked selling a live animal for a slaughtered one; Sufyān says his group sees no problem.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r6.anchor: وذكر عبد الرزاق عن الثوري عن يحيى بن سعيد عن سعيد بن المسيب أنه كره أن يباع حي بميت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r7.speaker: سفيان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r7.claim: Sufyān's own position is that exchanging a live animal for slaughtered meat is unobjectionable.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r7.anchor: قال سفيان: ونحن لا نرى به بأسا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r8.speaker: المزني
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r8.claim: Al-Muzanī says analogy permits animal for meat if the hadith is not sound, but if sound, analogy falls and the report must be followed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r8.anchor: قال المزني: إن لم يصح الحديث في بيع الحيوان باللحم فالقياس أنه جائز، وإن صح بطل القياس واتبع الأثر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r9.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r9.claim: Abū ʿUmar acknowledges the Kūfans' many analogical arguments for permissibility, but says sound transmitted evidence overrides analogy.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r9.anchor: قال أبو عمر: وللكوفيين في أنه جائز بيع اللحم بالحيوان حجج كثيرة من جهة القياس والاعتبار إلا أنه إذا صح الأثر بطل القياس والنظر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r10.claim: Mālik transmits from Zayd ibn Aslam, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, that the Prophet forbade selling an animal for meat.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r10.anchor: وروى مالك عن زيد بن أسلم عن سعيد بن المسيب: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نهى عن بيع الحيوان باللحم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r11.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r11.claim: Abū ʿUmar knows no established connected chain for the prohibition; its best chain is Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib's mursal report as Mālik gives it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r11.anchor: قال أبو عمر ولا أعلمه يتصل عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من وجه ثابت، وأحسن أسانيده مرسل سعيد بن المسيب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r12.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r12.claim: Although al-Shāfiʿī generally rejects mursal reports, he examined Saʿīd's and found most sound; he applies the prohibition generally across animal and meat kinds and will not qualify the text by analogy without a specific report or consensus.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r12.anchor: وإليه ذهب الشافعي وأصله أنه لا يقبل المراسيل إلا أنه زعم أنه افتقد مراسيل سعيد فوجدها أو أكثرها صحاحا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r13.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r13.claim: For al-Shāfiʿī, animal includes all creatures living on land or in water regardless of species, just as food names every edible or drinkable thing.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r13.anchor: والحيوان عنده اسم لكل ما يعيش في البر والماء وإن اختلفت أجناسه كالطعام الذي هو اسم لكل مأكول أو مشروب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r14.claim: Wine's sin includes quarrels, abuse, indecent and false speech, loss of reason needed to know duties to God, missed prayers, and distraction from God's remembrance.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r14.anchor: إثم الخمر ما يصدر عن الشارب من المخاصمة والمشاتمة وقول الفحش والزور، وزوال العقل الذي يعرف به ما يجب لخالقه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r15.speaker: عثمان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r15.claim: Al-Nasāʾī transmits from ʿUthmān the warning that wine is the mother of evils, illustrated by a devout man lured by a woman who offers sex, wine, or killing a boy.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#4/r15.anchor: روى النسائي عن عثمان رضي الله عنه قال: اجتنبوا الخمر فإنها أم الخبائث، إنه كان رجل ممن كان قبلكم تعبد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r1.speaker: عثمان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r1.claim: In the continuation of ʿUthmān's report, the man chooses wine, drinks until he commits adultery and kills the boy, showing how wine leads to grave acts.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r1.anchor: قال: فاسقيني من هذه الخمر كأسا فسقته كأسا. قال: زيدوني فلم يرم حتى وقع عليها، وقتل النفس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r2.speaker: راو غير مسمى
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r2.claim: A report says al-Aʿshā was persuaded on his way to Medina to return because he would not give up wine; he planned to drink for a year first, then fell from his camel and died before reaching home.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r2.anchor: وروي أن الأعشى لما توجه إلى المدينة ليسلم فلقيه بعض المشركين في الطريق فقالوا له: أين تذهب؟

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r3.speaker: راو غير مسمى
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r3.claim: The account says Qays ibn ʿĀṣim gave up wine after drunkenly groping his daughter, abusing his parents, speaking at the moon, and giving wealth to a wine seller.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r3.anchor: وكان قيس بن عاصم المنقري شرابا لها في الجاهلية ثم حرمها على نفسه وكان سبب ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r4.speaker: قيس بن عاصم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r4.claim: The poem first attributed to Qays condemns wine for ruining the intelligent, disgracing drinkers, and bringing great harm; it vows never to drink or pay for it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r4.anchor: وفيها يقول: رأيت الخمر صالحة وفيها خصال تفسد الرجل الحليما

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r5.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r5.claim: Abū ʿUmar cites Ibn al-Aʿrābī from al-Mufaḍḍal al-Ḍabbī, who attributes those verses instead to Abū Miḥjan al-Thaqafī.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r5.anchor: قال أبو عمر: وروى ابن الأعرابي عن المفضل الضبي أن هذه الأبيات لأبي محجن الثقفي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r6.claim: Abū Miḥjan famously wished to be buried by a vine; ʿUmar repeatedly flogged him for drinking and exiled him, later ordering Saʿd to detain him, but released him from chains after his courage at al-Qādisiyya.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r6.anchor: إذا مت فادفني إلى جنب كرمة تروي عظامي بعد موتي عروقها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r7.speaker: أبو محجن الثقفي
