QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r7.claim: After ʿUmar released him, Abū Miḥjan vowed never to drink again and kept the vow; another version says he drank when the penalty purified him but stopped once he was disgraced.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r7.anchor: قال أبو محجن: وأنا والله لا أشربها أبدا فلم يشربها بعد ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r8.speaker: الهيثم بن عدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r8.claim: Al-Haytham ibn ʿAdī says an informant saw Abū Miḥjan's grave in Azerbaijan or near Jurjān, with three fruiting vines growing over it and an inscription naming him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#5/r8.anchor: وذكر الهيثم بن عدي أنه أخبره من رأى قبر أبي محجن بأذربيجان، أو قال: في نواحي جرجان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r1.claim: Drunkards become a joke to sensible people and may play with or wipe themselves with urine and feces; one prayed to be among the repentant and pure while wiping his face, and another thanked a dog licking him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r1.anchor: ثم إن الشارب يصير ضحكة للعقلاء، فيلعب ببوله وعذرته، وربما يمسح وجهه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r2.claim: Gambling breeds enmity and hatred because it consumes another person's wealth wrongfully.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r2.anchor: وأما القمار فيورث العداوة والبغضاء لأنه أكل مال الغير بالباطل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r3.claim: The soundest account of wine's worldly benefit is trade profit: merchants brought it cheaply from Syria and sold it at high prices in the Hijaz, where buyers did not bargain.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r3.anchor: أما في الخمر فربح التجارة فإنهم كانوا يجلبونها من الشام برخص

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r4.claim: Other claimed benefits were aiding digestion and strength, sexual vigor, generosity, courage, clearer complexion, and pleasure.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r4.anchor: وقد قيل في منافعها: إنها تهضم الطعام، وتقوي الضعف، وتعين على الباه، وتسخي البخيل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r5.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r5.claim: Ḥassān ibn Thābit's poem depicts drinking as making the drinkers kings and lions who do not flinch from battle.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r5.anchor: قال حسان بن ثابت رضي الله عنه: ونشربها فتتركنا ملوكا وأسدا ما ينهنهنا اللقاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r6.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r6.claim: An anonymous poem says the drinker imagines himself lord of the Khawarnaq and Sadīr palaces, but sober owns only a small sheep and camel.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r6.anchor: وقال آخر: فإذا شربت فإنني رب الخورنق والسدير

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r7.claim: Maysir offered a share without work: the group bought a camel, winners received meat without paying, while the final loser paid the full price and got no meat.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r7.anchor: ومنفعة الميسر مصير الشيء إلى الإنسان في القمار بغير كد ولا تعب فكانوا يشترون الجزور

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r8.claim: Another view says gambling helped the poor because winners did not eat their shares but distributed the camel's meat to people in need.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r8.anchor: وقيل: منفعته التوسعة على المحاويج، فإن من قمر منهم كان لا يأكل من الجزور

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r9.claim: The lottery used eleven arrows; seven marked arrows had graded shares: al-fidh, al-tawʾam, al-raqīb, al-ḥalis, al-nafis or al-nafiz, al-misbal, and al-muʿallā. Al-Aṣmaʿī says their shares totaled twenty-eight portions.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r9.anchor: وسهام الميسر أحد عشر سهما منها سبعة لها حظوظ وفيها فروض على عدد الحظوظ

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r10.claim: Four arrows had no shares: al-maṣdar, al-muḍaʿʿaf, al-munīḥ, and al-safīḥ; another account lists three blanks, adding al-waghd, to prevent the drawer favoring anyone.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r10.anchor: وبقي من السهام أربعة، وهي الأغفال لا فروض لها ولا أنصباء، وهي: «المصدر» و «المضعف»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r11.claim: The drawer, also called the distributor or striker, drew from the covered arrow container while a watcher stood behind to prevent favoritism.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#6/r11.anchor: ويسمى المجيل المفيض والضارب والضريب والجمع الضرباء. وقيل: يجعل خلفه رقيب لئلا يحابي أحدا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r1.speaker: متمم بن نويرة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r1.claim: Mutammim ibn Nuwayra's verse calls a person who refuses to sponsor the winter camel slaughter a baram, a disfavored miser.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r1.anchor: ولا برما تهدى النساء لعرسه إذا القشع من برد الشتاء تقعقعا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya corrects al-Aṣmaʿī: the camel was divided into ten portions before the draw, not twenty-eight according to the arrow shares.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r2.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وأخطأ الأصمعي في قسمة الجزور، فذكر أنها على قدر حظوظ السهام ثمانية وعشرون قسما

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r3.claim: After the camel was split into ten parts, each winner took the number of portions his arrow entitled him to and gave them to the poor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r3.anchor: ثم يضرب على العشرة فمن فاز سهمه بأن يخرج من الربابة متقدما أخذ أنصباءه وأعطاها الفقراء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r4.claim: Rabbāba can mean the quiver-like container holding the gambling arrows; sometimes the collection of arrows itself was called rabbāba. Abū Dhuʾayb compares a donkey and she-asses to a rabbāba and its drawer.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r4.anchor: والربابة بكسر الراء: شبيهة بالكنانة تجمع فيها سهام الميسر وربما سموا جميع السهام ربابة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r5.claim: Rabbāba also means pledge or covenant, as an anonymous poet uses it for a bond entrusted to someone.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r5.anchor: والربابة أيضا: العهد والميثاق قال الشاعر: وكنت امرأ أفضت إليك ربابتي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r6.claim: Sometimes people gambled for themselves, so the person whose arrow did not win paid the camel's entire price; the practice fed poor people of the clan, as al-Aʿshā's verse says.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r6.anchor: وفي أحيان ربما تقامروا لأنفسهم ثم يغرم الثمن من لم يفز سهمه كما تقدم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r7.claim: Al-Aʿshā praises those who feed guests in winter and put food at the disposal of the gambler; another poem says loaned arrows return with food for the needy.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r7.anchor: ومنه قول الأعشى: المطعمو الضيف إذا ما شتوا والجاعلو القوت على الياسر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r8.claim: In the anonymous poem, al-munīḥ is a loaned arrow, smoothed by use and often winning; this is the praised loaned arrow, distinct from the blank arrow al-munīḥ.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r8.anchor: و «المنيح» في هذا البيت المستمنح لأنهم كانوا يستعيرون السهم الذي قد املس وكثر فوزه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r9.speaker: الأخطل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r9.claim: Al-Akhṭal's verse calls the blank al-munīḥ a kar; lexicographers define it as an arrow with no fixed share unless its owner gives it something.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r9.anchor: وإياه أراد الأخطل بقوله: ولقد عطفن على فزارة عطفة كر المنيح

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r10.speaker: لبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r10.claim: Labīd says that when his people gamble they do not produce shameful scandals recounted at summer gatherings; nevertheless maysir remains wrongful consumption of wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r10.anchor: ومن الميسر قول لبيد: إذا يسروا لم يورث اليسر بينهم فواحش ينعى ذكرها بالمصايف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r11.claim: God says the sin is greater and more harmful in the afterlife than the worldly benefits; the great sin is reckoned after prohibition, while the benefits were before it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r11.anchor: أعلم الله جل وعز أن الإثم أكبر من النفع، وأعود بالضرر في الآخرة فالإثم الكبير بعد التحريم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r12.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r12.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read kathīr with thāʾ; the plural fits plural benefits, and the cited hadith listing ten cursed categories connected with wine supports abundant sins.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r12.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «كثير» بالثاء المثلثة وحجتهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لعن الخمر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r13.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r13.claim: The hadith says the Prophet cursed wine and ten connected parties: its seller, buyer, agent buyer, presser, commissioner, pourer, drinker, carrier, person it is carried for, and consumer of its price.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r13.anchor: لعن الخمر ولعن معها عشرة: بائعها ومبتاعها والمشتراة له وعاصرها والمعصورة له وساقيها وشاربها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r14.speaker: باقي القراء وجمهور الناس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r14.claim: The other reciters and most people read kabīr with bāʾ because drinking and gambling are major sins and the comparative akbar supports this reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r14.anchor: وقرأ باقي القراء وجمهور الناس «كبير» بالباء الموحدة، وحجتهم أن الذنب في القمار وشرب الخمر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r15.speaker: جمهور القراء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r15.claim: All reciters reject akthar with thāʾ in the comparison, except Ibn Masʿūd's codex, which has kathīr and akthar with thāʾ in both places.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r15.anchor: وأجمعوا على رفض «أكثر» بالثاء المثلثة، إلا في مصحف عبد الله ابن مسعود فإن فيه «قل فيهما إثم كثير»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r16.speaker: قوم من أهل النظر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r16.claim: Some legal theorists infer that 2:219 prohibits wine because it says wine contains sin, and 7:33 declares sin forbidden.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#7/r16.anchor: قال قوم من أهل النظر: حرمت الخمر بهذه الآية لأن الله تعالى قد قال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects that inference: the sin within wine is forbidden, not wine itself as the argument would require.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r1.anchor: فأخبر في هذه الآية أن فيها إثما فهو حرام. قال ابن عطية: ليس هذا النظر بجيد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r2.claim: Some say the verse prohibits wine by calling it sin, and others equate wine with sin using a poet's line; al-Qurṭubī rejects both because it says wine contains sin, not that wine itself is sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r2.anchor: قلت: وهذا أيضا ليس بجيد، لأن الله تعالى لم يسم الخمر إثما في هذه الآية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r3.claim: Qatāda says this verse censures wine but its prohibition is established by another verse in Sūrat al-Māʾida; most exegetes hold this view.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r3.anchor: وهي آية «المائدة» وعلى هذا أكثر المفسرين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r4.claim: Most reciters read al-ʿafw in the accusative; Abū ʿAmr alone reads nominative, reports differ about Ibn Kathīr, and al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, and Ibn Abī Isḥāq also read nominative.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r4.anchor: قراءة الجمهور بالنصب. وقرأ أبو عمرو وحده بالرفع. واختلف فيه عن ابن كثير

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r5.speaker: النحاس وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r5.claim: Al-Naḥḥās and others prefer nominative if dhā means that which, and accusative if mādhā is one interrogative word; either form is acceptable, though the verse is interpreted accusatively.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r5.anchor: بمعنى الذي كان الاختيار الرفع، على معنى: الذي ينفقون هو العفو وجاز النصب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r6.claim: Grammarians consider both case endings sound in ماذا تعلمت أنحوا أم شعرا, while the verse is interpreted with the accusative: spend the surplus.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r6.anchor: وحكى النحويون: ماذا تعلمت: أنحوا أم شعرا؟ بالنصب والرفع، على أنهما جيدان حسنان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r7.claim: The earlier question asks whom to spend on and is answered accordingly; this question asks how much to spend, concerning ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ, who had asked about the amount.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#8/r7.anchor: كان السؤال الثاني في هذه الآية عن قدر الإنفاق وهو في شأن عمرو بن الجموح كما تقدم فإنه لما نزل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r1.claim: After 2:215 was revealed, ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ asked how much to spend, and the answer about al-ʿafw addressed that amount.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r1.anchor: قال: كم أنفق؟ فنزل «قل العفو» والعفو: ما سهل وتيسر وفضل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r2.claim: Al-ʿafw means what is easy and readily available, what is surplus without hardship; spend what remains after needs without harming yourself and becoming dependent.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r2.anchor: والعفو: ما سهل وتيسر وفضل، ولم يشق على القلب إخراجه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r3.claim: A poet's line uses al-ʿafw for leniency or what is readily given, supporting this sense of the word.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r4.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وعطاء والسدي والقرظي محمد بن كعب وابن أبي ليلى
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, ʿAṭāʾ, al-Suddī, Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Quraẓī, Ibn Abī Laylā, and others say to give the surplus after dependents' needs; Ibn ʿAbbās gives the same explanation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r4.anchor: هذا أولى ما قيل في تأويل الآية، وهو معنى قول الحسن وقتادة وعطاء والسدي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r5.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r5.claim: Mujāhid defines the giving as charity from a position of financial sufficiency, supported by the Prophet's saying that the best charity is what one gives when solvent.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: صدقة عن ظهر غنى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r6.claim: The Prophet is quoted in two formulations: the best charity is given from financial sufficiency.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r6.anchor: خير الصدقة ما كان عن ظهر غنى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r7.speaker: قيس بن سعد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r7.claim: Qays ibn Saʿd identifies the commanded spending as obligatory zakat, whereas the majority say it is voluntary spending.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r7.anchor: وقال قيس بن سعد: هذه الزكاة المفروضة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r8.speaker: جمهور العلماء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r8.claim: The majority of scholars say this command concerns voluntary expenditure rather than obligatory zakat.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r8.anchor: وقال جمهور العلماء: بل هي نفقات التطوع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r9.speaker: الكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r9.claim: Al-Kalbī says the command was abrogated by obligatory zakat: a wealthy person kept a year's provision and gave the rest, while a worker kept one day's needs and gave the rest.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r9.anchor: وقال الكلبي: كان الرجل بعد نزول هذه الآية إذا كان له مال من ذهب أو فضة أو زرع أو ضرع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r10.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r10.claim: Others say the verse remains in force and wealth carries an additional due beyond zakat; al-Qurṭubī says the apparent evidence favors the abrogated view.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r10.anchor: وقال قوم: هي محكمة، وفي المال حق سوى الزكاة. والظاهر يدل على القول الأول

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r11.speaker: المفضل بن سلمة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r11.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Salama says God's clarification of the signs here concerns spending.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r11.anchor: قال المفضل بن سلمة: أي في أمر النفقة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r12.claim: One explanation says keep enough wealth for worldly livelihood and spend the rest for the next life; another takes the syntax as inverted and urges reflection on the world's passing nature and the afterlife's permanence.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:219#9/r12.anchor: ما يصلحكم في معاش الدنيا وتنفقون الباقي فيما ينفعكم في العقبى

QASHANI:2:218-219/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:218-219/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:218-219/r3.claim: Wine signifies caprice and love of the world; gambling signifies the soul's contrivance to secure its meager share.
QASHANI:2:218-219/r3.anchor: خمر الهوى وحب الدنيا وميسر احتيال النفس في جدب الحظ

QASHANI:2:218-219/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:218-219/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:218-219/r4.claim: Their sin is veiling and distance from God.

QASHANI:2:218-219/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:218-219/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:218-219/r5.claim: Their benefits are livelihood and psychic pleasure, including relief from troubling traits and worries through heedlessness.
QASHANI:2:218-219/r5.anchor: في باب المعاش وتحصيل اللذة النفسانية، والفرح بالذهول

RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r1.claim: The question does not specify whether it asks what wine and gambling are, whether they may be used, or whether drinking is lawful; the answer about sin implies a question about permissibility.
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r1.anchor: ليس فيه بيان أنهم عن أي شيء سألوا ، فإنه يحتمل أنهم سألوا عن حقيقته وماهيته

RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r2.speaker: عمر ومعاذ ونفر من الصحابة
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r2.claim: A report of the staged prohibition says wine was initially lawful, then Umar, Muadh, and other Companions asked for a ruling because it ruins reason and wealth, prompting this verse; some drank and others abstained.
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r2.anchor: ثم إن عمر ومعاذا ونفرا من الصحابة قالوا : يا رسول الله أفتنا في الخمر

RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن عوف
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r3.claim: At a meal hosted by Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, guests drank, became intoxicated, and one recited the opening of al-Kafirun incorrectly; this occasioned the prayer-time restriction.
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r3.anchor: ثم دعا عبد الرحمن بن عوف ناسا منهم ، فشربوا وسكروا

RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r4.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص وعمر
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r4.claim: After intoxicated Ansar, including Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, boasted and exchanged insulting verse, an Ansari split Saʿd's head with a camel jaw; Umar prayed for decisive clarification, and the final prohibition followed, to which he assented.
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r4.anchor: أنشد سعد شعرا فيه هجاء للأنصار

RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r5.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r5.claim: Al-Qaffal explains the staged prohibition as compassionate gradualism: people were accustomed to wine and benefited from it, so an immediate ban would have burdened them.
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r5.anchor: والحكمة في وقوع التحريم على هذا الترتيب أن الله تعالى علم أن القوم قد كانوا ألفوا شرب الخمر

RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r6.speaker: ومن الناس من قال
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r6.claim: An alternative chronology says this verse prohibited wine first, the prayer verse then prohibited drinking at prayer time (implicitly stopping drinking since an intoxicated person cannot pray), and al-Maida made the ban emphatic.
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r6.anchor: الناس من قال بأن الله حرم الخمر والميسر بهذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r7.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r7.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas reports that this verse came down after wine had already been prohibited.
RAZI-FULL:v6p35/r7.anchor: وعن الربيع بن أنس أن هذه الآية نزلت بعد تحريم الخمر

RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r1.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r1.claim: Al-Shafiʿi defines wine broadly: every intoxicating drink is khamr.
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r1.anchor: قال الشافعي رحمه الله : كل شرب مسكر فهو خمر

RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r2.claim: Abu Hanifa defines khamr narrowly as strong grape juice that has thrown up foam.
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة : الخمر عبارة عن عصير العنب الشديد الذي قذف بالزبد

RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r3.claim: Ibn Umar reports that when wine was prohibited, it was made from five substances: grapes, dates, wheat, barley, and maize; Razi uses this to show these drinks were all called wine and covered by the prohibition.
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما ، قال : نزل تحريم الخمر يوم نزل وهي من خمسة

RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r4.claim: Razi draws three implications from Ibn Umar's report: wine included drinks from all five sources, the prohibition reached all five, and Umar treated every mind-altering drink as wine; Umar's linguistic authority strengthens the last point.
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r4.anchor: ولا شك أن عمر كان عالما باللغة ، وروايته أن الخمر اسم لكل ما خامر العقل فغيره

RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r5.claim: Al-Nuʿman ibn Bashir transmits the Prophet's statement that wine can come from grapes, dates, honey, wheat, and barley; Razi says this explicitly brings those drinks under the verse.
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r5.anchor: روى أبو داود عن النعمان بن بشير رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r6.speaker: الخطابي
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r6.claim: Al-Khattabi says the five sources are named because they were familiar then, not exclusive; maize, sult, and tree extracts share their rule, as unlisted usury goods share the rule of the six named goods.
RAZI-FULL:v6p35#2/r6.anchor: قال الخطابي رحمه الله : وتخصيص الخمر بهذه الأشياء الخمسة ليس لأجل أن الخمر لا يكون إلا من هذه الخمسة

RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r1.claim: Ibn Umar transmits the Prophet's statement that every intoxicant is wine and every intoxicant is forbidden.
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( كل مسكر خمر ، وكل مسكر حرام )

RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r2.speaker: الخطابي
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r2.claim: Al-Khattabi reads the report either as defining the Arabic or a new legal name for all intoxicants, or as declaring them legally equivalent to wine if the literal linguistic claim is impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r2.anchor: قال الخطابي : قوله عليه السلام ( كل مسكر خمر )

RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r3.claim: In response to a question about betʿ, the Prophet says every intoxicating drink is forbidden; betʿ is a honey drink, and the answer gives no allowance for small amounts.
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r3.anchor: روى أبو داود عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أنها قالت : سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن البتع ، فقال : ( كل شراب أسكر فهو حرام )

RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r4.speaker: الخطابي
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r4.claim: Al-Khattabi argues the betʿ report refutes permissive interpretations of nabidh and the claim that a small quantity of an intoxicant is lawful: the categorical answer covers the whole class and all amounts.
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r4.anchor: قال الخطابي : البتع شراب يتخذ من العسل ، وفيه إبطال كل تأويل يذكره أصحاب تحليل الأنبذة

RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r5.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet's rule that whatever intoxicates in a large amount is forbidden even in a small amount.
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r5.anchor: روى أبو داود عن جابر بن عبد الله ، قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( ما أسكر كثيره فقليله حرام )

RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r6.speaker: عائشة
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r6.claim: A report from Aisha says every intoxicant is forbidden and even a handful is unlawful if a farq of the drink intoxicates; al-Khattabi defines a farq as sixteen ratls, showing the ban covers every part.
RAZI-FULL:v6p36/r6.anchor: روى أيضا عن القاسم عن عائشة ، قالت : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : ( كل مسكر حرام

RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r1.claim: Umm Salama reports that the Prophet forbade every intoxicant and every drink that causes bodily torpor; al-Khattabi defines mufattir as inducing lassitude and numbness.
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r1.anchor: روى أبو داود عن شهر بن حوشب ، عن أم سلمة ، قالت : نهى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن كل مسكر ومفتر

RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r2.claim: Razi concludes that the hadiths collectively establish that every intoxicant is wine and forbidden.
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r2.anchor: فهذه الأحاديث كلها دالة على أن كل مسكر فهو خمر ، وهو حرام

RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r3.speaker: أهل اللغة
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r3.claim: Linguists derive khamr from covering: khimar covers the head, khamr can conceal something, and khamartu means covering a vessel; Razi takes the derivation to support concealment of the intellect.
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r3.anchor: قال أهل اللغة : أصل هذا الحرف التغطية ، سمي الخمار خمارا لأنه يغطي رأس المرأة

RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says khamr is so named because it mixes with the intellect; Razi cites Kathir's verse using the phrase dāʾ mukhāmir as evidence for the sense of intermixture.
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r4.anchor: ابن الأنباري : سميت خمرا لأنها تخامر العقل

RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r5.claim: Razi links covering and mixing: what mixes with something veils it; intoxication covers reason and blocks its light from reaching the limbs, so the name denotes an intoxicant.
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r5.anchor: لأن الشيء إذا خالط الشيء صار بمنزلة الساتر له ، فهذه الاشتقاقات دالة على أن الخمر ما يكون

RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r6.claim: Razi rejects the objection that this proves a language by analogy: derivation identifies a word's referent, just as Hanafis derive intercourse for nikah and restraint for fasting.
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r6.anchor: لأنا نقول : ليس هذا إثباتا للغة بالقياس ، بل هو تعيين المسمى بواسطة هذه الاشتقاقات

RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r7.claim: Razi says the community recognizes three wine-related verses: two use khamr, while the prayer verse refers to intoxication, confirming that khamr means an intoxicant.
RAZI-FULL:v6p37/r7.anchor: أن الأمة مجمعة على أن الآيات الواردة في الخمر ثلاثة واثنان منها وردا بلفظ الخمر

RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r1.claim: Because Umar and Muadh sought a ruling on wine as a destroyer of reason and wealth, Razi argues that anything with the same effect must be wine or share its ruling.
RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r1.anchor: سبب تحريم الخمر هو أن عمر ومعاذا قالا : يا رسول الله إن الخمر مسلبة للعقل

RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r2.claim: Razi reads al-Maida's stated harms—enmity, hatred, and diversion from remembrance and prayer—as certainly caused by intoxication, making intoxication the rationale and prohibition applicable to every intoxicant.
RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r2.anchor: ولا شك أن هذه الأفعال معللة بالسكر ، وهذا التعليل يقيني ، فعلى هذا تكون هذه الآية نصا

RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r3.claim: Abu Hanifa's side cites the blessing of making sugar and good provision from palms and grapes, arguing that the drink at issue is among God's blessings and therefore permissible.
RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r3.anchor: من الله تعالى علينا باتخاذ السكر والرزق الحسن ، وما نحن فيه سكر ورزق حسن

RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that at the Farewell Pilgrimage the Prophet declined a household nabidh offered by al-Abbas, then accepted it diluted with Zamzam and said to cut strong drinks with water.
RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r4.anchor: روى ابن عباس أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام أتى السقاية عام حجة الوداع فاستند إليها ، وقال : اسقوني

RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r5.claim: The Hanafi argument infers from the Prophet's frown and dilution with water that the drink was strong and that dilution removed its intensity.
RAZI-FULL:v6p37#2/r5.anchor: وجه الاستدلال به أن التقطيب لا يكون إلا من الشديد ، ولأن المزج بالماء كان لقطع الشدة بالنص

RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r1.claim: Razi answers the blessing argument: an indefinite mention of sugar and good provision does not prove that the disputed nabidh is meant; the earlier verse was superseded or qualified by the later prohibitions.
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r1.anchor: نكرة في الإثبات ، فلم قلتم : إن ذلك السكر والرزق الحسن هو هذا النبيذ

RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r2.claim: Razi suggests the offered nabidh may have been water with dates that slightly soured it; the Prophet's delicate taste could explain his frown without implying intoxication.
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r2.anchor: فلعل ذلك النبيذ كان ماء نبذت تمرات فيه لتذهب الملوحة فتغير طعم الماء قليلا إلى الحموضة

RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r3.claim: Razi adds that water may have been poured in to remove sourness or odor, not to reduce intoxicating strength; he judges the opposing inference too weak against his evidence.
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r3.anchor: كان المراد بصب الماء فيه إزالة ذلك القذر من الحموضة أو الرائحة

RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r4.claim: Since Companion reports conflict, Razi says they should be set aside in favor of the apparent wording of the Qur'an and the Prophet's Sunna.
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r4.anchor: وأما آثار الصحابة فهي متدافعة متعارضة ، فوجب تركها والرجوع إلى ظاهر كتاب الله وسنة الرسول

RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r5.claim: Razi argues that wine contains sin, and sin is forbidden by al-Aʿraf 7:33; together the verses prove wine prohibited.
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r5.anchor: والإثم حرام لقوله تعالى : { قل إنما حرم ربي الفواحش ما ظهر منها وما بطن والإثم

RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r6.claim: Whether ithm means punishment or the sins that deserve punishment, it can only describe what is forbidden; calling the sin greater than the benefit likewise entails prohibition.
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r6.anchor: وقد يراد به ما يستحق به العقاب من الذنوب

RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r7.speaker: منهم من قال
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r7.claim: Some deny that the verse prohibits wine: it says wine contains sin rather than that drinking is sinful, so the sin could be incidental rather than a ban on drinking.
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r7.anchor: الآية لا تدل على أن شرب الخمر إثم ، بل تدل على أن فيه إثما

RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r8.speaker: منهم من قال
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r8.claim: Some argue that the verse cannot prohibit wine because it explicitly recognizes benefits in it, and prohibited things cannot be beneficial.
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r8.anchor: أنه تعالى أثبت فيها منافع للناس ، والمحرم لا يكون فيه منفعة

RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r9.speaker: منهم من قال
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r9.claim: Some object that if this verse already prohibited wine, the later prayer restriction and al-Maida prohibition would have been unnecessary.
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r9.anchor: لو دلت هذه الآية على حرمتها فلم لم يقنعوا بها حتى نزلت آية المائدة وآية تحريم الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r10.speaker: منهم من قال
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r10.claim: Some argue that if the great sin applied whenever wine existed, its prohibition would have had to hold in every religious community.
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r10.anchor: فلو كان ذلك الإثم الكبير سببا لحرمتها لوجب القول بثبوت حرمتها في سائر الشرائع

RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r11.claim: Razi answers that the question concerns wine generally, so its sin necessarily accompanies it under every circumstance; drinking entails that forbidden consequence and is itself forbidden.
RAZI-FULL:v6p38/r11.anchor: فلما بين تعالى أن فيه إثما ، كان المراد أن ذلك الإثم لازم له على جميع التقديرات

RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r1.claim: Razi answers that immediate worldly benefit does not prevent something from being forbidden; a specific benefit does not negate the general ruling.
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r1.anchor: أن حصول النفع العاجل فيه في الدنيا لا يمنع كونه محرما

RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r2.claim: Razi cites Ibn Abbas as reporting that the verse was revealed to prohibit wine; no report says the Companions hesitated, and senior Companions could seek a stronger statement as Abraham sought reassurance about resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r2.anchor: أنا روينا عن ابن عباس أنها نزلت في تحريم الخمر ، والتوقف الذي ذكرته غير مروى عنهم

RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r3.claim: Razi answers the appeal to earlier communities by reading the statement as describing the present condition: wine harmed this community then, though it had not harmed earlier peoples.
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r3.anchor: أن قوله : { فيهما إثم كبير } إخبار عن الحال لا عن الماضي

RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r4.claim: Maysir means gambling and is the verbal noun of yasara, as mawʿid and marjiʿ derive from their verbs; yassartuhu means I gambled it.
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r4.anchor: الميسر القمار ، مصدر من يسر كالموعد والمرجع من فعلهما ، يقال يسرته إذا قمرته

RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r5.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r5.claim: Muqatil derives maysir from ease, since it takes another's wealth effortlessly, or from yasar, affluence, because gambling can make one wealthy.
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r5.anchor: قال مقاتل : اشتقاقه من اليسر لأنه أخذ لمال الرجل بيسر وسهولة من غير كد ولا تعب

RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says that in pre-Islamic times a man would wager his family and property.
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : كان الرجل في الجاهلية يخاطر على أهله وماله

RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r7.speaker: ابن قتيبة
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r7.claim: Ibn Qutayba derives maysir from apportioning: the camel is named for being divided, the butcher for portioning it, and gamblers are called yasirun because they divide its meat.
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r7.anchor: ابن قتيبة : الميسر من التجزئة والاقتسام

RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r8.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r8.claim: Al-Wahidi derives maysir from yassara li, meaning that something became due; the lot-winner is the one made entitled by the arrows.
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r8.anchor: قال الواحدي : إنه من قولهم : يسر لي هذا الشيء ييسر يسرا وميسرا إذا وجب

RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r9.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r9.claim: Al-Kashshaf describes ten named arrows used to divide a slaughtered camel into ten shares (or twenty-eight, excluding three blank arrows); each arrow had a fixed allotment.
RAZI-FULL:v6p39/r9.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : كانت لهم عشرة قداح ، وهي الأزلام والأقلام

RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r1.speaker: شاعر لم يسمه المصدر
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r1.claim: An unnamed poet lists waghad, safih, and manih as arrows with no winnings, illustrating the arrow names in the gambling practice.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r1.anchor: لي في الدنيا سهام … ليس فيهن ربيح وأساميهن وغد … وسفيح ومنيح

RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r2.claim: The arrows were shaken in a bag by a trusted person, then drawn for each player; winners took their marked meat shares, while blank-arrow players received nothing and paid for the whole camel.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r2.anchor: يجعلونها في الربابة ، وهي الخريطة ويضعونها على يد عدل ، ثم يجلجلها ويدخل يده

RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r3.claim: The players gave the meat to the poor rather than eating it themselves, took pride in doing so, and disparaged nonparticipants as baram.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r3.anchor: وكانوا يدفعون تلك الأنصباء إلى الفقراء ، ولا يأكلون منها ، ويفتخرون بذلك ويذمون

RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r4.claim: Razi reports disagreement over whether maysir names the camel-arrow game alone or all gambling.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r4.anchor: اختلفوا في أن الميسر هل هو اسم لذلك القمار المعين

RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r5.claim: A Prophetic report warns against two dice as a form of Persian gambling.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r5.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r6.speaker: ابن سيرين ومجاهد وعطاء
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r6.claim: Ibn Sirin, Mujahid, and Ata regard any game involving a stake as gambling, even children's play with nuts.

RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r7.speaker: علي
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r7.claim: Ali classifies backgammon and chess as gambling.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r7.anchor: عن علي عليه السلام أنه قال

RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r8.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r8.claim: Al-Shafiʿi permits chess when there is no wager, obscene speech, or neglect of prayer; without a transfer of money it is neither gambling nor maysir.

RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r9.speaker: أهل الاتفاق
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r9.claim: The scholars agree that wagers in races involving hoofed animals or horses are not maysir; the detailed rules are treated in the jurisprudence chapter on racing and archery.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40/r9.anchor: في الخف والحافر فبالاتفاق ليس من الميسر

RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r1.claim: Reason is humanity's noblest faculty and restrains base impulses like a camel's tether; wine removes that restraint, so drinking is among the vilest acts.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r1.anchor: أن عقل الإنسان أشرف صفاته ، والخمر عدو العقل ، وكل ما كان عدو الأشرف فهو أخس

RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r2.speaker: ابن أبي الدنيا
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abi al-Dunya recounts seeing a drunk man urinate into his hand as if performing ablution, praising Islam as light and water as pure.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r2.anchor: ذكر ابن أبي الدنيا أنه مر على سكران وهو يبول في يده ويمسح به وجهه

RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r3.speaker: العباس بن مرداس
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r3.claim: Al-Abbas ibn Mirdas explains that he refused wine despite claims it increased courage: he would not swallow his ignorance or be a leader by morning and a fool by night.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r3.anchor: وعن العباس بن مرداس أنه قيل له

RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r4.claim: Razi cites al-Maida's account of wine causing enmity and hatred and diverting people from remembrance and prayer as further harms.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r4.anchor: ما ذكره الله تعالى من إيقاع العداوة والبغضاء والصد عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r5.claim: Unlike other sins, repeated drinking strengthens desire and activity; it immerses a person in bodily pleasure and heedlessness of the afterlife, until God makes them forget themselves.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r5.anchor: فإنه كلما كان إقدامه عليه أكثر ، كان نشاطه أكثر ، ورغبته فيه أتم

RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r6.claim: Razi cites the Prophetic saying that wine is the mother of evils, since loss of reason opens the way to every vice.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r6.anchor: ولذلك قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( الخمر أم الخبائث )

RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r7.claim: Gambling's sin lies in the enmity caused by insults and disputes, taking another's property unjustly, and distracting people from remembrance and prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r7.anchor: وأما الميسر فالإثم فيه أنه يفضي إلى العداوة ، وأيضا لما يجري بينهم من الشتم والمنازعة

RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r8.claim: Wine brought merchants profit because imported wine sold at high prices, and buyers who did not haggle were considered generous and honorable.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r8.anchor: منافع الخمر أنهم كانوا يتغالون بها إذا جلبوها من النواحي ، وكان المشتري إذا ترك المماكسة

RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r9.claim: People attributed many bodily and emotional benefits to wine: strength, digestion, sexual vigor, consolation, courage, generosity, complexion, warmth, and ambition.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r9.anchor: ومنها أنه يقوي الضعيف ويهضم الطعام ويعين على الباه ، ويسلي المحزون ، ويشجع الجبان

RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r10.claim: Gambling could transfer meat to needy people; al-Waqidi says a player might win a hundred camels in one gathering and distribute the proceeds, earning praise.
RAZI-FULL:v6p40#2/r10.anchor: وذكر الواقدي أن الواحد منهم كان ربما قمر في المجلس الواحد مائة بعير

RAZI-FULL:v6p41/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p41/r1.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v6p41/r1.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read kathīr, many, arguing that wine and gambling bring numerous sins, the Prophet cursed ten connected to wine, and harms contrast with many benefits.
RAZI-FULL:v6p41/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي { كثير } بالثاء المنقوطة من فوق والباقون

RAZI-FULL:v6p41/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p41/r2.speaker: باقي القراء
RAZI-FULL:v6p41/r2.claim: The other readers say kabīr, great; Razi favors this reading because sin is magnified by greatness, supported by Quranic usage, and all readers use kabīr in the comparative phrase that follows.
RAZI-FULL:v6p41/r2.anchor: حجة الباقين أن المبالغة في تعظيم الذنب إنما تكون بالكبر لا بكونه كثيرا

RAZI-FULL:v6p41#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p41#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p41#2/r1.claim: The spending question had already been answered by identifying the recipient; it is repeated here to answer how much to give. Observing the call to generosity, people asked whether they must give everything or only part, and God accepts al-ʿafw.
RAZI-FULL:v6p41#2/r1.anchor: اعلم أن هذا السؤال قد تقدم ذكره فأجيب عنه بذكر المصرف وأعيد ههنا فأجيب عنه بذكر الكمية

RAZI-FULL:v6p41#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p41#2/r2.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v6p41#2/r2.claim: Al-Qaffal compares this answer to describing a person's beliefs and character when asked what they are like: the response gives relevant qualities rather than a literal definition.
RAZI-FULL:v6p41#2/r2.anchor: قال القفال : قد يقول الرجل لآخر يسأله عن مذهب رجل وخلقه ما فلان هذا

RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r1.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r1.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says al-ʿafw originally means increase or surplus, as in taking what is extra or people becoming more numerous.
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r1.anchor: قال الواحدي رحمه الله : أصل العفو في اللغة الزيادة ، قال تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r2.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r2.claim: Al-Qaffāl defines al-ʿafw as what is easy and available beyond one's sufficiency; Rāzī relates surplus to ease and removal of hardship.
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r2.anchor: قال القفال : العفو ما سهل وتيسر مما يكون فاضلا عن الكفاية

RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r3.claim: Rāzī explains the commanded expenditure as what remains beyond the needs of oneself, dependents, and those whose upkeep is one's responsibility.
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r3.anchor: فالغالب أن ذلك إنما يكون فيما يفضل عن حاجة الإنسان في نفسه وعياله

RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r4.claim: The spending command steers between wasteful generosity and miserliness, echoing commands to support kin and travelers, avoid waste, and spend without excess or stinginess.
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r4.anchor: أدب الناس في الإنفاق فقال تعالى لنبيه عليه الصلاة والسلام

RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r5.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r5.claim: A Prophetic report says the exemption from alms on horses and slaves lightens the obligation; instead, a quarter-tenth of other wealth is due.
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r5.anchor: قال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( عفوت لكم عن صدقة الخيل والرقيق فهاتوا ربع عشر أموالكم )

RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r6.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r6.claim: The Prophet says a person with something should begin with himself, then those he supports, proceeding outward in that order.
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r6.anchor: وقال صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( إذا كان عند أحدكم شيء فليبدأ بنفسه ، ثم بمن يعول وهكذا وهكذا )

RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r7.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r7.claim: The Prophet calls the best charity what leaves its giver self-sufficient, and says a person with only enough for bare needs is not blameworthy.
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r7.anchor: وقال / عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( خير الصدقة ما أبقت غني ولا يلام على كفاف )

RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r8.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r8.claim: Jābir reports that the Prophet angrily took a man's gold egg, his only wealth, threw it away, and said charity should come from abundance, not leave its giver begging.
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r8.anchor: وعن جابر بن عبد الله قال بينما نحن عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، إذ جاءه رجل

RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r9.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r9.claim: The Prophet kept a year's provision for his family, illustrating the need to reserve enough for dependents.
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r9.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان يحبس لأهله قوت سنة

RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r10.speaker: الحكماء
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r10.claim: The sages place virtue between excess and deficiency: lavish giving is waste, extreme parsimony is miserliness, and balance is the mean intended here.
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r10.anchor: وقال الحكماء : الفضيلة بين طرفي الإفراط والتفريط

RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r11.claim: Rāzī says Muḥammad's law balances these matters, unlike the Jews' complete severity and Christians' complete leniency, and is therefore more complete.
RAZI-FULL:v6p42/r11.anchor: فشرع اليهود مبناه على الخشونة التامة ، وشرع النصارى على المسامحة التامة ، وشرع محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم متوسط في كل هذه الأمور

RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r1.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads al-ʿafw with nominative wāw, parsing mā as a relative pronoun and the question as “what is it that they spend?”; others read it accusative as the answer “they spend the surplus.”
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ( العفو ) بضم الواو والباقون بالنصب

RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r2.claim: Abū Muslim says al-ʿafw may mean obligatory alms: the verse states the obligation generally while its details are given in the Sunna.
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r2.anchor: قول أبي مسلم يجوز أن يكون العفو هو الزكاة فجاء ذكرها ههنا على سبيل الإجمال

RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r3.claim: Another obligatory-spending view dates the command before the alms verse: people kept a year's needs and gave the remainder; the later alms verse abrogated it.
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r3.anchor: أن هذا كان قبل نزول آية الصدقات فالناس كانوا مأمورين بأن يأخذوا من مكاسبهم

RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r4.claim: The alternative view takes the spending as voluntary charity: because God leaves its amount to the addressee's judgment, it cannot be obligatory.
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r4.anchor: أن المراد من هذا الإنفاق هو الإنفاق على سبيل التطوع وهو الصدقة

RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r5.claim: Rāzī answers that God can impose a general obligation first and explain its details elsewhere, so lack of an amount here does not disprove obligation.
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r5.anchor: لا يبعد أن يوجب الله شيئا على سبيل الإجمال ، ثم يذكر تفصيله وبيانه بطريق آخر

RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r6.claim: God has clarified the kinds and destinations of spending asked about and will likewise explain all that people need in the days ahead.
RAZI-FULL:v6p42#2/r6.anchor: بينت لكم الأمر فيما سألتم عنه من وجوه الإنفاق ومصارفه

RAZI-FULL:v6p43/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p43/r1.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v6p43/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan proposes fronting and postponement: “in this world and the next” belongs with God's explaining the signs, before the purpose clause “so that you reflect.”
RAZI-FULL:v6p43/r1.anchor: قال الحسن : فيه تقديم وتأخير ، والتقدير : كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات في الدنيا والآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v6p43/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p43/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p43/r2.claim: The signs teach that wine and gambling bring worldly benefits but afterlife harms; reflection should lead people to prefer the next life over this one.
RAZI-FULL:v6p43/r2.anchor: فيعرفكم أن الخمر والميسر فيهما منافع في الدنيا ومضار في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v6p43/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p43/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p43/r3.claim: The verse also invites reflection on giving wealth for the afterlife versus retaining it for worldly life, which should again yield preference for the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v6p43/r3.anchor: أن إنفاق المال في وجوه الخير لأجل الآخرة وإمساكه لأجل الدنيا

RAZI-FULL:v6p43/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v6p43/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v6p43/r4.claim: Rāzī rejects al-Ḥasan's fronting because the straightforward readings preserve the apparent word order, and no evidence requires departing from it.
RAZI-FULL:v6p43/r4.anchor: فرض التقديم والتأخير على ما قاله الحسن يكون عدولا عن الظاهر لا لدليل وأنه لا يجوز

RAZI-FULL:v22p31/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p31/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p31/r1.claim: Razi distinguishes four answer forms: replies introduced by qul, by fa-qul, questions with no stated answer, and answers without either formula; he illustrates them with the cited questions.
RAZI-FULL:v22p31/r1.anchor: فالأغلب فيها أنه سبحانه وتعالى لما ذكر السؤال قال لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم قل

RAZI-FULL:v22p31/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p31/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p31/r2.claim: The explicit command qul functions as a seal confirming Muhammad's prophethood and honoring him as God's addressee for delivering revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v22p31/r2.anchor: لأن قوله تعالى قل كالتوقيع المحدد في ثبوت نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r1.claim: The prohibition of drinking wine is discussed at 4:43.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r1.anchor: For a discussion of the proscription of drinking wine, see 4:43c.

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r2.claim: Maysir literally names one form of gambling, while qimār is the broader term for gambling generally.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r2.anchor: Gambling renders maysir, which literally denotes one type of gambling; gambling more generally is known as qimār

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r3.claim: In maysir, players draw arrows to divide meat; the loser pays without receiving meat and is mocked, while winners give their shares to the poor as generosity.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r3.anchor: In maysir people draw arrows over meat, akin to drawing straws; the loser has to pay for the meat without getting any

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r4.claim: Commentators debate the legitimacy of various forms of play; Islamic law forbids wagering, while many frown on idle games such as chess and backgammon as spiritual distractions without outlawing them outright.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r4.anchor: In Islamic Law generally gambling in the form of wagering is forbidden, while playing games, such as chess and backgammon, as an idle pastime is frowned upon

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r5.claim: Chess and backgammon came to the West from the Islamic world and remain popular among Muslims, including many devout people.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r5.anchor: Both games in fact came to the West from the Islamic world, and not being forbidden in the technical legal sense, both are popular among Muslims

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r6.speaker: al-Qurṭubī
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r6.claim: Al-Qurṭubī lists wine’s benefits as aiding digestion, generosity, courage, facial color, sexual activity, and temporary well-being.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r6.anchor: al-Qurṭubī mentions that it helps with digestion, makes a miserly person magnanimous, gives boldness to the timid

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r7.claim: Although the verse names wine, Islamic law applies the ruling to every alcoholic drink.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r7.anchor: Islamic Law understands this ruling to apply to all alcoholic drinks

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r8.speaker: al-Qurṭubī
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r8.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says gambling can produce wealth without effort and benefit the poor through customary meat distribution by winners.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r8.anchor: As for the benefits of gambling, he mentions that one can acquire wealth without effort and that the poor can benefit

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r9.claim: Intoxication damages reason and judgment, causes quarrels, violence and promiscuity, and makes people forget God’s remembrance.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r9.anchor: intoxication leads to loss of one’s rational faculties, quarreling, violence, promiscuity, impaired judgment, and forgetting the remembrance of God

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r10.claim: Later legal philosophy treated protecting intelligence as one of the Law’s essential objectives, partly through its ruling on intoxication.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r10.anchor: the ruling on intoxication played a major part in identifying “protection of the intelligence” as one of the essential objectives of the Law

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r11.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r11.claim: Gambling creates enmity and despair, yields ill-gotten gains, and diverts people from wholesome pursuit of profit.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r11.anchor: gambling creates enmity and despair (R), produces ill-gotten gains, and is thus a diversion from the healthy and wholesome pursuit of profit

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r12.claim: Islamic financial theory invalidates some transactions for excessive risk; theorists relate that risk to the prohibition of ribā, which some discuss as a severe form of risk.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r12.anchor: certain kinds of transactions are invalid because they entail excessive risk, and this risk is related to the prohibition against ribā

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r13.claim: Al-ʿafw means what is easy or done without difficulty, and in other contexts can mean pardon or forgiveness.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r13.anchor: al-ʿafw, which means “what is easy” or “what is done without difficulty”

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r14.claim: Commentators disagree whether the spending command concerns voluntary charity or a required duty.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r14.anchor: There is disagreement over whether this refers to voluntary giving or to a required duty

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r15.speaker: Some
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r15.claim: Some consider the charity directive abrogated by the institution of zakāh.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r15.anchor: those who believe that this directive was abrogated by the institution of the alms

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r16.speaker: Others
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r16.claim: Others see no contradiction between zakāh and a continuing command to give charity.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r16.anchor: others point out that there is no contradiction between the existence of the institution of the zakāh and a command to give charity

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r17.speaker: Commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r17.claim: Charitable giving should avoid both miserliness and wastefulness and should not impoverish the giver.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r17.anchor: one should be neither miserly nor improvident in matters of charity and that one should never impoverish oneself

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r18.claim: This verse expands on 2:215 by addressing how much to give, complementing that verse’s account of charity’s recipients.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r18.anchor: This verse is seen as expanding upon the question of giving in v. 215, which describes the recipients of charity

STUDYQURAN:2:219/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r19.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r19.claim: The proper extent of charitable giving is also addressed in 17:29.
STUDYQURAN:2:219/r19.anchor: The extent of proper charitable giving is also discussed in 17:29

TAB-FULL:v3p676/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r1.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r1.claim: Al-Suddi says wine’s sin is that intoxication makes a person harm others, while gambling’s sin is withholding rights and injustice.
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r1.anchor: عن السدي: أما قوله: " {فيهما إثم كبير} [البقرة: 219] فإثم الخمر أن الرجل يشرب فيسكر فيؤذي الناس

TAB-FULL:v3p676/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r2.claim: Mujahid calls this the first criticism directed at wine.
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {قل فيهما إثم كبير} [البقرة: 219] قال: هذا أول ما عيبت به الخمر

TAB-FULL:v3p676/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains wine’s sin as the loss of religion suffered by its drinker.
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {قل فيهما إثم كبير} [البقرة: 219] يعني ما ينقص من الدين عند من يشربها

TAB-FULL:v3p676/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r4.claim: Tabari prefers that wine’s grave sin is loss of reason through intoxication, until the drinker loses awareness of his Lord; he takes this to be Ibn ʿAbbas’s meaning.
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r4.anchor: والذي هو أولى بتأويل الآية، الإثم الكبير الذي ذكر الله جل ثناؤه أنه في الخمر، والميسر

TAB-FULL:v3p676/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r5.claim: The sin in gambling is distraction from remembering God and prayer, and the enmity and hatred that arise between gamblers.
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r5.anchor: وأما في الميسر فما فيه من الشغل به عن ذكر الله، وعن الصلاة، ووقوع العداوة والبغضاء بين المتياسرين

TAB-FULL:v3p676/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r6.claim: Before prohibition, wine’s benefits included its price and the pleasure of drinking it.
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r6.anchor: فإن منافع الخمر كانت أثمانها قبل تحريمها، وما يصلون إليه بشربها من اللذة

TAB-FULL:v3p676/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r7.claim: Al-Aʿshā’s poem contrasts wine’s morning gloom and sorrow with evening pleasure and abundant wealth, as evidence of its worldly benefits.
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r7.anchor: كما قال الأعشى في صفتها. [البحر الطويل] لنا من ضحاها خبث نفس وكأبة

TAB-FULL:v3p676/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r8.claim: Ḥassān’s verse says wine leaves its drinkers kings and lions, illustrating the pleasure and perceived benefit people found in it.
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r8.anchor: وكما قال حسان: [البحر الوافر] فنشربها فتتركنا ملوكا … وأسدا ما ينهنهنا اللقاء

TAB-FULL:v3p676/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r9.claim: Gambling’s benefit was the share of camel meat won by the players, who wagered on a camel, slaughtered it when a player won, and divided it into ten lots according to the arrows.
TAB-FULL:v3p676/r9.anchor: وأما منافع الميسر فما يصيبون فيه من أنصباء الجزور، وذلك أنهم كانوا يياسرون على الجزور

TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r1.claim: Al-Aʿshā ibn Thaʿlaba’s camel-wager poem, beginning “wa-jazūru aysārin,” illustrates the camel meat won in maysir.

TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies the benefits of maysir as the portions of the camel won in gambling.
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: «المنافع هاهنا ما يصيبون من الجزور»

TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says wine’s benefits were pleasure and price, while maysir’s were its gambling winnings.
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r3.anchor: عن السدي: «أما منافعهما فإن منفعة الخمر في لذته وثمنه، ومنفعة الميسر فيما يصاب من القمار»

TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says the benefits of wine and gambling mentioned here were those they had before the two were prohibited.
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {قل فيهما إثم كبير ومنافع للناس} [البقرة: 219] قال: منافعهما قبل أن يحرما

TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the benefit was the pleasure and joy people experienced when drinking wine.
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {ومنافع للناس} [البقرة: 219] قال: يقول فيما يصيبون من لذتها، وفرحها إذا شربوها

TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r6.speaker: عظم أهل المدينة وبعض الكوفيين والبصريين
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r6.claim: Most Medinese readers and some Kufans and Basrans read kabīr with bāʾ, meaning a grave or great sin.
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r6.anchor: فقرأه عظم أهل المدينة وبعض الكوفيين، والبصريين {قل فيهما إثم كبير} [البقرة: 219] بالباء

TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r7.speaker: آخرون من أهل البصرة والكوفة
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r7.claim: Other Basran and Kufan readers understood the reading as denoting many sins, taking the singular ithm in a collective sense.
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r7.anchor: وقرأه آخرون من أهل المصرين: البصرة والكوفة: «قل فيهما إثم كبير» بمعنى الكثرة من الآثام

TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r8.claim: Tabari prefers the great-sin reading: agreement on akbar, “greater,” shows magnitude, whereas a numerical comparison would say akthar, “more.”
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r8.anchor: ولو كان الذي وصف به من ذلك الكثرة، لقيل وإثمهما أكثر من نفعهما

TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r9.claim: The comparative phrase “their sin is greater than their benefit” confirms that the earlier description means greatness, not a greater number of sins.
TAB-FULL:v3p676#2/r9.anchor: لإجماع جميعهم على قوله: {وإثمهما أكبر من نفعهما} [البقرة: 219] وقراءته بالباء

TAB-FULL:v3p679/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r1.claim: The harms of drinking wine and gambling exceed their gains: drunkenness led people to attack and fight, while gambling brought strife that led them into sin.
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r1.anchor: فأداهم ذلك إلى ما يأثمون به

TAB-FULL:v3p679/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r2.claim: The verse was revealed before explicit prohibition, and the sin attributed to wine and maysir is the sin caused by them, not a later sin of violating the ban.
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r2.anchor: بأن هذه نزلت قبل تحريم الخمر، والميسر، فكان معلوما بذلك أن الإثم الذي ذكر الله في هذه الآية

TAB-FULL:v3p679/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas is reported to say that the benefits were before prohibition and the sin came after prohibition; Tabari rejects this chronology.
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {وإثمهما أكبر من نفعهما} [البقرة: 219] قال: منافعهما قبل التحريم، وإثمهما بعدما حرما

TAB-FULL:v3p679/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r4.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r4.claim: Al-Rabīʿ likewise places the benefits before prohibition and the sin after it, an interpretation Tabari rejects.
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r4.anchor: عن الربيع: " {ومنافع للناس وإثمهما أكبر من نفعهما} [البقرة: 219] ينزل المنافع قبل التحريم، والإثم بعدما حرم

TAB-FULL:v3p679/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the sin after prohibition exceeds the benefit before it; Tabari rejects this reading of the verse.
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r5.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: " {وإثمهما أكبر من نفعهما} [البقرة: 219]

TAB-FULL:v3p679/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r6.claim: A further report from Ibn ʿAbbas says the loss to religion from wine exceeds the pleasure gained from drinking it.
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {وإثمهما أكبر من نفعهما} [البقرة: 219] يقوله: ما يذهب من الدين

TAB-FULL:v3p679/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r7.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr recounts the staged response: some avoided wine after 2:219 while others drank for its benefits; 4:43 restricted drinking around prayer, and 5:90 then ordered its avoidance, prompting ʿUmar’s exclamation.
TAB-FULL:v3p679/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: لما نزلت: " {يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر قل فيهما إثم كبير ومنافع للناس} [البقرة: 219] فكرهها قوم

TAB-FULL:v3p682/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p682/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
TAB-FULL:v3p682/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar recounts three stages: 2:219 first, then 4:43 forbidding prayer while drunk, and finally 5:90, after which the Messenger declared wine forbidden.
TAB-FULL:v3p682/r1.anchor: سمعت عبد الله بن عمر، يقول: " أنزل الله عز وجل في الخمر ثلاثا

TAB-FULL:v3p682/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p682/r2.speaker: عكرمة والحسن
TAB-FULL:v3p682/r2.claim: ʿIkrima and al-Ḥasan say the wine passages in 2:219 and 4:43 were superseded by the passage in 5:90.
TAB-FULL:v3p682/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة، والحسن، قالا: قال الله

TAB-FULL:v3p682/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p682/r3.speaker: أبو القموص زيد بن علي
TAB-FULL:v3p682/r3.claim: Abū al-Qamūṣ says wine was revealed about in three stages: after 2:219, some Muslims drank; two intoxicated men spoke incoherently in prayer, prompting 4:43, and another drinker later began lamenting the Badr dead.
TAB-FULL:v3p682/r3.anchor: عن أبي القموص زيد بن علي، قال: " أنزل الله عز وجل في الخمر ثلاث مرات

TAB-FULL:v3p683/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p683/r1.speaker: أبو القموص زيد بن علي
TAB-FULL:v3p683/r1.claim: Abū al-Qamūṣ’s report continues with the man’s verse lament for Badr’s dead; the Messenger rushed to him, he vowed never to drink again, and 5:90–91 prohibited wine, whereupon ʿUmar said they had stopped.
TAB-FULL:v3p683/r1.anchor: فبلغ ذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فجاء فزعا يجر رداءه من الفزع

TAB-FULL:v3p683/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p683/r2.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v3p683/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbī counts four wine passages: 2:219, the passage at 16:67 after which people drank, and the final prohibition in 5:90–91.
TAB-FULL:v3p683/r2.anchor: عن الشعبي، قال: " نزلت في الخمر أربع آيات: {يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر قل فيهما إثم كبير ومنافع للناس}

TAB-FULL:v3p683/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p683/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v3p683/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says drinking continued after 2:219; an intoxicated recitation at ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf’s meal led to 4:43, and later a drunken dispute at Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ’s meal led to 5:90–91 and prohibition.
TAB-FULL:v3p683/r3.anchor: عن السدي، قال: نزلت هذه الآية: " {يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر} [البقرة: 219] الآية، فلم

TAB-FULL:v3p685/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p685/r1.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p685/r1.claim: Qatada and a transmitter from Mujahid say that after this verse some people drank wine and others abstained until its prohibition in Sūrat al-Māʾida.
TAB-FULL:v3p685/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، وعن رجل، عن مجاهد، في قوله: " {يسألونك عن الخمر، والميسر،}

TAB-FULL:v3p685/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p685/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p685/r2.claim: Mujahid again describes this as the first criticism directed at wine.
TAB-FULL:v3p685/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: " {قل فيهما إثم كبير} [البقرة: 219] قال: هذا أول ما عيبت به الخمر

TAB-FULL:v3p685/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p685/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v3p685/r3.claim: Qatada says the verse initially disparaged wine and gambling without banning them; 4:43 then prohibited drunkenness around prayer, and after al-Aḥzāb 5:90 prohibited wine in every amount, whether intoxicating or not.
TAB-FULL:v3p685/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر، قل فيهما إثم كبير ومنافع للناس}

TAB-FULL:v3p685/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p685/r4.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v3p685/r4.claim: Al-Rabīʿ transmits that the Prophet called each successive revelation a sign that God was advancing the prohibition of wine, until it became forbidden.
TAB-FULL:v3p685/r4.anchor: عن الربيع، قوله: " {يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر، قل فيهما إثم كبير ومنافع للناس وإثمهما أكبر من نفعهما}

TAB-FULL:v3p686/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p686/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v3p686/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says the passage was superseded by three verses in al-Māʾida and discusses the Prophet’s wine punishment: he treated it as a hadd by his judgment, not a fixed, named hadd.
TAB-FULL:v3p686/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: " {يسألونك عن الخمر والميسر،} [البقرة: 219] الآية كلها، قال: نسخت ثلاثة في سورة المائدة

TAB-FULL:v3p687/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r1.claim: The companions ask what portion of their wealth to give as charity; God answers that they should give al-ʿafw.

TAB-FULL:v3p687/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas glosses al-ʿafw as what remains after one’s household support.
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " العفو: ما فضل عن هلك

TAB-FULL:v3p687/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r3.anchor: عن قتادة: " قل العفو: أي الفضل

TAB-FULL:v3p687/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r4.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r4.claim: ʿAṭāʾ also glosses al-ʿafw as surplus.
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r4.anchor: عن عطاء في قوله " العفو، قال: الفضل

TAB-FULL:v3p687/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r5.claim: Al-Suddī likewise glosses al-ʿafw as surplus.
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r5.anchor: عن السدي قال: " العفو، يقول: الفضل

TAB-FULL:v3p687/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r6.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses al-ʿafw as surplus wealth.
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r6.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: " {ويسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} [البقرة: 219] قال: هو الفضل فضل المال

TAB-FULL:v3p687/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says people should give what remains from that day’s earnings after providing for their families, without leaving them hungry.
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: " {ويسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} [البقرة: 219] قال: كان القوم يعملون في كل يوم

TAB-FULL:v3p687/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r8.claim: A second gloss from Ibn ʿAbbas is whatever does not show noticeably in one’s property.
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {ويسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} [البقرة: 219] يقول: ما لا يتبين في أموالكم

TAB-FULL:v3p687/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r9.speaker: طاوس
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r9.claim: Ṭāwūs says al-ʿafw is a small amount from each thing.
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r9.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن طاوس، في قول الله جل وعز: " {ويسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} [البقرة: 219] قال: اليسير من كل شيء

TAB-FULL:v3p687/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r10.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan also defines al-ʿafw as a middle level of spending: do not exhaust your wealth in giving it away.
TAB-FULL:v3p687/r10.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: " {ويسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} [البقرة: 219] يقول: لا تجهد مالك حتى ينفد للناس

TAB-FULL:v3p689/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r1.claim: Muhammad’s companions ask what wealth to give in charity, and God directs them to give al-ʿafw.

TAB-FULL:v3p689/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r2.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says al-ʿafw is an amount that does not exhaust one’s wealth and force one to ask others.
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r2.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: سألت عطاء، عن قوله: " {يسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} [البقرة: 219] قال: العفو في النفقة أن لا تجهد مالك حتى ينفد، فتسأل الناس "

TAB-FULL:v3p689/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r3.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ also explains al-ʿafw as spending without extravagance or miserliness in what is right.
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: سألت عطاء، عن قوله: " {يسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} [البقرة: 219] قال: العفو: ما لم يسرفوا، ولم يقتروا في الحق "

TAB-FULL:v3p689/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r4.claim: Mujāhid defines al-ʿafw as charity given while one remains comfortably provided for.
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r4.anchor: قال: وقال مجاهد «العفو صدقة عن ظهر غنى»

TAB-FULL:v3p689/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r5.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says al-ʿafw means not exhausting one’s wealth.
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r5.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله: " {يسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} [البقرة: 219] قال: هو أن لا تجهد مالك "

TAB-FULL:v3p689/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says to accept whatever people bring, whether little or much.
