TAB-FULL:v3p689/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {ويسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} [البقرة: 219] يقول: ما أتوك به من شيء قليل، أو كثير، فاقبله منهم "

TAB-FULL:v3p689/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r7.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r7.claim: Al-Rabīʿ interprets al-ʿafw as the good, best, and purest part of one’s wealth.
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r7.anchor: عن الربيع، قوله: " {يسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} [البقرة: 219] قال: يقول الطيب منه، يقول: أفضل مالك، وأطيبه "

TAB-FULL:v3p689/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r8.claim: Qatāda says al-ʿafw is the surplus, the best of one’s wealth.
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r8.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: كان يقول: " العفو: الفضل. يقول: أفضل مالك "

TAB-FULL:v3p689/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r9.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r9.claim: Mujāhid is also reported as identifying al-ʿafw with obligatory charity; Abū ʿĀṣim is uncertain in the transmission from Qays.
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r9.anchor: عن قيس بن سعد أو عيسى عن قيس، عن مجاهد

TAB-FULL:v3p689/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r10.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the surplus remaining after a person’s own, family, and necessary expenses; this is what the Prophet permitted as charity.
TAB-FULL:v3p689/r10.anchor: معنى العفو: الفضل من مال الرجل عن نفسه، وأهله في مئونتهم وما لا بد لهم منه

TAB-FULL:v3p692/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r1.claim: A man with one dinar is told to spend it on himself, then to provide for his family and child; with another remaining, he may decide what to do.
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r1.anchor: عن المقبري، عن أبي هريرة، قال: " قال رجل يا رسول الله عندي دينار قال: «أنفقه على نفسك؟»

TAB-FULL:v3p692/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r2.claim: The Prophet instructs a poor person to begin with himself, then dependents, and then charity to others if anything remains.
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r2.anchor: قال أخبرني أبو الزبير، أنه سمع جابر بن عبد الله، يقول: " قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إذا كان أحدكم فقيرا فليبدأ بنفسه

TAB-FULL:v3p692/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r3.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r3.claim: A man offers the Prophet a gold egg that is all he owns; the Prophet rejects this all-in charity and says charity is from sufficiency.
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r3.anchor: عن عاصم، عن عمر بن قتادة، عن محمود بن لبيد، عن جابر بن عبد الله، قال: " أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم رجل ببيضة من ذهب

TAB-FULL:v3p692/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r4.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r4.claim: The Prophet says to give from surplus, begin with those one supports, and that a person is not blamed for keeping sufficient means.
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r4.anchor: عن إبراهيم الهجري قال: سمعت أبا الأحوص يحدث عن عبد الله، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: « ارضخ من الفضل، وابدأ بمن تعول

TAB-FULL:v3p692/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r5.claim: These reports show that the Prophet permitted charity from surplus after need; al-Ṭabarī identifies that surplus as al-ʿafw.
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r5.anchor: فإذا كان الذي أذن صلى الله عليه وسلم لأمته الصدقة من أموالهم بالفضل عن حاجة المتصدق الفضل من ذلك، هو العفو

TAB-FULL:v3p692/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r6.claim: In Arabic, al-ʿafw in wealth and other things means increase and abundance; al-Ṭabarī cites the phrase in 7:95 as an example.
TAB-FULL:v3p692/r6.anchor: إذ كان العفو في كلام العرب في المال وفي كل شيء هو الزيادة والكثرة، ومن ذلك قوله جل ثناؤه: {حتى عفوا} [الأعراف: 95]

TAB-FULL:v3p693/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r1.claim: The poem’s description of fat-rich animals illustrates ʿāfiyāt as abundant in fat, supporting the sense of plenty.
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r1.anchor: ولكنا يعض السيف منا … بأسوق عافيات الشحم كوم يعني به كثيرات الشحوم.

TAB-FULL:v3p693/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r2.claim: The idiom “take what is left freely for you” means take what remains in excess after the other person’s effort; this supports al-ʿafw as surplus.
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r2.anchor: ومن ذلك قيل للرجل: خذ ما عفا لك من فلان، يراد به: ما فضل فصفا لك عن جهده بما لم تجهده.

TAB-FULL:v3p693/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r3.claim: The Prophet’s statement that the best charity is given from sufficiency confirms al-Ṭabarī’s surplus interpretation.
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r3.anchor: خير الصدقة ما أنفقت عن غنى

TAB-FULL:v3p693/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects equating al-ʿafw with obligatory zakāt: after neglect, even a person whose remaining property is only the zakāt due must pay it, which is exertion rather than surplus.
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r4.anchor: أن من حلت في ماله الزكاة المفروضة، فهلك جميع ماله إلا قدر الذي لزم ماله لأهل سهمان الصدقة، أن عليه أن يسلمه إليهم

TAB-FULL:v3p693/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r5.claim: He also rejects the view that al-ʿafw means whatever amount the owner gives, because that could include the whole wealth and so be exertion, not surplus.
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r5.anchor: وفي تسمية الله جل ثناؤه ما علم عباده وجه إنفاقهم من أموالهم عفوا، ما يبطل أن يكون مستحقا اسم جهد في حالة

TAB-FULL:v3p693/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r6.speaker: النبي
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r6.claim: When Abū Lubābah offers to give away his wealth in repentance, the Prophet says a third is enough; a similar report is transmitted about Kaʿb ibn Mālik. Al-Ṭabarī uses this against defining al-ʿafw as wealth whose surplus is not apparent.
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r6.anchor: لما قال له أبو لبابة: «إن من توبتي أن أنخلع إلى الله ورسوله من مالي صدقة» ، قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «يكفيك من ذلك الثلث»

TAB-FULL:v3p693/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r7.claim: Al-ʿafw is measured moderation: the amount the Prophet set according to one’s wealth and capacity, between extravagance and miserliness, as urged in 25:67 and 17:29.
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r7.anchor: {والذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا ولم يقتروا وكان بين ذلك قواما} [الفرقان: 67] وكما قال جل ثناؤه لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم: {ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك

TAB-FULL:v3p693/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r8.speaker: بعض أهل العلم
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r8.claim: Some scholars say the verse was abrogated by the obligatory zakāt; the dispute continues in the following segments.
TAB-FULL:v3p693/r8.anchor: ثم اختلف أهل العلم في هذه الآية: هل هي منسوخة، أم ثابتة الحكم على العباد؟ فقال بعضهم: هي منسوخة نسختها الزكاة المفروضة

TAB-FULL:v3p694/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p694/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p694/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this instruction came before charity was made obligatory.
TAB-FULL:v3p694/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: " {يسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} [البقرة: 219] قال: كان هذا قبل أن تفرض الصدقة "

TAB-FULL:v3p694/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p694/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v3p694/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says no fixed amount was prescribed at first; 7:199 followed, and named obligations were revealed afterward.
TAB-FULL:v3p694/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {يسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} [البقرة: 219] قال: لم تفرض فيه فريضة معلومة، ثم قال: {خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف

TAB-FULL:v3p694/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p694/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v3p694/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says zakāt abrogated this instruction.
TAB-FULL:v3p694/r3.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: " {يسألونك ماذا ينفقون قل العفو} [البقرة: 219] هذه نسختها الزكاة "

TAB-FULL:v3p694/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p694/r4.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v3p694/r4.claim: Other scholars hold that the verse remains in force and was not abrogated.
TAB-FULL:v3p694/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل مثبتة الحكم غير منسوخة

TAB-FULL:v3p695/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī holds, following Ibn ʿAbbās as transmitted by ʿAṭiyya, that this is guidance about approved voluntary giving, not a divine obligation; it remains in force and is neither superseded nor superseding.
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r1.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك ما قاله ابن عباس، على ما رواه عنه عطية من أن قوله: {قل العفو} [البقرة: 219] ليس بإيجاب فرض فرض من الله حقا في ماله.

TAB-FULL:v3p695/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r2.claim: This etiquette governs voluntary alms, gifts, and grants: spend first on oneself, family, and children, then direct remaining surplus to pleasing purposes.
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r2.anchor: فلا ينبغي لذي ورع ودين أن يتجاوز في صدقات التطوع وهباته وعطايا النفل وصدقته ما أدبهم به نبيه

TAB-FULL:v3p695/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r3.claim: The proper amount is balance between extravagance and stinginess, as described in the Qur’an’s account of moderate spending.
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r3.anchor: وذلك هو القوام بين الإسراف، والإقتار الذي ذكره الله عز وجل في كتابه إن شاء الله تعالى.

TAB-FULL:v3p695/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī argues abrogation is unproven: scholars agree a person may give charity, gifts, and bequests up to a third, and no evidence shows this guidance was once obligatory and then removed by zakāt.
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r4.anchor: وقد أجمع الجميع لا خلاف بينهم على أن للرجل أن ينفق من ماله صدقة، وهبة، ووصية الثلث. فما الذي دل على أن ذلك منسوخ؟

TAB-FULL:v3p695/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r5.speaker: قراء الحجاز، قراء الحرمين، عظم قراء الكوفيين، بعض قراء البصريين
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r5.claim: Most Hijazi, Ḥaramayn, and Kufan readers pronounce al-ʿafw accusative; some Basrans read it nominative. Both readings are sound, but al-Ṭabarī prefers accusative because it is more widely read and renowned.
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r5.anchor: قرأته عامة قراء الحجاز، وقراء الحرمين وعظم قراء الكوفيين: (قل العفو) نصبا، وقرأه بعض قراء البصريين: «قل العفو» رفعا.

TAB-FULL:v3p695/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r6.claim: With al-ʿafw accusative, mādhā is one word and the object of yanfiqūn; al-ʿafw is also accusative in the answer, meaning “what do they spend?—al-ʿafw.”
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r6.anchor: من قرأه نصبا جعل «ماذا» حرفا واحدا، ونصبه بقوله: {ينفقون} [البقرة: 3] على ما قد بينت قبل

TAB-FULL:v3p695/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r7.claim: With al-ʿafw nominative, mā is linked to dhā, and the reply means “what do they spend?—that which they spend is al-ʿafw.”
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r7.anchor: ومن قرأه رفعا جعل «ما» من صلة «ذا» ورفعوا العفو؛ فيكون معنى الكلام حينئذ: ما الذي ينفقون، قل الذي ينفقون العفو

TAB-FULL:v3p695/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r8.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the alternative parses are also valid Arabic: accusative al-ʿafw with mādhā as two words, or nominative al-ʿafw with mādhā as one.
TAB-FULL:v3p695/r8.anchor: ولو نصب العفو، ثم جعل «ماذا» حرفين بمعنى يسألونك ماذا ينفقون؟ قل ينفقون العفو

TAB-FULL:v4p693#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p693#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p693#2/r1.claim: As God clarified the direction and limits of spending in His way, He clarifies other signs, their rulings, lawful and forbidden matters, and their proofs as a favor to people.
TAB-FULL:v4p693#2/r1.anchor: ويوضح لكم حججها، إنعاما منه بذلك عليكم

TAB-FULL:v4p693#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p693#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v4p693#2/r2.claim: The invitation to reflect means using reason to consider God's proofs, take heed, act on their rulings, and thereby obey Him.
TAB-FULL:v4p693#2/r2.anchor: لتتفكروا بعقولكم فتتدبروا وتعتبروا بحجج الله فيها، وتعملوا بما فيها من أحكامها

TAB-FULL:v4p693#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p693#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v4p693#2/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses the phrase as “that you obey.”

TAB-FULL:v4p693#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v4p693#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v4p693#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says reflection concerns the world's passing and perishing and the hereafter's coming and permanence.
TAB-FULL:v4p693#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات لعلكم تتفكرون} [البقرة: 219] «يعني في زوال الدنيا وفنائها، وإقبال الآخرة وبقائها»

SULAMI:v1p73#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p73#2/r1.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p73#2/r1.claim: Wine and gambling are described as matters of conjecture and deception.
SULAMI:v1p73#2/r1.anchor: أنهما على فكر وخدعة ، ألا ترى أن طاوسا وسالما قرءا

SULAMI:v1p73#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p73#2/r2.speaker: طاوس وسالم
SULAMI:v1p73#2/r2.claim: On 36:55, they remarked that knowing whom the people of Paradise were distracted from would have changed how they enjoyed their occupation.
SULAMI:v1p73#2/r2.anchor: أن طاوسا وسالما قرءا : ﴿ إن أصحاب الجنة اليوم في شغل فاكهون ﴾ فقال : لو علموا

SULAMI:v1p73#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p73#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p73#2/r3.claim: Some people become transformed by the Divine Presence without realizing it.
SULAMI:v1p73#2/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : وقد تغير قوم بالحضرة وهم لا يعلمون

TABATABAI:2:219-220/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r1.claim: Khamr linguistically means any liquid made to intoxicate; its root sense is covering, since it veils the mind and its ability to distinguish good from evil.
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r1.anchor: الخمر على ما يستفاد من اللغة

TABATABAI:2:219-220/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r2.claim: The related words khimār, khammartu, and akhmartu refer respectively to a woman’s head covering, covering a vessel, and putting yeast into dough to make it rise.
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r2.anchor: ويقال لما تغطي به المرأة رأسها الخمار

TABATABAI:2:219-220/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r3.claim: Arabs originally knew wine made from grapes, dates, and barley; later varieties multiplied and all intoxicating kinds, across levels of potency, are khamr.
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r3.anchor: وقد كانت العرب لا تعرف من أقسامه إلا الخمر المعمول من العنب والتمر والشعير

TABATABAI:2:219-220/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r4.claim: Maysir means gambling and yāsir means gambler; its root connotes ease because it acquires another’s property without the toil of earning.
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r4.anchor: والميسر لغة هو القمار ويسمى المقامر ياسرا والأصل في معناه السهولة

TABATABAI:2:219-220/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r5.claim: A common Arabian form of gambling used arrows or lots to divide a slaughtered camel into twenty-eight shares among ten men; seven winning arrows awarded one to seven shares, while three losing arrows had no share and their holders paid the camel’s cost.

TABATABAI:2:219-220/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r6.claim: The ten arrows were al-fadhdh, al-tawʾam, al-raqīb, al-ḥils, al-nāfis, al-musbِل, al-muʿallā, al-manīḥ, al-sanīḥ, and al-raghd; the first seven drew assigned shares and the last three drew none.
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r6.anchor: وهي الفذ، والتوأم، والرقيب، والحلس، والنافس

TABATABAI:2:219-220/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r7.claim: A variant reading has kathīr, “much sin,” with thāʾ instead of the written reading kabīr, “great sin.”

TABATABAI:2:219-220/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r8.claim: Ithm is close to sin and describes a condition in an act or mind that slows a person from attaining good; wine and gambling have this quality.
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r8.anchor: والإثم يقارب الذنب وما يشبهه معنى وهو حال في الشيء أو في العقل يبطئ الإنسان عن نيل الخيرات

TABATABAI:2:219-220/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r9.claim: Wine causes grave medical harms to the stomach, intestines, liver, lungs, nerves, arteries, heart, and senses, as physicians’ writings and statistics document.
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r9.anchor: مضراته الطبية وآثاره السيئة في المعدة والأمعاء والكبد والرئة وسلسلة الأعصاب

TABATABAI:2:219-220/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r10.claim: Wine degrades character and leads to obscenity, violence, crimes, murder, divulging secrets, violating rights, and destroying human laws of life, especially protection of honor, life, and property.
TABATABAI:2:219-220/r10.anchor: وأما مضراته الخلقية من تشويه الخلق وتأديته الإنسان إلى الفحش

TABATABAI:2:219-220#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#2/r1.claim: The impairment of perception and intellect during intoxication and afterward is undeniable, is wine’s greatest sin and corruption, and generates its other corruptions.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#2/r1.anchor: وأما مضرته في الإدراك وسلبه العقل وتصرفه الغير المنتظم في أفكار الإنسان وتغييره مجرى الإدراك

TABATABAI:2:219-220#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#2/r2.claim: Islamic law protects sound reason and strongly forbids what disables it, including wine, gambling, fraud, and lies; wine and falsehood especially defeat reason’s governance.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#2/r2.anchor: والشريعة الإسلامية كما مرت إليه الإشارة وضعت أساس أحكامها على التحفظ على العقل السليم

TABATABAI:2:219-220#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#2/r3.claim: Actions and policies built on intoxication and lies threaten humanity and undermine happiness; a law grounded in reason and barring desire that corrupts it is a source of honor.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#2/r3.anchor: فهذه الأعمال أعني الأعمال المبطلة لحكومة العقل وعلى رأسها السياسات المبتنية على السكر والكذب هي التي تهدد الإنسانية

TABATABAI:2:219-220#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#2/r4.claim: Because sensual habits spread quickly and are hard to abandon, God legislates gradually and gently; wine prohibition is one example of that progressive approach.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#2/r4.anchor: ولذلك أن الله سبحانه شرع فيهم ما شرع

TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r1.claim: Meccan 16:67 mentions intoxicating drink and good provision; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī treats this as an early, non-explicit stage in wine’s gradual prohibition.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r1.anchor: ومن ثمرات النخيل والأعناب تتخذون منه سكرا ورزقا حسنا

TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r2.claim: The Medinan 4:43 bars drinking or drunkenness at prayer, limiting it at the best time and place; it precedes al-Baqara and al-Māʾida, since a specific ban after a universal one would reverse the gradual move from ease to severity.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r2.anchor: والآية مدنية وهي تمنع الناس بعض المنع عن الشرب والسكر

TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r3.claim: Al-Baqara 2:219 came after 4:43 and establishes prohibition by decisively calling wine a great sin, against the background of the earlier Meccan prohibition of sin.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r3.anchor: ثم نزلت آية البقرة أعني قوله تعالى

TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r4.claim: Some exegetes argue that this verse is not explicit in prohibition: sin means harm, and an item with both harm and benefit is not thereby forbidden; they say Companions differed, some abstaining and others continuing while avoiding harm, until al-Māʾida’s explicit ban.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r4.anchor: فساد ما ذكره بعض المفسرين أن آية البقرة ما كانت صريحة في الحرمة

TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r5.claim: First, sin does not simply mean harm; that definition fails for Qur’anic uses of ithm concerning associating partners, a sinful heart, liability for another’s sin, and acquired sins.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#3/r5.anchor: أما أولا فإنه أخذ الإثم بمعنى الضرر مطلقا وليس الإثم هو الضرر

TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r1.claim: Kibr compares to size what abundance compares to number; greatness and smallness are relational opposites first understood physically, then extended metaphorically to abstract matters.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r1.anchor: وأما الكبر فهو في الأحجام بمنزلة الكثرة

TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r2.claim: The author points to shirk as another sin called great, using the Qur’an’s description in 4:48 when arguing that wine’s sin is especially grave.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r2.anchor: ومن يشرك بالله فقد افترى إثما عظيما

TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r3.claim: The verse does not explain the ruling merely by harm; even on that assumption, it explicitly says the sin outweighs the benefit, so appeal to independent Companion reasoning contradicts the text.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r3.anchor: وأما ثانيا فإن الآية لم تعلل الحكم بالضرر

TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r4.claim: Even if 2:219 alone were insufficient to establish prohibition, its explicit naming of sin follows 7:33’s earlier general prohibition; wine is a complete instance of great sin.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r4.anchor: وهذه الآية قيدت الإثم بالكبر ولا يبقى مع ذلك ريب

TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r5.claim: The Qur’an calls killing, concealing testimony, and false accusation sin, but does not call these great sins; it calls wine’s sin great and describes shirk as a great sin.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r5.anchor: وقد وصف القرآن القتل وكتمان الشهادة والافتراء

TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r6.claim: After al-Baqara, al-Māʾida 5:90–91 calls wine and gambling satanic pollution and commands avoidance; its closing question shows Muslims had not fully ceased drinking before then.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r6.anchor: وذيل الكلام يدل على أن المسلمين

TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r7.claim: Gambling’s social harms and its destruction of the structure of life are visible directly; the author defers fuller discussion to Sūrat al-Māʾida.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#4/r7.anchor: وأما الميسر فمفاسده الاجتماعية وهدمه لبنيان الحياة

TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r1.claim: Benefit and harm describe things sought or avoided for something else, unlike good and evil, which describe things sought or avoided for their own sake.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r1.anchor: والنفع خلاف الضرر ويطلقان على الأمور المطلوبة لغيرها

TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r2.claim: The benefits people seek in wine and gambling are monetary gains from sale, purchase, and work, along with amusement and pleasure.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r2.anchor: والمراد بالمنافع فيهما ما يقصده الناس بهما من الاستفادات المالية بالبيع والشرى والعمل والتفكه والتلهي

TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r3.claim: Although benefits is plural earlier, the comparison says benefit in the singular: plurality does not affect greatness, so the quantity of benefits is left out of the comparison.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r3.anchor: فقيل وإثمهما أكبر من نفعهما ولم يقل

TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r4.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r4.claim: Al-Rāghib derives ʿafw from aiming at something to take it, then notes its later senses of forgiveness, effacing traces, and moderation in spending; moderation is intended here.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r4.anchor: العفو على ما ذكره الراغب قصد الشيء لتناوله ثم أوجب لحوق العنايات المختلفة الكلامية به

TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r5.claim: The intended ʿafw here is the moderate or surplus amount to spend; he adds “God knows best.”
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r5.anchor: وهذا هو المقصود في المقام، والله العالم

TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#5/r6.claim: The question and answer about what to spend match the earlier question answered by saying that whatever good is spent goes to parents and relatives.

TABATABAI:2:219-220#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#6/r1.claim: The invitation to reflection encompasses realities of existence, God and return, nature, society, ethics, and individual and communal life, namely all knowledge tied to human happiness and misery.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#6/r1.anchor: حث على البحث عن حقائق الوجود ومعارف المبدأ والمعاد

TABATABAI:2:219-220#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#6/r2.claim: Although the Qur’an commands full obedience to God and His Messenger, it does not approve receiving its rulings and teachings through blind rigidity without thought and reason.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#6/r2.anchor: غير أنه لا يرضى أن تؤخذ الأحكام والمعارف التي يعطيها على العمى والجمود المحض من غير تفكر وتعقل

TABATABAI:2:219-220#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#6/r3.claim: Tabyīn here means uncovering the reasons behind rulings and clarifying the foundations of teachings and knowledge.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#6/r3.anchor: وكأن المراد بالتبيين هو الكشف عن علل الأحكام

TABATABAI:2:219-220#7/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#7/r6.speaker: علي بن يقطين
TABATABAI:2:219-220#7/r6.claim: Ali ibn Yaqtin recounts the Mahdi questioning Abu al-Hasan about wine's Qur'anic prohibition; the Imam identifies Qur'anic sin with wine and cites 2:219, and the Mahdi acknowledges the Ahl al-Bayt's learning.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#7/r6.anchor: عن علي بن يقطين قال سأل المهدي أبا الحسن عليه السلام عن الخمر هل هي محرمة

TABATABAI:2:219-220#7/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#7/r7.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:2:219-220#7/r7.claim: One of the two Imams describes sin as a house with a door and lock, and wine as its key.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#7/r7.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أحدهما عليهما السلام قال إن الله جعل للمعصية بيتا

TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r1.claim: The Prophet calls wine the head of every sin.

TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r2.claim: When Quraysh ask which sin is greatest, Imam al-Baqir answers that drinking wine is the greatest.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r2.anchor: عن إسماعيل قال أقبل أبو جعفر عليه السلام في المسجد الحرام فنظر إليه قوم من قريش

TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r3.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r3.claim: One of the two Imams says no act disobeys God more severely than drinking intoxicants, which can lead an unaware drinker to abandon prayer and commit incest.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r3.anchor: عن أبي البلاد عن أحدهما عليهما السلام قال ما عصي الله بشيء أشد من شرب المسكر

TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r4.claim: Answering why wine is forbidden despite its pleasure, Imam al-Sadiq says it is the mother of abominations and head of evil, removing reason and leading to every sin.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r4.anchor: سأل زنديق أبا عبد الله عليه السلام لم حرم الله الخمر ولا لذة أفضل منها؟ قال حرمها

TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r5.claim: The reports explain one another, and experience and reflection confirm them.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r5.anchor: أقول والروايات تفسر بعضها بعضا، والتجارب والاعتبار يساعدانها

TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r6.claim: The Prophet curses ten participants in the wine trade, from its grower and keeper through its drinker, seller, buyer, and consumer of its price.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r6.anchor: عن جابر عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال لعن رسول الله في الخمر عشرة

TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r7.claim: The Prophet curses anyone who sits at a table where wine is being drunk.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r7.anchor: وفي الكافي والمحاسن عن الصادق عليه السلام قال قال رسول الله عليه السلام

TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r8.claim: The Prophet says God will not look on Judgment Day at four people: a disobedient child, a benefactor who reminds recipients of the gift, a denier of predestination, and a habitual wine drinker.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r8.anchor: وفي الخصال بإسناده عن أبي أمامة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r9.claim: A prophetic report says a wine drinker will receive an equal measure of boiling punishment in the afterlife, whether forgiven or punished, and describes the drinker's appearance on Judgment Day.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r9.anchor: وفي الأمالي لابن الشيخ بإسناده عن الصادق عليه السلام عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r10.claim: Imam al-Baqir says wine drinkers will be given a hellish drink made from the discharge of prostitutes, which he describes as pus and thick mixed blood.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#8/r10.anchor: في تفسير القمي عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال حق على الله أن يسقي من يشرب الخمر

TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r1.claim: The threats in the wine reports may be supported by the Qur'anic description of the sinner's food and boiling punishment.

TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r2.speaker: أبو الحسن عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r2.claim: Imam al-Rida identifies al-maysir as gambling.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r2.anchor: وفي الكافي عن الوشا عن أبي الحسن عليه السلام قال سمعته يقول الميسر هو القمار

TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r3.claim: Numerous reports support identifying al-maysir with gambling, a meaning the author regards as beyond doubt.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r3.anchor: أقول والروايات في هذا المعنى كثيرة لا غبار عليها

TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that companions ordered to spend in God's cause asked how much to give; the verse answered that they should give the surplus, after one man had given away even what he needed to eat.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس إن نفرا من الصحابة حين أمروا بالنفقة في سبيل الله أتوا النبي

TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r5.speaker: يحيى
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r5.claim: Yahya reports that Muadh ibn Jabal and Tha'laba, supporting dependents and servants, asked the Prophet how much of their property to spend, prompting the verse.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r5.anchor: عن يحيى أنه بلغه أن معاذ بن جبل وثعلبة أتيا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r6.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r6.claim: Imam al-Sadiq glosses al-afw as the middle amount.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r6.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام العفو الوسط

TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r7.speaker: الباقر والصادق عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r7.claim: Imams al-Baqir and al-Sadiq explain al-afw as enough for subsistence.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r7.anchor: عن الباقر والصادق عليهما السلام الكفاف

TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r8.speaker: أبو بصير
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r8.claim: A report from Abu Basir glosses al-afw as moderation or a reasonable amount.

TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r9.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r9.claim: Imam al-Sadiq relates the spending verse to the description of those who spend neither extravagantly nor stingily, saying this is the moderate course.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r9.anchor: وفيه أيضا عن الصادق عليه السلام في الآية الذين إذا أنفقوا لم يسرفوا وكان بين ذلك قواما

TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r10.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r10.claim: Imam al-Baqir defines al-afw as what remains beyond a year's provision.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r10.anchor: في المجمع عن الباقر عليه السلام العفو ما فضل عن قوت السنة

TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r11.claim: The reported glosses are compatible; the annual-provision account specifies an instance of the meaning.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r11.anchor: أقول والروايات متوافقة، والأخيرة من قبيل بيان المصداق

TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r12.claim: Reports on charity's virtues, proper manner, recipients, and amount are too numerous to count and will be cited where relevant later.
TABATABAI:2:219-220#9/r12.anchor: والروايات في فضل الصدقة وكيفيتها وموردها وكميتها فوق حد الإحصاء

AKHFASH:v1p185/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p185/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p185/r1.claim: If ماذا is treated as ما alone, العفو is accusative as the object of ينفقون: the question is what they spend, and the answer is that they spend surplus.
AKHFASH:v1p185/r1.anchor: واذا نصبت فكأنه قال: "ما ينفقون" فقال: "ينفقون العفو"

AKHFASH:v1p185/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p185/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p185/r2.claim: If ذا is the relative الذي, العفو is nominative as the predicate: what they spend is surplus; compare the two analyses of ماذا in 16:24 and 16:30.
AKHFASH:v1p185/r2.anchor: وان جعلت بمنزلة "الذي" فهو مرفوع بخبر الابتداء

AKHFASH:v1p185/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p185/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p185/r3.claim: The alternative case can also be licensed by meaning: a nominative answer can mean 'what I did was good,' while an accusative answer can mean 'I did good.'
AKHFASH:v1p185/r3.anchor: وقد يكون اذا جعلها بمنزلة "ما" وحدها الرفع على المعنى

AKHFASH:v1p185/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p185/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p185/r4.claim: In the poem دعي ماذا علمت, ما and ذا together mean ما alone; taking ذا as الذي would make دعي ما الذي علمت ungrammatical.
AKHFASH:v1p185/r4.anchor: دعي ماذا علمت سأتقيه * ولكن بالمغيب نبئيني

AKHFASH:v1p185/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p185/r5.speaker: أهل التأويل
AKHFASH:v1p185/r5.claim: Exegetes say the disbelievers denied that God sent anything and asked what the people themselves claimed was revealed; the author finds this like 'they are your brothers' in 2:220.
AKHFASH:v1p185/r5.anchor: وقال أهل التأويل في قوله {ماذا أنزل ربكم قالوا أساطير الأولين} لأن الكفار جحدوا أن يكون ربهم أنزل شيئا

TABRISI:2:219-220/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220/r1.claim: The Kufans count two verses across 2:219–220 and treat تتفكرون as a verse ending; the other regional count has one verse and does not count that word as a verse ending.
TABRISI:2:219-220/r1.anchor: آيتان في الكوفي وآية واحدة فيما عد الكوفي تتفكرون آية وتركها غيره

TABRISI:2:219-220/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220/r2.speaker: أهل الكوفة غير عاصم
TABRISI:2:219-220/r2.claim: Kufan readers other than ʿĀṣim read إثم كثير with thāʾ, while the other readers use bāʾ and read إثم كبير.
TABRISI:2:219-220/r2.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة غير عاصم إثم كثير بالثاء والباقون بالباء

TABRISI:2:219-220/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
TABRISI:2:219-220/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr alone reads العفو in the nominative; the other readers use the accusative.
TABRISI:2:219-220/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحده قل العفو بالرفع والباقون بالنصب

TABRISI:2:219-220/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220/r4.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:2:219-220/r4.claim: Abū ʿAlī supports كبير because كبير contrasts with صغير, while كبير denotes a grave sin; Qur'anic examples use صغير and كبير and call grave sins كبائر. The comparison أكبر also supports كبير rather than كثير.
TABRISI:2:219-220/r4.anchor: حجة من قرأ بالباء أن يقول الباء أولى لأن الكبر مثل العظم ومقابله الصغر

TABRISI:2:219-220/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220/r5.claim: The كبير reading is supported by Qur'anic wording about every small and great matter being recorded and by references to major sins.
TABRISI:2:219-220/r5.anchor: وقد استعملوا في الذنب إذا كان موبقا الكبيرة

TABRISI:2:219-220/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220/r6.claim: The كثير reading is supported by the following verse's account of Satan causing enmity and obstructing prayer and remembrance through wine and gambling, and a report that the Prophet cursed ten involved with wine.
TABRISI:2:219-220/r6.anchor: وجه قراءة من قرأ بالثاء أنه قد جاء فيهما إنما يريد الشيطان أن يوقع بينكم العداوة والبغضاء

TABRISI:2:219-220/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220/r7.claim: The argument for كثير cites the Qur'anic description of Satan's effects through wine and gambling.
TABRISI:2:219-220/r7.anchor: إنما يريد الشيطان أن يوقع بينكم العداوة والبغضاء

TABRISI:2:219-220/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220/r8.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:219-220/r8.claim: A Prophetic report curses ten wine-related parties: buyer and recipient, presser and commissioner, server and requester, carrier and recipient, and the consumer of its price.
TABRISI:2:219-220/r8.anchor: لعن الرسول في الخمر عشرة مشتريها والمشتراة له وعاصرها والمعصورة له وساقيها والمستقي لها

TABRISI:2:219-220/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220/r9.claim: For accusative العفو, ما ذا is one interrogative expression and ماذا ينفقون functions like ما ينفقون, asking what they spend; the answer is accusative.
TABRISI:2:219-220/r9.anchor: أن قولهم ماذا يستعمل على ضربين أحدهما

TABRISI:2:219-220/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220/r10.claim: The single-expression analysis is illustrated by the idiom عما ذا تسأل and a poem asking ماذا بال نسوتكم, meaning ما بال نسوتكم.
TABRISI:2:219-220/r10.anchor: قول العرب عما ذا تسئل أثبتوا الألف في ما لما كان ما مع ذا بمنزلة اسم واحد

TABRISI:2:219-220/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220/r11.claim: For nominative العفو, ذا means الذي, so the question means what is it that they spend; العفو answers as the predicate of an omitted subject.
TABRISI:2:219-220/r11.anchor: أن يجعل ماذا على الضرب الآخر فيكون تقديره ما الذي ينفقون فجوابه العفو على أن يكون خبر مبتدأ محذوف

TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r1.claim: The question about what God sent down is cited as a parallel for reading ذا as a relative pronoun.
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r1.anchor: ماذا أنزل ربكم قالوا أساطير الأولين

TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r2.claim: Sībawayh allows ذا to mean الذي only in this construction; the Kufans permit it elsewhere and cite poetry and Moses' question, but Tabrisi rejects their evidence because the quoted phrases may be circumstantial expressions.
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r2.anchor: سيبويه لا يجوز أن يكون ذا بمنزلة الذي

TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r3.claim: The Kufan evidence from Moses' question does not establish a relative-clause use, since بيمينك may be a circumstantial phrase.
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r3.anchor: يجوز أن يكون ظرفا في موضع الحال

TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r4.claim: Khamr derives from covering: foliage, a head covering, a concealing crowd, something mixed into a disease, and covering a vessel all illustrate the root.

TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r5.speaker: كثير
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r5.claim: The poet Kathīr uses مخامر for an affliction that mingles or remains mixed in, illustrating the root sense of khamr.
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r5.anchor:
كثير:
هنيئا مريئا غير داء مخامر لعزة

TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r6.claim: A small palm-fiber prayer mat is called khumra because it covers the face from the ground during prostration.

TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj recounts that Abū al-Aswad al-Duʾalī realized an intoxicant sold under another name was wine's sibling; he cited a poem saying both were nursed by the same mother.
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج وقد لبس على أبي الأسود الدؤلي

TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r8.claim: Maysir is gambling, named from yusr because the winner's share becomes due; the gambler is called yāsir because lots determine what is owed.
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r8.anchor: من اليسر وهو وجوب الشيء لصاحبه

TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r9.claim: Another derivation links maysir to division: whatever is divided is yassartahu; yāsir and maysir can also name the camel being divided.
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r9.anchor: وقيل أخذ من التجزئة لأن كل شيء

TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r10.claim: A further derivation connects maysir to ease, since people joined to make sharing the camel easier, though they did so by gambling.
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r10.anchor: وقيل أخذ من اليسر وهو السهولة

TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r11.claim: Al-ʿafw means increase or surplus, as in the description of a people increasing in number.
TABRISI:2:219-220#2/r11.anchor: العفو مأخوذ من الزيادة ومنه قيل حتى عفوا

TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r1.claim: Al-ʿafw can denote excess; the cited description of sheep as fat-rich supports the sense of surplus.
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r1.anchor: ولكنا يعض السيف منا بأسوق عافيات الشحم كوم أي زائدات الشحم

TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r2.claim: Al-ʿafw can also mean what is left or relinquished; the Prophet’s waived horse alms illustrate property one can dispense with.
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r2.anchor: أي تركتها فيكون العفو المتروك غنى عنه

TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r5.claim: The governing word for “in this world and the hereafter” is يبين; it may instead depend on تتفكرون.
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r5.anchor: العامل في الطرف من قوله في الدنيا والآخرة قوله يبين أي مبين لكم الآيات في أمر الدنيا والآخرة

TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r7.speaker: جماعة من الصحابة
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r7.claim: A group of Companions asked the Prophet about wine and gambling because they destroy reason and strip away wealth; this verse was revealed in response.
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r7.anchor: نزلت في جماعة من الصحابة أتوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالوا أفتنا في الخمر والميسر

TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r8.claim: The apparent sense in Imami reports, also adopted by al-Shafiʿi, is any intoxicating drink that covers the mind; even a little is forbidden if much intoxicates.
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r8.anchor: وهي كل شراب مسكر مخالط للعقل مغط عليه

TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r9.claim: Abu Hanifa restricts khamr to grape juice once it ferments and becomes strong.
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r9.anchor: وقيل الخمر عصير العنب إذا اشتد وغلى وهو مذهب أبي حنيفة

TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود ومجاهد وقتادة والحسن
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Masʿud, Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Hasan say maysir means all gambling; Imami reports count children’s nut games as gambling too.
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r10.anchor: عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود ومجاهد وقتادة والحسن وهو المروي عن أئمتنا

TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r11.claim: Kabir here means a great and abundant burden of sin.
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r11.anchor: أي وزر عظيم وكثير من الكثرة

TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r12.claim: Wine’s benefits were its sale proceeds and the pleasure, exhilaration, and strength people thought drinking brought.
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r12.anchor: منفعة الخمر ما كانوا يأخذونه في أثمانها وما يحصل من اللذة والطرب والقوة بشربها

TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r13.claim: Gambling’s benefit was winning another person’s money without labor or hardship, with the winner able to support the poor.
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r13.anchor: ومنفعة القمار هو أن يفوز الرجل بمال صاحبه من غير كد ولا مشقة ويرتفق به الفقراء

TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r14.claim: Their sin outweighs their worldly benefit because it incurs God’s displeasure in the afterlife, leaving only a small, impermanent gain.
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r14.anchor: لأن نفعهما في الدنيا وما يحصل من الإثم بهما يوجب سخط الله في الآخرة

TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r15.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r15.claim: Al-Hasan infers prohibition because harm exceeds benefit and because the verse calls it sin, which another verse forbids; its description as a major sin independently supports prohibition.
TABRISI:2:219-220#3/r15.anchor: قال الحسن: في الآية تحريم الخمر من وجهين

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r1.claim: Wine is called ithm in Arabic, as the cited poem shows; the verse’s description of it as a great sin also supports prohibition.
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r1.anchor: شربت الإثم حتى ضل عقلي كذاك الإثم يصنع بالعقول

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r2.claim: Calling the sin great is itself evidence of prohibition, since a major sin is prohibited without disagreement.

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak reads the comparison across time: after prohibition, their sin is greater than their benefit before prohibition.
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r3.anchor: إثمهما بعد تحريمهما أكبر من نفعهما قبل تحريمهما

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says both refer to the pre-prohibition period: the sin caused by them exceeds their benefit.
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r4.anchor: كلاهما قبل التحريم يعني أن الإثم الذي يحدث من أسبابهما أكبر من نفعهما

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r5.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r5.claim: Qatada says this verse does not establish prohibition; al-Maʾida 5:90 does.
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة هذه الآية لا تدل على تحريمهما

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r6.claim: The question means, “What thing should they spend?”

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r7.speaker: عمرو بن الجموح
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r7.claim: ʿAmr ibn al-Jamuh asked what should be spent in jihad; another report says the question concerned charity.
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r7.anchor: السائل عمرو بن الجموح سأل عن النفقة في الجهاد

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada interpret al-ʿafw as what remains beyond family needs and sufficiency.
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r8.anchor: ما فضل عن الأهل والعيال والفضل عن الغنى عن ابن عباس وقتادة

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r9.speaker: الحسن وعطاء
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r9.claim: Al-Hasan and ʿAtaʾ take al-ʿafw as the moderate amount, avoiding extravagance and stinginess; this is also transmitted from Abu Abd Allah.
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r9.anchor: أن العفو الوسط من غير إسراف ولا إقتار عن الحسن وعطا وهو المروي عن أبي عبد الله

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر الباقر
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r10.claim: Abu Jaʿfar al-Baqir says al-ʿafw is what remains after a year’s provisions; he says the zakat verse abrogated this, as al-Suddi also held.
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r10.anchor: أن العفو ما فضل عن قوت السنة عن أبي جعفر الباقر ع

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r11.claim: A fourth, unattributed interpretation takes al-ʿafw to mean the finest and best property.

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r12.claim: The demonstrative’s kāf is singular because the address is to the Prophet, while including the community.
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r12.anchor: إنما وحد الكاف لأن الخطاب للنبي ويدخل فيه الأمة

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r13.claim: Another construal makes the address “thus, people of this group.”

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r14.claim: The signs are proofs concerning spending, wine, and gambling.
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r14.anchor: أي الحجج في أمر النفقة والخمر والميسر

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r15.claim: Another explanation takes the signs to mean all the rulings of Islam.

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r16.claim: Here “this world and the hereafter” means their affairs.
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r16.anchor: أي في أمر الدنيا وأمر الآخرة

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r17.claim: Pondering worldly and afterlife affairs shows that this life is trial, hardship, and passing, while the afterlife is recompense and permanence, prompting renunciation of one and desire for the other.
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r17.anchor: فتعلمون أن الدنيا دار بلاء وعناء وفناء والآخرة دار جزاء وبقاء

TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r18.claim: Alternatively, “in this world and the hereafter” attaches to “He makes clear”: God explains signs in those matters so people ponder, showing He intends reflection whether or not they actually reflect.
TABRISI:2:219-220#4/r18.anchor: أي كما يبين لكم الآيات في الخمر والميسر

FARRA:v1p140/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p140/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p140/r8.claim: العفو is the surplus wealth one spends; al-Farrāʾ says the zakāt obligation later abrogated this ruling.
FARRA:v1p140/r8.anchor: وجه الكلام فيه النصب، يريد: قل ينفقون العفو. وهو فضل المال

THALABI:v2p141/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p141/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب ومعاذ بن جبل
THALABI:v2p141/r1.claim: Umar, Muadh, and several Ansar asked the Prophet for a ruling on wine and gambling, saying they destroy reason and consume wealth; the verse was revealed in response.
THALABI:v2p141/r1.anchor: نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب (رضي الله عنه) ومعاذ بن جبل ونفر من الأنصار أتوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v2p141/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p141/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p141/r2.claim: The source describes staged prohibition: an earlier Meccan verse mentioned intoxicating drink from dates and grapes, when Muslims still drank lawfully; 2:219 then identified the greater sin.
THALABI:v2p141/r2.anchor: هي أن الله أنزل في الخمر أربع آيات نزلت بمكة ومن ثمرات النخيل والأعناب تتخذون منه سكرا

THALABI:v2p141/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p141/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p141/r3.claim: The Prophet said God was moving toward prohibiting wine; some abandoned it, while others continued for its benefits and tried to avoid its harms.
THALABI:v2p141/r3.anchor: فلما نزلت هذه الآية قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن ربكم تقدم في تحريم الخمر»

THALABI:v2p141/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p141/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p141/r4.claim: At Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf's meal, companions became intoxicated; the prayer leader recited Surat al-Kafirun but omitted la, prompting the ban on prayer while drunk.
THALABI:v2p141/r4.anchor: وحضرت صلاة المغرب فقدموا بعضهم ليصلي بهم فقرأ قل يا أيها الكافرون أعبد ما تعبدون إلى آخر السورة فحذف لا

THALABI:v2p141/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p141/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
THALABI:v2p141/r5.claim: After the prayer incident, Umar said successive warnings suggested wine would soon be prohibited altogether; some abandoned it because it interfered with prayer.
THALABI:v2p141/r5.anchor: فقال عمر: إن الله يقارب في النهي عن شرب الخمرة، فلا أراه إلا وسيحرمها

THALABI:v2p142/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p142/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p142/r1.claim: Some continued drinking outside prayer. One Muslim drank, lamented those killed at Badr in verse, and vowed never to drink again when the Prophet rushed over angrily.
THALABI:v2p142/r1.anchor: وكانوا يتركونها أوقات الصلاة، ويشربونها في غير حين الصلاة إلى أن شربها رجل من المسلمين فجعل ينوح على قتلى بدر

THALABI:v2p142/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p142/r2.speaker: علي
THALABI:v2p142/r2.claim: Ali reports that intoxicated Hamza slaughtered and ate Ali's camels, which Ali planned to sell to fund his marriage to Fatima; Hamza insulted Ali's lineage, and the Prophet compensated him.
THALABI:v2p142/r2.anchor: [قال علي:] فجئت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو في بيت أم سلمة معه مولاه زيد

THALABI:v2p143/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p143/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p143/r1.claim: The morning after Hamza's drunken attack, he apologized; the Prophet said he had asked God, who had forgiven him.
THALABI:v2p143/r1.anchor: فلما أصبح غدا حمزة على رسول الله يعتذر فقال: مه يا عم فقد سألت الله فعفا عنك

THALABI:v2p143/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p143/r2.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
THALABI:v2p143/r2.claim: Atban's feast included wine and drunken boasting; Saʿd recited a poem insulting the Ansar, and an Ansari wounded him with a camel jawbone.
THALABI:v2p143/r2.anchor: قالوا: واتخذ عتبان بن مالك طعاما فدعا رجالا من المسلمين فيهم سعد بن أبي وقاص

THALABI:v2p143/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p143/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
THALABI:v2p143/r3.claim: After Saʿd complained, Umar prayed for a clear ruling; final prohibition came in al-Maida days after the Trench, and Umar declared they had stopped.
THALABI:v2p143/r3.anchor: فقال عمر (رضي الله عنه) : اللهم بين لنا رأيك في الخمر بيانا وافيا، فأنزل الله تحريم الخمر

THALABI:v2p143/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p143/r4.speaker: أنس
THALABI:v2p143/r4.claim: Anas says wine was cherished but, at its prohibition, people poured it into streets or broke and washed vessels; after rain Medina's alleys smelled of wine.
THALABI:v2p143/r4.anchor: قال أنس: حرمت ولم يكن يومئذ للعرب عيش أعجب منها إليهم يوم حرمت عليهم، ولم يكن شيء أثقل عليهم

THALABI:v2p143/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p143/r5.speaker: سفيان الثوري وأبو حنيفة وأبو يوسف وأكثر أهل الرأي
THALABI:v2p143/r5.claim: This legal school narrowly defines khamr as naturally fermented grape or date juice, without fire; other drinks are not khamr by name.
THALABI:v2p143/r5.anchor: وهذا مذهب سفيان الثوري وأبي حنيفة وأبي يوسف وأكثر أهل الرأي

THALABI:v2p143/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p143/r6.speaker: سفيان الثوري وأبو حنيفة وأبو يوسف وأكثر أهل الرأي
THALABI:v2p143/r6.claim: They say cooked juice is lawful though disliked after two-thirds evaporate; when two-thirds evaporate and one-third remains, drinking and selling are allowed unless intoxicating.
THALABI:v2p143/r6.anchor: فإن طبخ حتى يذهب ثلثاه وبقي ثلثه فهو حلال مباح شربه وبيعه إلا أن المسكر منه حرام

THALABI:v2p143/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p143/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p143/r7.claim: They support this with Abu Hurayra's report that the Prophet said wine comes from the date palm and grapevine.
THALABI:v2p143/r7.anchor: واحتجوا في ذلك بما روى أبو كثير عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «الخمر من هاتين الشجرتين

THALABI:v2p144/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p144/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
THALABI:v2p144/r1.claim: Ibn Sirin reports Umar told an official to cook the drink until two-thirds evaporated, leaving one share for people and removing the devil's two shares.
THALABI:v2p144/r1.anchor: وعن ابن سيرين أن عبد الله بن سويد الخطمي قال: كتب إلينا عمر بن الخطاب: أما بعد فاطبخوا شرابكم

THALABI:v2p144/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p144/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
THALABI:v2p144/r2.claim: Anas reports a story that Noah and Satan disputed ownership of the grapevine and settled that Noah would have one-third and Satan two-thirds.
THALABI:v2p144/r2.anchor: وعن أنس بن سيرين قال: سمعت أنس بن مالك يقول إن نوحا عليه السلام نازعه

THALABI:v2p144/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p144/r3.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
THALABI:v2p144/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib identifies the drink Umar permitted as one cooked until two-thirds evaporated and one-third remained.
THALABI:v2p144/r3.anchor: داود قال: سألت سعيد بن المسيب ما الرب الذي أحله عمر (رضي الله عنه)

THALABI:v2p144/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p144/r4.speaker: موسى الأموي
THALABI:v2p144/r4.claim: Musa al-Umawi is reported to have drunk tala after two-thirds evaporated and one-third remained.
THALABI:v2p144/r4.anchor: وعن قيس بن أبي حدث عن موسى الأموي أنه كان يشرب من الطلاء ما ذهب ثلثاه وبقي ثلثه

THALABI:v2p144/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p144/r5.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
THALABI:v2p144/r5.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib says tala cooked down to one-third is unobjectionable; al-Miswar agrees.
THALABI:v2p144/r5.anchor: وعن يحيى بن سعيد عن سعيد بن المسيب قال: إذا طبخ الطلاء على الثلث فلا بأس

THALABI:v2p144/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p144/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p144/r6.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi understands these reports to concern a nonintoxicating remainder; he cites Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz's order and rule that every intoxicant is forbidden.
THALABI:v2p144/r6.anchor: وقال الثعلبي: والذي عندي أن هذه الأخبار وردت في ثلث غير مسكر

THALABI:v2p144/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p144/r7.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
THALABI:v2p144/r7.claim: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz told officials not to drink tala until two-thirds evaporated and added that every intoxicant is forbidden.
THALABI:v2p144/r7.anchor: قال: كتب إلينا عمر بن عبد العزيز: لا تشربوا من الطلاء حتى يذهب ثلثاه ويبقى ثلثه، كل مسكر حرام

THALABI:v2p144/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p144/r8.speaker: إسماعيل بن علية وجماعة من أهل العراق
THALABI:v2p144/r8.claim: Some say even slight cooking makes juice tala; Ismail ibn Ulayya and a group of Iraqis hold this view.
THALABI:v2p144/r8.anchor: وقال قوم: إذا طبخ العصير أدنى طبخ فصار طلاء وهو قول إسماعيل بن علية

THALABI:v2p144/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p144/r9.speaker: عيسى بن إبراهيم
THALABI:v2p144/r9.claim: Isa ibn Ibrahim says no nabidh is forbidden, raw or cooked, except strong raw grape juice that has not been watered and has transformed into wine.
THALABI:v2p144/r9.anchor: وروي عن عيسى بن إبراهيم أنه لا يحرم شيئا من الأنبذة لا الني منها ولا المطبوخ إلا شراب واحد

THALABI:v2p144/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p144/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p144/r10.claim: Abu Burda ibn Sahl reports the Prophet told people to drink from vessels but not to become intoxicated.
THALABI:v2p144/r10.anchor: عن أبي بردة بن سهل قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «اشربوا في الظروف ولا تسكروا»

THALABI:v2p144/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p144/r11.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السدي
THALABI:v2p144/r11.claim: Al-Suddi calls that hadith munkar: Abu al-Ahwas erred, Samak's companions did not rely on him, and Samak was weak and accepted prompting.
THALABI:v2p144/r11.anchor: قال أبو عبد الرحمن السدي الحديث منكر، غلط فيه أبو الأحوص سلام بن سليم، لا نعلم أحدا كان يعول عليه

THALABI:v2p144/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p144/r12.speaker: أحمد
THALABI:v2p144/r12.claim: Ahmad says Abu al-Ahwas erred; Sharik differs in chain and wording, reporting that the Prophet prohibited several vessel types.
THALABI:v2p144/r12.anchor: قال أحمد: قيل: كان أبو الأحوص غلى في هذا الحديث. خالفه شريك في إسناده ولفظه

THALABI:v2p144/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p144/r13.speaker: قرصافة عن عائشة
THALABI:v2p144/r13.claim: They also invoke a report attributed to Aisha through Qursafa that permits drinking if one does not become intoxicated.
THALABI:v2p144/r13.anchor: وأجمعوا أيضا بما أسندوا إلى سماك عن قرصافة امرأة منهم عن عائشة قال: اشربوا ولا تسكروا

THALABI:v2p145/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p145/r1.speaker: الإمام أبو عبد الرحمن
THALABI:v2p145/r1.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman says the Qursafa report is unestablished and Qursafa unidentified; the better-known Aisha report rejects every intoxicant, even if made from bread.
THALABI:v2p145/r1.anchor: قال الإمام أبو عبد الرحمن هذا غير ثابت، وقرصافة لا ندري من هي

THALABI:v2p145/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p145/r2.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v2p145/r2.claim: Jisra bint Dajaja reports Aisha repeatedly saying she does not permit an intoxicant, even if made from bread, when asked about alternating batches of nabidh.
THALABI:v2p145/r2.anchor: قالت: سمعت عائشة سألها أياس عن النبيذ قالوا: ننبذ الخمر غدوة ونشربه عشيا

THALABI:v2p145/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p145/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p145/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas is cited as saying both little and much wine are forbidden, as is any intoxicant in any drink.
THALABI:v2p145/r3.anchor: هشيم عن ابن شبرمة قال: حدثني الثقة عن عبد الله بن شداد عن ابن عباس قال: حرمت الخمر منها، قليلها وكثيرها

THALABI:v2p145/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p145/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p145/r4.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi says the broad rule is more correct: Ibn Abbas held whatever intoxicates is forbidden and said nabidh should be prohibited as God and His Messenger prohibited.
THALABI:v2p145/r4.anchor: وهذا أولى بالصواب لما روى سفيان عن أبي الجويرية الجرمي قال: سألت ابن عباس عن الباذق قال: ما أسكر فهو حرام

THALABI:v2p145/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p145/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p145/r5.claim: Asked about bazidh, Ibn Abbas says whatever intoxicates is forbidden.
THALABI:v2p145/r5.anchor: عن أبي الجويرية الجرمي قال: سألت ابن عباس عن الباذق قال: ما أسكر فهو حرام

THALABI:v2p145/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p145/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p145/r6.claim: Abu al-Hakam reports Ibn Abbas saying whoever wants to prohibit what God and His Messenger prohibited should prohibit nabidh.
THALABI:v2p145/r6.anchor: وعن شعبة عن سلمة بن كميل قال: سمعت أبا الحكم يحدث قال: قال ابن عباس: من سره أن يحرم

THALABI:v2p145/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p145/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p145/r7.claim: A report attributed to Ibn Umar describes the Prophet tasting strong nabidh, returning it, diluting it with water, and telling people to weaken drinks in those vessels with water.
THALABI:v2p145/r7.anchor: فوجده شديدا فرده الى صاحبه، فقال له رجل من القوم: يا رسول الله أحرام هو؟

THALABI:v2p145/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p145/r8.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
THALABI:v2p145/r8.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman says the well-known Abd al-Malik report conflicts with al-Zubayr's version: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet saying every intoxicant is forbidden and every intoxicant is wine.
THALABI:v2p145/r8.anchor: قال أبو عبد الرحمن: عبد الملك بن رافع هو مشهور ولكن حدثنيه وأخبرنا عن الزبير خلاف حكاية

THALABI:v2p145/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p145/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v2p145/r9.claim: Ibn Sirin reports Ibn Umar saying intoxicants are forbidden in small and large amounts; another report says to avoid anything containing an intoxicating element.
THALABI:v2p145/r9.anchor: وروى ابن سيرين عن ابن عمر قال: المسكر قليله وكثيره حرام

THALABI:v2p146/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p146/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
THALABI:v2p146/r1.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman grades the Ibn Masud story about diluted nabidh at the Kaaba as weak because Yahya ibn Yaman alone reports it from Sufyan and has poor accuracy and memory.
THALABI:v2p146/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبد الرحمن: هذا خبر ضعيف لأن يحيى بن يمان انفرد به دون أصحاب سفيان

THALABI:v2p146/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p146/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p146/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet rejected gourd nabidh after it began to ferment, calling it the drink of one who does not believe in God and the Last Day.
THALABI:v2p146/r2.anchor: وعن زيد بن واقد عن خالد بن الحسين قال: سمعت أبا هريرة يقول: علمت أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصوم

THALABI:v2p146/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p146/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
THALABI:v2p146/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib reports that Umar diluted a drink offered by Thaqif and told them to do likewise.
THALABI:v2p146/r3.anchor: واحتجوا أيضا بما أسندوه إلى سفيان عن يحيى بن سعيد قال: سمعت سعيد بن المسيب يقول: تلقت ثقيف عمر

THALABI:v2p146/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p146/r4.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
THALABI:v2p146/r4.claim: A report attributed to Abu Rafi says Umar instructed people to dilute nabidh if they feared it was too strong.
THALABI:v2p146/r4.anchor: واحتجوا بما أسندوه إلى أبي رافع أن عمر بن الخطاب قال: إذا خشيتم من نبيذ لشدته فأكسره

THALABI:v2p146/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p146/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن المبارك
THALABI:v2p146/r5.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak interprets Umar's instruction to dilute as applying before the drink becomes strong; Umar imposed the full penalty after finding a drink intoxicating.
THALABI:v2p146/r5.anchor: عبد الله بن المبارك معنى أكسره بالماء من قبل أن يشتد

THALABI:v2p146/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p146/r6.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
THALABI:v2p146/r6.claim: Umar says he would impose the full penalty if a man's tala was intoxicating, and the source reports that he did so after smelling the drink.
THALABI:v2p146/r6.anchor: فإني سائل عما يشرب فإن كان مسكرا جلدته فجلد عمر الحد تاما

THALABI:v2p146/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p146/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد
THALABI:v2p146/r7.claim: Abu Said defines tala as a drink cooked until two-thirds evaporate; the name reflects its dark thickness like camel ointment.
THALABI:v2p146/r7.anchor: قال أبو سعيد الطلا الذي قد طبخ حتى ذهب ثلثاه وبقي ثلثه، سمي بذلك لأنه شبيه بطلاء الإبل

THALABI:v2p146/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p146/r8.speaker: عبيد بن الأبرص
THALABI:v2p146/r8.claim: Ubayd ibn al-Abras's verse shows wine was euphemistically called tala, as a wolf was called Abu Jaʿda.
THALABI:v2p146/r8.anchor: قال عبيد بن الأبرص: هي الخمر تكنى الطلاء … كما الذئب يكنى أبا جعدة

THALABI:v2p146/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p146/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p146/r9.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi says the tala granted as a concession is reb cooked down to one-third, after intoxication, harm, and devilish influence have gone.
THALABI:v2p146/r9.anchor: قال الثعلبي: الطلاء الذي ورد فيه الرخصة إنما هو الرب فإنه إذا طبخ حتى يرجع إلى الثلث فقد ذهب سكره وشره وخلا شيطانه

THALABI:v2p146/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p146/r10.speaker: إبراهيم
THALABI:v2p146/r10.claim: A report says Ibrahim tested a thick melon drink and removed or discarded its intoxicating element.
THALABI:v2p146/r10.anchor: واحتجوا أيضا بما روى هشيم عن المغيرة عن إبراهيم أنه أهدي له بطيخ خاثر فكان تبينه ويلغي فيه المسكر

THALABI:v2p147/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p147/r1.speaker: إبراهيم
THALABI:v2p147/r1.claim: Ibrahim is reported to have said there is no objection to melon nabidh.
THALABI:v2p147/r1.anchor: وعن مغيرة عن أبي معشر عن إبراهيم قال: لا بأس بنبيذ البطيخ

THALABI:v2p147/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p147/r2.speaker: ابن المبارك
THALABI:v2p147/r2.claim: Ibn al-Mubarak says he found no sound authority permitting intoxicants except Ibrahim.
THALABI:v2p147/r2.anchor: أبي أسامة قال: سمعت ابن المبارك يقول: ما وجدت الرخصة في المسكر عن أحد صحيح

THALABI:v2p147/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p147/r3.speaker: أم سلمة
THALABI:v2p147/r3.claim: Anas reports Umm Salama had a vessel and said she served the Prophet water, honey, milk, and nabidh.
THALABI:v2p147/r3.anchor: حماد بن سلمة عن عمر عن أنس قال: كان لأم سلمة قدح فقالت: سقيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كل الشراب

THALABI:v2p147/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p147/r4.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
THALABI:v2p147/r4.claim: Talha ibn Musarrif warned that nabidh makes the young grow and the old age, but said he disliked Muslims becoming intoxicated through his practice.
THALABI:v2p147/r4.anchor: وعن ابن شبرمة قال: قال طلحة بن مصرف لأهل الكوفة في النبيذ فقال: يربو فيها الصغير ويهرم فيها الكبير

THALABI:v2p147/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p147/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
THALABI:v2p147/r5.claim: Ibn Ishaq told Abu Ishaq that Ali's and Abdullah's companions served nabidh in the khawafi before Talha was born.
THALABI:v2p147/r5.anchor: فقال ابن إسحاق: قد سقيته أصحاب علي وأصحاب عبد الله في الخوافي قبل أن يولد طلحة

THALABI:v2p147/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p147/r6.speaker: ابن شبرمة
THALABI:v2p147/r6.claim: Ibn Shubruma says God have mercy on Ibrahim: he made people strict about nabidh while also permitting it.
THALABI:v2p147/r6.anchor: وعن ابن شبرمة قال: رحم الله إبراهيم شدد الناس في النبيذ ورخص فيه

THALABI:v2p147/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p147/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p147/r7.claim: Ibn Burayda reports the Prophet first forbade a group to drink from unsealed vessels; after they fell ill and blamed the restriction, he permitted drinking but said every intoxicant is forbidden.
THALABI:v2p147/r7.anchor: واحتجوا أيضا بما أسندوه إلى عبد الله بن بريدة عن أبيه

THALABI:v2p147/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p147/r8.speaker: قالوا
THALABI:v2p147/r8.claim: They explain the warning as targeting wine that causes intoxication, since nabidh's excitement and energy arise only from an intoxicating drink.
THALABI:v2p147/r8.anchor: قالوا: أراد بهذا الخمر الذي يحصل منه السكر، لأن التنبذ ذلك الطرب والنشاط ولا يحصلان إلا عن شراب مسكر

THALABI:v2p147/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p147/r9.speaker: جابر
THALABI:v2p147/r9.claim: Abu al-Zubayr reports from Jabir that the Prophet had nabidh prepared for him in a vessel.
THALABI:v2p147/r9.anchor: أبو الزبير عن جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان ينبذ له في [قدر من عفاره]

THALABI:v2p147/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p147/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p147/r10.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi says reports may predate prohibition or, more likely, concern date- or raisin-infused water before it fermented and intoxicated.
THALABI:v2p147/r10.anchor: قال الثعلبي: ويحتمل أن لهذه الأخبار وأمثالها معنيين: أحدهما أنها كانت قبل تحريم الخمر

THALABI:v2p147/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p147/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p147/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet drank prepared nabidh on the day it was made and on the next two days, supporting that it was not yet intoxicating.
THALABI:v2p147/r11.anchor: يدل عليه ما روي عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصنع له النبيذ فيشربه يومه والغد وبعد الغد

THALABI:v2p148/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p148/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p148/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet kept raisin infusion overnight, drank it that day and the next two days, then discarded any remainder.
THALABI:v2p148/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ينبذ له نبيذ الزبيب من الليل

THALABI:v2p148/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p148/r2.speaker: فيروز
THALABI:v2p148/r2.claim: Firuz says the Prophet advised soaking raisins for one meal and drinking the next, using skins rather than baskets so the drink would not ferment into wine.
THALABI:v2p148/r2.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن الديلمي عن أبيه فيروز قال: قدمت على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v2p148/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p148/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v2p148/r3.claim: Ibn Umar prepared raisin infusion morning and evening in washed skins without adding dates or anything else; Nafi says they drank it like honey.
THALABI:v2p148/r3.anchor: وعن نافع عن ابن عمر أنه كان ينبذ له في سقاء للزبيب غدوة فيشربه من الليل

THALABI:v2p148/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p148/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
THALABI:v2p148/r4.claim: Abu Jaafar says Ali ibn al-Husayn prepared raisin infusion overnight to drink in the morning, and in the morning to drink at night.
THALABI:v2p148/r4.anchor: وعن بسام قال: سألت أبا جعفر عن النبيذ قال: كان علي بن الحسين ينبذ له من الليل

THALABI:v2p148/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p148/r5.speaker: سفيان
THALABI:v2p148/r5.claim: Sufyan describes making the infusion in the evening and drinking it the following morning.
THALABI:v2p148/r5.anchor: وعن عبد الله قال: سمعت سفيان- وسئل عن النبيذ- قال: أنبذ عشاء وأشربه غدوة

THALABI:v2p148/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p148/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p148/r6.claim: These reports show that nabidh is raisin or date infusion before it ferments.
THALABI:v2p148/r6.anchor: فهذه الأخبار تدل على أنه نقيع الزبيب والتمر قبل أن يشتد

THALABI:v2p148/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p148/r7.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأحمد بن حنبل وأبو ثور وأكثر أهل الآثار
THALABI:v2p148/r7.claim: They define wine as every intoxicating drink, whether grape-based or otherwise, and forbid any amount; its drinker receives the penalty except for the specified cooked drink after a third evaporates, whose testimony remains valid.
THALABI:v2p148/r7.anchor: وقال مالك والشافعي وأحمد بن حنبل وأبو ثور وأكثر أهل الآثار: إن الخمر كل شراب مسكر

THALABI:v2p148/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p148/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p148/r8.claim: Khamr derives from covering: it names things that cover other things, including a woman's veil and a prayer rug; wine is so called because it covers the mind.
THALABI:v2p148/r8.anchor: أن الخمر أصله الستر، ويقال لكل شيء ستر شيئا من شجر أو حجر أو غيرهما خمر

THALABI:v2p148/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p148/r9.speaker: عمر
THALABI:v2p148/r9.claim: In a sermon reported through Ibn Umar, Umar says wine prohibition was revealed and wine is made from grapes, dates, wheat, barley, or honey; wine is whatever clouds the mind.
THALABI:v2p148/r9.anchor: ما روى الشعبي عن ابن عمر قال: خطب عمر فقال: إن الخمر نزل تحريمها، وهي من خمسة أشياء

THALABI:v2p148/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p148/r10.speaker: أنس بن مالك
THALABI:v2p148/r10.claim: Anas says wine was named for being left in jars until it fermented and changed.
THALABI:v2p148/r10.anchor: وقال أنس بن مالك: سميت خمرا لأنهم كانوا يدعونها في الدنان حتى تختمر وتتغير

THALABI:v2p149/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p149/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
THALABI:v2p149/r1.claim: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab says wine was named because its surface cleared and its sediment settled when left to stand.
THALABI:v2p149/r1.anchor: وقال سعيد بن المسيب: إنما سميت الخمر لأنها تركت حتى صفا صفورها ورسب كدرها

THALABI:v2p149/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p149/r2.speaker: أنس
THALABI:v2p149/r2.claim: Anas says the common wine in Medina at the time of prohibition was fadikh, made from dates and unripe dates without heating; Medina lacked grapes for wine.
THALABI:v2p149/r2.anchor: وقال أنس: لقد حرمت الخمر وإنما عامة خمورهم يومئذ الفضيخ

THALABI:v2p149/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p149/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v2p149/r3.claim: Ibn Umar gives the alternative name al-fudukh instead of al-fadikh for the date drink.
THALABI:v2p149/r3.anchor: وفيه روي عن ابن عمر أنه قال: ليس بالفضيخ ولكنه الفضوخ

THALABI:v2p149/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p149/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p149/r4.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that every intoxicant is wine and every wine is forbidden.
THALABI:v2p149/r4.anchor: دليلهم من السنة ما روى نافع عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «كل مسكر خمر

THALABI:v2p149/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p149/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p149/r5.claim: The Prophet says every intoxicant is wine and whatever intoxicates in a large quantity is forbidden even in a small quantity.
THALABI:v2p149/r5.anchor: سالم بن عبد الله عن أبيه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «كل مسكر خمر وما أسكر كثيره

THALABI:v2p149/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p149/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p149/r6.claim: Aisha reports that if a large vessel of a drink intoxicates, even a handful of it is forbidden; the vessel called gharaq holds sixteen ratls.
THALABI:v2p149/r6.anchor: عن أبي عثمان عمرو بن سالم الأنصاري عن القاسم عن عائشة عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

THALABI:v2p149/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p149/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p149/r7.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet saying that every intoxicant is forbidden from its beginning to its end.
THALABI:v2p149/r7.anchor: وعن أبي الغصن الملقب بحجى قال: قال لي: هشام بن عروة: هل تشرب النبيذ؟

THALABI:v2p149/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p149/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p149/r8.claim: The Prophet names intoxicating drinks made from dates, grapes, raisins, honey, wheat, barley, and corn, and forbids every intoxicant.
THALABI:v2p149/r8.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن من التمر لخمرا، وإن من العنب لخمرا

THALABI:v2p149/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p149/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
THALABI:v2p149/r9.claim: Ibn Umar forbids both small and large amounts of intoxicants, and identifies the named drinks made by his family and the people of Khaybar as wine.
