THALABI:v2p149/r9.anchor: وعن ابن سيرين قال: جاء رجل إلى ابن عمر فقال: إن أهلنا ينبذون لنا شرابا عشاء

THALABI:v2p149/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p149/r10.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v2p149/r10.claim: Ikrima says the Prophet poured away a wife's pitcher of infused juice and broke the pitcher.
THALABI:v2p149/r10.anchor: وعن عكرمة قال: دخل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على بعض أزواجه وقد نبذوا العصير لهم في كوز

THALABI:v2p150/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p150/r1.speaker: عبادة بن الصامت
THALABI:v2p150/r1.claim: The Prophet warns, according to Ubadah ibn al-Samit, that people from his community will declare wine lawful by giving it another name.
THALABI:v2p150/r1.anchor: روى عبادة بن الصامت أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «ليستحلن ناس من أمتي الخمر باسم يسمونها إياه»

THALABI:v2p150/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p150/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p150/r2.claim: A second prophetic report says wine is forbidden because of its intoxicating substance, not its name, and every drink whose end result is wine is forbidden.
THALABI:v2p150/r2.anchor: ويروى عنه أنه قال صلى الله عليه وسلم «أما الخمر لم تحرم لاسمها إنما حرمت لما فيها

THALABI:v2p150/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p150/r3.speaker: حكيم من حكماء العرب
THALABI:v2p150/r3.claim: An Arab sage explains that he will not drink nabidh because God gave him a sound mind and he will not admit what damages it.
THALABI:v2p150/r3.anchor: وحكي أن رجلا من حكماء العرب قيل له: لم لا تشرب النبيذ؟ فقال: الله منحني عقلي صحيحا

THALABI:v2p150/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p150/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p150/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says pre-Islamic gamblers wagered family and property; whoever lost to the other surrendered both, prompting this verse.
THALABI:v2p150/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان الرجل في الجاهلية يقامره الرجل على أهله وماله

THALABI:v2p150/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p150/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p150/r5.claim: Maysir is linked to yasara, meaning something became due; a yāsir is the lot-caster. Al-Nabigha and another poet use yāsir for a gambler.
THALABI:v2p150/r5.anchor: والياسر الرامي بقداح وجب ذلك أو مباحه أو غيرهما، ثم قيل للقمار: ميسر، وللمقامر: ياسر ويسر قال النابغة

THALABI:v2p150/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p150/r6.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v2p150/r6.claim: Mujahid says it was named maysir because gamblers said the camel's price had become theirs; wealthy Arabs bought a camel and divided it into shares.
THALABI:v2p150/r6.anchor: وقال مقاتل: سمي ميسرا لأنهم كانوا يقولون: يسر هو لنا ثمن الجزور

THALABI:v2p150/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p150/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
THALABI:v2p150/r7.claim: Abu Amr counts ten shares in the camel-gambling game.
THALABI:v2p150/r7.anchor: واختلفوا في عدد الأجزاء فقال أبو عمرو: عشرة

THALABI:v2p150/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p150/r8.speaker: الأصمعي
THALABI:v2p150/r8.claim: Al-Asmai says there were twenty shares, with ten additional lots added to them.
THALABI:v2p150/r8.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: إنما هي عشرون ثم يضمون عليها عشرة قداح

THALABI:v2p150/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p150/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p150/r9.claim: Seven lots carried shares: al-fadhdh one, al-taw'am two, al-raft three, al-jals four, al-nafis five, al-masil six, and al-mughli seven; three others carried none.
THALABI:v2p150/r9.anchor: ويقال: منه الأزلام والأقلام سبعة منها لها أنصباء هي: الفذ وله نصيب واحدة، والتوأم وله نصيبان

THALABI:v2p150/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p150/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p150/r10.claim: Lots were shaken in a bag by a trusted drawer; each named player won the share assigned to the drawn lot, while a blank lot triggered a dispute over who paid for the camel.
THALABI:v2p150/r10.anchor: ثم يجعلون القداح في خريطة تسمى الربابة، قال أبو ذؤيب: وكأنهن ربابة وكأنه

THALABI:v2p151/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p151/r1.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v2p151/r1.claim: Some said a player drawn with a blank lot neither took a share nor paid; that lot was void and the draw repeated.
THALABI:v2p151/r1.anchor: وقال بعضهم: لا يأخذ ولا يغرم، ويكون ذلك القداح لغوا فيعاد سهمه ثانيا

THALABI:v2p151/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p151/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p151/r2.claim: The camel game was the Arabs' original form of gambling, and God's prohibition here covers every kind of gambling.
THALABI:v2p151/r2.anchor: فأصل هذا القمار الذي كانت العرب تفعله وإنما نهى الله تعالى في هذه الآية عن أنواع القمار كلها

THALABI:v2p151/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p151/r3.speaker: طاوس ومجاهد وعطاء
THALABI:v2p151/r3.claim: They define maysir as anything involving gambling, even children's games with sticks and dice.
THALABI:v2p151/r3.anchor: ليث عن طاوس ومجاهد وعطاء قالوا: كل شيء فيه قمار فهو الميسر حتى لعب الصبيان بالعود والكعاب

THALABI:v2p151/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p151/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p151/r4.claim: The Prophet warns against the two marked dice, calling them a form of Persian gambling.
THALABI:v2p151/r4.anchor: عن أبي الأحوص عن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إياكم وهاتين الكعبتين الموسومتين

THALABI:v2p151/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p151/r5.speaker: علي
THALABI:v2p151/r5.claim: Ali calls backgammon and chess forms of maysir.
THALABI:v2p151/r5.anchor: وعن جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه أن عليا كرم الله وجهه قال في النرد والشطرنج: هي من الميسر

THALABI:v2p151/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p151/r6.speaker: القاسم بن محمد
THALABI:v2p151/r6.claim: Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad says anything that distracts from remembrance of God and prayer is maysir.
THALABI:v2p151/r6.anchor: وعن القاسم بن محمد أنه قال: كل شيء ألهى عن ذكر الله وعن الصلاة فهو الميسر

THALABI:v2p151/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p151/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p151/r7.claim: The grave sin in wine and gambling includes quarrels, insults, obscenity, falsehood, loss of reason, neglect of prayer, and wrongful appropriation of others' property.
THALABI:v2p151/r7.anchor: وقول الفحش والزور، وزوال العقل والمنع من الصلاة واستحلال مال الغير بغير حق

THALABI:v2p151/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p151/r8.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v2p151/r8.claim: Exegetes specify wine's sin as drunken harm to people and gambling's sin as withholding rights and acting unjustly.
THALABI:v2p151/r8.anchor: قال المفسرون: إثم الخمر هو أن الرجل يشرب فيسكر فيؤذي الناس، وإثم الميسر أن يقامر الرجل

THALABI:v2p151/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p151/r9.speaker: أهل الكوفة والباقون
THALABI:v2p151/r9.claim: Kufans other than Asim read kathīr with thāʾ; the others read kabīr with bāʾ, which Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim prefer because the verse compares sin and benefit and 4:2 says ḥūban kabīran.
THALABI:v2p151/r9.anchor: قرأ أهل الكوفة إلا عاصم: كثير بالثاء، وقرأ الباقون بالباء واختاره أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم

THALABI:v2p151/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p151/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p151/r10.claim: Wine's benefits included trade and pleasure, illustrated by al-A'sha's contrasting lines on its morning misery and evening enjoyment.
THALABI:v2p151/r10.anchor: ومنافع للناس وهي ما كانوا يصيبونها في الخمر من التجارة واللذة عند شربهما يقول الأعشى

THALABI:v2p151/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p151/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p151/r11.claim: The benefit of gambling was what a winner gained and the support thereby given to the poor.
THALABI:v2p151/r11.anchor: ومنفعة الميسر ما يصاب من القمار ويرتفق به الفقراء

THALABI:v2p151/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p151/r12.speaker: الضحاك والربيع
THALABI:v2p151/r12.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Rabi say the benefits occurred before prohibition, while the sin applies after prohibition.
THALABI:v2p151/r12.anchor: وقال الضحاك والربيع: المنافع قبل التحريم، والإثم بعد التحريم

THALABI:v2p151/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p151/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p151/r13.claim: After the Prophet encouraged charity without making it obligatory, people asked what to spend and whom to give it to.
THALABI:v2p151/r13.anchor: وذلك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حثهم على الصدقة ورغبهم فيها من غير عزم قالوا

THALABI:v2p151/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p151/r14.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو عمرو
THALABI:v2p151/r14.claim: These readers use the nominative al-afwu, meaning that what people spend is the surplus; al-Suddi prefers this reading, supported by 16:24.
THALABI:v2p151/r14.anchor: قرأ الحسن وقتادة وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو عمرو قل العفو بالرفع، واختاره محمد بن السدي

THALABI:v2p151/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p151/r15.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
THALABI:v2p151/r15.claim: Most readers use the accusative al-afwa, which Abu Ubayd and Abu Hatim prefer as the answer: spend the surplus.
THALABI:v2p151/r15.anchor: وقرأ الآخرون بالنصب واختاره أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم: قل ينفقون العفو

THALABI:v2p152/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p152/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو ومحمد بن كعب وقتادة وعطاء والسدي وابن أبي ليلى
THALABI:v2p152/r1.claim: They define al-afw as money left over after providing for one's dependents; this is also narrated from Ibn Abbas through Miqsam.
THALABI:v2p152/r1.anchor: فقال عبد الله بن عمرو ومحمد بن كعب وقتادة وعطاء والسدي وابن أبي ليلى: هو ما فضل من المال عن العيال

THALABI:v2p152/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p152/r2.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v2p152/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says one should not exhaust one's wealth in spending and then have to beg people.
THALABI:v2p152/r2.anchor: الحسن: هو أن لا تجهد مالك في النفقة ثم تقعد تسأل الناس

THALABI:v2p152/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p152/r3.speaker: الوالبي عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p152/r3.claim: Al-Walibi transmits Ibn Abbas's definition of al-afw as what is not conspicuous among one's assets.
THALABI:v2p152/r3.anchor: الوالبي عن ابن عباس: ما لا يتبين في أموالكم

THALABI:v2p152/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p152/r4.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v2p152/r4.claim: Mujahid defines it as charity that purifies the wealthy.

THALABI:v2p152/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p152/r5.speaker: عمرو بن دينار وعطاء
THALABI:v2p152/r5.claim: Amr ibn Dinar and Ata define it as moderate spending, neither extravagant nor miserly.
THALABI:v2p152/r5.anchor: عمرو بن دينار وعطاء: الوسط من النفقة ما لم يكن إسرافا ولا إقتارا

THALABI:v2p152/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p152/r6.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v2p152/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak defines al-afw as what one can afford.

THALABI:v2p152/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p152/r7.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p152/r7.claim: Al-Awfi transmits Ibn Abbas's view that one should accept whatever people offer, whether little or much.
THALABI:v2p152/r7.anchor: العوفي عن ابن عباس: ما أتوك به من شيء قليل أو كثير فاقبله منهم

THALABI:v2p152/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p152/r8.speaker: طاوس وعطاء الخراساني
THALABI:v2p152/r8.claim: Tawus and Ata al-Khurasani transmit from Bishr that al-afw is the easy or available amount of each thing.
THALABI:v2p152/r8.anchor: طاوس وعطاء الخراساني: سمعنا [بشرا] قال: العفو اليسر من كل شيء

THALABI:v2p152/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p152/r9.speaker: الربيع
THALABI:v2p152/r9.claim: Al-Rabi defines al-afw as good, meaning that one should spend the best of one's property.
THALABI:v2p152/r9.anchor: الربيع: العفو الطيب، يقول: أفضل مالك هو النفقة

THALABI:v2p152/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p152/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p152/r10.claim: The reported definitions are close in meaning; linguistically al-afw denotes increase and abundance, as in the verse about a people increasing and the prophetic instruction to grow beards.
THALABI:v2p152/r10.anchor: وكلها متقاربة في المعنى، ومعنى العفو في اللغة الزيادة والكثرة قال الله: حتى عفوا

THALABI:v2p152/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p152/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p152/r11.claim: The poet's عافيات means abundant in fat; al-afw also describes what someone receives or gives easily, without compulsion.
THALABI:v2p152/r11.anchor: قال الشاعر: ولكنا يعض السيف منا

THALABI:v2p152/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p152/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v2p152/r12.claim: A man is told by the Prophet to spend first on himself, then family, children, parents, and relatives; after that he decides what to do with any remainder.
THALABI:v2p152/r12.anchor: ما روى أبو هريرة أن رجلا قال: يا رسول الله عندي خير، قال: «أنفقه على نفسك»

THALABI:v2p152/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p152/r13.speaker: عامر بن عبد الله
THALABI:v2p152/r13.claim: A man offers the Prophet his only possession, a gold egg; the Prophet finally takes and throws it, teaching that charity should come from sufficiency and one should begin with dependents.
THALABI:v2p152/r13.anchor: وروى محمود بن سهل عن عامر بن عبد الله قال: أتى رسول الله رجل ببيضة من ذهب

THALABI:v2p153/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p153/r1.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v2p153/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi says people kept a year's family expenses and gave the rest, or kept one day's earnings if they worked by hand; obligatory zakat later abrogated this verse and earlier charity commands.
THALABI:v2p153/r1.anchor: قال الكلبي: فكان الرجل بعد نزول هذه الآية إذا كان له مال من ذهب أو فضة أو زرع أو ضرع

THALABI:v2p153/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p153/r2.speaker: الزجاج
THALABI:v2p153/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains the singular verb addressed to a plural audience by saying a group is treated as a single tribe or collective.
THALABI:v2p153/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: إنما قال: كذلك على الواحد وهو يخاطب جماعة لأن الجماعة معناها القبيل

THALABI:v2p153/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p153/r3.speaker: الزجاج
THALABI:v2p153/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj also allows the address to be directed to the Prophet, whose address includes his community, as in 65:1.
THALABI:v2p153/r3.anchor: وجائز أن يكون خطابا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لأن خطابه مشتمل على خطاب أمته

THALABI:v2p153/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p153/r4.speaker: المفضل بن سلمة
THALABI:v2p153/r4.claim: Al-Mufaddal says people should reflect on worldly and afterlife needs, keep enough wealth for earthly livelihood, and spend the remainder for their afterlife.
THALABI:v2p153/r4.anchor: وقال المفضل بن سلمة: معنى الآية كذلك يبين الله لكم الآيات في النفقة لعلكم تتفكرون

THALABI:v2p153/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p153/r5.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
THALABI:v2p153/r5.claim: Most exegetes say the reflection concerns the world's passing and the afterlife's approach, leading people to turn from the world and desire the afterlife.
THALABI:v2p153/r5.anchor: معناها: يبين الله لكم الآيات في أمر الدنيا والآخرة لعلكم تتفكرون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب ومعاذ بن جبل وسعد بن أبي وقاص
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r1.claim: The verse was revealed after Umar, Muʿadh, Saʿd, and others asked the Prophet about wine and gambling, saying they impair reason and take wealth.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r1.anchor: نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب ومعاذ بن جبل وسعد بن أبي وقاص وجماعة، أتوا رسول الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r2.speaker: أهل اللغة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r2.claim: Linguists derive khamr from covering because wine veils the intellect.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r2.anchor: والخمر عند أهل اللغة سميت خمرا لسترها العقل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r3.speaker: ابن المظفر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r3.claim: Ibn al-Muzaffar defines khamr, its ripening and boiling, its maker, and the veil affecting a drunk person.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن المظفر: الخمر معروف، واختمارها: إدراكها وغليانها، ومخمرها: متخذها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r4.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r4.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says one says ikhtamartu khamran, but not akhmartuha.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r4.anchor: قال الكسائي: اختمرت خمرا، ولا يقال: أخمرتها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r5.speaker: ثعلب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r5.claim: Thaʿlab transmits that khāmir can mean one who conceals testimony; the root sense is covering, also reflected in the Prophetic instruction to cover vessels.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r5.anchor: روى ثعلب عن عمرو عن أبيه (¬5) قال: الخامر: الذي يكتم شهادته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r6.claim: Khamr can mean a place or thing that conceals someone, such as trees or a mound; khāmiri umm ʿāmir means go into hiding.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r6.anchor: أي: ادخلي الخمر، واستتري، والخمر: ما واراك من شجر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r7.claim: Some say it is named for being covered until maturity; Ibn al-Anbari derives the name from mixing with the intellect, illustrated by poems about illness mixing with the heart.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: سميت خمرا؛ لأنها تغطى حتى تدرك، وقال ابن الأنباري: سميت خمرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r8.claim: The mixing derivation returns to covering, since what mixes with something becomes like a veil.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r8.anchor: وهذا (¬4) الذي ذكره راجع إلى الأول؛ لأن الشيء إذا خالط (¬5) الشيء يصير بمنزلة الساتر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r9.speaker: الثوري وأبو حنيفة وأكثر أهل الرأي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r9.claim: Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifa, and most jurists restrict khamr to grape or date juice that ferments naturally without fire; other drinks are not khamr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r9.anchor: فمذهب الثوري (¬1) وأبي حنيفة وأكثر أهل الرأي (¬2): أن الخمر ما اعتصر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r10.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأحمد وأهل الأثر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r10.claim: Malik, al-Shafiʿi, Ahmad, and hadith scholars define khamr as every intoxicating drink, from juice or infusion, cooked or raw; the author says Arabic supports this view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p146#2/r10.anchor: ومذهب مالك (¬5) والشافعي (¬6) وأحمد (¬7) وأهل الأثر (¬8): أن الخمر كل شراب مسكر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r1.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj argues by analogy that anything producing wine’s effect should be called wine and share its prohibition; consensus forbids all gambling though the verse names the camel-lottery form.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج: القياس أن ما عمل عمل الخمر أن يقال لها خمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says every intoxicant that mingles with and veils reason counts as wine; the Prophet’s hadith lists drink sources and bans every intoxicant.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r3.claim: The Prophet lists intoxicants made from dates, grapes, raisins, wheat, barley, and corn, then prohibits every intoxicant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r3.anchor: إن من التمر لخمرا، وإن من العنب لخمرا، وإن من الزبيب لخمرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r4.claim: Maysir means gambling; Ibn Abbas says a pre-Islamic man wagered his family and property, which the loser surrendered.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {والميسر} يعني: القمار، قال ابن عباس: كان الرجل في الجاهلية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r5.claim: Maysir is a mafʿil from yasara, to become due; yāsir is one whose lot or wager becomes due, then the terms meant gambling and gambler.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r5.anchor: والميسر عند أهل اللغة: مفعل، من قولهم: يسر لي هذا الشيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r6.speaker: طرفة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r6.claim: Ṭarafa’s verse uses aysār as the plural of yusr for participants in the lot-based camel gamble.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r6.anchor: قال طرفة: وهم أيسار لقمان إذا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r7.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r7.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrabi explains yasara al-yāsir as bringing one’s arrow to gamble.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r7.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: يقال: يسر الياسر ييسر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r8.claim: Another derivation links maysir to division and sharing; yasaru means to divide, illustrated by a poem about dividing the speaker like a camel’s limbs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r8.anchor: وقيل: أخذ الميسر من التجزئة والاقتسام (¬3)، ويقال: يسروا الشيء، أي: اقتسموه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r9.claim: Arabs slaughtered a camel, divided it into shares, and gambled over them using arrows.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p149/r9.anchor: يتقامر عليها بالقداح، على عادة لهم في ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r1.speaker: النضر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r1.claim: Al-Nadr says yāsir means butcher and yasarat al-nāqa means she divided the camel’s meat; al-Aʿsha uses yāsir for butcher.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r1.anchor: قال النضر: الياسر: الجزار، ويسرت الناقة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r2.claim: A further derivation takes maysir from ease because people shared a camel to make its cost easier; Muqatil says they asked to split its price.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r2.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب مقاتل؛ لأنه قال: (¬4) سمي ميسرا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r3.claim: This verse is not the prohibition of wine and gambling; the prohibiting verse is in al-Maʾida.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r3.anchor: وليست هذه الآية المحرمة للخمر {والميسر} (¬6) إنما المحرمة التي في المائدة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r4.claim: Their sin includes quarrels, insults, obscene and false speech, loss of reason, and missing prayer; gambling breeds hostility when one takes another’s money without compensation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r4.anchor: أراد: الإثم بسببهما من المخاصمة والمشاتمة، وقول الفحش

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r5.speaker: الربيع والضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r5.claim: Al-Rabiʿ and al-Dahhak say the sin became great after prohibition, while benefits existed before it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r5.anchor: وقال الربيع (¬1) والضحاك (¬2): إثم كبير بعد التحريم، ومنافع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r6.claim: The author prefers the first account: benefits meant wine profits and trade, pleasure and strength, and gambling winnings supporting the poor.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r6.anchor: عنى بالمنافع ما كانوا يصيبونه من المال في بيع الخمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r7.speaker: الأعشى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r7.claim: Al-Aʿsha’s poem contrasts daytime wine’s sickness and sadness with evening pleasure and earnings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r7.anchor: كقول الشاعر (¬4) الأعشى: لنا من ضحاها خبث نفس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r8.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r8.claim: Qatada says the verse condemned wine and gambling without prohibiting them, since they were still lawful then.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة: في هذه الآية ذمها ولم (¬7) يحرمها، وهي يومئذ حلال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r9.speaker: قوم من أهل النظر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r9.claim: Some rationalists argue wine was prohibited here because another verse prohibits sin generally and this verse calls wine and gambling sinful.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r9.anchor: وذهب قوم من أهل النظر: إلى أن الخمر حرمت بهذه الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r10.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r10.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read kathīr with thāʾ; the other readers read kabīr with bāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r10.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي (كثير) بالثاء، الباقون بالباء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r11.claim: The bāʾ reading is preferable because kabīr contrasts with small and other verses call grave sins kabāʾir; wine and gambling are major sins.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p151/r11.anchor: وحجتهم: أن الباء أولى؛ لأن الكبر مثل العظم، ومقابل الكبر الصغر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p154/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p154/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p154/r1.claim: The bāʾ reading is supported by using ṣaghīr for small, not qalīl for few, and by the contrast of small with great; readers agree on bāʾ in the comparison phrase.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p154/r1.anchor: وقالوا في اللمم: صغير وصغيرة، ولم يقولوا: قليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p154/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p154/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p154/r2.claim: The thāʾ reading is supported by the many sins in the wine-and-gambling verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p154/r2.anchor: وأما من قرأ بالثاء فلأنه قد جاء فيهما ما يقوي (4) وصف الإثم فيهما بالكثرة دون الكبر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p154/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p154/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p154/r3.claim: The Prophet cursed ten in connection with wine; sin is thereby abundant and may be called much.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p154/r3.anchor: ولأن (5) النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لعن عشرة في سبب الخمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r1.speaker: عمرو بن الجموح
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r1.claim: After the answer about parents and kin, ʿAmr ibn al-Jamuh asked how much to spend, prompting revelation of say, the surplus.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r1.anchor: نزل في سؤال عمرو بن الجموح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Suddi, Qatada, and ʿAta say al-ʿafw is wealth left after providing for dependents.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية مقسم: العفو: ما فضل من المال عن العيال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r3.claim: In the al-Walibi report, Ibn Abbas defines al-ʿafw as what is not conspicuous in one’s property.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r3.anchor: وقال في رواية الوالبي: ما لا يتبين (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r4.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r4.claim: Mujahid says al-ʿafw is charity given from sufficiency.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: صدقة عن ظهر غنى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r5.claim: Al-ʿafw means increase; the verse until they grew and a poem about fat camels illustrate abundance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r5.anchor: وأصل العفو في اللغة: الزيادة، قال الله تعالى: {حتى عفوا}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r6.claim: Exegetes say people were told to give surplus, keeping a year’s expenses; obligatory zakat later abrogated this verse and earlier charity commands.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r6.anchor: قال أهل التفسير: أمروا أن ينفقوا الفضل، وكان أهل المكاسب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r7.claim: Readers pronounce al-ʿafw accusative or nominative; with mā-dhā as one interrogative, it is object and the answer is accusative.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r8.claim: With mā plus relative dhā, the question means what thing do they spend, and al-ʿafw is the nominative answer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r8.anchor: ومن رفع العفو جعل ذا (¬4) بعد (ما) بمنزلة الذي، ورد العفو عليه فرفع

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r9.claim: Abu Ishaq allows accusative al-ʿafw as the object of yanfiqūn and also allows nominative if mā-dhā is one word.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p155/r9.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: ويجوز أن تنصب {العفو} وإن كان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r1.claim: Thus points to the explanation of spending: just as He explained al-ʿafw, God clarifies signs so people reflect and know the afterlife is superior.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r1.anchor: أشار إلى ما بين في الإنفاق، كأنه قال: مثل الذي بينه لكم في الإنفاق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes thus as referring to God’s clarification about wine and gambling.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r2.anchor: وقيل: مثل البيان في الخمر والميسر يبين الله لكم الآيات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r3.claim: The singular demonstrative is addressed to a plural because a group is grammatically treated as a tribe or collective.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r3.anchor: وهو يخاطب جماعة؛ لأن الجماعة معناها القبيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r4.claim: The Qurʾan uses a singular demonstrative for a plural group, as in the address to the Prophet’s wives followed by that is easy for God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r4.anchor: الأصل: (ذلكن) (¬6)، إلا أن الجماعة في معنى القبيل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r5.claim: Alternatively the kāf addresses the Prophet alone; addressing him includes his community, as in the verse O Prophet, when you divorce women.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p158/r5.anchor: وجائز أن يكون الكاف للنبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، أي: كذلك أيها النبي

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p82#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p82#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p82#3/r1.claim: Al-maysir means gambling; Ibn Qutayba refers readers to his discussion of its benefit in al-Māʾida.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p82#3/r1.anchor: والميسر} القمار. وقد ذكرناه في سورة المائدة، وذكرنا النفع به.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p82#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p82#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p82#3/r2.claim: The question asks what they should give in charity.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p82#3/r2.anchor: ويسألونك ماذا ينفقون} أي: ماذا يتصدقون ويعطون؟

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p82#3/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p82#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p82#3/r3.claim: Al-ʿafw is the surplus beyond one's own and dependents' sustenance; it can also mean what comes easily, without compulsion or hardship.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p82#3/r3.anchor: قل العفو} يعني: فضل المال. يريد: أن يعطي ما فضل عن قوته وقوت عياله.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p82#3/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p82#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p82#3/r4.claim: The command to accept what people freely volunteer means not to press them for more than they offer.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p82#3/r4.anchor: ومنه قوله عز وجل: {خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف} (1) ؛ أي: اقبل من الناس عفوهم، وما تطوعوا به من أموالهم؛ ولا تستقص عليهم.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r6.speaker: عمر، ومعاذ، وسعد بن أبي وقاص
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r6.claim: ʿUmar, Muʿādh, and Saʿd ibn Abī Waqqāṣ asked the Messenger for a ruling because wine and gambling destroy reason and strip away wealth.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r6.anchor: نزلت في عمر، ومعاذ، وسعد بن أبي وقاص

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r7.claim: Wine is any intoxicant that mixes with and overcomes the intellect.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r7.anchor: وهو كل مسكر مخالط للعقل مغط عليه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r8.anchor: الميسر }: القمار { قل فيهما إثم كبير

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r9.claim: Their sin includes the quarrels, insults, obscene speech, falsehood, and other evils they cause.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r9.anchor: الإثم بسببهما لما فيهما من المخاصمة والمشاتمة وقول الفحش والزور وغير ذلك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r10.claim: Wine benefits sellers through money from trade and drinkers through pleasure; gambling yields winnings and can support poor people.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r10.anchor: ما كانوا يصيبونه من المال في بيع الخمر والتجارة فيها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r11.claim: The harms and sins caused by wine and gambling outweigh their benefits.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r11.anchor: ثم بين أن ما يحصل بسببهما من الإثم أكبر من نفعهما

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r12.claim: This verse did not itself prohibit wine and gambling; it preceded their prohibition in Sūrat al-Māʾida.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:218-219/r12.anchor: وليست هذه الآية المحرمة للخمر والميسر، إنما المحرمة التي في سورة المائدة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r1.speaker: عمرو بن الجموح
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r1.claim: After the verse about spending for parents and relatives, ʿAmr ibn al-Jamūḥ asked again how much should be spent.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r1.anchor: نزلت في سؤال عمرو بن الجموح لما نزل قوله:

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r2.claim: Al-ʿafw is the money left over after providing for one’s dependents.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r2.anchor: أي: ما فضل من المال عن العيال

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r3.claim: After this verse, a person kept enough from his earnings for his needs and gave away the remainder until zakat was prescribed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r3.anchor: وكان الرجل بعد نزول هذه الآية يأخذ من كسبه ما يكفيه، وينفق باقيه إلى أن فرضت الزكاة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r4.claim: The zakat verse in Sūrat Barāʾa abrogated this instruction and the earlier commands to give charity before zakat.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r4.anchor: فنسخت آية الزكاة التي في براءة هذه الآية وكل صدقة أمروا بها قبل الزكاة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r5.claim: Likewise may refer either to God’s explanation concerning wine and gambling or to His explanation about spending.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r5.anchor: أي: كبيانه في الخمر والميسر، أو في الإنفاق

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r6.claim: God explains the signs so people reflect on this world and the next and recognize the superiority of the afterlife over worldly life.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:219/r6.anchor: لتتفكروا في أمر الدنيا والآخرة، فتعرفوا فضل الآخرة على الدنيا

ELMALILI:2:219-220/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r1.claim: Elmalılı renders al-khamr as wine and al-maysir as gambling.
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r1.anchor: sana hamr ü meysirden, şarab ve kumardan soruyorlar.

ELMALILI:2:219-220/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r2.claim: ʿUmar, Muʿādh, and other Companions asked the Prophet for a ruling on wine because it removes the intellect; this verse was revealed.
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r2.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer ve Muâz ile beraber sahâbeden birtakım zevat idi “Yâ Resûlallah, hamr hakkında bize bir fetvâ ver çünkü aklı gideriyor” dediler ve bu âyet nâzil oldu.

ELMALILI:2:219-220/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r3.claim: Hamr originally means covering; specifically it names fermented grape juice after its foam subsides because it covers the intellect or clouds the head.
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r3.anchor: “Hamr”, esasen örtmek mânasına masdar olduğu hâlde “çiğ üzüm şırasından iştidad etmiş ve köpüğünü atmış olan şaraba isim olmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:219-220/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r4.claim: By extension, hamr can mean any substance that intoxicates, so all intoxicants fall under the word in its broad sense.

ELMALILI:2:219-220/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r5.speaker: İbn Ömer
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that at the time the wine prohibition was revealed, hamr came from grapes, dates, wheat, barley, and millet, and meant what clouds the intellect.
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r5.anchor: İbn Ömer hazretlerinden mervîdir ki tahrîm-i hamr nâzil olduğu gün hamr beş şeyden: üzümden, hurmadan, buğdaydan, arpadan, darıdan idi

ELMALILI:2:219-220/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r6.speaker: Nu‘mân b. Beşir
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r6.claim: A report in Abū Dāwūd attributes to the Prophet the statement that wine is made from grapes, dates, honey, wheat, and barley.
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r6.anchor: Ebû Dâvûd’da Nu‘mân b. Beşir’den rivayet olunduğu üzere Resûllullah إِنَّ مِنَ الْعِنَبِ خَمْرًا

ELMALILI:2:219-220/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r7.speaker: İmam Mâlik, İmam Şâfiî and many jurists
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r7.claim: Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and many earlier and later jurists take hamr broadly as any intoxicant, making every kind Qurʾanically forbidden, including every drop and its trade.
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r7.anchor: İmam Mâlik ve Şâfiî ve bunlardan mukaddem

ELMALILI:2:219-220/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r8.speaker: Ebû Hanîfe, his Companions and many early jurists
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r8.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and many early scholars say Qurʾanic hamr definitively means grape wine; other intoxicants are forbidden for intoxication by analogy and hadith, not by the word's certain scope.
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r8.anchor: İmam-ı A‘zam Ebû Hanîfe hazretleriyle beraber ashâb ve tâbi‘înden birçok ulemâ ve fukahâ “hamr” kelimesinin beyyin ve kat‘î olan mânası bilhassa üzüm şarabı

ELMALILI:2:219-220/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r9.claim: Elmalılı distinguishes the definitive Qurʾanic prohibition of grape wine from the broader possible meaning: other intoxicants are prohibited through the intoxication rationale and hadith, not the wording alone.
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r9.anchor: Lafz-ı Kur’ân’ın ma‘nâ-yı e‘amma hamli muhtemil ise de ma‘nâ-yı hâssı gibi kat‘î değildir.

ELMALILI:2:219-220/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r10.claim: Grape wine and drinks made from it are intrinsically impure, and even a drop may not be consumed; impurity of other intoxicants is uncertain, so contact need not invalidate prayer.
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r10.anchor: Üzüm şarabı ve bundan ma‘mul olan müskirât aynen necistir. Öbürlerinin ise necis olması şüphelidir.

ELMALILI:2:219-220/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r11.speaker: Ebû Hanîfe
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r11.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa held that a small amount of non-grape intoxicant could be drunk for strength if it did not intoxicate and was not consumed to imitate immoral people or unbelievers.
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r11.anchor: Ebû Hanîfe hazretleri bu suretle şarabdan mâ‘adâ müskirâtın aynı ve katresi necis ve haram olmadığına

ELMALILI:2:219-220/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r12.claim: The preferred Hanafi view, shared with the other three schools, follows the hadith that whatever intoxicates in a large amount is forbidden even in a small amount.
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r12.anchor: muhtâr olan مَا اَسْكَرَ كَثِيرُهُ فَقَلِيلُهُ حَرَامٌ

ELMALILI:2:219-220/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r13.claim: For the legal question of drinking, all intoxicants count as hamr in the broad sense; chemically, fermentation gives intoxicants a shared wine-like nature, reflected in the word alcohol.
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r13.anchor: Şer‘an şürb nokta-i nazarından bütün müskirât ma‘nâyı e‘ammıyla hamrdır.

ELMALILI:2:219-220/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r14.claim: Medicinal treatment follows the Qurʾanic concession for necessity, including needs treated as necessities.
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r14.anchor: zarûret ve zarûret hükmünde bulunan ihtiyaç mesâilindendir.

ELMALILI:2:219-220/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220/r15.claim: In the verse's translation, al-ʿafw is rendered as what does not burden or strain the giver.

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r1.claim: Elmalılı says wine prohibition came in four stages: it was initially permitted, and Muslims drank while the Prophet remained silent.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r1.anchor: Dîn-i İslâm’da hamrın ve müskirâtın men‘i tedrîcen vâki‘olmuştur. Bidâyet-i İslâm’da hamr henüz mubah idi.

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r2.speaker: Hazret-i Ömer ve Muâz ve diğer bazı ashâb-ı kirâm
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r2.claim: Umar, Muadh, and other Companions sought a ruling because wine removes reason, occasioning this verse.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r2.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer ve Muâz ve diğer bazı ashâb-ı kirâmın

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r3.claim: This began the prohibition, but its wording still left a possibility of permissibility; some quit immediately while others continued.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r3.anchor: ilk tahrim bununla başladı. Bunda memnû‘iyet zâhir olmakla beraber cevaz ihtimâli de yok değil idi.

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r7.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r7.claim: Ali is reported to say he would neither pray from a minaret built over a well touched by a drop of wine nor graze animals where a wine-tainted sea had dried.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r7.anchor: Hazret-i Ali’nin “bir kuyuya bir katre hamr düşse, sonra oraya bir minare yapılsa o minarede ezan okumazdım

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r8.speaker: Abdullah b. Ömer
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r8.claim: Ibn Umar is reported to say he would cut off a finger that had been dipped in wine.

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r9.claim: Maysir is a verbal noun from yusr or yasar meaning gambling, associated with acquiring or transferring wealth easily and without effort.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r9.anchor: “Yüsr” veya “yesar”dan masdar-ı mîmî olarak kumar oynamak mânasınadır

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r10.claim: Gambling means staking money on an uncertain, risky outcome whose result is unknown, to give or receive wealth.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r10.anchor: Kumar demek de zar gibi ne olacağı belli olmayan muhâtaralı bir şeye ta‘lîk ile mal vermek veya almak demektir.

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r11.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs gambled using games learned from Arabs, Persians, and others, including backgammon and chess.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r11.anchor: Câhiliyede Arablar gerek kendilerinden ve gerek Acemlerden ve sâireden belledikleri “nerd” yani tavla, “şatranc” ve sâire gibi oyunlarla kumar oynarlardı.

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r12.claim: A lottery used ten named arrows to divide a slaughtered camel into twenty-eight shares, with seven arrows assigned increasing portions from one to seven.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r12.anchor: Zar makamında ezlâm ü aklâm denilen on okları vardı, bunlara fezz, tev’em, rakīb, hils, nâfis, müsbil, mu‘allâ, menîh, sefîh, vağd derlerdi

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r13.claim: Three arrows were blank; participants drew on one another's behalf, losers paid for the camel, and winners donated their portions to the poor.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r13.anchor: Menîh, sefîh, vağd okları boş ve mahrumdur. Bu on kalemin hepsi “rebâbe” denilen bir torbaya atılıp

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r14.claim: Because the lottery was treated as charity and an honorable practice despite being gambling, maysir came to denote gambling generally.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r14.anchor: meysir evvelemirde diğer kumarlara nazaran ehven-i şer gibi görünen ve hayır zannedilen böyle tevzî‘ü istiksam, yani piyango tarzına ıtlak edilmiş

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r15.claim: Elmalılı cites a hadith classifying children's knucklebone and walnut games as maysir.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r15.anchor: bir hadîs-i şerîfte çocukların aşık ve ceviz oynamaları bile meysirden ma‘- dud olduğu beyan buyurulmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r16.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r16.claim: Ali rejected a wager in which one person promised eggs to another who could eat a specified quantity, ruling that it was gambling.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r16.anchor: bunlar Hazret-i Ali’ye mürâfa‘a oldular, “bu kumardır” diye cevaz vermedi.

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r17.claim: If even a lottery framed as charity is forbidden, ordinary forms of gambling are forbidden all the more.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r17.anchor: Zaten hayır nâmına piyango haram olunca diğer kumarların haram olacağı evleviyetle anlaşılır.

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r18.claim: Asking about wine and gambling together points to their customary association.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r18.anchor: Hamr ile meysirin bir sualde derci de müskirât ile kumarın murâfakatlarına işârettir.

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r19.claim: Both waste wealth and ruin people, and each commonly leads to the other; wine removes reason, enabling innumerable crimes and evils linked to gambling.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r19.anchor: ikisi de malları telef ve insanları perişan eder, ‘ale’l-ekser bunlar birbirine sürükler. Evvelâ hamr aklı selb eyler

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r20.claim: Their benefits include some pleasure and enjoyment, substantial trade, courage for the fearful, strength of temperament, and windfall gains from gambling.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r20.anchor: Ezcümle biraz neşve ve lezzet duyulur, hayli ticaret yapılır

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r21.claim: The gains are temporary and illusory, while losses include hangovers, disaster, ruined health, worthless profit, addiction, and individual, social, physical, and moral harm.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r21.anchor: Hâsılı neşe ve lezzetleri ferdî ve muvakkat olduğu hâlde zararları, mefsedetleri hem ferdî ve ictimâ‘îdir

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r22.claim: Because preventing harm takes precedence over obtaining benefit, reason itself requires these practices to be forbidden; imagined small gains risk certain, sweeping loss.

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r23.claim: The verse entails legal prohibition, but by itself does not state an unambiguous intrinsic ban; some Companions missed the legal force of its rational warning until 5:90–91 gave an explicit, absolute command.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r23.anchor: bu tahrim, li-‘aynihi sarih bir tahrim olmazdı, aklına güvenerek mazarratlarını tahdid ve menfaatlerinden istifade edeceğiz zannedenler bulunabilirdi.

ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r24.claim: Elmalılı says the later command in 5:90–91 explicitly and absolutely forbade wine.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#2/r24.anchor: sûret-i sarîha ve mutlakada tahrîm-i şer‘î vârid olmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r1.claim: The question can ask either what causes or recipients should receive spending, or what amount or property should be spent; the first was answered earlier, the latter now.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r1.anchor: مَاذَا يُنفِقُونَ iki mânaya gelir: Birisi neye infak yapılacağını sormak, diğeri de ne infak edileceğini sormaktır

ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r2.claim: Al-afw means spending what remains beyond one's necessary needs.

ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r3.claim: Earn wealth through lawful means, then give its surplus beyond necessities to the charitable causes already described.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r3.anchor: piyango, kumar gibi gayr-i meşrû‘vesâit ile değil, esbâb-ı meşrû‘a ile mal kazanınız

ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r4.claim: Dependents include young children, a wife, needy parents, and comparable ascendants; their support counts as one's own, so charity must not leave them or oneself without necessities.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r4.anchor: evlâd-ı sığar, zevce, muhtaç olan ebeveyn ve bunlara mülhak olan usûl; ehl ü ‘iyâldendir

ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r5.claim: God explains legal signs and proofs so people may reflect, understand their purposes, and act on them.
ELMALILI:2:219-220#3/r5.anchor: tefekkür edip de makāsıdına vâkıf olabilesiniz ve muktezâsıyla amel edesiniz

MAJAZ:v1p73/r3.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p73/r3.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p73/r3.claim: Al-ʿafw is what one can afford, and also moderation or what is readily clear for one; take what is easy and available to you.
MAJAZ:v1p73/r3.anchor: قل العفو» (218) أي الطاقة التي تطيقها والقصد، تقول: خذ ما عفا لك، أي ما صفا لك.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r1.claim: The prohibition unfolded in stages: an early Meccan notice of fruit benefits, then a ban on praying while intoxicated, this comparison of harms and benefits, and finally categorical prohibition.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r1.anchor: Sarhoşluk veren içkiler hakkında dört âyet gelmiştir. Bunlardan ikisinde içkinin yanında kumar da zikredilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r2.speaker: Hz. Ömer ve birçok sahâbî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r2.claim: Umar and many Companions repeatedly asked for clarification about wine and gambling; their requests are cited among the occasions for the successive explanatory and prohibitory revelations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r2.anchor: Başta Hz. Ömer olmak üzere birçok sahâbînin çeşitli sebeplerle içki ve kumarın hükmünün açıklanmasını istemeleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r3.claim: The extant Torah and Gospels do not appear to prohibit wine.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r3.anchor: Eldeki Tevrat’a ve İncil’e bakıldığında içkinin bu kitaplarda yasaklandığını söylemek mümkün değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r4.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs prized wine’s intoxication and pleasure and gambling’s entertainment, excitement, hospitality, and aid to the poor, while overlooking the harms.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r4.anchor: içkinin sarhoşluk ve keyif veren tarafına, kumarın da eğlence, heyecan, eşe dosta ikram

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r5.claim: The verse stresses that wine and gambling do more harm than good; some people therefore gave up wine even before the final prohibition.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r5.anchor: içki ve kumarın bazı faydaları bulunsa da zararının daha fazla olduğuna dikkat çekti, bu yüzden

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r6.claim: The final prohibition explains that Satan uses wine and gambling to create enmity and hatred and to turn people from remembrance of God and prayer.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r6.anchor: şeytanın, insanların arasına düşmanlık ve kin sokmak, onları Allah’ı anmaktan ve namazdan alıkoymak için içki ve kumarı araç olarak kullandığı

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r7.claim: God may command or forbid without giving a reason and is not answerable for His acts; human beings, by contrast, are responsible.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r7.anchor: gerekçe göstermeden de bazı şeyleri farz ve bazı şeyleri de haram kılabilir. O, yaptıklarından hesap verme ve sorgulanma durumunda değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r8.claim: God’s explanations of the wisdom behind commands help people act consciously and apply divine intent without error where no explicit ruling exists.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r8.anchor: emir ve yasaklarının hikmet ve gerekçesini açıklaması, kulların neyi niçin yaptıklarının şuurunda olmalarını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r9.claim: Wine can cause addiction, impaired judgment, conflict and mockery, neglect of God and useful activity, waste, and harm to health and future generations.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r9.anchor: Giderek alışkanlık yapması, akıl ve iradenin doğru kullanılmasını engellemesi, düşmanlık ve kinin oluşmasına sebep olan tartışmalara ve kavgalara

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r10.claim: Wine’s benefits are commercial and economic returns and temporary pleasure for the user.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r10.anchor: Ticarî ve ekonomik getirilerinin bulunması ve kullanana geçici zevk vermesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r11.claim: Islam forbids intoxicating drinks and drugs with comparable or greater effects because their harms outweigh limited benefits that can be obtained elsewhere.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r11.anchor: sarhoşluk veren içkileri ve aynı etkiyi fazlasıyla hâsıl eden uyuşturucu vb. nesneleri kullanmayı haram kılmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r12.claim: Medina mainly used date-based wine, imported grape wine from Yemen, Taif, and Syria, and also consumed intoxicating raisin/date infusions and drinks made from honey, corn, or barley; intoxicating varieties were called khamr.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r12.anchor: Medine’de kullanılan içki daha çok hurma suyundan yapılırdı. Üzüm suyundan yapılan şarap ise Yemen, Tâif ve Suriye’den getirtilirdi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r13.claim: In Arabic, khamr commonly names all these intoxicating drinks.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r13.anchor: Bütün bu içkilerin sarhoşluk veren çeşitleri Arapça’da hamr kelimesiyle ifade edilmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r14.speaker: bazı lugatçılar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r14.claim: Some lexicographers restrict khamr to wine made from unboiled grape juice.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r14.anchor: Bazı lugatçılara göre ise “hamr” özellikle pişmemiş üzüm suyundan yapılan şarabın adıdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r15.speaker: bazı fıkıhçılar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r15.claim: Some jurists, following the narrow definition of khamr, held that every amount of grape wine is forbidden but other intoxicants are forbidden only in an intoxicating quantity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r15.anchor: bazı fıkıhçılar dar mânada “Hamrın yani ateşte kaynatılmamış üzümden yapılan şarabın, azı da çoğu da haramdır; diğer sarhoşluk veren içkilerin

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r16.claim: After later assessment ended the disagreement, all recognized Islamic legal schools agreed that every amount of any intoxicant is forbidden and may not be consumed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r16.anchor: muteber İslâm fıkıh mezheplerinin tamamı “Sarhoşluk veren nesnelerin azı da çoğu da haramdır, içilemez, vücuda alınamaz” hükmünde birleşmişlerdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r17.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r17.claim: A cited hadith says that a small quantity is forbidden when a large quantity of the substance intoxicates; no grading is stated.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r17.anchor: “Çoğu sarhoş eden nesnenin azı da haramdır” (Ebû Dâvûd, “Eşribe”, 5; Tirmizî, “Eşribe”, 3)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r18.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r18.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r18.claim: A cited hadith says khamr can be made from grape juice, raisins, dates, wheat, barley, or corn, and describes it as what clouds reason and intoxicates; no grading is stated.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r18.anchor: “Hamr üzüm suyundan, kuru üzüm, kuru hurma, buğday, arpa ve mısırdan olur; hamr, aklı örten, sarhoş eden nesnedir...”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r19.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r19.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r19.claim: A cited hadith states that every intoxicant is khamr and every intoxicant is forbidden; no grading is stated.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r19.anchor: “Sarhoş eden her şey hamrdır ve sarhoş eden her şey haramdır” (Müslim, “Eşribe”, 73-75; Tirmizî, “Eşribe”, 1-2)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r20.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r20.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r20.claim: Maysir was named alongside wine because it was entertainment and supplied meat to eat with wine.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r20.anchor: Hem eğlence olduğu hem de içki yanında meze olarak kullanılacak et teminine araç kılındığı için Kur’an’da içki ile birlikte zikredilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r21.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r21.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r21.claim: Maysir was played with a camel bought on credit, divided into 28 portions; ten arrows, seven marked with shares and three blank, were drawn, with winners receiving meat shares and losers paying the cost.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r21.anchor: Veresiye bir deve satın alınır, yirmi sekiz parçaya bölünürdü. On adet küçük okun yedisine hisseler yazılır, üçü de boş bırakılarak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r22.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r22.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r22.claim: Gambling offered some material benefits through entertainment, food, and drink, but brought far greater sin and harm, including idleness, hostility, neglect of worship, wasted time, lost wealth, and broken households.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r22.anchor: Kumar da eğlenme, yeme ve içme gibi bazı maddî faydalar sağlamakla beraber bunlarla ölçülemeyecek büyüklükte zarar ve günah getirmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r23.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r23.speaker: fıkıhçılar ve tefsirciler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r23.claim: Jurists and exegetes classify all games producing the same result and harms, even if their forms differ, as gambling and forbidden.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r23.anchor: Fıkıhçılar ve tefsirciler şekil bakımından farklı da olsa aynı sonucu doğuran ve aynı zararları hâsıl eden oyunların tamamını kumar saymış ve haram olduğunu ifade etmişlerdir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r24.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r24.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r24.claim: As wine and gambling began to be prohibited, people who used them to aid the poor asked what to give; God answered “al-afw,” meaning surplus after needs or a suitable part of it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r24.anchor: “Affı infak edin”, yani “İhtiyaçtan artan miktarı veya bu miktardan uygun bir kısmı yoksullara, muhtaçlara verin”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r25.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r25.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r25.claim: People should meet their own and close relatives’ needs first; providing maintenance to some relatives is a legal and moral duty for those able to do so.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r25.anchor: Aksine insanların yakınlarına infakta öncelik tanıması birçok âyet ve hadiste emredildi, imkânı olanların bir kısım yakınlarına nafaka sağlaması da ona hukukî ve ahlâkî olarak borç kılındı.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r26.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r26.speaker: Ebû Zer el-Gıfârî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r26.claim: Abu Dharr held that surplus wealth may not be hoarded or invested for profit and must go to the needy while they remain.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r26.anchor: Sahâbeden Ebû Zer el-Gıfârî’ye göre ihtiyaçtan artan malın saklanması, işletilip üzerinden kazanç sağlanması câiz değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r27.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r27.speaker: İslâm âlimlerinin büyük çoğunluğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r27.claim: The majority hold that obligatory transfers are limited to maintenance and zakat; other giving is voluntary, rewarded if done but not sinful to omit.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r27.anchor: İslâm âlimlerinin büyük çoğunluğuna göre ise farz olan servet aktarımı nafaka ve zekâtla sınırlıdır. Bunun dışında kalan infaklar nâfile ibadet hükmündedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r28.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r28.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r28.claim: The authors conclude that while people lack basic necessities, those who do not help meet those needs remain accountable for their surplus wealth.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r28.anchor: bizde hâsıl olan kanaat ve anlayışa göre toplum içinde temel ihtiyaçlarını temin edememiş insanlar bulunduğu müddetçe

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r29.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r29.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r29.claim: Broadening aid beyond gambling proceeds and zakat to surplus goods, food, and clothing promotes social justice and makes unmet basic needs rare.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:219/r29.anchor: Yoksullara ve ihtiyaç sahiplerine yardımın yalnızca kumara ve şans oyunlarına veya zenginlerin zekâtına bırakılmayıp daha geniş bir tabana yayılması

NAHHAS:v1p308/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p308/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p308/r6.claim: Al-Ḥaramayn and Abū ʿAmr read kabīr, while the Kufans read kathīr; kabīr is preferable, matching ṣaghīr/kabīr and the established pair kabāʾir/ṣaghāʾir.
NAHHAS:v1p308/r6.anchor: هذه قراءة أهل الحرمين وأبي عمرو بن العلاء وقرأ الكوفيون ( كثير ) وإجماعهم على حوبا كبيرا

NAHHAS:v1p308/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p308/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p308/r7.claim: The Ḥaramayn and Kufans read al-ʿafw accusative, while Abū ʿAmr, ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read nominative; both are grammatical, but the verse’s interpretation favors accusative.
NAHHAS:v1p308/r7.anchor: هكذا قرأ أهل الحرمين وأهل الكوفة وقرأ أبو عمرو وعيسى بن عمر وابن أبي إسحاق

NAHHAS:v1p308/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p308/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p308/r8.claim: If dhā means “that which,” nominative is preferred but accusative is allowed; if mādhā is one word, accusative is preferred but nominative is allowed. Both occur in the question ماذا تعلمت أنحوا أم شعرا.
NAHHAS:v1p308/r8.anchor: إن جعلت ذا بمعنى الذي كان الاختيار الرفع وجاز النصب وإن جعلت ما وذا شيئا واحدا

NAHHAS:v1p308/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p308/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v1p308/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains al-ʿafw as the surplus.
NAHHAS:v1p308/r9.anchor: قال ابن عباس الفضل وقال العفو ما يفضل عن أهلك

NAHHAS:v1p308/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p308/r10.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v1p308/r10.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes the instruction to mean: spend the surplus.
NAHHAS:v1p308/r10.anchor: وقال الحسن المعنى قل أنفقوا العفو

NAHHAS:v1p308/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p308/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p308/r11.claim: The reflection invited here concerns both worldly life and the Hereafter.
NAHHAS:v1p308/r11.anchor: وقال أبو جعفر وقد بينا ( لعلكم تتفكرون في الدنيا والآخرة )

ITQAN:v1p79#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p79#2/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
ITQAN:v1p79#2/r5.claim: Al-Tayalisi transmits Ibn Umar's account of alcohol's three-stage prohibition: first 2:219 left people free to benefit, then 4:43 prohibited drinking near prayer, and finally 5:90 prompted the Prophet to declare it forbidden.
ITQAN:v1p79#2/r5.anchor: روى الطيالسي في مسنده عن ابن عمر قال نزل في الخمر ثلاث آيات فأول شيء

ITQAN:v2p421/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
ITQAN:v2p421/r1.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb says plural الرياح denotes mercy throughout the Quran, while singular الريح denotes punishment.
ITQAN:v2p421/r1.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال كل شيء في القرآن من الرياح فهي رحمة وكل شيء فيه من الريح فهو عذاب

ITQAN:v2p421/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r2.speaker: الضحاك
ITQAN:v2p421/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak says every Quranic mention of a cup means wine.
ITQAN:v2p421/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك قال كل كأس ذكره الله في القرآن إنما عنى به الخمر

ITQAN:v2p421/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r3.speaker: الضحاك
ITQAN:v2p421/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses فاطر in the Quran as Creator.
ITQAN:v2p421/r3.anchor: وأخرج عنه قال كل شيء في القرآن فاطر فهو خالق

ITQAN:v2p421/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ITQAN:v2p421/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says every occurrence of إفك in the Quran means a lie.
ITQAN:v2p421/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال كل شيء في القرآن إفك فهو كذب

ITQAN:v2p421/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
ITQAN:v2p421/r5.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya says Quranic commands to enjoin right mean Islam, while prohibitions of wrong mean worship of idols.
ITQAN:v2p421/r5.anchor: عن أبي العالية قال كل آية في القرآن في الأمر بالمعروف فهو الإسلام والنهي عن المنكر فهو عبادة الأوثان

ITQAN:v2p421/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
ITQAN:v2p421/r6.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya says Quranic references to guarding sexual parts generally mean avoiding adultery.
ITQAN:v2p421/r6.anchor: عن أبي العالية قال كل آية في القرآن يذكر فيها حفظ الفرج فهو من الزنى

ITQAN:v2p421/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r8.speaker: مجاهد
ITQAN:v2p421/r8.claim: Mujahid says the Quranic phrase إن الإنسان كفور refers to unbelievers.
ITQAN:v2p421/r8.anchor: عن مجاهد قال كل شيء في القرآن إن الإنسان كفور إنما يعني به الكفار

ITQAN:v2p421/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r9.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
ITQAN:v2p421/r9.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz says every mention of abiding eternally means there is no repentance.
ITQAN:v2p421/r9.anchor: عن عمر بن عبد العزيز قال كل شيء في القرآن خلود فإنه لا توبة له

ITQAN:v2p421/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r10.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
ITQAN:v2p421/r10.claim: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam says يقدر means “decrease” wherever it occurs in the Quran.
ITQAN:v2p421/r10.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم قال كل شيء في القرآن يقدر فمعناه يقل

ITQAN:v2p421/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r11.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
ITQAN:v2p421/r11.claim: The same authority glosses التزكي throughout the Quran as Islam.
ITQAN:v2p421/r11.anchor: وأخرج عنه قال التزكي في القرآن كله إسلام

ITQAN:v2p421/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r12.speaker: أبو مالك
ITQAN:v2p421/r12.claim: Abu Malik says وراء means “before” throughout the Quran, except in two verses where it means “other than.”
ITQAN:v2p421/r12.anchor: وأخرج عن أبي مالك قال وراء في القرآن أمام كله غير حرفين

ITQAN:v2p421/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r13.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
ITQAN:v2p421/r13.claim: Abu Bakr ibn ʿAyyash distinguishes the Quranic forms كسفا: one denotes punishment and the other a piece of cloud.
ITQAN:v2p421/r13.anchor: عن أبي بكر بن عياش قال ما كان كسفا فهو عذاب وما كان كسفا فهو قطع السحاب

ITQAN:v2p421/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r14.speaker: عكرمة
ITQAN:v2p421/r14.claim: ʿIkrima distinguishes what God made from what people made using two forms of سد.
ITQAN:v2p421/r14.anchor: عن عكرمة قال ما صنع الله فهو السد ما صنع الناس فهو السد

ITQAN:v2p421/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r15.speaker: أبو روق
ITQAN:v2p421/r15.claim: Abu Rawq says every Quranic occurrence of جعل means “created.”
ITQAN:v2p421/r15.anchor: عن أبي روق قال كل شيء في القرآن جعل فهو خلق

ITQAN:v2p421/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r16.speaker: مجاهد
ITQAN:v2p421/r16.claim: Mujahid glosses المباشرة in the Quran as sexual intercourse.
ITQAN:v2p421/r16.anchor: عن مجاهد قال المباشرة في كل كتاب الله الجماع

ITQAN:v2p421/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r17.speaker: ابن زيد
ITQAN:v2p421/r17.claim: Ibn Zayd says فاسق means liar throughout the Quran, with a few exceptions.
ITQAN:v2p421/r17.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال كل شيء في القرآن فاسق فهو كاذب إلا قليلا

ITQAN:v2p421/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r18.speaker: السدي
ITQAN:v2p421/r18.claim: Al-Suddi says حنيفا means Muslim and حنفاء means Muslims who are pilgrims.
ITQAN:v2p421/r18.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن السدي قال ما كان في القرآن

ITQAN:v2p421/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p421/r19.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ITQAN:v2p421/r19.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr gives three Quranic senses of العفو: pardoning sin, the surplus to spend here, and forbearance between people.
ITQAN:v2p421/r19.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال العفو في القرآن على ثلاثة أنحاء نحو تجاوز عن الذنب ونحو في القصد في النفقة

ITQAN:v2p516/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p516/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p516/r1.claim: For the nominative reading, al-Suyuti prefers parsing ما as interrogative and ذا as relative, yielding “what they spend is the surplus”; this matches nominal question and answer.
ITQAN:v2p516/r1.anchor: ما استفهاما وذا موصولة وهو أرجح الوجهين

ITQAN:v2p516/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p516/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p516/r2.claim: For the accusative reading, he prefers ماذا as a single interrogative form, yielding “they spend the surplus”; a verb question is answered by a verb phrase.
ITQAN:v2p516/r2.anchor: الثالث أن تكون ماذا كلها استفهاما على التركيب وهو أرجح الوجهين

ITQAN:v2p516/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p516/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p516/r3.claim: Other possible parses make ذا demonstrative, ماذا a noun meaning “something” or a relative, ما extra, or ذا extra after interrogative ما.
ITQAN:v2p516/r3.anchor: الرابع أن يكون ماذا كله اسم جنس بمعنى شيء أو موصولا بمعنى الذي

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p42/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p42/r1.speaker: author
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p42/r1.claim: Al-Suyūṭī says the account concerning the question about wine will be given in his discussion of Surat al-Māʾida.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p42/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ يسألونك عن الخمر ﴾ يأتي حديثها في سورة المائدة

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p42/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p42/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p42/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that companions ordered to spend in God's cause asked what portion of their wealth they should give; the answer was to spend the surplus.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p42/r2.anchor: من طريق سعيد أو عكرمة عن ابن عباس أن نفرا من الصحابة حين أمروا بالنفقة في سبيل الله أتوا النبي

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p42/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p42/r3.speaker: يحيى
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p42/r3.claim: Yaḥyā relates that Muʿādh b. Jabal and Thaʿlaba asked what to spend from their wealth because they had dependents and families; this verse was revealed.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p42/r3.anchor: وأخرج أيضا عن يحيى أنه بلغه أن معاذ بن جبل وثعلبة أتيا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالا يا رسول الله إن لنا أرقاء وأهلين

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p71#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p71#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p71#2/r1.claim: Al-Wahidi reports that Umar, Muadh ibn Jabal, and some Ansar asked Muhammad for guidance about wine and gambling, saying both impair reason and consume wealth.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p71#2/r1.anchor: نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب ومعاذ بن جبل ونفر من الأنصار أتوا رسول الله

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r8.claim: Āyāt can mean commands and prohibitions that God makes clear.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p154/r8.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن الآية في القرآن على ستة أوجه : -

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p436/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p436/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p436/r1.claim: ʿAfw can mean pardon, as in God’s forgiving a servant.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p436/r1.anchor: العفو : يقال ويراد به الصفح . ومنه عفو الله

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p436/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p436/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p436/r2.claim: ʿAfw can mean disappearance of a trace, as when dust covers and hides a dwelling’s remains.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p436/r2.anchor: ويقال ويراد به : زوال الأثر . يقال : عفت الديار ، إذا غطى التراب أثرها فخفيت

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p436/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p436/r3.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p436/r3.claim: Ibn Fāris says ʿafw is lawful, good wealth; ʿafāt are petitioners, and ʿafw of wealth is what remains beyond expenses.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p436/r3.anchor: قال ابن فارس : والعفو : حلال المال وطيبه . والعفاة : طلاب المعروف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p436/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p436/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p436/r6.claim: ʿAfw can mean the surplus wealth available after one’s needs.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p436/r6.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن العفو في القرآن على أربعة أوجه : -

BURHAN:v4p52/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p52/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p52/r4.claim: The first three questions appear without conjunction because they arose at separate times; the later questions are joined with wāw because they were asked together.
BURHAN:v4p52/r4.anchor: لأن سؤالهم عن الحوادث الأول وقع متفرقا عن الحوادث

BURHAN:v1p133/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p133/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p133/r1.claim: The phrase لعلكم تتفكرون occurs twice in al-Baqara.
BURHAN:v1p133/r1.anchor: ﴿ لعلكم تتفكرون ﴾ فى القرآن اثنان فى البقرة

ITQAN:v3p302/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p302/r5.speaker: الكرماني
ITQAN:v3p302/r5.claim: Al-Karmani explains that four “they ask you” questions lack a conjunction because they were asked at separate times; three later questions use one because they arose together.
ITQAN:v3p302/r5.anchor: في العجائب للكرماني إن قيل كيف جاء ( يسألونك ) أربع مرات بغير واو
